name: s42_00000.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and round. Two glyphs sit side by side at the center. On the left is a Sights Set sign, an upward arrow on a stem ending in a small diamond. On the right is a water sigil, an S-curve between two teardrops, drawn slightly roughly. Each is small, about a quarter of the ring's radius. A Projection sign, a flat-topped bracket, sits at the south-southeast with its top toward the center. An Aeriforms Defined sign, three short strokes, sits near the ring at the northeast with its top toward the center. A Holding sign, two curved strokes each with a dot, sits at the west, turned with its top toward the ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell. Its small size gives a modest intensity, and its slightly rough lines make the effect a little weaker and shorter lived. Sights Set at the center lets the caster aim the spell at a chosen point. Projection works with it to send the effect outward from the seal toward that point. Holding is likely non-directional, so its rotation does not change its effect. It keeps the water in the shape the seal defines while still letting it move. Aeriforms Defined is a poorly understood air modifier. It is read here as giving the water an airy, vapor-like character, which is a guess. Aiming and projection serve one purpose, so the seal combines three kinds of modifier and stays coherent. The signs are balanced around the ring, so no side is favored beyond where the caster aims.
effect: Sends a small, cohesive cloud of misty water outward toward a point the caster aims at. The cloud keeps its shape as it travels. It is fairly weak and thins out and disperses somewhat sooner than a cleanly drawn version would.

name: s42_00003.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn neatly in black on a white background, with two concentric rings, both closed. A wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes, sits at the center at a moderate size relative to the ring. Inside the inner ring, a Concealment sign (an eight-armed star with eye marks) sits at the southeast and an Envelopment sign (a slanted stroke with hooked ends) sits at the southwest. In the band between the two rings are five Crushing signs at the north, east-northeast, southeast, south, and west-northwest. Each is drawn with its top toward the center, so the northern one reads as a W and the southern one as an M; all five are inverted. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil makes this a wind spell that moves and manipulates air, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. The second ring adds strength to the core spell. Crushing is semi-directional, so inverting it reverses its effect: instead of breaking solids apart, the five inverted signs pull crushed or scattered material back into its original form. Five of them spread evenly around the outer band make that reforming strong and even on all sides. Concealment hides a target, and Envelopment makes an effect surround what it targets. Together they wrap the target in a hiding layer, as in shadow-cloaking seals. Read together, the air current carries loose fragments and dust, the inverted Crushing reassembles them, and Concealment with Envelopment shapes the result into a covering that hides whatever it surrounds. These modifiers work toward one purpose and do not contradict each other.
effect: Stirs a steady current of air that sweeps up nearby dust and broken fragments and temporarily fuses them back into solid pieces. Those pieces are wrapped around the target as a shell that hides it from view. When the spell ends, the reformed material crumbles back into loose debris.

name: s42_00014.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a plain background, ring closed. Two glyphs sit side by side at the center. On the left is a small, slightly rough glyph resembling the wind sigil: the spiral and its flanking dashes are present, but the lower part of the spiral is missing. On the right is a somewhat larger, neatly drawn glyph resembling the light sigil, a diamond set in a square with four arms crossing it. Its halves are mirror images of each other. Six signs are spread evenly around the seal. Two Entwining signs sit at the north-northwest and southwest with their tops toward the center. Three Orb signs sit at the northeast, west-northwest and south. At the east-southeast is a glyph resembling a Solidification sign stretched wide and set at an angle. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: Neither central glyph matches a sigil exactly. The left one is closest to the wind sigil and the right one to the light sigil; both readings are guesses. The light glyph is larger and neater, so light dominates and sets the main element. The wind glyph is small, rough and incomplete, so its air-moving contribution is weak and short-lived. The three evenly spaced Orb signs define a spherical space above the seal where the spell's material collects, filling from the bottom up. The two Entwining signs make the effect wrap itself around other objects. The stretched glyph is read as Solidification, also a guess; stretched wide, it would make the magic firmer over a broader area. These three kinds of modifier do not contradict each other, and the signs are balanced, so the spell has no set direction.
effect: Gathers light into a firm, glowing sphere above the seal that can wrap itself around nearby objects. A faint stirring of air drifts the sphere about, but the movement is weak and patchy and dies out well before the light does. The light itself dims gradually over time.

name: s42_00020.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. Two sigils sit side by side at the center, both small relative to the ring. On the left is a light sigil, a diamond inside a square with four short spokes. On the right is a wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes. Three Purification signs, each a small curl with its top toward the center, sit about halfway between the center and the ring. One is at the north, one at the east-southeast and one at the west-southwest, spaced evenly around the seal. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The seal has two sigils. The light sigil creates light that diminishes over time. The wind sigil moves and manipulates existing air but does not create it. Both are small relative to the ring, so the intensity is modest. Purification normally separates waste from water. Paired with a wind sigil, it reads as separating dust and impurities from the air being moved. Purification is asymmetric, so its exact behavior is less predictable than that of symmetric signs. Still, all three copies are drawn the same way and evenly spaced, so the effect is balanced and favors no direction. Only one kind of modifier is present, nothing contradicts, and the neat drawing and closed ring mean the spell activates and holds.
effect: Stirs a gentle current of air through the area around the seal and strips dust and impurities out of it, leaving the air cleaner. A soft glow accompanies the current and lights up the drifting motes as they are separated out, then slowly dims over time.

name: s42_00021.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The main ring is closed and neatly drawn, though slightly uneven in outline. A small wind sigil sits at the center. Five Entwining signs are spaced evenly just inside the ring at the north, east-southeast, south-southeast, southwest and west-northwest positions. Four have their tops toward the ring, while the north one is turned at an angle. Two small sub-seals sit inside the main ring, each holding an earth sigil that is large relative to its own small ring. The north-northeast sub-seal is ring closed and a little rough. The south-southwest sub-seal is ring open, with a gap on its lower left, and its earth sigil is fainter and also a little rough. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the main spell moves and manipulates air. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Entwining makes an effect wrap itself around other objects. With five of them balanced around the ring, the moving air coils around nearby objects evenly from all sides rather than pushing in one direction. The angled north sign does not break this balance. The closed north-northeast sub-seal is a small earth spell that adds manipulation of solid matter such as soil and sand. Its sigil is strong for its ring, but the sub-seal is tiny and roughly drawn, so its contribution is weak and short-lived. The south-southwest sub-seal is ring open, so it does not activate and adds nothing. Wind, Entwining and earth work together without contradiction, so the seal is not unstable.
effect: Raises modest currents of air that wind around nearby objects and wrap them from every side. A thin trace of soil or sand is drawn along with the coiling wind, but it thins out and drops away well before the wind itself fades.

name: s42_00036.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A light sigil, a diamond set inside a square with four short spokes, sits at the center at moderate size relative to the ring. Three Gathering signs sit inside the inner ring at the north-northwest, east-northeast and south-southeast positions, roughly evenly spaced. Each is turned to a different angle, and their arrowheads all point roughly the same way around the ring rather than straight toward the center. A single small Partition sign sits in the band between the two rings at the west point, its peaked top facing the outer ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil makes this a light spell, and its moderate size gives the effect moderate strength. The second ring adds strength and room for further effects. Gathering lets a spell draw material in from its surroundings to build its effect, so here the spell pulls in ambient light. The three signs are evenly spaced, so they draw from all sides. Because their arrows all point the same way around the ring, the light may swirl as it gathers, though this reading is a guess. Partition outlines the border of an area of effect that extends outward and upward. Its place in the outer band frames the space where the gathered light settles. Since there is only one Partition sign, the boundary may be firmer on the west side. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they do not conflict, so the seal is steady.
effect: Draws in surrounding light from every side and collects it into a glowing, bounded space above the seal. The light may drift in a gentle swirl as it gathers. The glow is moderately bright and holds within its borders, then slowly dims over time.

name: s42_00037.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, made of two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A Rain sign sits upright at the center with no element sigil inside it, and it is small relative to the ring. Six Stretch signs sit in the band between the two rings. Four of them, at the east-northeast, south-southeast, west-southwest and north-northwest, have the top of their arch toward the center. The other two, at the east-southeast and west-northwest, are flipped so the top of their arch faces the outer ring. The west-southwest Stretch is a little rough, and the rest are neat. Inside the inner ring are two small closed sub-seals. One at the west-northwest holds an upright Refuse sign, drawn a little roughly. One at the east-southeast holds an upright Envelopment sign. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the Rain sign at the center is the core of the seal. Rain summons a target material, bringing it down from above, so the spell is tied to whatever material is in reach rather than to one element. Its small size gives it a modest strength. The second ring adds more effect and power to the core. The Stretch signs ring the seal and turn solid matter that touches it into long, flexible ribbons. Stretch is thought to be non-directional, so the two flipped signs should act the same as the other four. That keeps the effect even, and with the signs balanced around the ring, no side is favored. The Refuse sub-seal is a directional sign. Drawn upright, it collects unwanted material and waste toward the top of the seal, away from the useful material. The Envelopment sub-seal makes the effect wrap around whatever it targets. Rain sets the core, with Stretch, Refuse and Envelopment as three modifiers that support each other without contradiction, so the seal is not unstable. The slightly rough Stretch and Refuse signs weaken those parts a little.
effect: Draws down nearby material from above in a modest shower. Any solid matter that reaches the seal is spun into long, flexible ribbons that wrap around the target. Debris and waste in the material are sorted off toward the top of the seal, though a little grit slips through, and the ribbons on the west-southwest side form slightly thinner and give out sooner than the rest.

name: s42_00038.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. The second ring sits just inside the first. A Link sign sits upright at the center, drawn fairly large relative to the ring. There is no element sigil. Eight Aeriforms Defined signs, each made of three short strokes, are evenly spaced about halfway between the center and the inner ring. They sit at the north, northeast, east, southeast, south, southwest, west and northwest points, and all are oriented the same way, with the top of each glyph toward the center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the Link sign at the center serves as the core of the spell. Link identifies objects that were broken off from, removed from, or made from the same source and creates a link between them. Its fairly large size gives the core a strong presence. Aeriforms Defined has the same design as the strokes on the wind sigil and shares a name with the aeriforms sigil, which creates air. Here it is read as defining or giving form to air around the linked targets, though its exact function is uncertain. The eight signs are balanced and uniformly oriented, so no direction is favored and the effect acts evenly on all sides. The second ring adds strength and steadiness to the core spell. Only two kinds of glyph are present, and they do not contradict each other.
effect: Finds objects that came from the same source and joins them with shaped air, so the pieces stay connected to one another across the space between them, as if held by an invisible tether of air. The hold is even on all sides and stays steady while the spell lasts.

name: s42_00039.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background. It has two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A Collection sign sits upright at the center in place of a sigil, moderate in size relative to the ring. No element sigil is present. Three Refuse signs sit about two-thirds of the way out, at the northwest, east-northeast and west-southwest, each with its diamond end pointing toward the center. Three Envelopment signs sit at a similar distance. The one at the south faces the ring. The one at the east-southeast faces the center, and the one at the west-northwest faces the ring. The east-southeast and west-northwest Envelopment signs are drawn a little rougher and heavier than the rest. At the north-northeast is a hooked glyph that matches no known sign exactly; it resembles an Envelopment sign made symmetric by mirroring one half onto the other, and it faces the ring. The signs are spread evenly around the seal. Outside the outer ring at the south-southeast, a short line joins a small closed sub-seal holding a single Expansion sign at its center, drawn large within it with its corners pointing outward. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, Collection takes the central role. It gathers material from above and around the seal for the spell to use, so the spell is not tied to one element. The three Refuse signs point inward, and Refuse draws unwanted material and waste toward where it points, so they steer debris toward the central Collection. These two gathering signs reinforce each other. Envelopment makes the effect surround its target, so the gathered material is wrapped in an enclosing layer. The mixed inward and outward facing of the Envelopment signs suggests the wrapping closes from both sides. The north-northeast glyph is closest to Envelopment; reading it that way is a guess, and its mirrored, symmetric form would add an even share of the same wrapping. The two rougher Envelopment signs weaken the wrapping slightly on their sides. The second ring adds strength to the core spell. The linked sub-seal applies Expansion with its corners pointing outward, which makes the target grow. Because the sub-seal is small relative to the main ring, the growth is moderate. Gathering, wrapping and enlarging work together without contradiction, and the signs are balanced, so the seal is stable.
effect: Draws loose waste and debris from all around the seal into a single mass at its center and wraps that mass in an enclosing shell. It then swells the wrapped bundle to a moderately larger size. The shell holds firmly overall but is slightly thinner on its east-southeast and west-northwest sides, where it can sag or leak small bits of debris.

name: s42_00044.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. It has two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn, with a band between them. A Detection sign, three vertical strokes of increasing height, sits at the center of the inner ring at moderate size. Four Cooling signs sit in the outer band at the north, east-northeast, south and west-northwest, each rotated differently. The east-northeast and west-northwest ones are slightly rougher than the others. An Immobility sign sits in the band at the west, turned with its top toward the center. Inside the inner ring are two small closed sub-seals. The northern one holds a wind sigil at about half its ring's size, and the southern one holds a four-lobed Billow sign in place of a sigil. The outer signs cluster more on the northwest side. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The main seal has no element sigil, so the central Detection sign is its core. Its exact function is unclear, but it presumably senses a presence and triggers or guides the rest of the spell. The wind sub-seal supplies movement of air, and its small size gives a modest strength. The Billow sub-seal turns available material into a fluffy cloud, so the air moved by the wind sub-seal becomes cloud. The four Cooling signs chill the result. The two rougher ones cool their sides a little less, so the chill is slightly uneven. Immobility keeps the target fixed in relation to the seal so the cloud holds its shape and place. How its sideways orientation changes this is unknown. The signs are unbalanced toward the northwest, so the effect is weighted to that side. The modifiers are cooling, holding and cloud-forming, which work together without contradiction.
effect: Senses a presence, then stirs nearby air into a soft, chilled cloud that stays fixed in place beside the seal, sitting off toward the northwest. The cloud is cooler on some sides than others, and its overall strength is modest.

name: s42_00049.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The main ring is closed and neatly drawn. A large Dispersion sign sits upright at the center in place of a sigil, with its stem pointing up and its curve below. It spans almost half the ring's radius. Five smaller Dispersion signs sit near the ring at the north, north-northeast, east, south-southeast and west. Each has its stem toward the center and its curve toward the ring. A single Columns sign, drawn in a heavier stroke, sits at the southwest with its crossbar toward the ring and its stem pointing inward. The signs are spread evenly around the ring. Outside the main ring at the northeast, a smaller closed ring is joined to it by a short line. That smaller ring holds a single Entwining sign at its center. There is no element sigil anywhere, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: No fire, water, earth, wind or light sigil is present, so the spell is not tied to one element and acts on whatever material or magic is fed into it. The large central Dispersion sign takes the core position and sets the main behavior: magic pours out of the seal rather than being beamed in one direction. The five ring-side Dispersion signs share the same orientation and are spaced around the ring, so the outflow spreads on all sides. Columns gives an area of effect shaped like a column and drives magic in a direction. As the only Columns sign, it adds a narrower push of the outflow toward the southwest. The linked sub-seal carries Entwining, which makes affected material wrap itself around other objects, and the line joining it applies that behavior to the main seal's output. Dispersion, Columns and Entwining are three modifiers that do not contradict one another. Both rings are closed and neatly drawn, so the spell activates and holds steady.
effect: Material fed into the spell pours out strongly and evenly in every direction, with one denser stream pushed outward toward the southwest. Wherever the outflow reaches nearby objects, it wraps and twines around them instead of simply spilling past.

name: s42_00051.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. The center is empty, with no sigil. Three large Gathering signs sit just inside the ring at the east, south-southwest, and north-northwest positions, roughly evenly spaced. Each has its forked base against the ring and its arrowhead pointing in toward the center. A single, much smaller Pulling sign sits near the ring at the west-southwest. Its arrowhead also points inward toward the center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the spell is not tied to fire, water, earth, wind, or light, and it acts on whatever loose material is around it. The three Gathering signs let a spell draw material from its surroundings to build its effect. Their arrowheads point inward and they are spaced about evenly, so they draw from all around the seal without favoring a side. Pulling is directional, and with its arrow pointing inward it pulls targets toward the seal. Because only one sits at the west-southwest, it adds a pull from that side and makes the seal lean west. The sign is drawn small, so that extra pull is weak. Gathering and Pulling both bring material inward, so they reinforce each other rather than conflict. No sign gives the collected material a shape or purpose.
effect: Draws loose material from all around the seal inward and collects it on the drawn surface, piling it up without shaping it. Material on the west-southwest side gets an extra, gentler tug, so it arrives from that direction a little sooner and more steadily than from elsewhere.

name: s42_00055.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A Crosshair sign sits upright at the center in place of a sigil, its four separated strokes pointing north, east, south and west, and it is fairly large relative to the ring. Four Link signs sit near the ring at the north-northwest, northeast, east-southeast and west-northwest positions, each with its top toward the ring. A Holding sign, a pair of facing curves with dots, sits near the ring at the south-southwest with its top toward the center. A second, smaller Holding sign sits closer in at the west-southwest, turned on its side. There is no element sigil. The signs are spread evenly around the seal, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the central Crosshair acts as the core and makes the seal's effect target whatever its short ends point at. Its four arms point evenly in the four cardinal directions, so targets are picked out on all sides rather than one. Its fairly large size gives the effect reasonable strength. The four Link signs identify objects that broke off from, or were made from, the same source and tie them together. The two Holding signs are non-directional, so their orientation does not change their effect. They hold the target in the shape set by the seal while still letting it move. Linking and holding work together without contradiction, and only these two kinds of modifier are present, so the seal is stable. Because there is no element sigil, the spell is not bound to fire, water, earth or wind and works on whatever material it targets.
effect: Picks out objects around the seal that share a common source and links them together. It holds them in a fixed arrangement that can still be moved as a whole. The hold is steady and lasts as long as the magic does.

name: s42_00062.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A small Solidification sign, two little circles joined by a short vertical line, sits upright at the center where a sigil would normally go. There is no element sigil. Four Stillness signs sit near the ring at the northeast, northwest, southwest and southeast points, each rotated so its top faces the ring. The northeast and southwest Stillness signs are drawn with heavier strokes than the other two. The signs are evenly spaced, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: Solidification is a sign, but here it takes the center in place of a sigil and sets the core behavior: magic and material inside the seal become more solid. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest strength. With no element sigil, the spell is not tied to fire, water, earth or wind and acts on whatever material is within its reach. Stillness holds a magical effect static in a single location, and four of them evenly spaced keep that hold balanced on all sides, so the effect is not pushed in any direction. Solidification and Stillness are two compatible kinds of modifier that reinforce each other, and the ring is closed and neatly drawn, so the spell activates and stays steady.
effect: Firms up loose material placed on or over the seal and holds it fixed in one spot, so it keeps its shape and does not drift or shift. The hardening is modest, enough to set soft or loose matter rather than turn it rock-hard.

name: s42_00064.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A small upright fire sigil sits at the center. Three Sights Set signs lie inside the ring, each with its diamond end toward the ring and its arrow pointing inward. One is long and sits at the northwest, one is long and sits at the east, and a much shorter, compact one sits closer in at the west. Near the ring at the south-southwest is a glyph that matches no single known sign. It is a Columns-like stroke with a short crossbar on the end facing the center and a small open circle on the end near the ring. The signs are not evenly spaced and cluster more on the western side. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and shapes flame or heat. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Sights Set aims a spell at a point or target the caster chooses. With three of them pointing inward from different sides, the aim is strong and easy to steer. The south-southwest glyph most closely reads as a Columns sign joined to a Solidification circle, which is a guess. Under that reading, it gives the fire a column-shaped area of effect and makes it denser and more cohesive than loose flame. Only two kinds of modifier are present, aiming and a solidified column, and they do not contradict each other. The neat drawing and closed ring mean the spell activates and holds steady. Because the signs are unbalanced toward the west, the effect carries a pull to that side.
effect: Produces a modest, dense column of flame that holds together firmly and can be aimed at a chosen target. Left unsteered, the column tends to lean and drift toward the west.

name: s42_00068.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A Repetition sign sits upright at the center in place of a sigil, moderate in size relative to the ring. Four Glaives signs, each a stem ending in a three-pronged fork, sit well out toward the ring. Those at the northwest and southeast have their prongs toward the center. Those at the east-northeast and south have their prongs toward the ring. The signs are spaced unevenly, with more weight toward the east-southeast. There is no element sigil, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: Repetition takes the center as the core of the spell. It continuously resets whatever it affects to the state it had when the spell first took hold, undoing changes, and its moderate size gives a moderate strength. Glaives set how deeply magic embeds itself into flesh, so this resetting effect is driven into a living body rather than an object's surface. Glaives are semi-directional, so their orientation does not steer the spell. Reversing a semi-directional sign reverses its effect, though Glaives have never been shown reversed. Here two face inward and two face outward, so the pairs work against each other: one pair drives the magic deep and the other would hold it shallow or push it back out. Repetition dominates and sets what the spell does, while the opposed Glaives fight over how deep it reaches, so the result is likely unstable. The uneven spacing toward the east-southeast makes the effect stronger on that side.
effect: Sinks into a living body and keeps resetting it to the state it was in when the spell took hold, undoing wounds and other changes as they happen. How deep it reaches keeps shifting, gripping firmly in some places and slipping toward the surface in others. Some parts of the body snap back while others drift, and the hold is noticeably stronger on one side.

name: s42_00071.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A light sigil, a diamond set inside a square with four short spokes, sits at the center at moderate size relative to the ring. Six Partition signs, each a triangle resting on a doubled arched line, are spaced around the seal about two thirds of the way out from the center. They sit at the north-northeast, east, south-southeast, south-southwest, west, and north-northwest positions. Their rotations vary from sign to sign rather than all facing the same way. The eastern sign, for example, has its triangle turned toward the center, while the others are tilted at different angles. No other signs are present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil makes this a light spell, and its moderate size relative to the ring gives a moderate intensity. Partition is a directional sign that outlines the borders of an area of effect, extending outward and upward. Whatever effect fills that area is set by the glyphs inside it, which here is only the light sigil. Six Partition signs spread evenly around the ring enclose a region on all sides, so no single direction is favored. Because their angles differ, the outline they draw is likely irregular rather than a perfect circle. Only one kind of modifier is present and nothing contradicts it, so the seal activates and holds steady.
effect: Fills a clearly bounded zone around and above the seal with a moderate, even light, with distinct edges where the glow stops. The edges of the lit area are slightly irregular rather than perfectly round, and the light gradually dims over time.

name: s42_00074.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A large Link sign sits upright at the center, reaching about halfway to the ring, in place of a sigil. Three very small Mimicry signs sit about three quarters of the way out from the center, at the west-northwest, northeast and south-southeast positions. Each is rotated so its top faces the ring, and the three are spaced evenly around the seal. There is no element sigil, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: There is no element sigil, so Link takes the center and sets the core behavior. It identifies objects that broke off from, were removed from, or were made from the same source, and links them together. Drawn large relative to the ring, it forms a strong, clear link. Mimicry guides or imitates the movements of a target object. With no decorative sigil to copy, the linked pieces have only each other to imitate, so the movement of one is passed on to the rest. The three Mimicry signs are evenly spaced, so no direction is favored. They are drawn very small, however, which makes the imitation faint compared with the strong link. Only two kinds of modifier are present and they support each other, so the seal is stable. With no element sigil, it is not tied to any one material.
effect: Links pieces of any material that came from the same source, so that moving one piece makes the others copy its motion. The link holds firmly, but the copied movements are faint. The other pieces follow only loosely and lag behind, tracing smaller versions of the original motion.

name: s42_00075.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, made of two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A small earth sigil sits upright at the center. A Projection sign, a flat bracket, sits at the north point in the band between the two rings. Its flat side faces the center and its open side faces the outer ring. Inside the inner ring, a Stretch sign sits at the northeast, about halfway out, its arch toward the center and its opening and feet facing outward. A small Link sign sits at the southwest, about halfway out, rotated with its top toward the center. No other signs are present, and more of the signs sit on the northern side of the seal than the southern. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on solid matter such as stone, sand and soil. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. The second ring adds strength and further effects to the core spell. Stretch turns solid objects that touch the seal into long, flexible ribbons. Link identifies pieces that broke off from, or were made from, the same source and joins them. Projection pushes the effect outward from the seal. Because it is the only Projection sign and sits alone at the north, with the other signs also weighted northward, the outward push favors that side. The seal uses three kinds of modifier that work together without contradiction, and the neat drawing and closed rings mean it activates and holds steady.
effect: Turns stone or soil that touches the seal into long, flexible ribbons, joins together ribbons that came from the same source, and sends them out from the seal toward the north. The effect is modest in strength but steady, slightly reinforced compared to a single-ringed version.

name: s42_00077.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. The band between the outer and inner rings is empty. A water sigil, an S-curve flanked by two teardrops, sits upright at the center and is modest in size relative to the rings. Six Cooling signs, each a vertical stroke with two dots on either side, are spaced evenly just inside the inner ring at roughly the north, northeast, east-southeast, south-southeast, southwest and west-northwest positions. Each is oriented with its top toward the ring. No other signs are present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell that manipulates, collects or creates water. Its modest size relative to the rings gives a moderate intensity. Cooling cools its target, and six of them strengthen that chilling. Cooling has no set direction and no directional signs are present. The signs are evenly spaced, so the effect stays at the seal and spreads evenly rather than being pushed toward any side. The second ring holds no signs, so it adds no modifier of its own. Only one kind of modifier is present, and the neat drawing and closed rings mean the spell activates and holds steady.
effect: Chills water at the seal to a steady cold, cooling it evenly from all sides without moving it in any direction. The effect is moderate and holds consistently while the spell lasts.

name: s42_00086.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. An Entwining sign sits upright at the center, small relative to the ring, and there is no element sigil. Six Strengthening signs, each a triangle crossed by a bar, are evenly spaced just inside the ring at the north, northeast, east-southeast, south, southwest and west-northwest. Each points its apex inward toward the center, and a few sit close enough to touch the ring. The southern Strengthening sign is drawn slightly rougher than the others. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the spell is not tied to fire, water, earth or wind. The Entwining sign takes the center in place of a sigil and sets the core behavior: it makes the object the seal is drawn on wrap itself around other objects. It is small relative to the ring, so the wrapping is of modest strength. Strengthening makes its target harder, stronger and more durable, so the six signs reinforce whatever the spell acts on. They are evenly spaced and all face inward the same way, so the reinforcement is balanced and favors no direction. Entwining and Strengthening are compatible, and only two kinds of modifier are present, so the seal is not unstable. The slightly rough southern sign makes the reinforcement a little weaker on that side.
effect: Makes the object the seal is drawn on wind itself around a nearby object and grip it with modest force. The wrapped object is hardened and made durable so it resists tearing or loosening, though the hold is marginally less firm on one side.

name: s42_00091.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A large Convergence triangle sits upright at the center with one point facing down. It fills a sizable share of the inner ring. There is no element sigil. Four Rain signs, each a square with its sides curved inward and short strokes radiating from the corners, sit inside the inner ring at the north-northeast, east-southeast, south-southwest and west-northwest positions. Each is set with its top toward the center, in normal orientation. Their centers are empty. The north-northeast Rain sign is a little rougher than the other three. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: No fire, water, earth, wind or light sigil is present, so Convergence takes the central position and sets the core behavior. It focuses the spell's magic down to a single point and packs loose particles tightly together. Its large size relative to the ring makes that focusing strong. Rain summons a target object, as a sudden fall or as rainfall. These four Rain signs are in normal orientation rather than flipped inside-out, so they summon instead of repelling. They hold no sigil in their centers, so the summoning is not tied to one element and acts on whatever material the spell is given. The four signs are evenly spaced, so the fall comes equally from all sides. The second ring strengthens the effect. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they work together without contradiction. The slightly rough Rain sign at the north-northeast is a little weaker than the others, so the fall from that side is thinner and shorter lived.
effect: Calls down a rain of material over the seal and draws it together into a single point above the center, where it packs into a dense, compact mass. The fall comes evenly from all sides with notable strength, though the stream from the north-northeast runs thinner and dies off sooner than the rest.

name: s42_00092.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A fire sigil, an upright triangle with three short strokes, sits at the center and is moderate in size relative to the ring. Six small Crosshair signs sit about two-thirds of the way from the center to the ring, at the north, east-northeast, southeast, south, west-southwest and northwest positions. Each is rotated so its top faces the ring. They are spaced evenly around the seal, and no other signs are present. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil makes this a fire spell, so it creates and shapes flame or heat. Its moderate size relative to the ring gives a moderate intensity. Crosshair makes a seal's effect target whatever its short ends point at. With six Crosshairs all facing outward, the fire is aimed at six separate points around the seal rather than spreading as a general blaze or rising as a single column. Because the signs are evenly spaced, no direction is favored. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing conflicts. The neat drawing and closed ring mean the spell activates and holds steady.
effect: Sends moderate bursts of fire outward from the seal, each striking a separate target at one of six points spaced evenly around it. The flames stay focused on those points instead of spreading into a general blaze.

name: s42_00093.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but slightly uneven and roughly drawn. At the center is a fairly large glyph of six crossing spokes, two long diagonal strokes crossed by a short horizontal bar. It matches no named sign exactly. Two small Mimicry signs sit far out toward the ring, one at the west-southwest and one at the east-northeast, each with its top toward the ring. The east-northeast one is drawn roughly. Three zigzag Crushing signs sit about halfway out at the northwest, north-northeast and south-southwest, each with its top toward the center. A single neatly drawn wide arc sits at the southeast, opening toward the center. The signs are evenly spread around the seal, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: No fire, water, earth, wind or light sigil is present, so the central glyph acts as the core. It most closely resembles Concealment without its eye marks. This is a guess, and read that way it hides a target. Its large size relative to the ring points to a fairly strong effect. The three Crushing signs face the center, the same orientation as inverted Crushing. Inverted Crushing pulls broken or powdered material back into its original shape, but only temporarily. The southeast arc is closest to a single-curve Binding sign, also a guess. Binding would halt the reformed material and make it move as one unit. The two Mimicry signs make the spell imitate the movements of a target. Concealment, reforming, binding and imitation all point toward one coherent purpose, so nothing contradicts. The signs are balanced, so no direction is favored. The rough ring and the rough strokes on most signs weaken the spell and shorten how long it lasts. The roughest Mimicry sign makes the imitation the least reliable part.
effect: Pulls broken or powdered material back into the shape it originally had and holds it together as a single piece. The reformed object is shrouded from sight and copies the movements of its target. The copied motion is jerky and lags behind, and the concealment thins in patches. The whole effect fades fairly quickly, at which point the material falls back into its broken state.

name: s42_00095.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, drawn as two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A water sigil sits upright at the center and is small relative to the ring. Five Columns signs sit in the band between the two rings. Four of them, at the northwest, northeast, southeast and southwest, are inverted, with their stems pointing out toward the outer ring and their crossbars resting on the inner ring. The southwest one is drawn a little roughly. The fifth, at the south, faces the normal way, with its crossbar toward the outer ring and its stem pointing toward the center. Inside the inner ring are three small round Windows signs, each a circle lined with slanted hatching, at the north, south and southwest, roughly halfway between the center and the inner ring. The signs cluster toward the south-southwest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell, and its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. The second ring adds extra strength and room for further effects. Inverted Columns manifests horizontally rather than vertically, letting magic spread outward much like Dispersion. With four of them on the diagonals, the water spreads sideways from the seal instead of rising. The single normal Columns at the south gives a column-shaped push. Because the signs are unbalanced and cluster toward the south-southwest, the effect leans that way. Windows connects two spaces that are not physically joined. With three of them inside the inner ring, part of the water passes through a linked opening and comes out in another place. The rough southwest Columns weakens that part of the spread slightly. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they do not contradict each other, so the seal works steadily.
effect: Water spills outward from the seal in a low, sideways spread that leans toward the south-southwest, with a modest stronger surge pushing south. Part of the water flows through a linked opening and comes out at a separate connected location. The spread on the southwest side is a little thinner and fades sooner than the rest.

name: s42_00096.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A small earth sigil sits upright at the center. Five Levitation signs surround it. The largest sits at the northeast, its crossbar almost touching the ring and its arrowhead pointing inward toward the center. The other four point outward, which is inverted: a small one at the north-northwest and another at the south-southeast, both near the ring; a medium one at the west-southwest near the ring; and a medium, slightly roughly drawn one at the east, set noticeably closer to the center than the others. The signs are spread fairly evenly around the ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell moves existing solid matter such as stone and soil. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Levitation floats its target into the air. Longer signs carry more weight and send it farther or faster. The northeast sign has its arrowhead inward, the usual orientation, and is the longest, so it supplies the main lift. The other four are inverted, and inverted Levitation works to cancel normal Levitation. One upright sign set against four inverted ones is a direct contradiction. The large northeast sign dominates in strength, but the inverted signs keep pulling against it, so the result is likely unstable. The even spacing keeps the lift from favoring any one side, though the slightly rough east sign is a little weaker. Its position closer to the center makes the push on that side uneven.
effect: Lifts a modest amount of stone or soil from beneath the seal, but the lift keeps fighting itself. The material rises in fits, bobs and stalls partway up, and drifts slightly off center, and it tends to sink back down well before the magic would otherwise run out.

name: s42_00097.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed and neatly drawn. The center is empty, with no sigil. Four Crosshair signs sit roughly two-thirds of the way out from the center. Two larger ones face each other across the seal at the north-northeast and south-southwest, with their tops toward the ring. Two smaller ones sit at the southeast and northwest, with their tops toward the center. The north-northeast Crosshair is drawn slightly rougher than the rest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: There is no element sigil, so the seal names no kind of magic to deliver. Crosshair is directional and makes a seal's effect target whatever its short ends point at. The north-northeast and south-southwest pair point outward along one axis, so they aim at points beyond the ring on opposite sides. Being larger, they reach farther and hold more firmly. The smaller southeast and northwest pair point inward along a crossing axis, so they aim at points drawn in toward the center. These are four signs of a single kind, spread evenly around the ring, so they do not contradict each other and the seal is not unstable. The slightly rough north-northeast sign makes the aim on that side a little weaker and less precise.
effect: Fixes four target points: two farther out beyond the edge on opposite sides, and two closer in toward the middle along a crossing line. With no element to carry, nothing visible appears at those points; it only marks them. The far point toward the north-northeast is held a little less steadily than the others.

name: s42_00098.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and roughly round. A fire sigil sits upright at the center, about half the ring's radius. Eight Levitation signs are spaced around the outer part of the seal, at the north-northwest, northeast, east-northeast, east-southeast, south-southeast, southwest, west-southwest, and west-northwest. Seven have their arrowheads pointing inward toward the sigil. The northeast sign is inverted, with its arrowhead pointing outward toward the ring. The northeast, east-southeast, and west-northwest signs are drawn larger and bolder than the other five. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and shapes flame. Its size, about half the ring's radius, gives a fairly strong intensity. Levitation floats its target into the air, and when the signs are balanced around the ring it shapes the target into a sphere. Here the eight signs are spread evenly, so the fire rises as a ball above the seal. Levitation's length sets how far the target travels, how much it can carry, or how fast it moves. The longer east-southeast and west-northwest signs add reach and lift on those sides. The inverted northeast sign works against the regular Levitation signs, and it is also one of the longer ones. This is a direct contradiction. The seven inward-pointing signs dominate, so the fire still floats, but the opposing pull on the northeast side makes the result likely unstable.
effect: Creates a fairly strong ball of fire that floats in the air above the seal. The sphere does not hold steady: its northeast side keeps dipping and dragging against the lift, so the ball wobbles, sags lopsidedly toward that side, and may sink or lose its round shape before the spell would otherwise end.

name: s42_00100.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. There is no element sigil. Two signs sit side by side at the center, both small relative to the ring. On the left is a Stretch sign, an arch open at the bottom with small feet. On the right is a Windows sign, drawn as a small ring of slanted strokes. Eight Detection signs, each three parallel strokes of increasing length, surround them. Six sit in the band between the two rings, at the north-northeast, east-northeast, southeast, south-southwest, west-southwest and northwest, each rotated at a different angle. Two more sit just inside the inner ring at the west and the south, with the tops of their strokes toward the center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, Stretch and Windows share the center as the spell's core. Stretch turns solid objects into long, flexible ribbons on contact with the seal. Windows connects two spaces that are not physically joined, like a portal. The second ring adds strength to the core effect. Detection is tied to sensing presence. Eight Detection signs spread evenly around both bands give the seal a wide, balanced sensing range with no favored direction, so the core effect responds to whatever is detected nearby. Only three kinds of modifier are present and none contradict each other, so the spell holds steady. The small center signs keep its intensity modest.
effect: Senses solid objects that come near the seal from any direction. Each one that touches it is drawn out into a long, flexible ribbon and fed through into another, distant space, as if threaded through a portal. The stretching is modest in strength, so it works best on small or soft objects.

name: s42_00103.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A small upright fire sigil, roughly a fifth of the ring's radius, sits at the center. Six Stretch signs, each an arch with short feet, are spaced evenly around it about three quarters of the way to the ring. They sit at the north-northeast, east, southeast, south-southwest, west and northwest. Each has its rounded top toward the center and its open, footed side facing the ring. No other signs are present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and manipulates flame and heat. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Stretch draws what the spell acts on out into long, flexible ribbons, and it is meant to surround a central sigil, as it does here. Applied to fire, it pulls the flames into ribbon-like streamers rather than a ball or a beam. Stretch is most likely non-directional, so pointing the signs' tops inward should not change their effect. Six of them evenly spaced give a balanced result with no favored direction. There are no Columns, Regions or other directional signs, so nothing drives the flame outward. Only one kind of modifier is present, and the neat drawing and closed ring mean the spell activates and holds steady.
effect: Produces modest flames that draw out into long, flexible ribbons of fire, curling evenly on all sides of the seal rather than shooting in any one direction. The ribbons stay fairly gentle and close to the seal.

name: s42_00107.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. There is no element sigil. A large Gathering sign sits upright at the center, its arrowhead pointing north, spanning about half the ring's radius. Eight Repetition signs surround it. Three sit in an inner band, about halfway out, at the south-southwest, north-northwest and east. Five sit close to the ring, at the west-northwest, northeast, south, north-northwest and west-southwest. Their orientations vary: some have their tops toward the ring and others toward the center. The Repetition signs at the south and west-southwest are drawn with heavier, slightly rougher strokes than the rest. The signs are spread evenly around the ring, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the large central Gathering sign acts as the core of the seal. It lets the spell draw material in from its surroundings, and its size relative to the ring gives that pull considerable strength. Repetition continually resets whatever the spell affects to the state it had when the spell first touched it, like a spring that restores an object if it is changed. Eight of them spread evenly around the ring make the reset strong and even on all sides, with no favored direction. The differing orientations of the Repetition signs have no known effect. The few roughly drawn Repetition signs slightly weaken the reset on the south and west-southwest sides. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they do not contradict each other, so the seal works steadily.
effect: Draws loose material from around the seal into it and holds that material fixed in the state it had when it arrived. The material does not rot, cool or change shape, and if it is disturbed it springs back to its original form. On the south and southwest side the hold is slightly weaker, so material there may shift or change briefly before snapping back.

name: s42_00109.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in thin black line on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. The center is empty, with no sigil and no central sign. Four small Crosshair signs sit inside the ring: one at the north, one at the east-southeast and one at the west-southwest, each about two-thirds of the way out, plus one at the south-southwest close to the ring. Four Glaives signs, each a straight stem ending in a three-pronged fork, are spread among them. At the west-northwest the prongs face the ring. At the east-northeast the stem runs out to touch the ring and the prongs face the center. At the south, partway out, the prongs point down toward the ring. At the north-northeast the Glaives sits at a slant, with its prongs angled down and inward. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: There is no element sigil and no sign standing in for one at the center, so nothing sets what kind of magic the seal produces. Crosshair makes a seal's effect target whatever its short ends point at. With four spread around the ring, the effect is aimed at several separate points rather than one. Glaives set how deeply magic embeds itself into flesh, so the targeted magic is driven into living bodies. Glaives have never been seen inverted, so reading the mixed orientations is a guess. Read that way, prongs facing the ring and prongs facing the center give different depths, so the embedding is not uniform. Only two kinds of modifier are present, targeting and embedding, and they work together without contradiction. The signs are balanced around the ring, so no direction is favored. Because the core is empty, the spell has little substance to deliver.
effect: Picks out several living targets around the seal and sinks magic into their bodies, lodging deeper in some than in others. With nothing at its core to give the magic a form, what it embeds is faint and shapeless, so each target feels at most a brief pressure or prickle where it settles.

name: s42_00115.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A water sigil, an S-curve flanked by two teardrops, sits upright at the center at a moderate size relative to the ring. Five Binding signs, each a pair of stacked arcs with the larger arc toward the ring, sit about halfway out from the center: one at the north-northeast, one at the east-southeast, two side by side at the south-southwest and south-southeast, and one at the west. Three Envelopment signs, each a slanted stroke hooked at both ends, sit right at the edge of the ring and overlap its line, at the north, east-northeast, and west-southwest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil sets the element, so the spell manipulates, collects, or creates water. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Binding halts the movement of the target material and binds it together so it acts and moves as a single unit, and five of them make that hold firm. Envelopment makes the effect surround whatever it targets, and its three signs at the ring's edge push that wrapping quality to the outside of the bound mass. No directional signs are present and the signs are spread evenly around the ring, so no side is favored and the water moves as one piece rather than in a set direction. Only two kinds of modifier are used, and both work toward the same result, so the seal is stable.
effect: Draws water together into a single cohesive mass that holds its shape and moves as one body instead of splashing or flowing apart. The mass wraps around its target and encloses it evenly on all sides, holding it with moderate strength.

name: s42_00117.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, made of two concentric rings, both closed. The outer ring is slightly uneven rather than perfectly round. A neatly drawn wind sigil sits upright at the center: an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes on either side, of moderate size relative to the ring. Three Coil signs, each a pair of crossing curved strokes, sit just inside the inner ring at the west-northwest, east-northeast, and south positions. Each is rotated to a different angle, and the three are evenly spaced. No other signs are present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves and manipulates air without creating it. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Coil softens a target object but only affects physical matter, so it cannot act on the air itself. It instead applies to solid objects the moving air reaches. Coil is likely non-directional, so the different rotations of the three signs do not change their effect. Their even spacing means no direction is favored, so the air moves around the seal rather than toward one side. The second ring adds strength to the core spell. The slightly uneven outer ring weakens the hold a little, so the effect does not last quite as long as a cleanly drawn seal would. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing conflicts.
effect: Stirs a moderate breeze around the seal with no set direction, softening and loosening the solid objects it passes over so they become pliable. It has no softening effect on water or other liquids, or on the air itself. The breeze tapers off somewhat sooner than expected, and the softening fades with it.

name: s42_00119.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but slightly uneven and not quite round, bulging a little in places. Two glyphs share the center, both upright and neatly drawn. An earth sigil sits just left of center, small relative to the ring. A smaller Entwining sign sits just right of center. Four Stillness signs sit about two thirds of the way out toward the ring, at the north, east, south and west points. Each is rotated so its top faces the center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell manipulates existing solid matter such as stone, soil, sand and wood rather than creating it. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Entwining shares the center and serves as a second core, making the affected material wrap itself around other objects. Stillness holds a magical effect static in a single location. Four of them, evenly spaced and all facing the center, favor no direction and fix the effect firmly in place. Only two kinds of modifier are present, wrapping and holding, and they work together without contradiction. The neat glyphs give a clean reading, but the slightly rough, not fully round ring makes the effect weaker and shorter lived than a cleanly drawn seal would.
effect: Causes nearby soil, stone or roots to coil around a target and hold it fixed where it stands, with modest strength. The grip stays locked in place while it lasts, but it begins to loosen and crumble sooner than expected, letting the target work free after a short time.

name: s42_00120.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A wind sigil sits at the center, small relative to the inner ring and a little roughly drawn. Five Solidification signs, each two small circles joined by a line, are spaced evenly inside the inner ring at the west, north-northwest, northeast, east and south-southeast, about halfway out from the center. A larger, boldly drawn Partition sign sits inside the inner ring at the southwest, with its peak pointing toward the center. Four smaller Partition signs sit in the band between the two rings at the west-northwest, north-northeast, east-southeast and south-southwest, each angled along the ring with its peak facing outward. The south-southwest one rests against the inner ring line. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil makes this a wind spell, so it moves and shapes existing air rather than creating it. Its small size gives a modest intensity, and its rough drawing slightly weakens and shortens the effect. The second ring adds strength to the core spell. Solidification makes the magic within the seal more solid, and five balanced Solidification signs firm up the moved air evenly on every side. Partition is directional and outlines the borders of an area of effect, extending outward and upward. The four outward-facing Partitions in the outer band set a boundary all the way around the seal. The single large Partition at the southwest points inward, so that side's border is drawn in toward the center, and its larger size makes this pull fairly pronounced. Only two kinds of modifier are present and they reinforce each other, so the seal is not unstable.
effect: Draws the surrounding air into a firm, invisible barrier that rises around and above a bounded area. The barrier is solid enough to push against and stop light objects. Its southwest side bends inward toward the center, leaving the enclosure dented on that side. The barrier is modest in strength and holds steadily, but it thins and fades somewhat sooner than a cleanly drawn version would.

name: s42_00122.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, made of two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A small fire sigil sits upright at the center, well under a quarter of the ring's radius. In the band between the two rings sit six Strengthening signs, spread evenly at roughly the south-southwest, west, northwest, north-northeast, east and southeast positions. Each has its apex toward the center. Inside the inner ring, four bold Launch signs sit at the north, east, south and west points, about halfway between the sigil and the inner ring. Each has its peak toward the center and its arms opening outward. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and shapes flame. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest base intensity. Launch drives its effect in the direction it points as a powerful but short-lived burst. All four Launch signs point inward and are evenly balanced, so no side is favored and the bursts converge on the center instead of pushing the flame off to one side. The second ring adds further effects and stronger magic to the core spell. The six Strengthening signs in that ring make the result harder and more durable, which toughens the flame and lets the burst hold together a little longer than a bare launch would. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they reinforce each other rather than conflicting. A couple of strokes are slightly less even than the rest, which only marginally affects the balance.
effect: Throws out a sudden, forceful burst of flame from all four sides that converges over the seal and erupts upward. The flame is dense and resilient for its modest size and holds together through the burst before quickly burning out. One side of the eruption may come through very slightly weaker than the others.

name: s42_00126.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but slightly uneven and not perfectly round. A wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes, sits at the center and is small relative to the ring. Six Gathering signs sit near the ring at roughly even intervals: west-northwest, north, northeast, east-southeast, south, and southwest. Each has its arrowhead end toward the ring and its forked stem toward the center. The southern one is drawn slightly more roughly than the others. No other signs are present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil makes this a wind spell, so it moves and manipulates existing air rather than creating it. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Gathering lets a spell draw material in from its surroundings to build its effect. Six of them strengthen that pull. Because they are spread evenly around the ring, no side is favored, and air is drawn in equally from every direction instead of being pushed one way. Only one kind of modifier is present, so the seal is coherent and not unstable. The slightly rough ring and the rougher southern sign make the spell a little weaker and shorter lived than a clean drawing would.
effect: Draws surrounding air in toward the seal evenly from all sides, creating a gentle, steady inward breeze that gathers at its center. The pull is modest, runs slightly weaker on the southern side, and fades somewhat sooner than a cleaner drawing would allow.

name: s42_00127.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. An earth sigil sits upright at the center and is fairly large relative to the ring. Three Partition signs sit about two-thirds of the way out from the center, at the north-northwest, east-southeast and southwest positions, spaced roughly evenly around the ring. Each has its peaked, triangle-topped end facing the center and its stacked arcs toward the ring. No other signs are present. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell manipulates existing solid matter such as stone, sand and soil without creating any. Its large size relative to the ring gives a fairly strong effect. Partition is a directional sign that outlines the borders of an area of effect. That area extends outward and upward, and whatever the other glyphs call for manifests inside it. Three Partition signs placed at even intervals mark out a balanced, roughly three-sided boundary around the seal. With the earth sigil as the only other element, the earth magic is confined to that outlined region. No sign pushes the effect toward one side. Only one kind of modifier is present, and the neat drawing and closed ring mean the spell activates and holds steady.
effect: Marks out a roughly three-sided area around the seal and forcefully works the existing stone and soil inside it. The ground within the boundary shifts and rises while the earth beyond the edges stays untouched, leaving sharply defined borders.

name: s42_00128.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A fire sigil sits upright at the center, moderate in size relative to the ring. Five Binding signs, each a larger arc paired with a smaller one, sit about two-thirds of the way out at the north-northwest, north-northeast, east, south-southwest and west. Each has its larger arc nearer the center and curving toward it. At the south-southeast is a small, thinly drawn glyph shaped like a Gathering sign with a small circle on its stem, its forked end toward the center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil makes this a fire spell, and its moderate size gives moderate intensity. Binding halts the movement of the target material and binds it together so it acts and moves as a single unit. With five Binding signs spread around the ring, the flame is held in one cohesive mass rather than spreading or flickering outward. The south-southeast glyph matches no known sign exactly. Its closest match is Gathering, though the circle on the stem is unexplained, so this reading is a guess. Read as Gathering, it lets the spell draw material and heat from its surroundings to feed the effect, and with its fork toward the center that pull runs inward. The signs are balanced around the ring, so no direction is favored. Only two kinds of modifier are present and they work together, so the seal is stable.
effect: Draws in heat and fuel from the surroundings and holds it as a single compact, steady mass of fire that stays in place over the seal instead of spreading. The flame burns at a moderate intensity and moves as one body if disturbed.

name: s42_00134.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with two concentric rings, both closed and drawn a little roughly. A water sigil sits upright at the center, drawn a little roughly and large relative to the ring. Six signs sit about midway between the sigil and the inner ring, each with its top toward the ring. Three Immobility signs sit at the north, southeast and west-southwest. Two Stillness signs sit at the south and west-northwest. At the northeast is a heavier glyph that matches no known sign exactly; it looks like a Stillness sign with a small Columns sign attached at its left. The signs are evenly spaced around the seal, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell. Its large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect, and the second ring adds further strength. Immobility makes the target immovable relative to the seal, so it holds its shape as if frozen. Stillness keeps a magical effect static in a single location. These two signs reinforce each other rather than conflict. The northeast glyph is read as Stillness with an attached Columns sign, which is a guess. Under that reading it adds more stillness and gives the held effect a column-shaped area. Because only one small Columns stub is present and the signs are balanced around the ring, it does not push the effect in any clear direction. Only three related kinds of modifier are present, so the seal is not unstable. The slightly rough rings, sigil and signs make it somewhat weaker and shorter lived than a neatly drawn version.
effect: Locks a large body of water in place above the seal, holding it rigidly in a column-like shape as if frozen while it stays liquid. The hold is strong at first, but it loosens sooner than it should. The water's edges slowly sag and drip before the whole mass is released.

name: s42_00138.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A Diamond sign sits upright at the center, neatly drawn and fairly large relative to the inner ring, with no element sigil present. An inverted Expansion sign sits at the east-southeast against the inner ring, with its nested corner brackets pointing inward, drawn a little roughly. A Refuse sign sits at the west-southwest just inside the inner ring, turned on its side with its diamond head facing roughly toward the center and its crossed legs toward the ring, also a little rough. In the band between the two rings, at the south-southwest, sits a small glyph of a vertical stroke flanked by dots. It resembles Cooling but with its halves mirrored. The signs are unevenly spread and gather toward the south.
justification: With no element sigil, the central Diamond serves as the core. It limits the spell to whatever is held inside the container the seal is drawn on, not the container itself, and the spell works on any material. The second ring strengthens the whole seal. Expansion is semi-directional, and inverted with its corners inward it shrinks its target. Refuse is directional and collects unwanted material toward where it points; its head faces inward, so waste is drawn toward the middle. The outer-band glyph matches no known sign exactly. Its closest match is Cooling, which is a guess, and under that reading it lowers the temperature of the contents. Shrinking, waste collection and cooling do not contradict each other. The slightly rough Expansion and Refuse signs make those two effects a little weaker and shorter lived. Because the signs lean south, the effect is heavier on that side.
effect: Shrinks and chills the contents of the container it is drawn on while leaving the container itself untouched. Any waste or unwanted matter among the contents is drawn together toward the middle. The shrinking and sorting are somewhat weak, fade sooner than the chill, and act more strongly on the contents toward the south side than elsewhere.

name: s42_00139.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes, sits upright at the center. It is small relative to the ring and its lines are slightly rough. Four Launch signs sit just inside the ring at the north-northeast, east, south-southwest and west positions. Each has its peak pointing outward toward the ring. The signs are evenly spaced, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil makes this a wind spell that moves existing air rather than creating it. Its small size relative to the ring gives it a modest intensity, and its slightly rough drawing makes the effect a little weaker and shorter-lived than a clean sigil would. Launch sends the spell's magic out in the direction it points, as a powerful but short-lived burst. All four Launch signs point outward and are evenly spaced, so no single direction is favored and the air is driven out on four sides at once. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing in the seal works against itself.
effect: Blasts sudden bursts of air outward from the seal in four directions at once, like a quick shove of wind on every side. The gusts are modest and die away almost as soon as they start, with some bursts fading slightly sooner or weaker than the others.

name: s42_00140.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A large earth sigil sits upright at the center, reaching about halfway to the outer ring. Eight Binding signs, each a pair of stacked arcs, surround it. Five sit inside the inner ring: at the north-northwest and west-northwest with their tops toward the ring, and at the east, southwest and south-southeast in varied orientations. The southwest sign is drawn with a heavier stroke than the rest. Three more sit in the band between the two rings, at the northwest, east-northeast and south, each tilted at a different angle. The signs are spread evenly around the seal. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil makes this an earth spell acting on solid matter such as stone, sand and soil. Its large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect. Every modifier is Binding, which halts the movement of the target material and binds it together so it acts and moves as a single unit. Eight of them reinforce that one effect. Binding's directional behavior is unknown, so their varied rotations are not read as changing the result. Because the signs are balanced, no side is favored. The second ring adds strength to the core spell. With only one kind of modifier and neat, closed rings, nothing in the seal conflicts.
effect: Halts loose earth, stone and sand within its range and locks the material together into a single solid mass. The mass holds firmly and moves only as one piece. The hold is strong and spreads evenly on all sides of the seal.

name: s42_00141.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed. The ring's outline is slightly lumpy rather than perfectly round. A wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes on either side, sits upright at the center and is large, reaching about half the ring's radius.
