Seven Cooling signs, each a short stroke flanked by dots, are spread evenly around the outer part of the seal at the north-northeast, east-northeast, east-southeast, south-southeast, south-southwest, west-northwest and northwest positions. They face different directions. The one at the northwest is drawn noticeably larger than the others. There are no directional signs, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves and manipulates existing air without creating it. Its large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect. Cooling lowers the temperature of what the spell acts on. The sign is semi-directional or non-directional and has never been seen reversed, so its different rotations are read as making no difference. The larger Cooling sign at the northwest strengthens the chill slightly on that side. All seven signs share one modifier, so nothing contradicts and the seal is not unstable. With the signs evenly spread and no Columns, Regions or other directional signs, the moving air is not sent in one set direction. The slightly uneven ring is still round enough to activate, but it may shorten how long the effect lasts.
effect: Stirs the surrounding air into a strong, chilling wind that swirls around the seal without blowing in any single direction. The cold is slightly sharper on the northwest side. The wind may die down somewhat sooner than a perfectly drawn version would.

name: s42_00145.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A water sigil sits upright at the center, an S-curve between two teardrops. It is fairly large, reaching about half the ring's radius. Three Convergence triangles sit near the ring at the north-northeast, east-southeast and west-northwest, each with one point facing inward toward the sigil. Two Detection signs, each three parallel strokes of increasing length, sit at the south-southeast and north-northwest, set at different angles. At the south-southwest is a small glyph of crossing spokes with no eye marks, closest in form to Concealment. The signs are spread evenly around the ring, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell. Its fairly large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect. The three inward-pointing Convergence signs focus the magic down to a single point and pack loose material tightly together. Because they are evenly spaced, the water gathers at the center instead of being pushed to one side. Detection lets the spell sense presences around it. The spoked glyph matches no known sign exactly. Reading it as Concealment without its eyes is a guess, and under that reading it hides the gathered water from view. That makes three kinds of modifier: focusing, sensing and hiding. They do not contradict one another, and the balanced layout and closed ring let the spell activate and hold steady.
effect: Draws water together into a single tight, dense mass above the seal with considerable strength. The mass responds to presences that come near it. It is also kept hidden from sight, so the water stays concealed until something approaches.

name: s42_00149.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn, though slightly uneven in roundness. The center is empty, with no sigil. A Binding sign, two stacked arcs, sits at the north point about two thirds of the way out, turned so its top faces the center and the arcs open toward the ring. A Solidification sign, two small circles joined by a short line, sits at the northwest, slightly tilted. A Mimicry sign sits near the ring at the northeast, rotated with its top toward the center and drawn a little heavier and rougher than the rest. A small Piercing sign, a diamond on a line, sits near the ring at the southeast. All signs are small relative to the ring, and three of the four crowd the upper half, so the layout leans toward the north-northeast. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no sigil, the spell is not tied to an element and acts on whatever material falls within its reach. Solidification makes that material more solid, and Binding halts its movement and holds it together as a single unit. These two are closely related and reinforce each other. Piercing is non-directional and makes the target manifest as a projectile. Binding's orientation toward the center is read as its usual effect, though how it behaves when turned this way is a guess. Mimicry makes the target imitate the movements of something else. Without a decorative sigil to copy, it would follow the motion of whatever the material is directed at. Because the Mimicry sign is roughly drawn, that part of the effect is weaker and shorter-lived than the rest. The modifiers fall into three compatible kinds, hardening and binding, projectile shaping, and imitation, so the seal is not unstable. The signs cluster to the north-northeast, which biases the effect toward that side. Their small size keeps the overall strength modest.
effect: Draws loose material together, hardens it into a single solid piece shaped like a projectile, and sends it out toward the north-northeast. The projectile then copies the movements of what it is aimed at. This copying is loose and lags behind its target, and it fades well before the hardened piece itself loses its shape.

name: s42_00154.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, main ring closed and neatly drawn. A small light sigil, a diamond inside a square with four short spokes, sits at the center. Six cross-shaped signs sit about two thirds to four fifths of the way out from the center. Five match Crosshair: north-northwest, west-northwest, east-southeast, south-southwest, and a darker, heavily stroked one at south-southeast. Some point their tops toward the ring and others toward the center. The sixth, at north, is a Crosshair with an extra stroke from its bottom edge, matching no named sign exactly. The east-southeast and south-southeast Crosshairs and the north glyph are drawn somewhat roughly; the rest are neat. Three small closed sub-seals sit outside the main ring, each joined to it by a short line: a fire sigil at west-northwest, a wind sigil at east-northeast, and a Piercing sign at south. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil sets the core element, and its small size gives modest intensity. The fire sub-seal adds flame and heat, which shares light's domain and reinforces it. The wind sub-seal adds moving air, which can carry the effect. The Piercing sub-seal makes the magic manifest as projectiles. Crosshair makes an effect target whatever its short ends point at. Here the Crosshairs face both inward and outward and are balanced around the ring, so the shots go to several separate targets rather than one direction. The north glyph is read as a Crosshair variant, which is a guess, and its extra stroke would stretch that aim farther along its line. Targeting and projectile shaping do not conflict, and the extra elements support each other, so the seal is coherent. The rougher Crosshairs weaken the aim on those lines.
effect: Fires several small, hot bolts of light, driven along on rushing air, each striking a separate target around the seal. Bolts on a few lines fly less true and hit more weakly, scattering slightly off their mark, and the glow of every bolt dims as it travels.

name: s42_00156.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with the ring closed and neatly drawn. The center is empty, and there is no element sigil. Eight Binding signs, each a pair of nested arcs, are spread around the seal. Five sit close to the ring at the north, east, south, southwest and west, with the curved top of each facing outward toward the ring. Three sit about halfway out at the northeast, south-southeast and west-northwest, with their tops facing inward toward the center. The southern sign is drawn slightly rougher than the rest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no sigil and an empty center, the seal is not tied to any element and acts on whatever material is within its reach. Binding halts the movement of the target material and binds it together so it acts and moves as a single unit. It is the only kind of modifier present, so nothing contradicts it, and eight of them strongly reinforce the hold. Binding's directional type is unknown, so the outward-facing outer signs and inward-facing inner signs are read as working toward the same effect. That reading is a guess. The signs are balanced around the ring, so the hold favors no direction. The single slightly rough sign at the south weakens that side a little.
effect: Stops material over the seal from moving and holds it together as one solid mass, so it can only be moved as a single unit. The hold is firm and even, though it grips a little more loosely along the southern edge, where loose bits occasionally slip free.

name: s42_00157.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed but slightly uneven in shape. A large fire sigil sits upright at the center, neatly drawn and spanning about half the ring's radius. Six Detection signs, each a set of three parallel strokes of increasing length, surround it. Three sit about halfway out, at the southwest, north-northwest and east-southeast, with their tops toward the ring. The southwest one is drawn heavier and rougher than the rest. The other three sit close to the ring, at the east-northeast, southeast and west-southwest, with their tops toward the center. A single Columns sign sits near the ring at the south, with its crossbar toward the ring and its stem pointing toward the center. More signs sit on the southern and eastern side than elsewhere. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and shapes flame and heat. Its large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect. Detection is tied to sensing presence, so the six Detection signs make the fire respond to things around the seal rather than burning blindly. Some face outward and some inward, so the sensing covers both the space near the center and the area out by the edge. The lone Columns sign gives the fire a column-shaped area of effect. Because it is unbalanced and sits alone at the south, together with the overall lean of the signs, the column is pushed toward the south-southeast instead of rising straight up. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they do not contradict each other. The slightly rough ring weakens the spell a little and shortens how long it lasts. The rougher southwest Detection sign makes the sensing on that side less reliable.
effect: Produces a strong flame that senses nearby presences and flares toward them as a column of fire, angled toward the south-southeast rather than straight up. The fire burns out somewhat sooner than a neater seal would allow, and it reacts sluggishly or sometimes not at all to things approaching from the southwest.

name: s42_00160.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. There is no element sigil. A Partition sign sits upright at the center, a small triangle atop a flat bar with two outer strokes splaying downward. It is small relative to the ring. Six Stillness signs sit about halfway between the center and the ring, at the southwest, west, north-northwest, north-northeast, east, and south-southeast positions. Each is turned so its top faces the center. They are spread evenly around the seal, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, Partition takes the center and sets the spell's core behavior. It outlines the borders of an area of effect, and that area extends outward and upward in all directions from the seal. Whatever manifests inside the area is set by the other signs present. Here those are the six Stillness signs, which hold magic in place so the effect stays static in a single location. Because they are evenly balanced around the ring, no side is favored, and the boundary is not pushed in any direction. The small central glyph gives the area a modest strength. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they reinforce each other rather than conflict. The neat drawing and closed ring mean the spell activates and holds steady. Without an element, the spell does not act on fire, water, earth, or wind. It shapes and fixes a space rather than producing a substance.
effect: Marks out a modest bounded zone that rises outward and upward from the seal and stays fixed in place without drifting or shifting. Any magic within that zone is held static, so effects inside it stay put instead of spreading or moving away.

name: s42_00161.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A small fire sigil sits upright at the center, about a quarter of the ring's radius in size. Six Crosshair signs surround it. Four sit roughly halfway out at the northeast, southeast, southwest and northwest, each facing outward toward the ring. A fifth, larger and slightly rougher, sits farther out at the south-southeast. A sixth sits at the east, turned the other way so it faces the center. More signs gather on the southeast side than anywhere else. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil makes this a fire spell, and its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Crosshair is a directional sign that makes a seal's effect target whatever its short ends point at. The four intercardinal Crosshairs aim the fire at separate points around the seal, and the extra one at the south-southeast adds another target on that side. Because it is a little rough, its share of the effect is weaker and shorter lived. The east Crosshair is reversed to face the center, so it turns its targeting back toward the seal itself. With most signs clustered toward the southeast, the effect favors that side. Only one kind of modifier is present, and the reversed sign changes aim rather than contradicting the others, so the seal holds together.
effect: Sends small, modest flames or bursts of heat to several separate points around the seal, with more of them landing toward the southeast. One flame is drawn back onto the seal's own center. The farthest flame to the south-southeast burns weaker than the rest and gutters out sooner.

name: s42_00163.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, made of two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. The center is empty, with no sigil. Five Aeriforms Defined signs, each a fan of three short strokes with a longer middle stroke, sit just inside the inner ring at the north-northeast, east-northeast, southeast, south and west, each with its tip toward the center. The east-northeast sign is a little rougher than the others. Four smaller Aeriforms Defined signs sit in the band between the two rings at the northeast, southeast, southwest and northwest, each turned at a different angle. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no sigil, the seal has no element, so the spell's character comes entirely from its signs. Aeriforms Defined shares its design with the modifier strokes of the wind sigil and its name with the Aeriforms sigil, so it is tied to air and to making gases apparent or defined. It likely acts as a semi-directional sign, so the varied rotations of the outer signs change only their strength, not the direction of the effect. The five inner signs all point inward and are spread evenly, so the effect gathers within the inner ring instead of pushing to one side. The second ring adds a further layer and strengthens the magic, and the four outer signs set a matching air effect in the band between the rings. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing contradicts. However, there is no sigil to supply power, so the effect stays mild. The slightly rough sign at the east-northeast gives that side a little less hold than the rest.
effect: Gives shape to the air over the seal, holding a calm, defined body of air inside the inner circle with a thinner layer of air around it. The effect is gentle and spread evenly, though it is held slightly more loosely toward the east-northeast, where the air thins and drifts a little sooner than on the other sides.

name: s42_00165.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. An Expansion sign of four nested corner brackets sits upright at the center in place of a sigil, with its corners pointing outward. It is fairly large, taking up a bit over a third of the ring's radius. Three Pulling signs sit just inside the ring at the north, east-southeast and southwest points, evenly spaced. Each has its arrowhead pointing inward toward the center. There is no element sigil, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: There is no element sigil, so the Expansion sign at the center acts as the core of the spell and is not tied to any one element. Expansion is semi-directional. With its corners pointing outward, it makes its target grow, and its fairly large size gives that growth notable strength. Pulling draws the target toward the seal when its arrow points inward, as all three do here. None of them is angled, so they add no twisting. The three Pulling signs are evenly spaced, so the pull is balanced from every side and favors no direction. With no Selection or Diamond sign present, the spell is not limited to the object the seal is drawn on, and the Pulling signs point the effect at things drawn in from around it. The two kinds of modifier work together without contradiction.
effect: Draws nearby objects steadily toward the seal from all sides and makes them grow noticeably larger as they are pulled in. The pull runs straight inward, without twisting.

name: s42_00166.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A small upright light sigil, a diamond inside a square with four short spokes, sits at the center. Six Partition signs, each a peaked roof shape over a long bar, are spaced evenly about two-thirds of the way out from the center. They sit at the west, north-northwest, northeast, east, south-southeast and southwest, each with its peaked top toward the center. No other signs are present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil makes this a light spell, and its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Partition is a directional sign that outlines the borders of an area of effect, extending both outward and upward. The effect inside that area is set by the glyphs within it, here the light sigil. Six evenly spaced Partition signs all face the center the same way, so together they mark out a closed, roughly six-sided boundary around the sigil with no side favored. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing conflicts. The neat drawing and closed ring mean the spell activates and holds steady.
effect: Fills a bounded, roughly six-sided region over the seal with soft light, walled off so it rises upward within that space rather than spreading beyond its edges. The glow is even throughout but modest, and it slowly dims over time.

name: s42_00169.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A small earth sigil, upright and about a quarter of the ring's radius, sits at the center. Three Expansion signs, each made of nested corner brackets with the corners pointing outward, sit near the ring at the west-northwest, northeast and south-southeast. The west-northwest one is drawn in heavier, darker strokes than the other two. Two Pointing signs sit near the ring at the east and south-southwest. The eastern one is drawn a little more roughly. The signs are spaced unevenly and cluster more on the southeast side. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil makes this a spell that works on existing solid matter such as stone, sand and soil. Its small size relative to the ring gives it a modest intensity. Expansion is semi-directional, so its position does not steer the spell. With its corners pointing outward, it makes the target grow. Pointing is non-directional and makes the target take a conical shape. No Columns or other directional sign is present to send the cones anywhere, so they form in place. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they work together without contradiction. Because more signs sit toward the southeast, the effect is weighted toward that side. The slightly rough eastern Pointing sign is weaker and shorter lived than the rest of the seal.
effect: Shapes nearby stone or soil into cones and enlarges them, producing modest spikes of earth that rise in place around the seal. The spikes grow larger and fuller toward the southeast. On the eastern side, the points come out less sharp and lose their shape sooner than the others.

name: s42_00170.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A water sigil, an S-curve flanked by two teardrops, sits upright at the center and is moderate in size relative to the ring. Six small Mimicry signs are spread around the seal about three quarters of the way to the ring, at the north-northwest, northeast, east, south-southeast, southwest and west positions. Those at the north-northwest, northeast and southwest have their tops toward the ring, while those at the east, south-southeast and west have their tops toward the center. A single Gathering sign sits at the east-southeast, drawn noticeably larger and with heavier strokes than the other signs. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Mimicry guides or imitates the movements of a target object. With no decorative sigil present, there is no creature design to copy, so the water follows a target's motions in a simpler way. Six Mimicry signs strengthen this imitation. Their mixed orientations are spread evenly around the ring, and no inverted effect is known for this sign, so the mix adds no steering or reversal. Gathering lets a spell draw material in from its surroundings. Drawn large and bold, it pulls water in strongly, so the spell does not need to create its own. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they do not contradict each other. The signs are balanced around the closed, neat ring, so the spell activates and holds steady.
effect: Draws in water from the surroundings and gathers it into a mass that follows and copies the movements of a nearby target. The copied motions are simple rather than detailed, and the effect is of moderate strength.

name: s42_00172.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The main ring is closed and neatly drawn. A small fire sigil sits upright at the center. Six Refuse signs, each a diamond above crossed legs, are spaced evenly just inside the ring at the east, south-southeast, south-southwest, west, north-northwest and northeast. They are turned at differing angles, most lying sideways along the ring rather than pointing straight in or out, and the south-southwest one is drawn a little roughly. Three small sub-seals sit inside the main ring. At the west-northwest is a slightly rough closed ring holding an earth sigil. At the east-northeast is a slightly rough closed ring holding an Entwining sign. At the south is a neat sub-seal whose ring is open, with a gap at its upper left, holding a Solidification sign. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, and its small size relative to the ring gives modest flames and heat. Refuse is directional and collects unwanted material toward where it points. These six are balanced around the ring but turned at varied angles, so the waste is gathered toward several points along the edge rather than pushed one way. The earth sub-seal adds control over solid matter such as soil, grit and stone, letting the spell move solid debris as well as burn it. The Entwining sub-seal makes the affected material wrap around other objects. Both sub-seal rings are a little rough, so their contributions are weaker and shorter-lived than the core. The Solidification sub-seal has an open ring, so it does not activate. If closed, it would make the gathered material more solid. The active modifiers work together without contradiction, so the seal is not unstable.
effect: Draws waste and loose debris, including dirt and grit, toward several points around the seal's edge and burns it with modest flames. The gathered refuse is wound around nearby objects as it burns, but this wrapping is weak and loosens well before the burning stops. The part meant to compact the remains into a solid mass does not take hold, so the leftover ash and grit stay loose.

name: s42_00176.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. An upright earth sigil sits at the center at a moderate size relative to the ring. Six Strengthening signs, each a triangle crossed by a bar, are spaced evenly about three quarters of the way out, at the south-southwest, west, northwest, north-northeast, east, and southeast. Each has its apex pointing toward the center. The west, north-northeast, and southeast signs are drawn a little more roughly than the others. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on existing solid matter such as stone, soil, sand, and wood rather than creating it. Its moderate size relative to the ring gives a moderate intensity. Strengthening makes objects stronger, harder, and more durable. All six signs share one orientation and are evenly spread, so no direction is favored and the reinforcement applies equally on all sides. There is only one kind of modifier, so nothing conflicts. The three slightly rough signs weaken their share of the effect a little, making the hardening less even on those sides and shorter lived there.
effect: Hardens and reinforces solid earth, stone, or wood around the seal, making it tougher and more resistant to breaking with a moderate degree of strength. The reinforcement is slightly patchier toward the west, north-northeast, and southeast, where it holds a little less firmly and fades somewhat sooner than elsewhere.

name: s42_00180.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed and neatly drawn. Two sigils sit side by side near the center, both modest in size relative to the ring. On the left is a light sigil, a diamond inside a square with four short spokes, drawn slightly rough. On the right is an earth sigil, drawn neatly. Six Levitation signs surround them, each with its crossbar toward the ring and its arrowhead pointing inward toward the center. Four sit close to the ring at the north-northwest, east-northeast, south-southeast and west-southwest; the southern two touch it. Two slightly smaller ones sit closer in, at the east and west-northwest. They are spread fairly evenly around the seal. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil makes the spell act on solid matter such as stone, soil and sand, and the light sigil adds the creation of light, which fades over time. Both are about a quarter of the ring's radius, so the intensity is moderate. The light sigil's slightly rough drawing makes the glow a little weaker and shorter lived than the earth effect. Levitation floats its target into the air, and its inward-pointing arrows are its usual orientation. Balanced Levitation shapes the floating material into a sphere. Here the six signs are evenly spread, so no direction is favored. The two shorter inner signs carry slightly less lift than the outer four but do not unbalance the whole. Only one kind of modifier is present alongside two compatible sigils, so the seal is not contradictory.
effect: Lifts nearby stone or soil into the air and holds it hovering above the seal as a rounded, sphere-like mass that gives off light. The earth holds steady, but the glow is somewhat weaker and dims over time, fading before the floating mass comes down.

name: s42_00181.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A fire sigil sits upright at the center and is fairly large, reaching about two fifths of the way to the ring. Four Piercing signs, each a straight stroke through a small diamond, are scattered around it at different distances: one near the ring at the northeast, drawn small and neat; one at the west-northwest, larger and closer in; one at the south, about midway out; and one near the ring at the southwest, drawn with a thicker, slightly rough line. The signs are not evenly spaced, and more of them sit on the western and southern side. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and shapes flame. Its fairly large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect. Piercing is non-directional and makes the magic manifest as projectiles, and the number of Piercing signs sets how many are made, so four signs give four projectiles. Because Piercing has no direction, the uneven placement does not aim the spell. There is no Columns, Regions, Crosshair or Sights Set sign to steer the projectiles, so they are not sent toward any chosen target. The roughly drawn southwest sign is weaker than the others, so the projectile it governs is less reliable. Only one kind of modifier is present, so the seal is not unstable.
effect: Forms four strong bolts of fire that shoot out from the seal. With nothing to aim them, the bolts fly off in loose, scattered directions rather than at a chosen target. One bolt comes out thinner than the rest and burns out sooner.

name: s42_00185.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. Two sigils sit side by side at the center, both small relative to the ring. A light sigil, a diamond inside a square with four short spokes, sits on the left. An earth sigil sits on the right. A single Windows sign, drawn as a small circle lined with hatch marks, sits at the southwest about halfway to the ring and is slightly rough. A Binding sign of two stacked arcs sits at the northeast near the inner ring, with its larger arc bulging toward the center; it is also slightly rough. A second, neatly drawn Binding sign sits at the south, rotated so its arcs bulge toward the east. More of the signs sit in the lower half of the seal than the upper. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the material as solid matter such as stone, soil and sand. The light sigil adds light, so the spell both acts on matter and produces a glow. Both sigils are small relative to the ring, which gives a modest intensity, and the second ring adds strength to the core spell. Binding halts the movement of the target material and binds it together so it acts and moves as a single unit. Two Binding signs reinforce this. Windows connects two spaces that are not physically joined. Here it appears as a single small sign rather than a full lining ring, so the connection is narrow. The signs lean toward the south, so the effect is weighted toward that side of the seal. The Windows sign and one Binding sign are slightly rough, which weakens and shortens their part of the effect a little. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they do not contradict each other.
effect: Binds loose stone or soil into a single glowing mass that holds together and moves as one piece. A small window links that mass to another location, so it can be seen or reached from elsewhere. The effect gathers more heavily on the southern side of the seal. The glow and the window are modest, and the window tends to narrow and fade a little sooner than the binding.

name: s42_00188.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. An upright Immobility sign sits at the center and is large, reaching about half the inner ring's radius. Four Aeriforms Defined signs, each three short strokes, sit about two thirds of the way out at the north-northwest, east-northeast, south-southeast and west-southwest positions, each with its top toward the ring. They are evenly spaced around the seal. The north-northwest sign is drawn a little more roughly than the others. There is no element sigil, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the Immobility sign at the center acts as the core and sets the spell's behavior: the target becomes immovable relative to the seal and holds its shape as if frozen. Its large size points to a strong hold. Aeriforms Defined shares its design with the strokes on the wind sigil and its name with the aeriforms sigil, which creates air, so it ties the effect to gases rather than solids. Four of them evenly spaced add no direction, so the effect is centered on the seal. The second ring adds strength and further effect to the core spell. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they do not contradict each other. The slightly rough north-northwest sign weakens the effect a little on that side.
effect: Fixes a pocket of air around the seal in place, holding it still and firm as if frozen so it keeps its shape and moves with the seal. The hold is strong overall but slightly softer toward the north-northwest, where the still air can drift a little.

name: s42_00189.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. The center of the main seal is empty, with no sigil. Nine Columns signs are spread evenly around the seal. Three larger, bolder Columns signs sit at the north-northwest, east-southeast and southwest, each with its crossbar against the inner ring and its stem reaching toward the center. Three thinner Columns signs sit inside the inner ring at the north-northeast, west and south-southeast, each with its crossbar toward the ring and its stem toward the center. Three more small Columns signs sit in the band between the two rings: the one at east-southeast faces the center like the others, while the ones at northwest and south-southwest are inverted, with their crossbars toward the center. Outside the main ring at the north-northwest, a small closed sub-seal is joined to the outer ring by a short line. It holds a single upright light sigil of moderate size relative to its own ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The main seal has no sigil, so its element comes from the linked sub-seal, whose light sigil makes this a light spell. That sigil is moderate relative to its small ring, so the effect has moderate intensity. The second ring inside the main ring adds strength to the core spell. Columns gives the magic a column-shaped area of effect, and more Columns signs widen its range and the amount of magic produced. Because the signs are balanced around the ring, no side is favored, so the column rises straight up rather than leaning. The two inverted Columns in the outer band make part of the magic spread out horizontally, much like Dispersion, around the base of the column. This is a variation on the same modifier rather than a contradiction, so the seal holds steady. Both rings are closed and neatly drawn, so the spell activates and lasts.
effect: Raises a broad, upright column of light straight up from the seal, with some of the light spilling outward horizontally around its base. The light is moderately bright and gradually dims over time.

name: s42_00193.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. An upright earth sigil sits at the center, fairly large relative to the ring. Four Rain signs, each a small square with spiky strokes at its corners, sit about halfway out at the northeast, southeast, southwest and northwest points. A fifth Rain sign sits closer to the ring at the east, rotated relative to the others and drawn with heavier, rougher strokes. Three Stretch signs, each an open arch with small feet, sit just inside the ring at the north, west and south-southeast. The north and south-southeast arches have their tops toward the ring, while the west arch has its top toward the center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell moves existing solid matter such as soil, sand and stone rather than creating it. Its fairly large size relative to the ring gives a fairly strong effect. Rain summons the spell's material so it falls from above in the area around the seal. Rain is semi-directional but radially symmetric, so only an inside-out flip would invert it. The rotated east Rain is not flipped and still acts as normal Rain, but its rough drawing makes its share of the effect weaker and less even. Stretch turns solid matter that contacts the seal into long, flexible ribbons. It is most likely non-directional, so the differing orientations of the three arches do not change it. The signs are balanced around the ring, and their two kinds of modifier work together without contradiction.
effect: Draws up nearby soil and stone and lets it fall back over the surrounding area like a heavy rain, while solid matter that touches the seal is drawn out into long, flexible ribbons. The downpour is fairly strong and even overall, but it thins out and falls patchily on the east side.

name: s42_00195.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed and neatly drawn. At the center is an unfamiliar sigil: an S-curve inside a small circle, ringed by eight evenly spaced dots. It is moderate in size relative to the ring and its lines are slightly uneven. Four Immobility signs sit about two-thirds of the way out, at the northeast, northwest, southeast and southwest points. Each has its curved top toward the ring and its base line toward the center, and the southeast one is a little rough. Four Crosshair signs sit just inside the ring at the north, east, south and west points. The east Crosshair is drawn heavier and rougher than the others. The signs are evenly balanced around the ring, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The central glyph matches no named sigil exactly. Its S-curve most closely resembles the wind sigil, so reading it as a wind variant is a guess. Under that reading the spell acts on air, and the circle and dots around the S suggest air held within a bounded space rather than blown freely. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Immobility makes its target immovable relative to the seal, holding its shape as if frozen. With four of them evenly spaced, that hold is applied evenly on all sides. Crosshair makes the effect target whatever its short ends point at. With four of them at the cardinal points facing outward, the effect is aimed at separate points in four directions instead of spreading as a general field. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they do not contradict each other. The ring is closed and round, so the spell activates. The slightly rough sigil and a few rough signs weaken it a little and shorten how long it lasts.
effect: Locks the air at four points around the seal, one in each cardinal direction, into fixed, motionless pockets that hold their position relative to the seal like invisible stoppers. The hold is moderately strong but lets go somewhat sooner than a cleanly drawn version would. The eastern pocket is the first to loosen and drift.

name: s42_00199.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A water sigil, an S-curve between two teardrops, sits upright at the center at a moderate size relative to the ring, its strokes slightly rough. Five small four-lobed glyphs are spaced around it. Four of them are Billow signs, at the south, northeast, southeast, and southwest. The south one sits close to the ring, and the other three sit a little farther in. The fifth sits near the ring at the north. It looks like a Billow sign, but its halves are drawn as mirror copies of each other rather than as one continuous shape. The northwest, west, and east stretches hold no signs. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil sets the element, so the spell manipulates, collects, or creates water, and its moderate size gives moderate intensity. Billow is a non-directional sign that turns available material into a fluffy cloud. Placed around a water sigil, several Billow signs turn the spell's water into soft, cloud-like masses. The mirrored northern glyph matches no known sign exactly. Its closest match is Billow, so reading it as a variant Billow is a guess, and under that reading it adds to the same cloud-forming effect. Billow is non-directional, so the uneven spacing does not push the effect toward any side. All the modifiers are of one kind and do not conflict. The slightly rough sigil makes the spell a little weaker and shorter-lived than a cleanly drawn one would be.
effect: Gathers water at the seal and puffs it into soft, fluffy clouds that billow up around it. The clouds are moderately sized and thin out somewhat sooner than they otherwise would, with some patches loosening back into damp mist before the rest.

name: s42_00202.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. Two sigils share the center: a light sigil (a diamond inside a square with four spokes) on the left and a slightly smaller wind sigil (an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes) on the right. Both are of moderate size relative to the ring. Four Stretch signs, each an arch with small outturned feet, sit about three-quarters of the way out at the east-northeast, south-southeast, west-southwest and north-northwest positions. Each has its curved top toward the ring and its open side toward the center. Two Cooling signs, each a slanted stroke with a pair of dots on either side, sit at the north-northeast and south-southwest, set diagonally across from each other. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil makes the seal create and shape light, and the wind sigil adds the movement of air, so the light is carried and moved rather than held still. Both are of moderate size, which gives a moderate intensity. Stretch, placed around the central sigils as it is meant to be, draws whatever the spell acts on into long, flexible ribbons. It normally acts on solids, but alongside a light sigil it is read as drawing the light itself out into ribbon-like strands. The four Stretch signs are evenly spaced, so the stretching favors no direction. The two Cooling signs sit opposite each other and cool the effect, keeping the light cold instead of warm, despite light belonging to the fire domain. This is only two kinds of modifier on two compatible sigils, with no contradiction, and the neat drawing and closed ring let the spell activate and hold steady.
effect: Draws light out into long, flexible ribbons that drift and curl through the air around the seal, carried evenly in every direction by gentle currents. The ribbons give off no warmth, staying cool to the touch, and glow at a moderate strength that gradually dims over time.

name: s42_00203.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A fire sigil sits upright at the center and is moderate in size relative to the ring. Six Stability and Level Planes signs, each a pair of wavy parallel strokes, surround it at about half the distance to the ring. They sit at roughly the north-northwest, northeast, east-southeast, south, southwest and west-northwest positions. The signs at the south, southwest, northeast and east-southeast are drawn a little rougher than the other two. No other signs are present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil makes this a fire spell, creating and shaping flame or heat. Its moderate size relative to the ring gives a moderate intensity. Stability and Level Planes is non-directional, so its orientation does not matter. It makes its target balance on a level plane in the air, like something floating on water that can turn and drift but stays on the surface. Six of these signs are spread evenly around the ring, so no side is favored and the balancing hold is strong. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing conflicts. The slight roughness of four signs weakens their hold a little and makes it less even than the neat signs.
effect: Creates a moderate flame that floats in the air above the seal and stays balanced on a level plane. It can drift and turn, but it keeps its height like something floating on water. The flame holds level most of the time, though it dips or tilts slightly from time to time toward one side.

name: s42_00208.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A Stability and Level Planes sign, drawn as three wavy vertical lines, sits upright at the center in place of a sigil. It is moderate in size relative to the ring. There is no element sigil. Inside the inner ring, six Reflection signs (hourglass shapes) are spaced around the center at roughly north, east-northeast, east-southeast, south, southwest and west-northwest. Each has its top toward the ring, and the west-northwest one is drawn with noticeably heavier strokes. In the band between the rings sit four smaller Reflection signs at the north-northwest, east-northeast, south-southeast and west-southwest. The east-northeast and west-southwest ones touch the inner ring line, and the east-northeast one is slightly rough. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, Stability and Level Planes takes the central role. It is a non-directional sign that makes its target balance on a level plane in the air, able to turn and drift but always staying level, like something floating on water. Reflection targets the reflected image on the object the seal is drawn on, so the reflection becomes the material the spell works on. Ten Reflection signs spread evenly across both rings give the effect a wide reach without favoring any direction. The second ring carries the smaller outer set and adds strength to the core effect. Those outer signs are small and slightly rough, so they contribute less than the inner six. Only two kinds of glyph are present, and they work together without conflict.
effect: Lifts the reflection held in the surface the seal is drawn on and holds it as a flat image floating level above the seal. The image can turn and drift but always stays level. Its center holds clear and steady, while its outer edges are fainter and fade sooner than the rest.

name: s42_00211.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A small water sigil sits upright at the center, about a quarter of the ring's radius. Three Collection signs sit roughly two-thirds of the way to the ring at the north, east-southeast, and west-southwest positions. Each has its barred end toward the ring and its open side facing the center. Three Aeriforms Defined signs alternate with them at the east-northeast, south, and west-northwest positions. Each is a fan of three short strokes whose converging end points toward the center. The Aeriforms Defined signs at east-northeast and south are drawn a little roughly. All other glyphs are neat, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell. Its small size relative to the ring gives it a modest intensity. Collection gathers material from above and around the seal so the spell can use it. With their open sides facing inward in their usual orientation, the three Collection signs draw surrounding moisture toward the center. Aeriforms Defined is tied to air and gases, and its strokes match the marks beside a wind sigil. Here they converge toward the center the same way, so they are read in their normal orientation rather than inverted. Applied to water, they most likely give the gathered water a gaseous, airborne form. The two kinds of sign alternate evenly, so no direction is favored. They do not contradict each other. The two slightly rough Aeriforms Defined signs weaken their part of the effect a little on those sides.
effect: Draws moisture from the surrounding air and holds it above the seal as a modest, gently drifting cloud of mist. The mist is slightly thinner toward the east-northeast and south and fades a little sooner there than on the other sides.

name: s42_00214.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. There is no element sigil. A Partition sign sits upright at the center, about a third of the ring's radius in size. Four Envelopment signs, slanted strokes hooked at both ends, sit near the ring at the northeast, southeast, southwest and northwest. Detection signs, three parallel strokes of decreasing length, sit at the north and south, each with its top toward the center. At the east is a matching glyph of three stacked horizontal strokes shortening downward, which reads as a Detection sign stretched wide. At the west is a glyph that matches no known sign: a narrow right-angled triangle tapering downward, with a small circle crossed by a bar at its upper corner. The signs are evenly spaced, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no sigil, the central Partition sign is the core of the seal. It outlines the borders of an area of effect that extends outward and upward, and the other signs decide what happens inside that area. The four Envelopment signs at the diagonals make the effect surround whatever it targets, so the bounded zone wraps around its contents evenly. The three Detection signs at north, east and south, the eastern one stretched, add a sensing quality, so the zone responds to presences within its borders. The stretched eastern sign likely widens that sensing on its side. The western glyph is closest to Pointing because of its tapering cone shape, though this is a guess. Read as Pointing, it gives the effect a tapered, conical form, and its circled bar loosely echoes Orb. Only three kinds of modifier surround the core and none contradict each other. The neat drawing, closed ring and balanced layout mean the seal activates and holds steady.
effect: Marks out a bounded zone around the seal that wraps evenly around everything inside it and senses any presence within its borders. The zone tapers slightly to a point on one side, and its sensing reaches a little wider on the opposite side. It holds steady for as long as the seal stays intact.

name: s42_00222.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, made of two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A water sigil, an S-curve flanked by two teardrops, sits upright at the center and is fairly large relative to the inner ring. Six Gathering signs are spread around it inside the inner ring, at the west, northwest, north-northeast, east-northeast, southeast and south-southwest, each with its arrowed top pointing out toward the ring. Three smaller, lighter Gathering signs sit in the band between the two rings, at the north-northwest, east-southeast and southwest, also with their tops toward the outer ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell that collects, creates and manipulates water. Its fairly large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect. Gathering lets a spell draw material in from its surroundings to build its effect, and nine of them focus the whole seal on pulling in water. The signs are spaced evenly in both rings, so no side is favored and water comes in from all directions alike. The second ring strengthens the core spell, and the three Gathering signs in it extend the draw further out, though their smaller size makes their added pull lighter. With no directional signs, the gathered water is not sent anywhere and stays at the seal. Only one kind of modifier is present, so the seal is consistent and steady.
effect: Draws water from the surroundings, such as moisture in the air and nearby sources, in toward the seal evenly from every side. The water collects in a strong, steady supply at the seal instead of being sent away from it.

name: s42_00224.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes, sits upright at the center at a moderate size relative to the ring. Nine small Rain-like signs, each a square with concave sides and short strokes at its corners, are scattered around it. Six form an inner circle about halfway to the ring, at the west-northwest, north, northeast, east-southeast, south and southwest positions. Three more sit close to the ring: one at the west-northwest, one at the south, and one at the north-northwest. The north-northwest glyph has a small circle crossed by a line, matching an Orb sign, attached to the side facing the center. None of the signs are inverted, and they are spread evenly around the seal. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves and manipulates existing air rather than creating it. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Rain summons its seal's material down from above in a rainfall-like way. Here the Rain signs are drawn small and scattered rather than surrounding the sigil, and none are flipped inside-out, so they act in their normal form. Paired with wind, they bring air down in many separate falling streams. Eight plain Rain signs spread evenly around the ring mean the effect falls across the whole area with no favored side. The glyph combining Rain with an attached Orb matches no known sign. As a guess, it reads as Rain feeding an Orb, which defines a spherical space where the material collects, so the air falling at that point would pool into a small sphere. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they do not contradict each other, so the seal is stable.
effect: Brings air sweeping down from above in many small, steady downdrafts that fall evenly across the area around the seal, like a rainfall of wind. At one point near the edge, the falling air gathers into a small, contained sphere of swirling air instead of spreading out.

name: s42_00227.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. The inner ring sits just inside the outer one, leaving a narrow empty band between them. A fire sigil sits upright at the center and is moderate in size relative to the ring. Six Dancing Puppets signs are spaced around the sigil, about two thirds of the way out toward the inner ring, at the north-northeast, east-southeast, south-southeast, south-southwest, west and northwest positions. Each is drawn as a small ring with little circles on it and curved strokes crossing outward, and each is rotated differently. The east-southeast sign is drawn slightly larger and bolder than the others. There are no other signs, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil makes this a fire spell that creates and controls flames or heat. Its moderate size gives a fair intensity, and the second ring adds strength to the core spell. Dancing Puppets allows the movement of the spell's target to be consciously steered, even at long distance. Paired with wind it makes objects fly, so paired with fire it makes the flames themselves move and dart through the air. Six of these signs repeat a single modifier and are evenly balanced, so no direction is favored. With no directional signs, the motion follows the caster's control rather than a fixed path. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing contradicts and the seal is stable.
effect: Creates fairly strong flames that rise from the seal and can be steered freely through the air, darting, weaving and circling as the caster directs. With no fixed direction of their own, they go wherever they are guided, even at a distance.

name: s42_00228.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, made of two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A small wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes, sits upright at the center and is small relative to the rings. Six Cooling signs, each a vertical stroke flanked by two pairs of dots, sit in the band between the inner and outer rings. They are at the north, northeast, east-southeast, south, southwest, and west-northwest positions. They are spaced evenly around the seal. The north and west-northwest signs are drawn slightly less cleanly than the others. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil makes this a wind spell. It moves and manipulates existing air rather than creating it, and its small size gives a modest intensity. The second ring adds strength to the core spell. Cooling cools things down. The Cooling glyph is symmetric, so pointing some signs toward the center and others toward the ring should not change their effect. Six of them together give a strong chilling effect on the air the spell moves. The signs are evenly balanced, and there is no Columns, Regions, or other directional sign, so the air is not pushed in any one direction. It stays and circulates around the seal. Only one kind of modifier is present, so the seal is not unstable. The two slightly rough signs only weaken the chill a little on their sides.
effect: Draws the surrounding air into a gentle, steady circulation around the seal and chills it, producing a cool breeze. The breeze spreads evenly on all sides and does not blow in one direction. It is noticeably cold but not forceful, and is slightly less chilly toward the north and west-northwest.

name: s42_00232.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A large earth sigil sits upright at the center, reaching about half the ring's radius. Six Pointing signs, each an A-shaped peak flanked by small curls, surround it about two thirds of the way out toward the ring. They sit at the west-southwest, northwest, north-northeast, east-northeast, southeast and south-southwest positions, each rotated so its top faces the ring. The signs are evenly spaced, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell manipulates existing solid matter such as stone, sand and soil rather than creating it. Its large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect. Pointing is non-directional and makes the target material manifest in a conical shape. It normally needs a sign such as Columns to direct those cones, and none is present here. Six identical Pointing signs spaced evenly around the ring favor no side, so the shaping acts evenly all around the seal. Only one kind of modifier is present, and the neat drawing and closed ring let the spell activate and hold steady.
effect: Forcefully reshapes nearby stone and soil into sharp, cone-shaped spikes that form evenly all around the seal. Nothing drives the spikes outward or launches them, so they stay fixed where they form.

name: s42_00239.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. Two sigils share the center: a fire sigil on the left and a wind sigil on the right. The fire sigil is moderate in size relative to the ring, and the wind sigil is slightly smaller. Six small Crosshair signs sit near the ring at the north-northwest, northeast, east, southeast, southwest and west positions, each rotated so it faces outward. The Crosshairs at the north-northwest and southeast are drawn a little roughly, and the rest are neat. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets flames and heat as one element, and the wind sigil adds the movement of air. Together they make heat or flame that is carried on moving air. Their moderate sizes give a moderate intensity, with fire slightly dominant over wind. Crosshair makes a seal's effect target whatever its short ends point at. Six outward-facing Crosshairs spread evenly around the ring send the effect toward six separate points around the seal, with no side favored. Crosshair is the only kind of modifier present, so nothing contradicts. The ring is closed and neatly drawn, so the spell activates. The two roughly drawn Crosshairs make their targets slightly weaker than the others.
effect: Sends gusts of hot, flame-tinged air outward from the seal in six directions, each striking a separate target around it with moderate force. The gusts aimed toward the north-northwest and southeast are somewhat weaker and die down sooner than the other four.

name: s42_00240.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, made of a main ring and two smaller linked rings. All three rings are closed. A small wind sigil sits at the center of the main ring. Six Repetition signs are spread evenly around it, about two-thirds of the way to the ring: at the north-northeast, east-northeast, southeast, south-southwest, west-southwest and northwest. Each is turned with its top toward the center. The one at the west-southwest is drawn in noticeably darker, heavier strokes than the others. A smaller ring is joined by a short line to the north side of the main ring, holding a fire sigil that fills about half of it. A matching smaller ring is joined to the south side, holding a wind sigil of similar relative size. Its ring line is slightly less even than the others. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The central wind sigil sets the main element, so the spell moves and manipulates existing air. Its small size relative to the main ring gives a modest intensity. Repetition continually resets whatever the spell affects to the state it had when the spell first took hold, and that reset includes temperature. Six of them, evenly spaced, apply the reset evenly on every side, so the moved air keeps returning to its starting condition instead of drifting or dissipating. The linked northern ring adds fire magic, and its large sigil relative to that small ring supplies a fair amount of heat. The linked southern ring adds a second wind source that strengthens the air movement. Its slightly rough ring makes that added push a little weaker and shorter lived than the rest of the seal. All parts point the same way: moving air, warmed, held steady. Nothing contradicts anything else, so the seal is not unstable.
effect: Produces a gentle, warm current of air around the seal that keeps resetting to its original flow and temperature, so it neither cools nor dies away. The extra strength behind the draft fades somewhat sooner than the warmth, leaving a softer but still steady warm breeze.

name: s42_00241.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A large, boldly drawn Launch sign sits upright at the center in place of a sigil, reaching about half the ring's radius and opening downward. A Collection sign sits at the north-northwest, with its barred end toward the ring and its open side facing inward, drawn a little roughly. A Gathering sign sits at the northeast, with its arrowhead pointing toward the center. A single small Piercing sign sits at the southeast, drawn a little roughly. Three Rain signs, starbursts with short strokes on their sides, sit at the southwest, south-southwest, and west-northwest. None of the Rain signs is turned inside out. There is no element sigil, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, Launch takes the center and sets the core behavior. It sends the spell's material out in the direction it points, here straight up, in a powerful but short-lived burst. Its large size relative to the ring makes that burst strong. Collection, in its usual inward-facing orientation, takes material above and around the seal. Gathering, with its arrowhead pointing inward, actively draws more material in. Together they supply what Launch fires. Without a sigil the spell is not tied to one element and works on whatever material it gathers. Rain summons material and brings it down like rainfall. It is radially symmetric, so rotating it does not invert it, and all three act normally. They make the launched material come back down as a shower around the seal. Piercing makes material manifest as projectiles, and its count sets how many, so one sign yields a single projectile. The modifiers are gathering, rainfall, and projectiles, which is three kinds that do not contradict one another, so the seal is not unstable. Collection and Piercing are drawn a little roughly, which makes their parts slightly weaker and shorter lived than the rest.
effect: Draws loose material in from around the seal and hurls it straight upward in a strong, brief burst. The material then falls back down as a rain-like shower around the seal. Part of it forms a single sharp projectile, which holds its shape less reliably than the rest. The gathering also pulls in a little less than the burst can carry, so the launch thins out quickly.

name: s42_00242.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. Two glyphs sit side by side near the center, both modest in size relative to the ring. On the left is a four-lobed Billow sign. On the right is an Expansion sign of nested corner brackets with its corners pointing outward. Four Envelopment signs, each a slanted stroke with short hooks at both ends, sit about halfway between the center and the ring at the north-northwest, east-northeast, south-southeast, and west-southwest positions, each angled to follow its position around the seal. A single Cooling sign, a short line between pairs of dots, sits close to the ring at the north-northeast. There is no element sigil. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, Billow takes the center as the core of the spell. It turns available material into a fluffy cloud, and because no element is set, it works on whatever material is directed into the seal. Expansion shares the center. It is semi-directional, and with its corners pointing outward it makes its target grow, so the cloud swells. The four evenly spaced Envelopment signs make the effect surround its target, so the cloud wraps around whatever it acts on instead of sitting in one spot, and no side is favored. Cooling is not directional, so its position near the ring adds no direction. It cools the result, and as a single small sign its effect is mild. Billow and Expansion are both drawn modestly in size, which keeps the cloud moderate rather than overwhelming. The three modifiers of growth, envelopment, and cooling work together without contradiction. The neat drawing and closed ring let the spell activate and hold steady.
effect: Turns material directed into the seal into a soft, fluffy cloud that swells in size and wraps around its target, enveloping it on all sides. The cloud is noticeably cool to the touch, though only mildly so.

name: s42_00243.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn neatly in black on a white background, ring closed. A water sigil sits upright at the center and is moderate in size, about a third of the ring's radius. Seven Repetition signs are spread evenly around it in two layers. Three sit about halfway between the center and the ring, at the north, east-southeast and southwest, each turned at a different angle. Four sit just inside the ring at the northeast, south-southeast, west-southwest and northwest, each with its top toward the ring. Outside the main ring, two small sub-seals are joined to it by short straight lines, one at the north-northeast and one at the south-southwest. Each has a closed ring with a wind sigil at its center. The sigil fills roughly half of each small ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Repetition continuously resets whatever the spell affects to the state it had when the spell first took hold. That reset covers both form and temperature. Seven Repetition signs, balanced around the ring, make this hold strong and even on every side. The varied rotations of the inner signs favor no direction. The two linked sub-seals each carry a wind sigil, which moves air but does not create it. Their sigils are large relative to their own rings, so each gives a fairly strong current, but the sub-seals are small, so their reach is limited. Sitting on opposite sides of the main seal, they move air across the water from two directions. The seal combines only two kinds of effect, which do not contradict each other, and it is neatly drawn with every ring closed, so it activates and holds steady.
effect: Keeps a body of water locked in the state it was in when the spell began. Any change to its shape, amount or temperature is steadily undone. At the same time, two opposing currents of air sweep across it, stirring and rippling the surface, but the water keeps returning to its original form.

name: s42_00245.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. The center is empty, with no sigil. Four small Billow signs, each a four-lobed clover shape, sit about halfway between the center and the ring at the north, east, south and west points. The western one looks slightly rougher than the others. Four Partition signs sit close to the ring at the northeast, west-northwest, east-southeast and south-southwest. Three of them have their peaked tops toward the ring. The northeast one is flipped, with its top facing the center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: There is no element sigil, so the spell is not tied to fire, water, earth or wind. Billow is a sign that turns available material into a fluffy cloud. Four of them spaced evenly around the center make that the core behavior of the seal, applied on all sides. Their small size gives a modest effect, and the slightly rough western Billow makes that side a little weaker and shorter lived. With no Collection or Gathering signs, the seal does not draw in material on its own; it only works on material directed into it. Partition is directional and outlines the borders of an area of effect, extending outward and upward. The three Partitions facing the ring set an outward boundary. The flipped northeast Partition faces inward, so the boundary on that side is drawn in toward the center rather than pushed out. This is a single reversed sign within one kind of modifier, not a contradiction. With only two kinds of modifier, the seal is balanced and stable.
effect: Turns material brought into the seal into soft, fluffy cloud that fills a bounded space rising up and out around the seal. The space is pinched inward on the northeast side, so the cloud is shallower there. The western part of the cloud is slightly thinner and fades a little sooner than the rest.

name: s42_00255.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, drawn as two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A fire sigil sits upright at the center of the inner ring, moderate in size relative to the seal. The inner ring holds nothing else, and all modifiers sit in the band between the two rings. Two Coil signs sit at the east-northeast and the southeast, both drawn small. A taller, stretched glyph resembling Coil sits at the northwest, angled along the ring. At the west-southwest is a small octagon with an X inside that matches no known sign exactly. The signs are spread evenly around the band. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell produces and works with heat. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. The second ring adds strength to the core spell. Coil softens physical matter and does nothing to liquids or gases, so paired with fire it turns the heat toward making solids soft and pliable. Reading the stretched glyph as an elongated Coil is a guess; it would extend or deepen the softening along one axis. The octagon with an X is closest to Selection, also a guess. Read that way, it limits the effect to the object the seal is drawn on. The Coil signs are drawn small, which keeps the softening gentle rather than extreme. The modifiers are evenly spaced, so the effect favors no direction. Only softening and object selection are combined, and they do not conflict.
effect: Warms the object the seal is drawn on just enough to soften it, leaving it pliable and easy to bend or shape, much like wax or metal held near a flame. The heat spreads evenly through the object and is not thrown outward as fire. It has no effect on liquids or gases.

name: s42_00258.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. The band between the outer and inner rings is empty. A Rain sign sits upright at the center, a square with inward-curving sides and short triple strokes at each corner. It takes the place of a sigil and is moderate in size relative to the ring, with nothing drawn in its open middle. Six Holding signs are evenly spaced about halfway out from the center, at the east, southeast, south-southwest, west, northwest and north-northeast. Each is a pair of facing curves with small dots, its top toward the ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: There is no element sigil. Rain is a sign that can sit in the center, and here it acts as the core of the seal. Rain summons a target, bringing it down from above like rainfall. Because it is upright and not turned inside out, it summons rather than repels. Its moderate size gives a moderate strength. The six Holding signs are non-directional and keep the target in the shape the seal defines while still letting it move. They are evenly balanced, so no side is favored and the held form stays round and centered. The extra inner ring adds strength to the spell even with its band left empty. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they work together without contradiction. With no element sigil, the spell is not tied to fire, water, earth or wind and acts on whatever material it is directed at.
effect: Draws down a steady, rain-like fall of material over the seal and gathers it into a round mass matching the seal's outline. The mass can sway and shift without losing its shape, and it holds together firmly for as long as the spell lasts.

name: s42_00260.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A light sigil, a diamond set inside a square with four short spokes, sits upright at the center at a moderate size relative to the ring. Six Refuse signs, each a small diamond above a crossed pair of legs, are spread evenly around it about halfway to the ring. The two at the north and south-southeast have their diamond ends facing the center. The four at the west-northwest, northeast, east-southeast and southwest have their diamond ends facing the ring. The southwest Refuse sign is drawn with heavier, slightly rougher strokes than the others. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil makes this a light spell. Its moderate size relative to the ring gives a fairly strong but not overwhelming intensity, and light from this sigil diminishes over time. Refuse is a directional sign that collects unwanted material toward where it points. Four Refuse signs face outward and two face inward. The outward pull and the inward pull work against each other, so the signs directly contradict. The four outward signs outnumber the inward pair and dominate, so the net effect sweeps waste away from the seal toward its edges, while the inward pair draws some back toward the center. Because of this opposition the result is likely unstable. The rough southwest sign is weaker and shorter lived, so that side is cleared less firmly. The signs are evenly spaced, so the outward sweep favors no single direction.
effect: Gives off a fairly bright glow that sweeps dust, grime and debris outward from the seal, clearing the space around it. Some of the debris is tugged back toward the middle, so the mess shifts back and forth and never fully settles, and the southwest side clears more weakly and gives out first. The light gradually dims, and the sweeping fades with it.

name: s42_00261.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. An Immobility sign sits upright at the center in place of a sigil, drawn as a vertical stroke on a base bar flanked by two curved brackets. It is fairly large, reaching a little under half the ring's radius. Six Coil signs, each two crossing curved strokes, surround it. Four sit close to the ring at the northwest, northeast, southeast and southwest. Two sit closer to the center, one at the north-northwest and one at the east. There is no element sigil, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, Immobility takes the center and sets the core of the spell. It makes the target immovable relative to the seal, holding its shape as if frozen while still allowing the seal and target to be carried together. Its fairly large size gives the effect solid strength. Coil softens a target and works only on physical matter, not liquids or gases. It is non-directional, so the different orientations of the six signs and their two spacings do not change their effect. Their number strengthens the softening, and their spread around the ring keeps it even. Softening and holding work on different aspects of the target, so they combine rather than conflict. With only two kinds of modifier, a closed ring and neat drawing, the spell activates and holds steady.
effect: Softens solid matter touched by the seal while locking it firmly in place relative to the seal, so it becomes pliant yet cannot shift or lose its shape. The softening is thorough and even across the whole target. It has no effect on liquids or gases.

name: s42_00262.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A small wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes, sits upright at the center, and its lines are slightly rough. Three Stretch signs sit just inside the ring at the north-northeast, west, and south-southeast positions, roughly evenly spaced. Each has its rounded top toward the center and its open, footed side toward the ring. No other signs are present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves and manipulates existing air. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity, and its slightly rough lines make the effect a little weaker and shorter lived. Stretch turns solid objects that contact the seal into long, flexible ribbons. It works by surrounding the central sigil, and these three signs do that. They are evenly spaced, so no direction is favored. Stretch acts on solids while wind acts on air, so the two divide the work rather than contradict each other: matter touching the seal is drawn out into ribbons, and the moving air carries them. There are no directional signs, so the motion has no set heading.
