effect: Draws solid objects that touch the seal out into long, flexible ribbons and sets them rippling and drifting on a gentle current of air around the seal, with no particular heading. The breeze is light and slackens after a fairly short time, leaving the ribbons to settle.

name: s42_00265.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A fire sigil sits upright at the center, moderate in size at a little under half the ring's radius. Three Selection signs sit just inside the ring at the north, east-southeast, and west-southwest points. Each is drawn as a small square crossed by a grid of lines that extend past its edges. Two Columns signs sit about halfway out, one at the north-northeast and one at the west. Each has its crossbar toward the ring and its stem pointing toward the center. Three Crushing signs sit near the ring at the northeast, south, and west-northwest points, all inverted so they face outward. The three sets of signs alternate evenly around the ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and shapes flame and heat, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Selection is non-directional and confines the spell's effect to the object the seal is drawn on. Its three evenly spaced copies keep the flame bound to that surface. Columns gives the magic a column-shaped area of effect. Only two Columns signs are present, at the north-northeast and west, so they are not balanced on opposite sides. The column therefore leans toward the side between them, roughly northwest, instead of rising straight up. Crushing is semi-directional, and inverted it reverses its usual breaking effect, pulling scattered material back into one form for as long as the spell lasts. Crushing is only known from work on solid matter, so its effect on fire is uncertain. Read here, the inverted signs would draw stray sparks and embers back into the main flame, keeping it compact. This reformed state lasts only while the spell holds. The seal uses three kinds of modifier that work together without contradiction, so it should be stable.
effect: Raises a moderate column of fire from the object the seal is drawn on, leaning toward the northwest rather than straight up. Loose sparks and embers are pulled back into the flame, so the fire stays dense and tightly formed instead of scattering. When the spell ends, the flame loses this cohesion and breaks apart.

name: s42_00270.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A Purification sign, a hooked curl, sits upright at the center in place of a sigil and is moderately large relative to the ring. Ten Binding signs, each a pair of nested arcs, surround it in two loose bands. Four sit about halfway out at the west-southwest, north-northwest, east-northeast and south-southeast, with the tops of their arcs toward the center. Six sit close to the ring at the north-northeast, east-northeast, southeast, south-southwest, west-southwest and northwest, with the tops of their arcs toward the ring. The signs are spread evenly around the seal, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: There is no element sigil, so the Purification sign at the center serves as the core of the spell. It separates waste from water, which ties the seal to water without a water sigil. Its moderate size gives a moderate strength. Binding halts the movement of the target material and binds it together so it acts and moves as a single unit. That is the only modifier present, so the seal is not unstable. The inner Binding signs face the center and the outer ones face the ring. Reading this as a hold applied from both inside and outside is a guess, since Binding's directional behavior is unknown. Under that reading, the separated waste is gathered and held firmly in place rather than allowed to drift. The even spacing means no side is favored. Purification is asymmetric, so the fine details of how the separation proceeds are less predictable than the binding.
effect: Separates waste from water and binds the separated waste into firm, cohesive clumps that stop drifting and move as single units. This leaves clean water behind and makes the waste easy to lift out whole. The cleansing works at a moderate strength and holds steady while the spell lasts.

name: s42_00279.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed. The ring is slightly lumpy and not perfectly round. A water sigil, an S-curve flanked by an upward and a downward teardrop, sits upright at the center at moderate size relative to the ring, with slightly shaky lines. Six Solidification signs, each two small circles joined by a short line, are spaced around the ring at the northwest, north-northeast, east, south-southeast, south-southwest, and west, each with its top toward the ring. Most are drawn with thin, even strokes, but the west sign and one lower sign are drawn heavier and less evenly. No other signs are present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Solidification makes the magic it is tied to more solid, so the water is firmed rather than left to flow. All six modifiers are the same sign, so nothing contradicts them. They are evenly spread around the ring, so no direction is favored, and the effect stays centered on the seal instead of being projected outward. The slightly irregular ring and the shaky sigil and signs weaken the seal and shorten its duration, and the uneven roundness makes the hold less consistent.
effect: Firms water at the seal into a moderate, semi-solid, jelly-like mass that holds together instead of flowing. The mass is not uniformly firm, and some edges stay softer and sag. It loosens back into ordinary water sooner than expected.

name: s42_00282.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A Rain sign sits upright at the center in place of a sigil. Its square has inward-curving sides and short triple strokes at each edge, and its middle is empty, with no element sigil inside it. It is moderate in size relative to the ring. Six Binding signs, each a large arc paired with a smaller arc, form an inner circle about two-thirds of the way out. They sit at the north, east-northeast, southeast, south, west-southwest and northwest, each with its larger arc toward the center. Two more Binding signs sit just inside the ring at the north and west-southwest, directly beyond the inner ones at those points. These two face the opposite way, with their larger arcs toward the ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: No fire, water, earth, wind or light sigil is present, so the Rain sign at the center sets the core behavior: summoning a target material. Because no sigil sits inside it, the spell is not tied to one element. It is drawn upright rather than inside out, so it summons rather than repels. Binding halts the movement of the target material and binds it together so it acts and moves as a single unit. With six evenly spaced inner Binding signs facing the center, the summoned material is drawn into one cohesive mass and held still within the seal's area. The two outer Binding signs face outward, the reverse of the inner ones. They add a second, outward binding at the north and west-southwest, so the mass is held somewhat more firmly toward those sides. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they do not contradict each other. The neat drawing and closed ring mean the spell activates and holds steady.
effect: Summons material from above in a moderate amount. Instead of scattering like rainfall, it gathers into a single cohesive mass that stops and hangs in place over the seal, where it can be moved as one piece. The mass holds slightly more firmly on its northern and west-southwestern sides than elsewhere.

name: s42_00284.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short strokes on either side, sits upright at the center and spans about half the ring's radius. Six Solidification signs, each two small circles joined by a short straight line, sit near the ring at the north-northwest, northeast, east-southeast, south-southeast, west-southwest, and west-northwest. They are drawn at slightly different angles and sizes. The north-northwest sign has its upper circle toward the ring, and the others have theirs toward the center. The west-northwest sign is a little rougher than the rest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves and manipulates existing air rather than creating it. Its fairly large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect. Solidification makes the magic drawn with it more solid, so the moved air is firmed into something that holds together instead of flowing freely. The six signs are spread evenly around the ring with no directional signs, so the effect is not pushed toward any side and stays centered on the seal. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing contradicts. The single slightly rough Solidification sign weakens that part a little without breaking the spell.
effect: Gathers the surrounding air and firms it into a dense, solid-feeling mass centered on the seal, strong enough to push against and hold back objects. The firmness is even all around, though it is slightly softer and less steady toward the west-northwest side.

name: s42_00288.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The outer ring is closed but drawn roughly and is slightly egg-shaped rather than truly round. A small Link sign sits upright at the center. Five Diamond signs sit near the ring at the west, northeast, southeast, south-southeast and southwest, each tilted at a different angle, with the southeast and southwest ones drawn in heavier strokes. Two Collection signs sit near the ring, one at the east and one at the north-northwest, where it crosses the edge of a smaller circle. That small circle is a neatly drawn sub-seal near the north with a closed ring, holding a single Stillness sign at its center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: There is no element sigil, so Link serves as the core. It identifies pieces that were broken off from, or made from, the same source and links them, and its small size gives a modest intensity. The five Diamond signs limit the spell to objects inside a container the seal is drawn on, leaving the container itself untouched. The two Collection signs gather material from above and around the seal so the spell can use it. The Stillness sub-seal adds a self-contained effect that holds magic static in one place. These are three kinds of modifier that work together without contradiction, and the signs are spread evenly, so no direction is favored. The rough strokes and the not-quite-round outer ring make the main seal weaker and shorter lived, and its effect is fleeting. The neatly drawn sub-seal is steadier than the seal around it.
effect: Gathers loose fragments inside a container that came from the same source, links them together and holds them still in place, without affecting the container itself. The pull is gentle, and the hold is brief: linked pieces begin to slip and drift apart well before the spell would normally end. Only the stilling at one spot near the edge lingers somewhat longer than the rest.

name: s42_00290.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A water sigil, an S-curve flanked by two teardrops, sits upright at the center and is small relative to the ring. Six Selection signs, each a small square crossed by a grid of lines, are spread around it. Four sit near the ring at the north-northwest, northeast, southeast, and southwest. The southwest one is drawn with heavier, darker strokes and touches the ring. The other two sit about halfway out, at the west-northwest and south-southeast. A single Concealment sign, an eight-armed star with eye marks on four of its arms, sits about halfway out at the southwest. More signs crowd the southwestern side than the northeast, which is mostly empty. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Selection is non-directional and confines a spell's effect to the object the seal is drawn on. Six of them strongly limit the water to that object, so nothing around it is affected. Concealment hides a target. Paired with water and held to the drawn object by Selection, it uses the water to hide that object. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they do not contradict each other, so the seal holds together. Concealment sits alone off-center at the southwest, the side where the signs cluster, so the hiding is strongest there rather than even all around. The heavy southwest Selection adds to that bias.
effect: Draws a thin veil of water over the object the seal is drawn on and hides it from view, without touching anything around it. The veil is fullest on the southwest side and thins toward the northeast, where the object may still show faintly through the water.

name: s42_00291.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background. The outer ring is closed and neatly drawn, and its center is empty. Four Crosshair signs sit just inside the ring at the north-northeast, northeast, east-southeast, and southwest positions. Three Immobility signs sit just inside the ring at the north-northwest, west-northwest, and south-southeast positions, each with its base bar toward the center and its curved top toward the ring. A small closed sub-seal sits inside the main ring at the south-southeast, just inside the southern Immobility sign. It holds an upright fire sigil that fills more than half of its small ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The main seal has no central sigil, so the fire sigil in the sub-seal supplies the element, and the spell creates and shapes flame or heat. The sigil is large for its ring, which makes the fire concentrated, but the sub-seal itself is small, so the overall output is modest and short-lived. Crosshair makes a seal's effect target whatever its short ends point at. The four Crosshairs are spread around the ring and face outward, so the fire is aimed at several separate points rather than one. Immobility makes its target immovable relative to the seal and holds its shape. Its outward-facing orientation has never been seen to change its effect, so it is read here as holding. The signs are balanced around the ring. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they work together without contradiction, so the seal is stable.
effect: Places small, concentrated flames at several separate points around the seal. Each flame is locked in place relative to the seal and keeps a fixed shape instead of spreading or drifting. The fire is modest in size and burns out sooner than a larger fire seal would.

name: s42_00293.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. An earth sigil sits upright at the center, at a moderate size relative to the ring. Five Rain signs sit about three quarters of the way out from the center, at the northwest, north-northeast, east-northeast, east-southeast and southwest positions. Each is a small concave four-pointed shape with short tick marks on its outer edges, and none is flipped inside-out. The east-northeast sign is turned differently from the others. The signs cluster more on the eastern half, leaving the west and south sparser. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell works on existing solid matter such as sand, soil and grit. Earth does not create matter, so the spell can only use material already present. The sigil's moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Rain summons the spell's material and brings it down from above, like rainfall. Rain is semi-directional with radial symmetry, so rotating it does not change its effect. Only flipping it inside-out would invert it, so the differently turned east-northeast sign still reads as normal Rain. Five Rain signs reinforce the same behavior, so the fall is fuller and more rain-like than an abrupt drop. Rain's own direction does not steer a spell, but the signs are bunched toward the east-northeast, so more of the effect is concentrated on that side. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing conflicts. With a closed, neatly drawn ring, the spell activates and holds steady.
effect: Draws up loose earth such as sand, soil and grit from the surroundings and lets it fall back over the area around the seal as a steady, moderate shower. The fall is heaviest on the east-northeast side and thinner toward the west and south.

name: s42_00294.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. An earth sigil sits upright at the center, moderate in size relative to the ring and drawn a little roughly. Six signs sit near the ring, evenly spread. Four are Rain signs, each a small square with inward-curving sides and short lines on its edges, at the east, south-southeast, west and north-northwest positions. The south-southeast one is drawn more roughly than the others, and the west one is slightly rough. Two are Aeriforms Defined signs, each made of three short slanted strokes of rising length, at the northeast and south-southwest, with their tops toward the center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell works on existing solid matter such as sand, soil and grit rather than creating it. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity, and its slight roughness weakens the spell a little and shortens how long it lasts. Rain is semi-directional and summons its target so that it comes down from above. All four are drawn in their normal orientation, not flipped inside-out, so they call material down rather than pushing it away. Aeriforms Defined is tied to air and gases, so with earth it would loosen the material into fine, airborne particles. Reading it this way is somewhat uncertain because its exact function is not well established. The two kinds of modifier work together without contradiction. The signs are balanced, so no direction is favored. The rough Rain sign at the south-southeast makes the effect weaker on that side.
effect: Draws loose earth such as sand and soil into the air above the seal and lets it fall back over the surrounding area like a fine, dusty rain. The fall is moderate in strength and thinner and patchier toward the south-southeast. The shower thins out sooner than a cleanly drawn version would.

name: s42_00295.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. An upright earth sigil sits at the center, moderate in size relative to the ring. Three four-lobed Billow signs sit close to the ring at the north-northeast, south-southwest, and west-northwest positions. Two Aeriforms Defined signs, each a cluster of three short strokes, sit about halfway between the center and the ring, one at the north and one at the east-southeast. Both point their tops toward the center. The east-southeast one is drawn a little rougher than the rest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell works on solid matter such as soil, sand, and stone. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Billow is non-directional, so its orientation does not matter, and it turns available material into a fluffy cloud. Here it acts as a modifier on the earth sigil rather than taking the center. Three Billow signs spread around the ring apply that effect evenly. Aeriforms Defined is an air-related modifier, likely semi-directional. Both signs face inward in the normal orientation, so neither is inverted, and they add an airy, gaseous quality to the material. The two kinds of modifier complement each other rather than conflict, and the signs are balanced, so no direction is favored. The slightly rough east-southeast sign weakens the airy quality a little on that side.
effect: Loosens nearby soil and sand into a light, airy, cloud-like mass that is soft to the touch, at moderate strength and spread evenly around the seal. On the east-southeast side the cloud comes out a little denser and less buoyant than elsewhere, and it settles back sooner there.

name: s42_00300.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A small Partition sign, a peaked roof shape over a flat bar, sits upright at the center. There is no element sigil. Six Repetition signs are evenly spaced inside the inner ring at roughly the east, south-southeast, southwest, west, north-northwest and northeast positions, all about the same distance from the center. Two of these, at the south-southeast and southwest, look slightly rougher than the rest. Two more Repetition signs sit in the band between the rings, one at the north and one at the south. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the central Partition sign acts as the core of the seal. Partition outlines the borders of an area of effect that extends outward and upward, and the other symbols within that area decide what happens inside it. Here every other symbol is Repetition, which continuously resets whatever it affects to the state it was in when the spell first took hold, including its shape and temperature. The six inner Repetition signs are evenly spaced, so the effect is balanced across the whole area. The second ring strengthens the core spell, and the two Repetition signs in the outer band at north and south reinforce the resetting. Only two kinds of glyph are present, and they work together without contradiction. The two slightly rough signs make the effect a little less steady on the south-southwest side.
effect: Marks out a bounded area around the seal and holds everything inside it in place in time. Anything within that area that is damaged, moved, spoiled, warmed or cooled is steadily restored to the state it was in when the spell began. Along the south-southwest edge of the area, the restoring lags slightly behind the rest of the space.

name: s42_00305.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with the outer ring closed and neatly drawn. An Immobility sign, upright and modest in size relative to the ring, sits at the center: a short vertical stroke over a horizontal base, bracketed by two curves. Three small sub-seals sit inside the main ring, each with its own ring closed. The one at the north-northeast holds a wind sigil, the one at the west holds a light sigil, and the one at the south-southeast holds an earth sigil. Each sigil fills roughly half of its small ring. Three hooked glyphs sit near the outer ring, roughly evenly spaced. At the west-southwest is a plain Envelopment sign. At the north-northeast is an Envelopment-like stroke with an extra stroke off one end. At the southeast is a glyph shaped like Envelopment with one half mirrored onto the other, so it looks somewhat like an arrow. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The main seal has no element sigil, so the central Immobility sign acts as the core. It makes its target immovable relative to the seal, so the target holds its shape as if frozen while still able to be carried along with the seal. The three closed sub-seals each add an element. Wind moves air, light creates light that fades over time, and earth works on solid matter. Each sigil fills about half of its small ring, which gives a moderate intensity within its sub-seal, but the sub-seals are small, so their overall contribution is limited. The plain Envelopment sign makes the effect surround its target. The two altered glyphs most closely resemble Envelopment, though reading them that way is a guess. On that reading they add the same surrounding behavior, and the extra and mirrored strokes do not clearly change it. The three are spread evenly, so the wrapping is balanced on all sides. Only two kinds of modifier are present, holding in place and surrounding, and they work together. The neat drawing and closed rings mean the spell activates and holds steady.
effect: Wraps the target in a layered shell of held air, soft light and firmed earth, and locks it so it cannot move relative to the seal while keeping its shape. The air and earth stay fixed around the target. The light glows gently and slowly dims over time.

name: s42_00308.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with two concentric closed rings and a wide band between them. A small earth sigil, upright, sits at the center of the inner ring. Four Partition signs sit in the band between the rings, at the west-northwest, north-northeast, east-southeast and south-southwest positions. Each has its peaked top toward the outer ring. They are spaced evenly around the seal. The west-northwest and south-southwest signs are cleanly drawn, while the north-northeast and east-southeast signs show slightly doubled, rough strokes. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell manipulates solid matter such as soil, stone and sand rather than creating it. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Partition is a directional sign that outlines the borders of an area of effect, extending outward and upward. The effect that fills that area is set by the symbols inside it, here the earth sigil. With all four Partition signs facing outward and spaced evenly, the boundary spreads evenly around the seal with no favored direction. The second ring holds the Partition signs apart from the core and adds strength to the outlined area. No signs contradict each other, and only one kind of modifier is present. The two roughly drawn Partition signs weaken the boundary slightly on their sides.
effect: Marks out a bounded area that spreads outward and upward from the seal, and moves nearby soil, stone or sand to fill and shape it along that outline. The effect is modest in strength. The boundary on the north-northeast and east-southeast sides holds less firmly and fades sooner than the rest.

name: s42_00311.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes, sits upright at the center and is fairly large relative to the ring. Nine Mimicry signs surround it, all pointing radially with their tops toward the ring. Six form an inner circle about halfway out, at the north-northeast, east, southeast, south-southwest, west-southwest and northwest. Three more sit closer to the ring, at the north-northeast, south-southwest and west-northwest. A few of the Mimicry signs are drawn with slightly rougher strokes than the rest. The signs are spread evenly around the seal, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves and manipulates air. Its fairly large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect. Mimicry guides or imitates the movements of a target object. No decorative sigil gives it a creature to copy, so it copies the target the spell acts on. Nine Mimicry signs reinforce one another and strengthen how closely the air follows that motion. Because the signs are balanced around the ring, no direction is favored. The effect follows wherever the target moves. Only one kind of modifier is present, so there is no conflict. The few slightly rough signs only make the tracking a little less exact.
effect: Stirs up a strong current of air that follows and copies the movements of its target, moving with it in any direction. The current tracks the target closely, though now and then it lags or drifts slightly out of step before catching up.

name: s42_00313.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. An earth sigil sits upright at the center and is fairly large relative to the ring. Six Strengthening signs are evenly spaced inside the inner ring, roughly at the south-southwest, west, north-northwest, northeast, east, and south-southeast positions. Each sign is turned with its top toward the center. Outside the outer ring at the north-northwest, a short line joins a small linked seal. That seal has its own closed ring and holds a small upright fire sigil. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on existing solid matter such as stone, soil, sand, and wood rather than creating it. Its fairly large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect, and the second ring adds further strength to the core spell. Strengthening makes its target harder, stronger, and more durable. Six of them, evenly spaced, reinforce the effect without favoring any side, and no directional sign moves it away from the seal. The linked seal adds fire magic, meaning heat, to the main spell. That seal is small and its sigil is modest, so the heat is gentle rather than a flame. Heat working alongside reinforced earth points to baking or tempering the material. There is only one kind of modifier plus two complementary sigils, so the seal is coherent and stable.
effect: Hardens and reinforces the stone, soil, or sand it acts on, leaving the material much tougher and more durable. The effect is even all around the seal. A gentle, steady heat runs through the material as it hardens and bakes it solid, much like firing clay.

name: s42_00314.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A fire sigil sits upright at the center, moderate in size relative to the ring. Four Gathering signs sit about two-thirds of the way out from the center, at the north-northeast, east-southeast, south-southwest and northwest positions. Each has its arrowhead pointing outward toward the ring. Two four-lobed Billow signs sit closer to the ring at the east and west points. The eastern one is drawn in a heavier, filled line and the western one in a lighter outline. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and shapes flame and heat. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Gathering lets a spell draw material from its surroundings to build its effect. Four of them spread evenly around the seal pull that material in from every side. Billow turns available material into a soft, fluffy cloud. Here it acts as a modifier beside the fire sigil, not in place of one, so the gathered material is puffed into cloud and charged with the fire's heat. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they support each other: one supplies material and the other shapes it. The signs are balanced around the ring, so no direction is favored and the effect stays centered on the seal.
effect: Draws in loose material from all around the seal and puffs it into a soft, billowing cloud that carries a moderate warmth. The cloud gathers evenly over the seal rather than drifting in any one direction.

name: s42_00318.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, drawn neatly with two concentric rings, both closed. The inner ring sits well inside the outer one, leaving a wide band between them. An earth sigil sits upright at the center and is small to moderate relative to the ring. Eleven Cooling signs, each a short bar flanked by dots, surround it. Five sit in the band between the rings, at the north, east-northeast, east-southeast, south and west-northwest, all facing outward toward the ring. Six sit inside the inner ring, at the north, northeast, east-southeast, south, west-southwest and west-northwest, and most of these are turned to various angles. The outer north sign and the inner south sign are drawn a little roughly. The signs are spread evenly around the seal, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on existing solid matter such as stone, soil and sand rather than creating it. Its small-to-moderate size relative to the ring gives a modest base intensity. A second ring adds strength to the core spell. Cooling is the only kind of modifier present. It is semi- or non-directional, so the varied rotations do not steer the spell. Instead, the large number of Cooling signs deepens the chilling effect. Because the signs are evenly placed in both bands, no side is favored and the cold spreads uniformly. The two slightly rough signs are minor and only slightly weaken their spots. With a single kind of modifier, nothing contradicts and the spell holds steady.
effect: Steadily chills the stone, soil or sand the seal acts on, drawing heat out evenly on all sides. The cold builds well beyond a mild coolness, though it runs a touch weaker at the northern and southern edges.

name: s42_00321.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but hand-drawn and a little lumpy, so it is not quite round. Two glyphs share the center, both a little rough. On the left is a Detection sign, three vertical strokes of increasing height. On the right is a tall, narrow glyph resembling a fire sigil stretched vertically, slightly smaller than the Detection sign. Five Immobility signs surround them. Those at the north, south, northeast and southeast have their tops toward the center. The one at the west is turned the other way, with its top toward the ring. The north and south signs sit closer in, about halfway to the ring, while the others sit near the ring. Two small, faint glyphs sit near the ring at the northwest and southwest. Each looks like a Gathering sign with a small circle on its stem, oriented with its top toward the center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The tall center glyph matches no known sigil exactly. Its closest match is the fire sigil, so reading it as fire is a guess. Under that reading the spell works with flame and heat, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. The Detection sign shares the center as a second core; it is likely a sensing component, so the spell responds to something it detects nearby. The two circled Gathering-like glyphs are read as Gathering, also a guess, and would draw heat or material in from the surroundings. The small circle may lend a slight firming quality like the circles of Solidification. The Immobility signs hold the effect fixed in shape and position relative to the seal. Four face the usual way, but the one at the west is reversed and pulls against that hold. The four normal signs dominate, but the conflict makes the result likely unstable on the west side. The slightly irregular ring and rough strokes further weaken the spell and shorten how long it lasts.
effect: Draws heat in from the surroundings and holds it as a fixed, upright flame anchored to the seal. The flame flares up when something comes near. The western side never quite settles, so the flame periodically leans or drifts that way before snapping back. The whole effect gutters and fades sooner than a cleanly drawn version would.

name: s42_00322.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes, sits upright at the center at a moderate size, a little under half the ring's radius. Seven Dispersion signs are scattered around it. Four sit roughly two-thirds of the way out with their tops toward the ring, at the north-northeast, southeast, southwest and west. Three more sit right against the ring with their tops toward the center, so they are inverted, at the east-northeast, west-southwest and north-northwest. The north-northeast sign is a little roughly drawn. At the northwest, about two-thirds out, is a short straight stroke that matches no known sign exactly. More signs cluster on the western and northwestern side than elsewhere. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves and manipulates existing air rather than creating it. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Dispersion makes a seal's magic pour or leak outward instead of beaming in one direction, so the moved air spreads out from the seal rather than forming a jet. Inverted Dispersion works much like normal Dispersion, and inverted Columns also behaves this way, so the three signs set against the ring add to the outward spill rather than opposing it. The northwest stroke is closest to Dispersion with its two halves mirrored onto each other, which is a guess. With no distinct front or back, it would leak air both ways along its line and add a little untargeted spill on that side. The signs are unevenly spread and weighted toward the west-northwest, so more of the outflow goes that way. The slightly rough north-northeast sign makes the flow on that side a bit weaker and shorter-lived. Only one kind of modifier is present, so the seal holds together.
effect: Stirs the surrounding air and lets it pour outward from the seal as a spreading, moderate breeze rather than a focused gust. The flow is noticeably stronger toward the west-northwest. It is a little weaker toward the north-northeast, and that side fades sooner than the rest.

name: s42_00327.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with the ring closed and neatly drawn. A Link sign sits at the center in place of a sigil. It is moderately sized, about a third of the ring's radius, upright, and its strokes are a little rough. There is no element sigil. Two Envelopment signs, each a slanted stroke with hooked ends, sit near the ring at the east-northeast and west-southwest. A small six-spoked star, like a Concealment sign without its eye marks, sits at the north, about two thirds of the way out from the center. A Cooling sign, a short line flanked by dots, sits at the east-southeast at a similar distance. The signs are unevenly spread and weighted toward the east-northeast. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, Link at the center sets the spell's core behavior. It identifies objects that were broken off from, or made from, the same source and links them. Because no element is present, the spell is not tied to fire, water, earth, or wind. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity, and its slightly rough strokes make it somewhat weaker and shorter lived than a clean drawing would be. The two Envelopment signs make the effect wrap around its targets instead of acting on a single point. The six-spoked star matches no known sign exactly. Its closest match is Concealment, which hides a target, so reading it as Concealment is a guess. Without the eye marks it may hide its targets less fully than the complete sign would. Cooling lowers the temperature of whatever the spell acts on. Envelopment and Concealment work together, Cooling adds one further quality, and none of the signs contradict each other, so the seal holds together. Because the signs are weighted toward the east-northeast, the effect is stronger on that side.
effect: Finds objects or fragments that share a common source, links them, and wraps each one in a cool, partly concealing shroud that hides it from casual view. The shroud is thicker and colder on the east-northeast side and thinner on the opposite side. It fades somewhat sooner than a cleaner drawing would allow.

name: s42_00001.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A water sigil sits at the center, moderate in size relative to the ring. Three Crosshair signs sit near the ring at the north, east-southeast and south, with the southern one drawn more roughly. A Convergence triangle at the east-northeast is drawn large, heavy and slightly jagged, with one point facing inward, and it overlaps the edge of a nearby sub-seal. A small, slightly rough Partition sign sits at the west, pointing inward. A Stillness sign sits at the northwest, and a small Windows sign sits at the southwest. Four smaller closed sub-seals lie inside the main ring. At the north-northwest is a neat ring holding a Glaives mark. At the east-northeast is a roughly drawn ring holding a small water sigil. At the south-southeast is a slightly rough ring holding a wind sigil. At the west-southwest is a lumpy, clearly out-of-round ring holding a light sigil. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil sets the element, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. The three Crosshairs aim the effect at whatever their short ends point toward, which here is north, east-southeast and south. Convergence draws the water toward a single point and packs it tightly. Stillness holds that water in place. Partition outlines a boundary on the western side. Windows connects the seal to a space that is not physically joined to it. The sub-seals add their own effects. Glaives set how deeply the magic embeds into flesh. The extra water sub-seal adds more water, but its rough ring weakens that contribution. The wind sub-seal moves air along with the water. The light sub-seal's ring is not round enough, so its glow is fleeting at best. That gives five unrelated kinds of modifier in the main ring, plus four sub-seals. The water sigil and the three Crosshairs dominate, with Convergence and Stillness secondary, and Partition and Windows least reliable, so the result is likely unstable. The rough drawing of several signs further weakens and shortens the effect.
effect: Gathers water into tight, held clumps aimed at points to the north, east-southeast and south, where it sinks into any flesh it strikes, pushed along by fitful gusts with a brief flicker of light. The water holds unevenly within a loose western boundary and partly slips away as if through an opening to somewhere else. The effect lurches between these behaviors and breaks apart early.

name: s42_00002.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A light sigil, a diamond set inside a square with four short spokes, sits upright at the center and is small relative to the ring. A four-lobed Billow sign sits near the ring at the south-southwest, drawn neatly. A Partition sign sits near the ring at the north-northwest, with its top toward the ring, drawn slightly roughly. No other signs are present, and both signs sit on the western side, leaving the eastern half empty. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil makes this a light spell, and its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Billow is not at the center here, so it acts as an ordinary modifier rather than the core. It turns the spell's output into a soft, fluffy cloud, so the light takes a diffuse, puffy form instead of a beam or point. Partition is directional and outlines the borders of an area of effect, extending outward and upward. With its top toward the ring it pushes that boundary outward, and because it sits at the north-northwest the bounded area lies on that side. Both signs sit on the western side, so the effect leans west instead of centering on the seal. The slight roughness of the Partition sign makes the boundary less crisp. Only two kinds of modifier are present and they do not contradict each other.
effect: Produces a modest, soft cloud of diffuse light that billows up within a bounded area off the western side of the seal, with slightly uneven, wavering edges. The glow is gentle rather than bright and gradually dims over time.

name: s42_00005.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed and neatly drawn. Two glyphs sit side by side at the center, both small relative to the ring: a Strengthening sign on the left and a water sigil on the right. Four Crushing signs sit about two thirds of the way out, at north, east, south and west, each with its peaks turned toward the center, so all four are inverted. The north one reads as a W, the south one as an M, and the east and west ones as upright zigzags. The east sign is drawn a little rougher than the others. A Concealment sign, an eight-armed star with four eye marks on its diagonals, sits near the ring at the southeast. No other signs are present, and the extra sign at the southeast makes the layout lean toward that side.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell, and Strengthening shares the center as a second core, making what the spell shapes harder and more durable. Both are small relative to the ring, so the intensity is modest. Crushing is semi-directional, so its placement does not steer the spell, but inversion reverses it. Inverted Crushing pulls broken or scattered material back into its original form for as long as the spell lasts. With water, that means drawing dispersed droplets back into the body they came from. The slightly rough east sign makes that pull a little weaker on the east side. Concealment hides its target. Because it is the only sign at the southeast, the hiding effect is weighted toward that side and is not spread evenly. That makes three kinds of modifier: reforming, strengthening and concealment. They do not contradict each other.
effect: Draws scattered droplets and spray back into the water they came from and holds the reformed water firm and durable at a modest strength. The pull is slightly weaker on the east side. The water is partly hidden from view, most fully on its southeast side, and falls back apart once the spell wears off.

name: s42_00006.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background. The main ring is closed but drawn roughly and badly out of round, bulging into a lumpy, blob-like outline. A small water sigil sits at the center, about a quarter of the ring's radius and roughly drawn. Three Dispersion signs sit near the ring at the west, north-northeast and south-southeast, each with its stem toward the center and its curve toward the ring. Two Glaives signs sit at the west-northwest and east-northeast. The western one has its tines toward the ring, while the eastern one is turned the other way, tines toward the center. A Crushing sign sits at the south, drawn as a W with its peaks toward the center, in its normal orientation. Three smaller sub-seals sit inside the main ring. At the north is a neatly drawn closed ring holding a Projection sign, a flat bracket. At the southwest is a closed ring holding a slightly rough water sigil. At the east-southeast is a neatly drawn ring that is open on its western side, holding an earth sigil. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil sets the element, and its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. The closed water sub-seal adds a second, smaller source of water. Three Dispersion signs make the water pour outward rather than rise as a beam, and their spacing spreads it on all sides. The closed Projection sub-seal pushes the effect further out from the seal. Normal Crushing breaks its target into smaller pieces. On water it would break the flow into fine droplets. The two Glaives set how deeply the magic embeds into flesh, so the spray would sink into anyone it reaches. They face opposite ways, and an inverted Glaive has no known effect, so the two may partly cancel and make that depth uneven. The open earth sub-seal contributes nothing. That leaves four unrelated kinds of modifier: dispersion, projection, crushing and embedding. Water with Dispersion dominates, Projection sets the outward push, and Crushing and the mismatched Glaives are the least reliable parts. The result is likely unstable. Combined with the rough linework and the badly out-of-round ring, the effect would be fleeting, and the seal may fail to activate at all.
effect: Sputters out a weak, uneven spray of fine water droplets in all directions away from the seal. The spray sinks into the skin of anyone it reaches, sometimes shallowly and sometimes deeper, and no earth effect takes part. It wavers, may not start at all, and collapses after a brief burst.

name: s42_00007.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background with two concentric rings, both closed and slightly rough. A small, neatly drawn water sigil sits upright at the center. A large Reflection sign, an hourglass of two triangles, sits at the northeast just inside the inner ring. A Glaives sign sits at the north-northwest about halfway out, with its prongs toward the center. Three small Repetition signs sit out near the rings at the north-northwest, west-northwest and south. The west-northwest one is drawn heavier and rougher than the others. A small Refuse sign sits at the west-southwest on the inner ring with its diamond end toward the center. A small Purification sign sits at the east-southeast on the inner ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil sets the element. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity, and the second ring adds some strength. Purification separates waste from water. Refuse is directional and points inward here, so the separated waste is collected toward the center of the seal. Three Repetition signs, spread around the ring, keep resetting the water to the state it had when the spell first touched it. That directly contradicts Purification, which is trying to change the water. Reflection targets a reflected image, here the water's surface. Glaives set how deeply magic embeds into flesh, which has no clear tie to the rest. The seal stacks five kinds of modifier: purification with refuse, repetition, reflection and glaives. Water, Purification and Refuse dominate because they work together, and Repetition fights them. The result is likely unstable, and the rough linework weakens it further.
effect: Draws a modest amount of water and begins cleansing it, dragging grime toward the middle of the seal. The water keeps snapping back toward its dirty state, so it clears and clouds in uneven pulses. Its surface flickers with stray reflected images, and the spell wavers and collapses before the water is ever fully clean.

name: s42_00009.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A large wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes, sits upright at the center and reaches about half the ring's radius. Closer in, about halfway to the ring, sit four modifiers. A Strengthening sign is at the west-northwest with its top toward the center. A Cooling sign is at the east-southeast, rotated. A Partition sign is at the south with its top toward the center. Three Convergence triangles sit at the northeast, southwest and north-northwest, each rotated at a different angle. Near the ring are three Binding signs, double arcs with their tops toward the center, at the north, southeast and west-southwest. A fourth Convergence triangle sits at the northeast with one point facing inward, and its outer edge touches the ring line. The signs are spread evenly around the seal, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves and manipulates existing air rather than creating it. Its large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect. Four Convergence signs draw the magic together toward a single point and pack loose matter tightly until it is somewhat rigid. The three Binding signs halt the gathered air's movement and make it act as one unit. Strengthening makes that unit harder and more durable. These three signs all work toward compacting and firming the air, so they act as one family of modifier. Partition outlines the borders of the area of effect, extending outward and upward, so the compacted air stays within a defined space. Cooling chills the air. This gives three kinds of modifier in total (compaction, boundary and cooling), and none of them contradicts another. The seal is evenly balanced and cleanly drawn, so no direction is favored and the effect holds steady.
effect: Draws the surrounding air inward and packs it into a dense, chilled mass that holds together as a single firm body within a bounded space above and around the seal. The compressed cold air is strong and durable, behaving almost like a solid, and stays in place rather than drifting or dispersing.

name: s42_00010.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but drawn roughly and is noticeably lumpy and out of round. There is no element sigil. A Strengthening sign, a triangle crossed by a horizontal bar, sits upright at the center in place of a sigil. It is large, about half the ring's radius, and drawn with thick, uneven strokes. Five Orb signs, each a small circle crossed by a diagonal line, sit about three quarters of the way to the ring at the north-northeast, east, south-southeast, south-southwest and northwest. A single Crosshair sign sits at the west, also near the ring. All the signs are drawn roughly. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the Strengthening sign at the center acts as the core of the seal. It makes its target stronger, harder and more durable, and its large size relative to the ring would normally give a strong effect. The Orb signs are non-directional. They define a spherical space above the seal where the spell's material collects when it is added directly, filling from the bottom up under gravity. Five evenly spread Orbs keep that space balanced rather than pushed to one side. Crosshair is directional and makes the seal's effect target whatever its short ends point at. Placed alone at the west, it aims the effect at what lies west of the seal. This is only three kinds of modifier, and they do not contradict each other, so the seal is coherent. However, the rough strokes and the out-of-round ring weaken it and make it short-lived, and the uneven ring risks a fleeting effect or a failure to activate.
effect: Forms a faint, wavering spherical space aimed at a point west of the seal. Material poured directly into it settles from the bottom up and is only patchily hardened, so it stays more fragile than intended. The space flickers in and out and collapses after a short time, and on some attempts it fails to form at all.

name: s42_00011.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background, ring closed but drawn roughly and noticeably out of round, bulging into a lumpy egg shape. A fire sigil sits upright at the center, fairly large relative to the ring and slightly rough. Two four-lobed Billow signs sit about halfway out, one at the east and one at the west, the western one drawn more roughly than the eastern. A heavily drawn Convergence triangle sits near the ring at the south-southwest, its flat side toward the ring and its point facing inward. Two neatly drawn Immobility signs sit close to the ring, one at the north-northwest and one at the south-southeast. Each has its bar toward the ring and its paired arcs facing the center. The signs cluster more heavily toward the south-southwest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and shapes flame and heat. Its fairly large size relative to the ring gives a moderately strong intensity. Billow turns available material into a soft, fluffy cloud, so paired with fire it shapes the flame into a billowing mass. Two Billow signs make this the dominant behavior. Convergence centers magic on a single point and packs loose particles tightly and rigidly, which works directly against Billow's loose, fluffy form. With only one Convergence sign, it pulls part of the mass toward a tighter knot rather than overriding the cloud. Because it sits off to one side and the signs are unbalanced, that pull leans toward the south-southwest. The two Immobility signs hold the result fixed in relation to the seal, so it keeps its place and rough shape. Billow and Fire dominate and Immobility steadies them, but the clash between Billow and Convergence makes the result likely unstable. The rough linework and the out-of-round ring further weaken the effect, make it short-lived and fleeting, and may cause the spell to fail to activate.
effect: Raises a puffy, billowing cloud of flame that stays fixed over the seal, burning with moderate heat. The cloud repeatedly tightens into a denser knot on its south-southwest side and loosens again, flickering unevenly between soft and compact before it gutters out after only a short time.

name: s42_00012.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background, neatly drawn, with two concentric rings. The outer ring is open, with a wide gap on the west side. The inner ring sits just inside it and is also open, with a gap at the north. A Purification sign, a small hooked curl, sits upright at the center in place of a sigil. It is modest in size relative to the ring. Three Stretch signs, each an arch with short outward-turned feet, sit about two thirds of the way out at the north, east-southeast and southwest. The north sign sits in the inner ring's gap. Each Stretch sign has its open, footed side turned away from the center and its rounded top toward the center. The three signs are evenly spaced. No element sigil is present.
justification: There is no element sigil, so the Purification sign at the center serves as the core of the seal. Purification separates waste from water. Its modest size relative to the ring gives a moderate intensity. Stretch turns solid matter into long, flexible ribbons on contact. Three Stretch signs spaced evenly around the center apply that effect equally on all sides and push it in no direction. Read together, the solid waste that Purification pulls out of the water is the solid matter Stretch acts on, so the waste is drawn out into ribbons. The inner ring adds strength to the core effect. There are only two kinds of modifier, and they do not contradict each other. Both rings are open, so the seal cannot activate until each gap is closed.
effect: Once the ring is closed, and the inner ring with it, the seal separates solid waste from water at moderate strength. The separated grime is drawn out into long, flexible ribbons that can be lifted cleanly out of the water.

name: s42_00013.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn; the inner ring sits just inside the outer one. At the center is an upright fire-like sigil, drawn neatly and stretched tall, with a narrow elongated triangle, two short strokes crossing its upper sides and a short stem below. It reaches about half the ring's radius. Six small identical glyphs sit in the band between the two rings at the north, east-northeast, southeast, south-southwest, west-southwest and northwest, each with its top toward the center. Each looks like a Stillness sign with its right part missing. The ones at the east-northeast and northwest are drawn neatly, while the north, southeast, south-southwest and west-southwest ones are a little rough and heavier. An Aeriforms Defined sign, three short fanned strokes, sits alone at the east, about two thirds of the way out, with its top toward the center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The central glyph is closest to the fire sigil drawn tall. Reading it as fire is a guess, and the stretched form would lengthen the flame upward. Its size relative to the ring gives a fairly strong intensity. The second ring adds strength to the core spell. The six band glyphs match no known sign exactly. Their closest match is Stillness, which holds a magical effect static in one location, so reading them as Stillness is a guess. Their missing halves would give a weaker hold. Four of them are rough, so the hold would be uneven around the ring. They are evenly spaced, so they favor no direction. Aeriforms Defined concerns gases and is most likely semi-directional, so its placement at the east sets no direction. Paired with fire, it would carry the heat into the surrounding air rather than leaving it as bare flame. Only a few compatible kinds of modifier are present, and none contradict each other.
effect: Raises a tall, strong flame that stays fixed in place above the seal and heats the air around it into a warm envelope. The hold is uneven, so the flame sways and drifts slightly on some sides, and the warmth flickers rather than staying perfectly still.

name: s42_00016.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background. The ring is open, with a gap at the upper right between the north and east. It is drawn roughly and is noticeably out of round, closer to a lopsided square. An earth sigil sits upright at the center at moderate size relative to the ring, also drawn roughly. Six signs sit about three quarters of the way out toward the ring. A small Piercing sign sits at the east, tilted at an angle. Two larger, heavily drawn Strengthening signs sit at the southeast and the northwest, the northwestern one rotated. Two Entwining signs sit at the northeast and the southwest, each with its top toward the ring. A small Coil sign lies on its side at the west. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil makes this an earth spell that moves existing solids such as stone and soil rather than creating them. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Piercing is non-directional and makes the target material manifest as projectiles, and a single sign gives a single projectile. Strengthening makes the material harder and more durable. Entwining makes it wrap itself around other objects. Coil softens solid matter, which directly contradicts Strengthening. The seal also stacks four unrelated kinds of modifier: projectile, hardening, wrapping and softening. Strengthening dominates, with two large, bold signs against one small Coil, and the two Entwining signs set the main behavior. The single small Piercing sign sets the form, so the result is likely unstable. There are no directional signs, and the signs are balanced around the ring, so no direction is set. The rough linework and the poor roundness of the ring make the effect weak and fleeting, and the spell may fail to activate at all. It does not activate until the ring is closed.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it pulls nearby stone or soil into a single earthen shard that tries to coil around a target close to the seal. The shard flickers between rigid and pliant, wraps only partway and unevenly, and crumbles back into loose earth after a moment, if it forms at all.

name: s42_00017.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but drawn a little roughly and slightly out of round. A wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes, sits upright at the center at about a third of the ring's radius, drawn roughly. Four Diamond signs sit about halfway out, at the northwest, north-northeast, east-northeast and south-southwest, each tilted at a different angle and drawn roughly. Two Purification signs, small hooked curls, sit at the southeast and west-southwest at a similar distance, each with its top toward the center. Two small Dancing Puppets signs sit near the ring at the northwest and northeast; the northeast one is neater than the northwest one. The signs are spread fairly evenly around the seal, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves and manipulates air. Its moderate size relative to the ring gives a moderate intensity. Dancing Puppets paired with wind lets objects be lifted and manipulated in the air. These two are small and set out near the ring rather than around the sigil, so that control is limited. The four Diamond signs confine the spell to objects within the container the seal is drawn on, leaving the container itself unaffected. Purification is asymmetric and normally separates waste from water. Read with wind, it would sift dust and grime out of the air and from the stirred contents. These three kinds of modifier work toward one result without contradicting each other, and the balanced placement favors no direction. The rough sigil, the rough signs and the slightly uneven ring weaken the spell and shorten how long it lasts.
effect: Stirs the air inside the container the seal is drawn on, lifting its contents so they flit erratically about while dust and grime are sifted away from them, and the container itself stays still. The motion is moderate and uneven, sputtering in fits and dying out sooner than a cleanly drawn seal would.

name: s42_00018.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background. The ring is closed but drawn roughly and noticeably out of round, bulging unevenly. A neatly drawn wind sigil sits upright at the center, moderate in size relative to the ring. A single Regions sign sits near the ring at the east-northeast, its point aimed outward toward the ring. Two Convergence triangles sit about halfway out, one at the north-northeast and one at the east-southeast, each with a point facing the center. Two very small Mimicry signs sit about three quarters of the way out, one at the west-northwest and one at the south. The southern one is a little rougher. Most of the signs cluster on the eastern side. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves and manipulates existing air. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. The lone Regions sign points outward at the east-northeast. That makes the magic manifest outside the ring and sends it toward that side, and the eastern clustering of the other signs reinforces the lean. The two inward-pointing Convergence signs focus the moving air down toward a single point, so it travels as a tight stream rather than a broad gust. Mimicry makes an effect guide or imitate the movements of a target. With no decorative sigil to copy, it would make the air follow the motion of the object it reaches. Both Mimicry signs are tiny and one is rough, so that following is weak. Only three kinds of modifier are present and none contradict each other, so the seal is not unstable. However, the out-of-round ring makes the effect fleeting and somewhat unreliable to start.
effect: Sends a narrow, focused stream of air out from the seal toward the east-northeast. The stream loosely and sluggishly follows the movements of the object it strikes. The current is moderate in strength and sputters briefly into being, dying away after only a short burst.

name: s42_00019.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is open, with a wide gap on the west to southwest side, and its outline is slightly uneven. A fire sigil sits upright at the center, about a third of the ring's radius in size. Two Collection signs sit near the ring at the north and south points, each with its barred end toward the ring and its open side facing the center. A Gathering sign sits at the west-southwest with its fork pointing toward the center. A small Pulling sign sits at the east-southeast with its arrowhead pointing inward. A Reflection sign, an hourglass drawn heavier than the other signs, sits near the ring at the east-northeast. Beside it at the northeast is a Projection sign, a bracket with its open side facing outward toward the ring. A small Envelopment sign sits at the northwest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and manipulates flame and heat. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. The two inward-facing Collection signs and the Gathering sign draw material from above and around the seal into the spell. The inward Pulling sign pulls the fire toward the seal, so these four signs form one dominant inward-drawing group. Envelopment makes the effect surround its target. Reflection targets a reflected image. Projection pushes an effect outward from the seal, which directly contradicts the inward pull. The seal stacks four unrelated kinds of modifier: drawing in, enveloping, reflecting and projecting. The fire sigil and the inward-drawing group dominate. Pulling and Envelopment are drawn small, so their contributions are weak. Projection and Reflection pull against the rest, so the result is likely unstable. The seal will not activate while the ring is open.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it draws heat and flame inward toward the seal from all around and wraps them thinly about the object it is drawn on in a moderate blaze. At the same time, a flickering image of the fire is thrown outward to the northeast in uneven pulses. The opposing inward pull and outward push make the flames surge and falter, and the spell gutters out early.

name: s42_00022.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background. It has two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn, forming a band between them. A water sigil sits at the center, moderate in size relative to the ring, with slightly uneven strokes. Six Dancing Puppets signs sit in the band between the rings, at the north-northwest, east-northeast, east-southeast, south-southeast, west-southwest and west-northwest. They are spread evenly around the seal, and the east-northeast one is drawn darker and heavier than the others. Inside the inner ring at the west-northwest is a small sub-seal holding a fire sigil that fills much of its ring. That sub-seal's ring is open, with a gap at its lower right. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil sets the element, so the spell manipulates water. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity, and its slightly rough drawing makes the effect a little weaker and less steady. Dancing Puppets lets the target's movement be manipulated, and when paired with an element it sets that element moving freely, so the water is set in motion. Six of these signs give a strong hold over that motion. They are evenly spread, and no directional sign is present, so the motion follows no set course and behaves erratically. The second ring adds strength to the spell. The fire sub-seal's ring is open, so it never activates and contributes nothing. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing conflicts.
effect: Sets nearby water darting and twisting through the air in erratic, undirected motion, with fair strength but a slight waver that loosens its hold now and then. The small heating part adds no heat, so the water stays at its natural temperature.

name: s42_00023.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A Purification sign, a curled hook, sits at the center in place of a sigil, moderate in size relative to the ring. Two Reflection signs, hourglass shapes of two touching triangles, sit just inside the ring: one at the west, lying on its side, and one at the north-northeast, drawn slightly rougher. A small Sights Set sign sits at the east, with its diamond end toward the center and its arrow pointing outward toward the ring. Two smaller closed rings sit inside the main ring. The one at the north-northeast holds a neatly drawn water sigil, and the one at the south-southwest holds a roughly drawn earth sigil. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil in the main ring, the Purification sign at the center is the core of the seal. It separates waste from water. The water sub-seal supplies the water for that work, and the earth sub-seal handles the solid matter pulled out of it, such as grit and sediment. The earth sigil is drawn roughly, so that sediment handling is weaker and less even. The Reflection signs make the spell target the reflected image on the surface bearing the seal, so the cleansing acts on water reflected there. The Sights Set sign lets the caster aim the effect, and its arrow points east. The signs lean toward the north-northeast, and the rougher Reflection sign on that side makes the effect slightly weaker there. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they do not contradict each other.
effect: Cleanses the water that shows its reflection on the surface bearing the seal, aimed by the caster toward the east, separating dirt and grit from it so clear water remains. The separated sediment drops out patchily and unevenly, and the cleansing is somewhat weaker toward the north-northeast.

name: s42_00024.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A light sigil, a diamond set inside a square with four short spokes, sits upright at the center at a moderate size relative to the ring. Six Collection signs are spaced evenly around it, roughly two thirds of the way to the ring, at the north-northeast, east, southeast, south-southwest, west and northwest. Their orientation alternates. The signs at the northwest, east and south-southwest have their open crossed ends toward the center and their closed triangular ends toward the ring, which is the usual orientation. The signs at the north-northeast, southeast and west are inverted, with their open ends toward the ring, and are drawn noticeably larger and bolder than the other three. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil makes this a light spell, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Collection gathers material above and around the seal for the spell to use. The three normally oriented signs draw surrounding light inward to feed the spell. The three inverted signs most likely do the opposite and release material outward, though inverted Collection is not well understood and this reading is a guess. Gathering inward and releasing outward directly contradict each other. The two sets are equal in number and evenly balanced, so neither pulls the effect toward any direction. The inverted signs are larger, so the outward release dominates and the inward gathering only partly offsets it. Because the signs work against each other, the result is likely unstable. The neat drawing and closed ring mean the seal does activate.
effect: Produces a moderate light that briefly draws in faint ambient light, then sheds it outward from the seal in uneven pulses. The glow swells and dims erratically instead of holding steady, and it fades sooner than a steady light would.

name: s42_00025.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background with two concentric rings, both closed. The outer ring is a little rough. The center of the inner ring is empty. Four Cooling signs, each a short vertical stroke flanked by two pairs of dots, sit in the band between the two rings. They are at the west-northwest, north-northeast, east-southeast and south-southwest, with their tops toward the outer ring, and are spaced evenly. The north-northeast and east-southeast signs are drawn neatly, and the other two are a little rough. Three smaller closed sub-seals sit inside the inner ring. The northwest one holds a light sigil, the east one holds a wind sigil, and the south-southwest one, a little rough, holds a fire sigil. Each sigil is upright and modest in size relative to its own ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The main seal has no central sigil, so the three sub-seals supply its elements. Light creates a glow, wind moves air, and fire creates heat. The second ring adds strength to the whole seal. The four Cooling signs are balanced around the seal and cool things down, which directly contradicts the heat from the fire sub-seal. The four Cooling signs outweigh the single, slightly rough fire sub-seal, so cooling dominates and the heat is mostly suppressed. That clash makes the result likely unstable. Wind carries the cooled air outward, and light adds a glow that diminishes over time. The slightly rough linework on part of the outer ring and on some signs makes the spell somewhat weaker and shorter-lived.
effect: Gives off a soft, fading glow and a moving draft of cool air around the seal. Brief pockets of warmth flicker against the cold, so the temperature wavers unevenly. The effect weakens and dies out somewhat sooner than a cleanly drawn seal would.

name: s42_00026.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, with the main ring closed and neatly drawn. A Pulling sign sits upright at the center in place of a sigil, its arrow pointing south. It is about a quarter of the ring's radius. Six Link signs sit just inside the ring at the north-northeast, east-northeast, east-southeast, south, southwest and west-northwest. Four of them have their tops toward the ring. The two at the north-northeast and east-northeast are turned with their tops toward the center, so they are inverted. A Reflection sign, an hourglass shape, sits at the north-northwest. Two small closed sub-seals sit inside the main ring. The one at the west-northwest holds a Rain sign at its center. The one at the east-southeast holds an earth sigil, which takes up about half of its small ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: There is no element sigil in the main ring, so the central Pulling sign sets the core behavior. Pulling is directional, and its arrow points south, so it draws targets across the seal toward the south. The closed earth sub-seal supplies the element, solid matter such as stone and soil. Because that sub-seal is small, the intensity is modest. The closed Rain sub-seal summons material so it falls within the seal's area. The four normally placed Link signs identify pieces that broke off from, or were made from, the same source and link them. Inverting a semi-directional sign gives the opposite effect, so the two inverted Links work to break those links. This directly contradicts the other four. Reflection adds a reflected-image targeting quality that fits poorly with the rest. The seal stacks pulling, linking, summoning and reflection, which is more than three unrelated kinds of modifier. Pulling and the normal Links dominate because they outnumber the inverted Links and anchor the center, with the earth sub-seal setting the material. The inverted Links and Reflection are the least reliable parts, so the result is likely unstable.
effect: Draws fragments of stone and soil that share a common source southward across the seal, while a light fall of grit sprinkles down inside the circle. The pieces join unevenly, with some snapping together and others pulling apart again. Faint reflected images flicker across the stone, and the pull wavers and gives out before the fragments fully gather.

name: s42_00027.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with the main ring closed and neatly drawn. A Pointing sign sits upright at the center, moderate in size relative to the ring. There is no element sigil in the main seal. Six Projection signs sit just inside the ring, evenly spaced at the east, south-southeast, southwest, west-northwest, north-northwest and northeast. Each is a flat bracket with its top toward the ring and its open side facing the center. Two small sub-seals sit inside the main ring. The one at the east-southeast is neatly drawn, ring open with a gap on its right side, and holds a Binding sign at its center. The one at the west-northwest is drawn roughly and somewhat out of round, ring open, and holds a small, roughly drawn water sigil. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the Pointing sign at the center serves as the core of the seal. Pointing makes the target material take a conical, tapering shape that other signs can then direct. Projection sends a given effect outward from the seal.
