The six Projection signs are evenly balanced around the ring, so no direction is favored and the effect goes out equally on all sides. Pointing and Projection work together without contradiction, so the seal is not unstable. Both sub-seals have open rings, so neither activates. The water sigil therefore supplies no water, and Binding does not hold the material together as one unit. Because the main seal has no element, it acts on whatever material is supplied to it, not on one element.
effect: Shapes whatever material is fed into the seal into tapering, cone-shaped points and casts them outward evenly in all directions around it. The two unfinished inner seals add nothing, so no water is drawn in and the points are not held together as a single mass.

name: s42_00028.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed. The ring is hand-drawn and slightly uneven in outline but still reads as round. A Collection sign, an X capped by a horizontal bar on top, sits upright at the center, drawn boldly and moderate in size relative to the ring. There is no element sigil. Four Convergence triangles sit evenly around it near the ring, at the north-northwest, east-northeast, south-southeast and west-southwest. Each has its flat side toward the ring and a point facing inward toward the center. The east-northeast triangle sits slightly farther out and is drawn a little more roughly than the others. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, Collection takes the center and sets the core of the spell. It gathers material located above and around the seal so the spell can use it. Its moderate size gives a moderate strength. Convergence, with a point facing inward in its usual orientation, focuses the magic down to a single point and makes loose particles pack tightly together and become somewhat rigid. The four Convergence signs are evenly spaced, so the effect is balanced on all sides and pushed in no direction. The slightly rough east-northeast triangle and the slightly uneven ring make that side marginally weaker, but not enough to unbalance the seal. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they reinforce each other. Because there is no sigil, the spell is not tied to fire, water, earth or wind and acts on whatever loose material is nearby.
effect: Draws loose material from above and around the seal inward and packs it into a single compact, somewhat rigid mass at its center, working on any loose matter regardless of element. The packing is slightly looser on one side but holds together steadily.

name: s42_00029.png
description: A fully visible, neatly drawn seal on a plain background made of two concentric rings. Both are ring open: the outer ring has a gap at the upper right, between the north-northeast and the east, and the inner ring has a gap across the top. There is no element sigil. An upright Dispersion sign, with its stem pointing up and its curve below, sits at the center and is moderately large relative to the ring. An Orb sign sits at the north-northeast in the band between the two rings, beside the outer ring's gap. A Diamond sign, slightly tilted, sits inside the inner ring at the east-southeast. A Link sign sits inside the inner ring at the south, with its top toward the ring. A small Billow sign sits on the outer ring line at the west-southwest. The signs are unevenly spread and lean toward the south-southeast. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the central Dispersion sign is the core, so the spell pours its magic outward. Its moderate size gives a moderate strength, and it acts on whatever material is brought into it. Orb defines a spherical space where material collects from the bottom up. This contradicts Dispersion, which leaks material outward. Diamond limits the effect to objects inside a container the seal is drawn on. Link connects pieces that came from the same source. Billow turns material into a fluffy cloud. Together the seal stacks more than three unrelated kinds of modifier on top of the Dispersion and Orb conflict. Dispersion dominates as the central sign. Diamond and Link come second because the seal's lean favors their side. Orb and Billow, out near the rings, are the weakest. The result is likely unstable. Because the signs lean toward the south-southeast, the outflow is pushed that way. The seal will not activate until both rings are closed.
effect: Once both rings are closed, it pours material held inside a container outward in uneven surges toward the south-southeast. It tugs fragments from the same source along together, while a faint sphere keeps trying to gather them back and collapsing. Patches of the outflow puff into brief wisps of cloud before the spell falters and gives out early.

name: s42_00030.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a plain background, with two concentric rings. Both are roughly drawn, slightly out of round, and open. The outer ring has a wide gap at the lower left, and the inner ring has a gap at the bottom. A fire sigil sits upright at the center, neatly drawn and of moderate size relative to the ring. Five Windows signs surround it about halfway to two thirds of the way out, each a small circle lined with short radial hatch marks. They sit at the northwest, northeast, southwest, southeast and east-southeast. The east-southeast sign is drawn noticeably heavier and darker than the rest. No other signs are present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and manipulates flame and heat. Its moderate size relative to the ring gives a moderate intensity. Windows connects two spaces that are not physically joined, acting as a portal between locations. Here it is drawn as five small separate signs rather than as a band lining the ring, so each one reads as its own opening. They are spread around the seal without favoring one side, so no direction is set. The second ring holds no signs of its own and adds no clear modifier. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing contradicts. Both rings are open, so the seal will not activate until they are closed. The rough, uneven rings would make the effect weaker and short-lived even then.
effect: Once the rings are closed, it passes moderate flame and heat from the seal through several small openings to a separate, unconnected place, so the fire appears there rather than at the seal itself. The passages flicker and burn unevenly, and they close well before a cleanly drawn seal would.

name: s42_00031.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a plain background, with two concentric rings, both closed. The rings are a little rough and somewhat out of round. A roughly drawn earth sigil sits at the center, modest in size relative to the ring. Four Dispersion signs sit on the inner ring line, straddling the band between the rings, at the west, east, southwest and north-northwest. Each has its stem toward the outer ring and its curve facing inward, which reverses their usual orientation. Two Gathering signs, drawn heavier and rougher, sit at the south and northeast with their arrowheads toward the ring and their forks toward the center. Three small sub-seals sit inside the inner ring. The one at the north-northeast holds a small, neat fire sigil, and its ring is open with a gap at the lower left. The one at the southeast holds a fire sigil, and its ring is closed. The one at the west-southwest holds a Stability and Level Planes sign at its center, and its ring is closed. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on solid matter such as soil, sand and stone. Its small size gives a modest intensity. The two Gathering signs draw material in from the surroundings for the spell to use. The four Dispersion signs make the magic pour outward rather than beam in one direction. They are drawn with their curves facing inward, a reversed orientation whose difference in effect is unclear, so they are read as spreading the effect around the seal. Gathering pulls material in and Dispersion pours magic out, so the two act on different things and do not contradict each other. The signs are spaced evenly, so no direction is favored. The closed fire sub-seal adds heat. The Stability and Level Planes sub-seal holds the target balanced in a flat plane. The open fire sub-seal contributes nothing until it is closed. The modifiers amount to three kinds alongside a second element, so the seal is not unstable. However, the rough linework and uneven rings weaken the spell and shorten how long it lasts.
effect: Draws loose soil and stone in from around the seal and pours it back out in all directions as a thin, roughly level layer that is gently warmed. The spread is patchy, the warmth is uneven, and the effect fades sooner than a cleanly drawn seal would. The unfinished second fire component adds no extra heat.

name: s42_00032.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background. The main ring is closed but drawn roughly and noticeably out of round, with flattened, lumpy sides. A small Expansion sign sits upright at the center, its nested corner brackets pointing outward. It has no element sigil. Two small Coil signs sit near the ring at the east-northeast and west-southwest, each rotated at an angle. Four Binding signs sit about two thirds of the way out, at the northwest, north-northeast, southeast and south-southwest, each with the top of its arcs toward the center. The signs are evenly balanced around the ring. Three smaller rings sit outside the main ring, each joined to it by a short line. The ring at the southeast is closed and neatly drawn, with an earth sigil at its center. The ring at the west-southwest is closed and slightly rough, with a fire sigil. The ring at the north-northeast holds a fire sigil but has a gap, so that ring is open. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The main seal has no sigil, so its elements come from the attached sub-seals. The closed earth sub-seal makes the spell act on solid matter such as stone, wood and soil. The closed fire sub-seal adds heat. The fire sub-seal at the north-northeast has an open ring and contributes nothing. At the center, upright Expansion with its corners outward makes the target grow in size. Coil softens physical matter, and paired with the heat from the fire sub-seal, the material becomes pliable enough to swell. Binding halts the target's movement and binds its material together, so the enlarged mass holds as a single unit instead of spreading apart. That makes three kinds of modifier: growth, softening and binding. They work toward the same goal without contradiction, and they are evenly balanced, so no direction is favored. The rough linework and the out-of-round main ring weaken the spell and shorten its life. They also risk the effect only flickering on.
effect: Warms and softens solid matter such as stone, wood or soil and makes it swell larger while holding it together as one mass. The growth comes out modest and uneven, with the heat from only one of its two sources taking part. It may sputter at first and fades back quickly.

name: s42_00033.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background. The main ring is closed and neatly drawn. A Collection sign sits upright at the center in place of a sigil, moderately small relative to the ring. Two Link signs sit just inside the ring, one at the west-northwest and one at the east-southeast, facing each other across the seal. Eight Purification signs surround the center. Two sit near the ring at the northeast and southwest. The other six form an evenly spaced inner circle about halfway out, at the west, north-northwest, northeast, east, south-southeast and southwest. The inner northeast one is drawn heavier and a little rougher than the rest. Two small sub-seals are joined to the main ring by short lines from outside. The one at the northeast is closed and holds a fire sigil. The one at the southwest is open, with a gap in its lower right, and holds an earth sigil. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The main ring has no element sigil. Collection takes the center as the core, so the spell gathers material located above and around the seal for its own use. The eight Purification signs separate waste from water. Their number and even spread make the cleansing thorough and balanced on all sides, and the one slightly rough sign only weakens its own share a little. The two opposed Link signs identify pieces that came from the same source and link them, so the separated waste holds together as connected matter instead of scattering. The closed fire sub-seal adds heat to the gathered material. The earth sub-seal's ring is open, so it contributes nothing. That leaves three related kinds of modifier in the main seal, gathering, purifying and linking, with heat as an added element. None of them contradict one another, and the seal is neatly drawn and balanced, so it holds steady.
effect: Draws in water from above and around the seal and thoroughly strips the waste out of it, binding that waste into connected clumps of matter from the same source so it can be removed together, while the cleaned water is gently warmed. The attached earth portion stays inert and adds nothing.

name: s42_00034.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed. The ring is drawn roughly and is noticeably out of round, with lumpy, flattened stretches along its edge. A water sigil, an S-curve flanked by two teardrops, sits upright at the center. It is fairly large relative to the ring and a little roughly drawn. Four Strengthening signs, each a triangle crossed by a bar, surround it. A large, heavily drawn pair sits at the north-northeast and south-southwest, with the top of each glyph turned toward the center. A smaller pair sits at the east and west, close to the ring, with the top of each glyph turned toward the ring. All four signs are slightly rough. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil sets the element, so the spell manipulates, gathers or creates water. Its large size relative to the ring points to a fairly strong effect. Strengthening makes its target stronger, harder and more durable, so the water is firmed and made resilient rather than left loose. There are no directional signs and the four signs are balanced around the ring, so the effect stays at the seal instead of being pushed outward. Strengthening has never been confirmed as an invertible sign, so the two pairs facing opposite ways are read as all reinforcing rather than cancelling. The larger, heavier inward-facing pair carries most of the effect, and the smaller outward-facing pair adds less, which makes the reinforcement uneven. Only one kind of modifier is present, so the seal is not contradictory. However, the rough linework weakens and shortens the spell, and the badly out-of-round ring makes the effect fleeting and may keep it from activating at all.
effect: Draws a fairly strong mass of water over the seal and firms it into a dense, resilient body that holds together more tightly than ordinary water. The firming is uneven, stronger along one diagonal than the other. The whole effect flickers and lasts only a moment before the water slackens and spills away, if it takes hold at all.

name: s42_00035.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background, drawn neatly. The ring is open, with a gap at the north-northwest just left of the north sign. Two small glyphs share the center, each small relative to the ring. On the left is an Orb sign, a circle crossed by a vertical line, with a small Collection sign attached on top. On the right is a light sigil, a diamond set inside a square with four short spokes. Four Immobility signs sit near the ring at the north, south, west-northwest and east-southeast. Each has its bar toward the ring and its paired curves toward the center, so all four face the same way. An Entwining sign sits at the northeast, angled. At the southwest is another Entwining sign with a small earth sigil attached at its base, drawn a little rougher than the rest. The signs are spread evenly around the ring.
justification: The light sigil sets the element, and its small size gives a modest intensity. Orb shares the center as a second core. It defines a spherical space above the seal where the spell's material collects. The Collection attached to it draws material from around the seal into that space, so the light is pooled into a sphere rather than spreading. Immobility makes the target hold its shape and stay fixed relative to the seal. Four evenly placed, matching Immobility signs hold the sphere steady on all sides. Entwining makes the effect wrap itself around other objects. The southwest Entwining carries a small earth sigil, so on that side the wrapping is tied to solid matter such as stone or soil. Its rougher drawing makes it slightly weaker than the northeast one. These three kinds of modifier work together: collecting into a sphere, fixing it in place, and wrapping. None directly contradicts another, so the seal is not unstable. While the ring is open, the seal does not activate.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it gathers light into a modest glowing sphere that hangs fixed above the seal and keeps its shape. Strands of that light wind around nearby objects, clinging most firmly to stone or soil on the southwest side but a little more loosely there than on the northeast. The glow gradually dims over time.

name: s42_00040.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed and neatly drawn. No element sigil is present. A Coil sign, two crossing arcs, stands upright at the center and reaches a little under half the ring's radius. Seven signs surround it. A Sights Set sign sits near the ring at the northeast, its diamond end toward the center and its arrow pointing outward to the northeast. An inverted Rain sign, slightly rough, sits near the ring at the north-northwest. A Selection sign, a square grid crossed by lines, sits at the west-northwest. A Glaives sign at the west-southwest lies on its side, prongs toward the ring and stem toward the center. A Concealment sign, an eight-armed star with eye marks, sits at the south. A small Crosshair sign sits at the east-southeast, and a Stability and Level Planes sign, drawn as wavy parallel strokes, sits at the east-northeast. The Sights Set strokes are also slightly rough. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, Coil takes the center and sets the core behavior: softening solid physical matter, with no effect on liquids or gases. Its fairly large size relative to the ring gives it real strength. Sights Set aims the effect, and its arrow points northeast, while Crosshair aims the effect at whatever its short ends face, here toward the east-southeast. Inverted Rain creates an area that pushes material away. Glaives set how deeply magic embeds in flesh, Selection confines the effect to the object the seal is drawn on, Stability and Level Planes hold a target balanced in a plane, and Concealment hides it. This stacks far more than three unrelated kinds of modifier, and several contradict each other directly. Selection confines the effect while Sights Set and Crosshair send it outward, and inverted Rain pushes matter away while Glaives drive the effect inward. Coil dominates as the core, with Sights Set setting a northeast aim and Concealment the strongest secondary sign. The other modifiers pull against them, so the result is likely unstable, and the rough Rain and Sights Set signs weaken those parts further.
effect: Softens solid matter in a wavering burst aimed toward the northeast, partly blurring the softened area from sight. The effect lurches unevenly between pressing into the material and pushing it away, and sometimes stays on the marked object instead of reaching outward. It tends to collapse early.

name: s42_00041.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A light sigil, a diamond set inside a square with four short spokes, sits upright at the center and is large relative to the ring, reaching about half the radius. Its lines are slightly rough. Five Pulling signs surround it, each with its arrowhead pointing inward toward the center. Four sit close to the ring at the south-southwest, west-northwest, north-northeast and east-southeast, roughly a quarter turn apart. A fifth, drawn heavier, sits closer to the center at the west. The west-northwest one is a little rough. Three Expansion signs, each made of nested corner brackets with the corners pointing outward, sit near the ring at the north-northwest, east-northeast and south-southeast. The east-northeast one is drawn noticeably bolder than the others. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil makes this a light spell, and its large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect. Pulling is directional, and with the arrows pointing inward it draws its target toward the seal. Because the signs are spread around the ring, the draw comes from all sides. The extra Pulling sign at the west adds a little more pull from that side. Expansion is semi-directional, and with its corners pointing outward in its normal orientation, it makes its target grow. Together the seal gathers light in toward itself and enlarges it. There are only two kinds of modifier, and they work together, so the spell is not unstable. The slightly rough sigil makes the light a little less steady than a cleanly drawn one would be.
effect: Draws surrounding light in toward the seal from every side, slightly more strongly from the west, and swells it into a large, bright glow that grows as it gathers. The glow wavers a little at its edges and gradually dims over time.

name: s42_00042.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, drawn as two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A Concealment sign sits upright at the center, about half the inner ring's radius: an eight-armed star with an eye mark at the end of each of its north, east, south and west arms. There is no element sigil. Three Reflection signs, each an hourglass of two triangles meeting at a point, sit in the band between the two rings. One is at the north, slightly east of true north, one at the southeast, and one at the west-southwest. All three are roughly evenly spaced and oriented with their tops toward the center. The north sign is cleanly drawn, while the southeast and west-southwest signs are slightly rough. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the Concealment sign at the center is the core of the seal and sets its purpose, which is hiding a target. Its large size relative to the ring makes that concealment strong. The Reflection signs target a reflected image found on the object the seal is drawn on, so the concealment works through the reflections on that surface rather than through shadow. The three signs are evenly spaced around the band, so no direction is favored and the effect covers the object uniformly. The second ring strengthens the core spell. No Projection sign is present, so the reflected image stays on the object's surface instead of being cast outward. The two slightly rough Reflection signs make the reflective part a little weaker and less even on those sides. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they work together without contradiction.
effect: Strongly hides the object the seal is drawn on by covering its surface with the reflections it catches of its surroundings, so it blends in like a mirror. The disguise is slightly patchy toward the southeast and west-southwest, where the reflected image is a little less convincing.

name: s42_00043.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is neatly drawn but open, with a wide gap at the south-southwest between its lower end and its left end. There is no element sigil. An Entwining sign sits upright at the center, drawn boldly and moderate in size relative to the ring. Four small Crosshair signs sit about three quarters of the way to the ring at the northwest, northeast, southeast and southwest points. Each is rotated so its arms form an X, with its top facing the ring. A single Coil sign, two crossing curved strokes, sits near the ring at the north. Because of the lone Coil, the signs lean toward the north. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the Entwining sign at the center is the core of the seal. It makes the object the seal is drawn on wrap or twine itself around other objects, and its moderate size gives the effect moderate strength. Crosshair makes a seal's effect target whatever its short ends point at. With all four facing outward at the diagonals, the entwining is aimed at targets in four directions: northwest, northeast, southeast and southwest. Coil softens physical matter and has no effect on liquids or gases. It is likely non-directional, so its place at the north adds no direction of its own, but it makes the material supple enough to wrap. Being the only sign there, it tilts the seal's emphasis slightly northward. The seal uses only two kinds of modifier around its core, and they do not contradict each other, so it should hold steady. Because the ring is open, it will not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: Once the ring is closed, the object the seal is drawn on turns soft and supple and twines itself around solid targets lying along the northwest, northeast, southeast and southwest diagonals from the seal. It grips each target with moderate strength and has no hold on liquids or gases.

name: s42_00045.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A small Concealment sign, an eight-armed star with eye marks on its arms, sits at the center in place of a sigil and spans about a quarter of the ring's radius. Six Crushing signs surround it. Four are drawn in the normal orientation, with their points toward the center: one at the north near the ring, drawn heavier and a little rough, one at the north-northeast, one at the south-southeast near the ring, and one at the south-southwest, which is also slightly rough. Two are inverted, with their points toward the ring: one at the northwest and one at the southeast. No element sigil is present. The signs are spread evenly around the seal.
justification: No element sigil is present, so the Concealment sign at the center is the core of the spell and hides the target. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Crushing is semi-directional, so its placement does not steer the spell, but its orientation reverses its effect. The four normal Crushing signs break solid matter into smaller and smaller pieces. The two inverted ones do the opposite and pull crushed material back into its original form. These signs directly contradict each other. The four normal signs outnumber the two inverted ones, so crushing dominates while the inverted pair keeps fighting it, and the result is likely unstable. Because the signs are balanced around the ring, neither effect is pushed toward one side. The two slightly rough Crushing signs further weaken the breaking effect.
effect: Hides the target in a modest shroud of concealment while grinding it into fragments that keep partly reassembling, so the target crumbles and flickers back together unevenly. The concealment wavers as the pieces shift, and the spell gives out early before the target is either fully broken or fully restored.

name: s42_00046.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background. The main ring is neatly drawn but open, with a wide gap across the top between the north-northwest and the north. A light sigil, a diamond set inside a square with four short spokes, sits upright at the center and is fairly small relative to the ring. Four Diamond signs sit just inside the ring at the south-southwest, west-northwest, north-northeast and east-southeast, each turned at a slight angle. The west-northwest one is a little rougher than the others. A single Glaives sign, a small trident shape, sits near the ring at the east-northeast, angled with its prongs toward the lower right. A closed sub-seal sits inside the main ring at the north-northwest, just below the gap. It is slightly rough and holds a small wind sigil at its center. The signs are unevenly spread, with more weight toward the east-northeast. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil makes this a light spell, and its modest size relative to the ring gives a moderate intensity. Light produced this way fades over time. The Diamond signs make the spell act only on objects within a container the seal is drawn on, without affecting the container itself. Four of them around the ring reinforce that confinement, and the slightly rough one weakens it a little on the west-northwest side. Glaives set how deeply magic embeds itself into flesh, so the light sinks into living matter inside the container instead of resting on its surface. A single Glaives sign gives only a shallow depth. Diamond and Glaives are not directional, so the lean toward the east-northeast does not send the effect in any direction. It only makes the effect a little stronger on that side. The closed wind sub-seal adds a small movement of air. Its small size and rough linework keep that movement faint and brief. The seal has three kinds of modifier and none of them contradict each other. The main ring is open, so nothing activates until it is closed.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it fills only the contents of the vessel the seal is drawn on with a moderate light, leaving the vessel itself untouched. The light sinks shallowly into any living flesh inside, glowing slightly stronger toward the east-northeast and a little weaker toward the west-northwest. A faint, brief stir of air moves through the contents with it, and the light gradually dims over time.

name: s42_00047.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but drawn roughly and noticeably out of round, bulging into a soft triangular shape. Two small sigils sit side by side at the center, each small relative to the ring: a light sigil on the left and a wind sigil on the right, both drawn roughly. Three inverted Crushing signs sit near the ring, evenly spaced: one at the north, one at the east-southeast and one at the west-southwest. All three are drawn roughly, the east-southeast one slightly less so. No other signs are present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil sets the creation and manipulation of light, and the wind sigil sets the movement of air. Both are small relative to the ring, so the intensity is low. Crushing is semi-directional, so its position does not steer the spell, but inverting it reverses its effect. Instead of breaking material into smaller pieces, inverted Crushing pulls broken or scattered material back into its original form, and only temporarily. The three signs are evenly spaced, so the effect favors no direction. Wind supplies the motion that carries scattered material back together, and light makes the result glow. Only one kind of modifier is present and it does not conflict with either sigil, so the seal is not unstable. However, the rough linework and the poorly rounded ring make the spell weak and fleeting, and it may fail to activate at all.
effect: Draws scattered dust and fragments on a faint, uneven draft back toward the shape they came from, lighting the gathering pieces with a dim, flickering glow. The reformed shape wavers and falls back apart almost at once, and the spell may sputter out before it takes hold.

name: s42_00048.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The outer ring is closed but a little rough and slightly out of round, and a second closed ring sits just inside it. A small Windows sign, a circle lined with short slanted markings, sits at the center in place of a sigil. It is small relative to the ring. Four Cooling signs sit about halfway between the center and the inner ring, at the north, east, south and west points. Each is a single line flanked by two pairs of dots, with its top toward the ring. Several glyphs are drawn somewhat roughly. There is no element sigil, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the Windows sign at the center serves as the core of the seal. It links two spaces that are not physically connected, much like a portal. Its small size gives only a narrow, modest connection. The four Cooling signs make the spell cool things down. They are evenly spaced around the center, so the chill spreads evenly rather than favoring one side. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they do not contradict each other. Without an element sigil, the cooling is not tied to fire, water, earth or wind and acts on whatever lies in the linked space. The second ring adds strength to the core spell. Even so, the rough linework and the slightly out-of-round outer ring make the effect weaker and fleeting.
effect: Opens a small, faint connection between the seal and another space and lets a mild, even chill pass through it, cooling whatever lies on either side. The link and the cold both waver and fade quickly instead of holding steady.

name: s42_00050.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background, drawn as two concentric rings. The outer ring is open, with a wide gap at the north-northwest. The inner ring also appears to be open, with a gap at the east-northeast. A water sigil sits upright at the center. It is fairly large relative to the ring, at a little under half its radius. Nine Holding signs, each a pair of facing curves with dots, surround it, all with their tops toward the ring. Three larger ones sit inside the inner ring at the east, south-southwest and northwest. Six smaller ones sit in the band between the rings at the north, east-northeast, east-southeast, south, southwest and west-northwest. Most of the linework is neat. The Holding signs at the northwest, west-northwest, east-southeast and southwest are a little rough. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell, and its fairly large size relative to the ring gives a solid, moderately strong intensity. Holding is non-directional. It keeps the target in the shape the seal defines while still letting it move. Nine Holding signs spread evenly over both the inner circle and the outer band give a firm, balanced hold with no side favored and no direction set. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing contradicts. The second ring strengthens the core effect. The four slightly rough Holding signs make the hold a little weaker and less steady on those sides. The seal will not activate until both gaps are closed.
effect: Once the rings are closed, it gathers water into a firm round mass that keeps its rounded shape even as it is moved about. The water wobbles a little and seeps at the edges where the hold is weaker.

name: s42_00052.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A fire sigil sits upright at the center and is small relative to the ring, about a quarter of its radius. Five small Crosshair signs surround it. Four sit close to the ring at the northwest, northeast, southeast and southwest, and a fifth sits a little farther in at the west. Each is rotated so its top faces the ring. The northeast Crosshair is drawn slightly rougher than the others. No other signs are present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil makes this a fire spell, and its small size relative to the ring gives it a modest intensity. Crosshair makes a seal's effect target whatever its short ends point at. With five Crosshairs facing outward, the heat is aimed at five separate points around the seal rather than spreading as a general blaze. The signs are spread roughly evenly, so no single direction is favored overall. The slightly rough northeast sign makes the heat aimed that way a little weaker and less steady than the others. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing conflicts.
effect: Sends modest bursts of heat or small flames outward from the seal to five separate points around it, aimed northwest, northeast, southeast, southwest and west. The northeast point receives a slightly weaker, less steady flame than the rest.

name: s42_00053.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. Two light sigils sit side by side near the center, each a diamond set inside a square with four short spokes. The left one is larger, about a third of the inner radius, and neatly drawn. The right one is smaller and slightly rougher. Six Detection signs sit in the band between the rings, each three short parallel strokes of stepped length. They are at the south-southwest, west, north-northwest, northeast, east and south-southeast, spaced evenly. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The two light sigils make this a light spell that creates and shapes light, which naturally diminishes over time. The larger, neat sigil gives a moderate, steady light. The smaller, slightly rough one adds a dimmer light that is a little less stable and shorter lived. The second ring adds further effects and strength to the core spell. Detection's exact function is not fully known, but its name means sensation, and it supports spells that light the way in response to presence. Here it would make the light react to things sensed nearby. The six Detection signs are evenly spaced and balanced, so no direction is favored and sensing covers all sides of the seal. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing conflicts.
effect: Produces two lights, one moderate and steady, the other dimmer and faintly flickering, that respond to presences sensed on any side of the seal and brighten as something draws near. Both lights gradually dim over time, the smaller one fading first.

name: s42_00054.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn neatly in black on a white background, ring closed. A wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes on either side, sits upright at the center and is fairly large relative to the ring. Seven Billow signs, each a four-lobed clover shape, surround it. Three larger ones sit close to the ring at the west-northwest, east-northeast and south. Four smaller ones sit about halfway between the center and the ring at the northeast, southeast, southwest and northwest. No other signs are present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil makes this a wind spell, which moves and manipulates air but does not create it. Its fairly large size relative to the ring gives a fairly strong effect. Billow turns available material into a fluffy cloud. It is non-directional, so the different orientations of the inner and outer signs do not change its behavior. All seven modifiers are the same sign, so nothing contradicts. They are spread evenly around the seal, so no direction is favored. With no Collection or directional signs, the spell works on the air already around the seal and does not send it anywhere in particular. The wind sigil stirs the surrounding air, and the many Billow signs convert it into cloud. The neat drawing and closed ring let the spell activate and hold steady.
effect: Stirs the surrounding air with fairly strong force and gathers it into soft, fluffy clouds that billow up evenly on all sides of the seal without drifting in any set direction.

name: s42_00056.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed but noticeably lumpy and out of round. Two glyphs sit side by side at the center, both small relative to the ring: a wind sigil on the left and an earth sigil on the right. Six Expansion signs, each made of nested corner brackets, are spread around the ring at roughly three quarters of the way out from the center. Four of them sit at the northeast, south-southeast, west and southwest with their corners pointing outward. Two sit at the north and east with their corners pointing inward, so they are inverted. The southwest Expansion sign is drawn larger than the others. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil moves and manipulates air, and the earth sigil manipulates solid matter such as stone, sand and soil, so the spell acts on both. Their small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Expansion is semi-directional. Its placement does not steer the spell, but its orientation matters: corners outward make the target grow, and corners inward make it shrink. Here four outward signs, one of them enlarged, directly contradict two inverted ones. Growth dominates because it has more signs and the largest one, while the inverted pair keeps pulling against it. The result is likely unstable. The signs are spread evenly, so the effect favors no direction. The ring is closed, so the seal activates, but its uneven roundness makes the effect fleeting.
effect: Makes nearby stone or soil and the air moving around it swell in size, but the growth surges and falls back unevenly, wavering between enlarging and shrinking. It settles into only a modest enlargement that fades quickly.

name: s42_00057.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is neatly drawn but open, with a wide gap at the bottom between the south-southwest and south-southeast. A wind sigil sits at the center: an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes on either side, drawn fairly large, a little under half the ring's radius. Four Envelopment signs, each a slanted stroke with short hooks at both ends, sit close to the ring at the north-northwest, east-northeast, south-southeast and west-southwest. The north-northwest and south-southeast signs stand with their tops toward the ring, the east-northeast one is nearly upright, and the west-southwest one is turned to lie closer to horizontal. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil makes this a wind spell, which moves and manipulates existing air rather than creating it. Its fairly large size relative to the ring gives a solid, fairly strong intensity. Envelopment makes a spell's effect surround and wrap around its target instead of acting on a single point or projecting outward. The four Envelopment signs are spread evenly around the ring, so the wrapping is balanced on all sides and no side is favored. There are no directional signs, so the moving air is not sent anywhere and stays around the target. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing conflicts. The ring is open, so the seal will not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it wraps the object it is drawn on in a fairly strong, steady current of moving air that flows evenly around it on all sides. The air stays close around the object instead of blowing away in any direction.

name: s42_00058.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background. The main ring is closed but drawn roughly and noticeably out of round, bulging into a lumpy, almost triangular shape. The center is empty. Four small, roughly drawn glyphs sit about two thirds of the way out from the center. Inverted Rain signs, each a square with spiked edges flipped inside-out, sit at the west, north and east. At the south is a broken version of the same glyph with its left part missing. Three smaller sub-seals sit outside the main ring, each joined to it by a short line. The one at the south-southeast has its ring closed and holds a neatly drawn fire sigil. The one at the west has its ring open, with a gap at the lower left, and holds a neatly drawn wind sigil. The one at the northeast has its ring closed and holds a neatly drawn Detection sign. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The main seal has no sigil of its own. Its element comes from the closed fire sub-seal, so the spell acts on flame and heat. The fire sigil fills nearly half of that small sub-ring, which would give a moderate intensity, but feeding it through a rough main seal weakens it. Rain is semi-directional, and inverting it reverses its effect: instead of bringing its material down, it creates an area where that material cannot exist or is pushed away. The three intact inverted Rain signs, together with the southern glyph, are balanced around the ring, so the warding area is centered on the seal with no favored direction. The southern glyph matches no sign exactly. Its closest match is Rain with its left half missing, so reading it as a partial inverted Rain is a guess. Read that way, it adds only a weakened push on that side. The Detection sub-seal is closed, so it contributes. Its function is unclear, but it appears to make the spell sense presences, so the warding reacts to what comes near. The wind sub-seal's ring is open, so it adds nothing. The rough linework and the out-of-round main ring make the effect weak and fleeting, and it may fail to hold at all.
effect: Creates a faint, flickering zone around the seal that pushes flame and heat away from it, reacting as something approaches. The zone is noticeably thinner on its southern side. No wind joins the effect, and the barrier wavers and collapses after only a short time.

name: s42_00059.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, neatly drawn. The ring is open, with a gap at the top just east of north. A light sigil sits at the center, drawn as a diamond inside a square with four short spokes, at a moderate size relative to the ring. Eight Strengthening signs, each a triangle crossed by a bar, are spaced evenly around it. Four sit at the north, east, south and west points, a little closer to the center. The other four sit at the northeast, southeast, southwest and northwest points, slightly farther out toward the ring. Every Strengthening sign is turned so its apex points roughly toward the center. No other signs are present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil makes this a light spell, and its moderate size relative to the ring gives a moderate intensity. Light made by this sigil normally diminishes over time. Strengthening makes its target stronger, harder and more durable. Applied here, the eight signs reinforce the light so it holds its strength rather than fading quickly. All eight face the same way relative to the center and are evenly spaced. As a result, none is inverted against the others, no side is favored, and no direction is set for the light. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing conflicts. The neat linework supports a steady effect, but the seal will not activate until the gap in the ring is closed.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it produces a steady glow of moderate brightness that spreads evenly from the seal in all directions. The light is reinforced, so it holds its strength far longer than ordinary magical light before it slowly dims.

name: s42_00060.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A water sigil, an S-curve flanked by two teardrops, sits upright at the center at moderate size relative to the ring. A Concealment sign, an eight-armed star with eye marks on four of its arms, sits at the south about halfway to the ring, drawn upside down and slightly rough. A Binding sign, two stacked arcs, sits near the ring at the north with its arcs bowing toward the ring. Two small Purification signs sit on the western side, one at the northwest and one near the ring at the west-southwest. The east side holds no signs, so the layout leans west. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Purification separates waste from water, which fits the water sigil directly. Binding halts the water's movement and makes it act as a single unit. Concealment hides its target. Its star is nearly radially symmetric, so drawing it upside down most likely does not reverse it, and its slightly rough lines make the hiding weaker. Purification is asymmetric and its behavior is less predictable, and both copies sit on the western side. With no directional signs, this placement does not send the spell west, but the cleansing is likely uneven and strongest on that side. The seal uses three kinds of modifier that work together without contradiction.
effect: Cleanses a moderate amount of water of its waste and holds it together as a single still mass while hiding it from view. The cleansing works unevenly and is strongest on its western side. The concealment is patchy, so the water flickers partly into sight at times.

name: s42_00061.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed and neatly round. A small earth sigil sits upright at the center. Six signs sit near the ring. A Rain sign at the east-southeast is drawn the normal way. A second Rain sign at the west is flipped inside-out, so it is inverted. A Strengthening sign at the north-northwest is tilted, with its apex angled away from the center. A Repetition sign, small and not at the center, sits at the north-northeast, slightly rotated. An Aeriforms Defined sign of three strokes sits at the east-northeast, angled toward the center. A Launch sign at the south-southwest opens toward the center, with its point toward the ring. The Launch and Strengthening signs are drawn with heavier strokes than the rest, and the Launch strokes are slightly wavy. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell moves existing solid matter such as soil and stone. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Launch is the only directional sign. It sends the material in a powerful but short-lived burst toward where it points, the south-southwest. The two Rain signs directly contradict each other. The normal one summons material down from above, while the inverted one makes an area where that material is pushed away, so the two largely cancel and leave material falling unevenly. Strengthening makes the moved earth harder and more durable. Repetition keeps resetting the affected material to its first state, so the burst tends to snap back and recur. Aeriforms Defined modifies air and has little to act on in an earth spell. With contradicting Rain signs and more than three unrelated kinds of modifier stacked together, the earth sigil and Launch dominate, Strengthening is secondary, and the result is likely unstable.
effect: Hurls a modest, short-lived burst of hardened soil and stone toward the south-southwest, while loose grit patters down unevenly and is shoved back on the western side. The burst sputters, snaps back toward its starting state and fires again in erratic pulses, then collapses well before it settles into any lasting shape.

name: s42_00063.png
description: A fully visible seal on a white background. The ring is closed, neatly drawn and close to round. A large earth sigil sits at the center, reaching nearly half the ring's radius. A Link sign sits at the west, a little over halfway out, rotated with its top toward the ring. An Entwining sign sits near the ring at the south, with its top toward the ring. A small Piercing sign sits at the southeast, about halfway out, angled along the radius. A Glaives sign sits at the east-southeast, about three quarters out, with its prongs pointing inward toward the center. A single Regions sign sits at the northeast with its point toward the center. The signs are spread unevenly and cluster toward the southeast. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell manipulates existing solid matter such as stone and soil rather than creating it. Its large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect. A single Piercing sign makes the material manifest as one projectile or offensive form. Glaives set how deeply magic embeds into flesh, and here they sit inside the ring with their prongs turned inward. The inward-pointing Regions sign confines the manifestation to the space within the ring. Entwining makes the material wrap around other objects, and Link ties together pieces that came from the same source. That is five unrelated kinds of modifier on one seal. The earth sigil with Piercing and Glaives dominates, producing a deep-biting earthen spike, and Regions holds it inside the ring. Entwining and Link pull the material in other directions, so the result is likely unstable. The clustering toward the southeast adds no drive, because no sign there pushes the effect outward.
effect: Draws stone or soil within the seal's bounds into a single heavy spike made to bite deep into flesh. The spike keeps trying to coil around nearby objects and to drag toward other fragments of the same stone, so it twists and reshapes unevenly. It never settles into a steady form and breaks apart early.

name: s42_00065.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background. The main ring is open, with a gap at the top near the north, and is drawn a little roughly. Two glyphs share the center, both small relative to the ring: an Immobility sign on the left and a neatly drawn light sigil on the right. Seven Diamond signs are spread evenly around them at about two thirds of the way to the ring, at the north, north-northeast, east-northeast, east-southeast, south-southeast, west-southwest and west-northwest. Each is rotated differently, and several, notably those at the west-northwest and east-northeast, are drawn heavier and rougher than the rest. Three smaller rings are attached outside the main ring by short lines. The ring at the west-northwest is closed and holds a Binding sign. The ring at the northeast is open and holds an earth sigil. The ring at the south is also open, with a gap on its left side, and holds another earth sigil. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and shapes light. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity, and the light diminishes over time. Immobility shares the center and makes the effect immovable in relation to the seal, holding its shape as if frozen. Diamond makes a spell affect only what sits inside the container it is drawn on, not the container itself. The seven Diamond signs are balanced around the ring and set no direction, so the effect fills that interior evenly. The closed Binding sub-seal joins the held light into a single unit. Both earth sub-seals have open rings, so they contribute nothing. Only three kinds of modifier are present, and they agree with one another. The seal will not activate while the main ring is open. Its rough linework and the rough Diamond signs would make the effect weaker and shorter-lived than a clean drawing would.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it fills the inside of the container it is drawn on with a modest light that stays fixed in place as one solid, unmoving glow, leaving the container itself unlit. The light is faint and uneven, dims steadily, and gives out sooner than a cleanly drawn seal would, while the two attached earth sub-seals add nothing as long as their rings stay open.

name: s42_00066.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, neatly drawn. The ring is open, with a gap at the top between the north and north-northeast. A fire sigil sits upright at the center, about a third of the ring's radius in size. Four Orb signs, each a small circle crossed by a diagonal line, sit near the ring at the east, southwest, north-northwest and west-southwest. The west-southwest one sits a little closer to the center than the others. The east Orb is drawn with heavier, slightly rough strokes, while the other three are clean. Three of the four signs sit on the western half, so the arrangement leans toward the west-southwest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil makes this a fire spell, and its moderate size relative to the ring gives a moderate intensity. Orb is a non-directional sign that defines a spherical space above the seal, where the material the spell controls collects. That material fills the space from the bottom up and only enters if it is added directly. All four modifiers are the same sign, so nothing contradicts. Orb has no direction of its own, but the signs are crowded onto the western side, so the sphere is likely weighted toward the west-southwest instead of centered. The slightly rough east Orb makes that side of the space weaker. The seal does not activate while the ring is open.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it forms an invisible sphere above the seal that holds fire of moderate strength. Flames fed directly into it settle at the bottom and fill the sphere upward, the way liquid fills a cup. The sphere sits lopsided toward the west-southwest, and its eastern side holds less firmly than the rest.

name: s42_00067.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A fire sigil sits upright at the center and is fairly large, reaching about half the ring's radius. Six Windows signs, each a small ring lined with short slanted hatch marks, are spaced evenly about halfway between the center and the ring, at the north, northeast, east-southeast, south-southeast, southwest and west-northwest. The east-southeast Windows sign is drawn with a noticeably heavier, darker stroke than the others, and the north one is slightly rougher. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and manipulates flame and heat. Its large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect. Windows connects two spaces that are not physically joined, letting magic pass through the seal from one place to another. Here it is drawn as six separate small rings rather than one band lining the seal, so it reads as six distinct openings rather than a single portal. The six signs are evenly balanced, so no direction is favored. No Doorways sigil is present to fix where the openings lead. Only one kind of modifier is used alongside the sigil, so nothing conflicts. The slight roughness of the north sign and the heavier east-southeast sign make those two openings a little less even than the rest.
effect: Produces strong flames that pass through six small linked openings around the seal and emerge somewhere else, carrying fire and heat to a separate location without crossing the space between. The flow is steady and even overall, with one or two of the openings flickering slightly less smoothly than the others.

name: s42_00069.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background, drawn neatly. The ring is open, with a wide gap on the west side running from about west-northwest down to southwest. A fire sigil sits upright at the center and is modest in size relative to the ring. Four Refuse signs sit about halfway out. Those at the north, east and west have their diamond ends toward the center and their crossed legs toward the ring. The one at the south-southwest is reversed, with its diamond toward the ring and its legs toward the center. Four Crushing signs sit farther out near the ring. The ones at the northwest and south-southeast are drawn normally, and the northwest one is drawn larger and heavier than the others. The ones at the east-northeast and west-southwest are inverted, and the west-southwest one sits beside the gap in the ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil makes this a fire spell, and its modest size gives a moderate intensity. Refuse is directional and draws unwanted material toward where it points. Three Refuse signs point inward, so they pull waste in from the north, east and west toward the center. The reversed one at the south-southwest points outward and lets some of that material be pushed back out on that side. Crushing is semi-directional. The two normal Crushing signs break material into smaller and smaller pieces, while the two inverted ones reverse that and pull crushed material back into its original form. These directly contradict each other. The larger normal sign at the northwest gives breaking a slight edge, so fire and the inward Refuse signs dominate, but the clash between crushing and reforming makes the result likely unstable. The seal will not activate until the ring is closed.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it draws waste in from the north, east and west toward the center of the seal and burns it with moderate heat, while part of the gathered refuse spills back out to the south-southwest. The waste is broken apart and pulled back together by turns, so it crumbles unevenly into charred fragments, and the flame flickers and gives out early.

name: s42_00070.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A Levitation sign sits upright at the center in place of a sigil, its arrow pointing north, at moderate size relative to the ring. There is no element sigil. Eight Regions signs surround it. Three sit just inside the ring at the north, east-southeast and west-southwest, all with their points facing outward toward the ring. Three more sit about halfway out at the north-northwest, east-northeast and west-southwest, also pointing outward. Two Regions signs sit at the south, one near the ring and one about halfway in, both pointing inward toward the center, that is, northward. The inner southern one is drawn larger and heavier than the others. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the Levitation sign at the center acts as the core. It floats objects into the air, and as a directional sign its arrow sets the direction to north. Its moderate length gives a modest reach, carrying capacity and speed. Six of the Regions signs point outward, so the magic manifests outside the ring and not within its bounds. The two southern Regions signs point inward, but because they sit at the south, they point north, the same way as the outward sign at the north and the Levitation arrow. Read together, they act as a northward bias rather than a contradiction, so the outside effect is pushed toward the north. The larger southern sign strengthens that pull. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they agree on direction, so the seal holds steady.
effect: Lifts objects lying around the outside of the seal into the air and carries them steadily northward, leaving anything within the ring untouched. The lift is modest, suited to light objects over a short distance.

name: s42_00072.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed. The ring is a little rough and noticeably out of round, with a lumpy outline. A neatly drawn earth sigil sits upright at the center, moderate in size at a little under half the ring's radius. Three neatly drawn Dispersion signs sit close to the ring at the east-southeast, southwest and north-northwest. Each has its stem pointing toward the center and its curve facing outward toward the ring. The three signs are spaced roughly evenly around the seal. No other signs are present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell manipulates existing solid matter such as soil, sand and stone rather than creating it. Its moderate size relative to the ring gives a moderate intensity. Dispersion makes a seal's magic pour or leak outward instead of beaming it in one direction. All three signs are in their usual orientation and balanced around the ring, so no side is favored and the earth magic spreads out evenly on all sides. Only one kind of modifier is present, so there is no conflict between signs. The clean sigil and signs keep the spell legible, but the slightly rough, out-of-round ring weakens it and shortens how long it lasts.
effect: Stirs the surrounding ground and lets soil, sand and loose stone spill outward from the seal in an even, spreading flow on all sides, with moderate force that runs unevenly at the edges and fades sooner than expected.

name: s42_00073.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A water sigil sits upright at the center, an S-curve flanked by two teardrops. It is of moderate size relative to the ring, and its lines are slightly rough. Four Binding signs, each a pair of stacked arcs, sit near the ring at the northwest, east-northeast, southeast and south. Each has its top toward the center, so the arcs open outward. Two Aeriforms Defined signs, each a cluster of three short strokes, sit at the north-northeast and west-southwest, also with their tops toward the center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell, and its moderate size gives a fair intensity. Binding halts the movement of the target material and binds it together so it acts and moves as a single unit. Four Binding signs make that cohesion strong. Aeriforms Defined is a modifier tied to air and gases. Its exact function is uncertain, so reading it as giving the water an airy, gaseous quality is a guess. The signs are evenly spread around the ring and no directional sign is present, so the effect is not pushed to any side. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they do not contradict each other. The slight roughness of the sigil makes the spell somewhat weaker and shorter lived than a clean drawing would.
effect: Draws water together into a single cohesive, mist-like mass that hangs still above the seal and moves only as one body. The mass is moderately sized, and its edges thin and loosen a little sooner than a cleanly drawn seal would allow.

name: s42_00076.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, neatly drawn. The ring is open, with a gap at the south-southwest between the lower left and the bottom. A large water sigil sits at the center, filling about half the ring's radius. Four Dancing Puppets signs sit about halfway out at the northwest, northeast, southeast and southwest, each drawn small. Six Aeriforms Defined signs, each three short strokes, sit just inside the ring. The ones at the north-northwest, east-southeast and southwest point inward toward the center. The ones at the west-northwest, northeast and south-southeast are flipped to point outward toward the ring. The signs are spread evenly around the seal, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell, and its large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect. Dancing Puppets lets the target's movement be manipulated. With four of them evenly spaced and no directional sign, nothing sets a course, so the water darts about erratically rather than travelling one way. Aeriforms Defined shares its design with the wind sigil's modifiers and its name with the air-creating sigil, so it most likely gives the magic an airy, gaseous quality. The sign is most likely semi-directional, which means an inverted copy reverses its effect. Here three point inward and three point outward. Their effects directly oppose each other and largely cancel. The water sigil and the Dancing Puppets signs therefore dominate the spell, while the airy quality pulls back and forth, so the result is likely unstable. The ring is open, so nothing activates until it is closed.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it lifts a large mass of water and sends it darting and twisting erratically through the air around the seal. The water keeps lurching between a frothy, mist-like state and a dense stream, so its movement stutters and wavers instead of flowing smoothly.

name: s42_00078.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background with two concentric rings, both closed. The outer and inner rings are drawn a little roughly and are somewhat out of round, bulging toward a rounded-square shape. The center is empty, with no sigil. A Strengthening sign sits at the north-northwest on the inner ring, drawn at a tilt so its triangle and crossbar lie askew. A small Glaives sign sits at the south, just inside the inner ring, its three prongs toward the center and its stem toward the ring. A small Holding sign, a pair of facing curves with dots, sits at the southwest near the inner ring. The southern half holds two of the three signs, so the layout leans toward the southwest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no sigil and no sign standing in for one, the spell is not tied to an element and acts on the object or body the seal marks. Strengthening makes its target harder, stronger and more durable. Holding is non-directional and keeps the target in the shape set by the seal while still letting it move. Glaives set how deeply magic embeds itself into flesh, and this one is small, so the embedding is shallow. These three modifiers work together without contradiction. None of them is directional, so the lean toward the southwest gives no direction and only makes the effect slightly uneven. The second ring normally adds effects and strength, but its band is empty, so it contributes little. The rough, out-of-round rings make the effect weaker and shorter-lived.
effect: Hardens and reinforces the object or body it marks, holding it in its present shape while still letting it move. The magic sinks only shallowly into flesh, and the hold is modest and slightly uneven, weakening and fading sooner than a cleanly drawn seal would.

name: s42_00079.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background, with the main ring closed and neatly drawn. A wind sigil sits upright at the center at moderate size, about a third of the ring's radius. Six signs sit near the ring. A Stability and Level Planes sign is at the north. A small Detection sign is at the east. A small Pulling sign is at the south-southeast, with its arrowhead pointing inward toward the center. A Gathering sign is at the south-southwest, with its arrowhead toward the ring. An inverted Crushing sign is at the west. A large, boldly drawn Levitation sign is at the northwest, with its arrow pointing outward toward the ring. Two smaller closed rings sit outside the main ring, each joined to it by a short line. The northwest sub-seal holds a fire sigil filling about half its ring. The southeast sub-seal holds a water sigil of similar size. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves and manipulates air, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. The attached fire and water sub-seals each feed their own element into the spell, adding heat and water to the moving air. Levitation lifts the target, and because it points outward at the northwest, it drives that lift toward the northwest. Pulling points inward, so it draws the target toward the seal. Gathering draws material in from the surroundings. Inverted Crushing reforms crushed material into its earlier shape, which here packs loose matter back together for a time. Stability and Level Planes keeps the lifted target balanced on a level plane. Detection's role is unclear and adds no clear effect. The seal stacks well over three unrelated kinds of modifier: lifting, pulling, gathering, reforming, levelling and detection. Inward Pulling also works against the outward Levitation. The wind sigil with Levitation and Pulling dominates, and the sub-seals color the air. The rest act only weakly, so the result is likely unstable.
effect: Draws air and loose debris in toward the seal and lifts them in a warm, misty current that drifts toward the northwest. The current tugs back and forth and only roughly holds level. Gathered debris clumps together for a moment before scattering, and the current gutters out early.

name: s42_00080.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, with the ring closed and neatly drawn. A wind sigil sits upright at the center. It is an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes and is moderate in size relative to the ring. A Stability and Level Planes sign, drawn as two wavy lines, sits near the ring at the west-northwest. A small Expansion sign of nested corner brackets sits at the east-southeast, turned in its usual orientation with its corners pointing outward. A Coil sign, two crossing curved strokes, sits at the south, also in its usual inward-facing orientation. A Partition sign sits at the west-southwest, turned so its peak faces the ring. An Immobility sign sits close to the ring at the east, with its arcs toward the ring and its base toward the center, which reads as turned outward. The signs are unevenly spread and lean toward the south. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves air. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Stability and Level Planes is non-directional and keeps a target balanced in a level plane. Expansion in its usual orientation, with its corners outward, makes the effect grow. Coil softens physical matter but cannot act on gases, so it touches only solid objects caught by the wind, not the air itself. Partition is directional and outlines the borders of the area of effect. Facing the ring at the west-southwest, it sets that boundary on that side. Immobility is likely semi-directional. Turned outward it reads as inverted, so as a guess it would reverse its usual hold and let a target shift instead of keeping it fixed. That works against the leveling of Stability. The seal stacks five unrelated kinds of modifier: leveling, growth, softening, boundary and inverted holding. The wind sigil dominates, with Expansion and Partition shaping its reach and Stability trying to keep it level. Softening and the reversed hold are secondary and pull against that leveling, so the result is likely unstable. The southward lean of the signs makes the effect act unevenly.
effect: Raises a moderate current of air that swells outward within a boundary pressed toward the west-southwest and tries to carry whatever it lifts on a level plane. Solid objects caught in it soften and sag instead of holding their shape. The current wavers and tilts unevenly toward the south, slipping in and out of level, and breaks apart before it settles.

name: s42_00081.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background. It has two concentric rings, both closed but drawn roughly, lumpy and noticeably out of round, with the inner ring sitting just inside the outer one. A water sigil sits upright at the center. It is moderate in size relative to the ring and drawn roughly. Six Envelopment signs, each a slanted stroke with short hooks at both ends, sit on or just against the inner ring at the north-northeast, east-northeast, south-southeast, south-southwest, west and northwest. They are spaced fairly evenly. Most have their tops toward the ring, while the south-southwest one is turned at an angle and touches the edge of a sub-seal. The sub-seal is a small, neatly drawn closed circle inside the inner ring at the southwest, holding a light sigil that fills about half of it. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Envelopment makes a spell's effect surround what it targets. Six of them spread evenly around the seal wrap the water around the target on all sides, with no direction favored. The neat light sub-seal adds light, a fire-domain effect, so the enveloping water also glows. That light comes from a single point and dims over time. The second ring adds strength to the core spell. However, the rough linework and the rings' poor roundness weaken it and shorten its life, and they risk a fleeting effect or a failed activation. Only one kind of modifier plus one sub-seal is present, and they do not contradict each other, so the seal is not unstable.
effect: Wraps the object the seal is drawn on in a thin, uneven shell of water that gives off a soft glow, brightest on one side and dimming over time. The shell wavers and sloshes loose in patches, and it drains away quickly, sometimes flickering out before it fully closes around the object.

name: s42_00082.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background. The main ring is closed but drawn a little roughly and slightly out of round. A water sigil sits upright at the center, roughly drawn and about half the ring's radius across. Two Pulling signs sit opposite each other, one at the northeast and one at the southwest, both with their arrows pointing inward toward the center. Five Crushing signs, drawn as zigzags, surround the sigil. The ones at the southeast, north-northeast and northwest are in normal orientation, and the ones at the west and east are inverted. Several of the signs are drawn roughly. Three smaller closed rings sit outside the main ring, each joined to it by a short line. The ring at the north-northeast holds a wind sigil, the one at the west-southwest holds a light sigil, and the one at the southeast holds an earth sigil. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil sets the element, and its size, about half the ring's radius, gives a fairly strong intensity. The two Pulling signs point inward and face each other across the seal, so they draw water toward the seal from the northeast and southwest without adding any twist. Crushing breaks its target into smaller and smaller pieces, which here would shatter water into fine spray. Inverted Crushing does the opposite and reforms crushed material. Normal and inverted Crushing directly contradict each other. The three normal signs outnumber the two inverted ones, so breaking apart dominates over reforming, and the result is likely unstable. The attached sub-seals each add their own element. Earth lets the effect act on loose solid matter, light adds a glow, and wind stirs the surrounding air. The rough main ring and sigil weaken the spell and shorten how long it lasts.
effect: Draws water and loose grit toward the seal from the northeast and southwest and shatters it into a glowing spray that swirls in stirred air. The spray keeps trying to pull back together, so it flickers unevenly between scattered droplets and half-formed clumps. The effect wavers and collapses well before a cleanly drawn seal would.

name: s42_00083.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background. The ring is closed but noticeably lumpy and out of round, bulging unevenly on several sides. Two small sigils sit side by side at the center, each a little over a quarter of the ring radius: a fire sigil on the left, slightly rough, and a water sigil on the right, drawn more roughly. Three Detection signs, each a set of three slanted parallel strokes, sit about two thirds of the way out at the west-northwest, east-southeast and south-southeast. The east-southeast and south-southeast ones are a little rough. Two neatly drawn Concealment signs, eight-armed stars with eye marks, sit at the northeast and southwest. Near the ring at the north are two slightly rough Pulling signs. The one at the north-northeast has its arrowhead pointing in toward the center. The one at the north-northwest is inverted, with its arrowhead pointing out toward the ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire and water sigils share the center, so the spell works both heat and water. Both are small and rough, which gives a weak, combined effect such as warm water or steam. Detection's exact function is uncertain, but it senses presences, and three of them spread around the seal give that sensing a wide reach.
