The two Concealment signs hide the target and work directly against the Detection signs, which try to sense. The Pulling sign pointing inward draws the target toward the seal, while the inverted one pushes it away. These two sit side by side at the north and directly contradict each other, so the pull and push largely cancel and leave a jerking motion along that side. The paired sigils dominate, with Concealment the steadiest part because those signs are drawn neatly. The contradiction between the Pulling signs and the tension between hiding and sensing make the result likely unstable. The ring is not round enough, which makes any effect fleeting, and the seal may fail to activate at all. The rough sigils weaken it further.
effect: Produces a faint wisp of warm steam that is hard to see. It is tugged toward the seal and shoved away from it at once, so it sputters back and forth along the north side. It may briefly react to something nearby before collapsing almost immediately, and it often fails to form at all.

name: s42_00084.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background. The ring is open, with a gap at the upper right between the north-northeast and the east, and it is drawn roughly and somewhat out of round. A large Diamond sign sits upright at the center, drawn neatly with a heavy line, and reaches about halfway to the ring. Two small Expansion signs, each made of nested corner brackets, sit near the ring at the northeast and southwest. They face each other across the center and are drawn upright, not inverted. Two small Solidification signs, each two little circles joined by a short line, sit at the north-northwest and southeast. There is no element sigil, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the Diamond sign takes the center and sets the core behavior. It makes the spell act only on objects held within the container the seal is drawn on, leaving the container itself untouched. The spell is therefore not tied to fire, water, earth or wind and works on whatever those contents are. Expansion is semi-directional. Drawn upright with its corners outward, it makes its target grow, and placing one at each of two opposite points keeps that growth even. Solidification makes the affected material more solid, so the enlarged contents firm up instead of loosening as they swell. The two Solidification signs also sit at opposite points, so the seal is balanced and favors no direction. That makes three kinds of modifier, and they work together without contradiction. The open ring keeps the seal from activating. The rough, out-of-round ring and the slightly rough strokes on some signs make the effect weaker and shorter-lived once the ring is closed.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it makes the contents of the container the seal is drawn on swell to a larger size and grow firmer, while the container itself stays unchanged. The growth is modest and uneven, wavering as it takes hold, and it fades and lets the contents shrink back sooner than a cleanly drawn seal would.

name: s42_00085.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn neatly in black on a white background, ring closed. An earth sigil sits at the center, upright and fairly large, reaching about half the ring's radius. Six Envelopment signs surround it in three pairs spaced roughly evenly around the seal. One pair is at the north-northwest, one at the east and east-southeast, and one at the south-southwest and southwest. In each pair, one sign sits about halfway out with its top toward the center. The other sits close to the ring, slightly offset, with its top toward the ring. No other signs are present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell manipulates existing solid matter such as stone, soil, sand and wood rather than creating it. Its large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect. Envelopment makes a spell's effect envelop and surround what it targets, so the moved earth wraps around the target instead of rising or shooting off. The three pairs are spread evenly, so no side is favored and the covering forms uniformly all the way around. Within each pair the inner sign faces the center and the outer sign faces the ring. This reads as a double layer, one wrapping inward against the target and one closing over it from outside, rather than as a contradiction. Only one kind of modifier is present, and the neat drawing and closed ring mean the spell activates and holds steady.
effect: Draws nearby stone, soil or sand in from all sides and wraps it firmly around the target. This forms a thick, even shell of earth that fully encases it, built up in an inner and an outer layer.

name: s42_00087.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed. The ring is lumpy and noticeably out of round. A small Selection sign, a cross drawn through a small square, sits upright at the center in place of a sigil. A Levitation sign sits at the north with its arrow pointing inward toward the center. A neatly drawn Columns sign sits at the west-northwest, its crossbar toward the ring and its stem toward the center. A Coil sign, two crossing curved strokes, sits at the east-northeast, closer to the center than the other signs and turned on its side. A roughly drawn Detection sign, three parallel strokes of increasing length, sits at the southeast. A Cooling sign, a central stroke flanked by dots, sits at the southwest. There is no element sigil. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: No fire, water, earth, wind, or light sigil is present. Selection takes the center, so the spell confines its effect to the object the seal is drawn on and works on that object's own matter. Levitation pointing inward floats that object. The single Columns sign is directional and has no partner, so it pushes the effect toward the west-northwest. Coil softens physical matter. Cooling lowers its temperature. Detection's role is the least defined, so its contribution is unclear. Together these stack five unrelated kinds of modifier: lifting, directional push, softening, cooling, and detection. Selection with Levitation and Columns dominates and sets the core motion. Coil and Cooling act as secondary changes to the object. Detection adds little that can be predicted. The result is likely unstable. The rough linework weakens the spell and shortens how long it lasts. The ring is not round enough, so the effect is fleeting or may fail to activate at all.
effect: The object the seal is drawn on lifts weakly and lurches toward the west-northwest. It turns faintly cool and slightly soft in uneven patches, then wavers and drops after only a moment. With its lopsided ring, the seal may fail to activate at all.

name: s42_00088.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn, the inner one set a little inside the outer. A four-lobed Billow sign sits at the center in place of a sigil, fairly large relative to the ring. Six Rain signs sit inside the inner ring, a bit over halfway from the center: north, east-northeast, southeast, south-southwest, west-southwest and northwest. Each is drawn inside-out, so it is inverted. They are spaced roughly evenly, so no side is favored. There is no element sigil and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, Billow takes the center and sets the core behavior: turning available material into a fluffy cloud. Its fairly large size gives a moderately strong effect, and the second ring reinforces the spell. Rain is semi-directional, and for its radially symmetric form, drawing it inside-out inverts it. Inverted Rain creates an area where the target material cannot exist or is pushed away. Six of them spaced evenly push that material outward on all sides. No Collection signs are present, so the seal does not draw material in; it only acts on what reaches it. There is one kind of modifier, and it shapes rather than cancels the cloud. Billow makes the cloud, and the inverted Rain signs keep it pushed back, so the seal holds together.
effect: Turns any material that reaches the seal into a soft, fluffy cloud and pushes it outward on all sides. This leaves a clear space over the seal ringed by a thick cushioning bank of cloud. The cloud holds steady and evenly, with a fairly strong push.

name: s42_00089.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with two concentric rings, both closed and drawn a little roughly and slightly out of round. The band between the two rings is empty. A fire sigil sits at the center, upright and neatly drawn. It is small relative to the ring, and its bottom stroke extends a little further than usual. At the west-southwest, about two thirds of the way out, sits a glyph that matches Repetition, a circle crossed by an S-curve around a central dot, with a small Columns sign attached to its left side. At the southeast is a Sights Set sign with its diamond end toward the center and its arrow pointing out toward the ring. At the northwest is a single Envelopment sign. More of the signs sit on the west-southwest side than elsewhere. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil makes this a fire spell, and its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. The extra stroke at its base does not match a separate sigil, so it is read as fire. The west-southwest glyph is read as Repetition with a Columns sign fused to it, which is a guess. Read that way, it keeps resetting the flame and its heat to their starting state, so the fire renews itself instead of burning out. The attached Columns, together with the overall lean of the signs, pushes that effect as a column toward the west-southwest. Envelopment makes the fire surround whatever it targets. Sights Set lets the caster aim the effect, and its arrow points southeast. That aim directly opposes the west-southwest push. The fire sigil and the self-renewing core dominate, while the two directions pull against each other, so the result is likely unstable. The second ring holds no signs in its band, so it adds no further effect. The rough, slightly out-of-round rings make the spell weaker and shorter-lived.
effect: Wraps a target in a modest, self-renewing flame that keeps returning to its original heat. The aim wavers between the southeast and a drag toward the west-southwest, so the flame lands unevenly and flickers before guttering out sooner than a steady fire would.

name: s42_00090.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed but slightly rough and a little out of round. A light sigil, a diamond inside a square with four spokes, sits upright at the center and is fairly large relative to the ring. A small, faint Crosshair sign sits near the ring at the west. Two Strengthening signs are present, both drawn in heavy strokes: one at the northeast about halfway to the ring, and one at the west-southwest closer to the center. A Collection sign sits at the east-southeast, rotated so its crossed legs and triangular head lie at an angle. A small Binding sign, two stacked arcs, sits near the ring at the southeast. A rotated Refuse sign, a diamond with crossing tails, sits at the south-southwest. More signs crowd the southern half than the northern half. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil makes this a light spell, and its fairly large size relative to the ring gives a fairly strong effect. Collection draws in material from around the seal, and Refuse, a directional sign, collects unwanted material toward where it points, here off to the south-southwest. Binding halts the gathered material and makes it act as a single unit. The two Strengthening signs make the result harder and more durable. Crosshair makes the effect target whatever its short ends point at, here to the west. The five sign kinds fall into three related groups: gathering (Collection and Refuse), consolidating (Binding and Strengthening), and targeting (Crosshair). They do not contradict each other, so the seal is not unstable. However, the signs lean toward the south, so the effect is weighted unevenly toward that side. The rough ring and the rough Crosshair make the activation and the aim less steady.
effect: Draws in the surrounding light and packs it into a dense, firm glow that holds together as one mass and is aimed at a target to the west, while loose debris is swept off toward the south-southwest. The glow is fairly bright but sits heavier on its southern side. Its aim wavers slightly, and it dims over time, fading a little sooner than a cleanly drawn seal would.

name: s42_00094.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a plain background. The ring is open, with a gap at the northeast, and is drawn a little roughly. A Refuse sign, a diamond set on two crossed legs, sits upright at the center and is moderate in size relative to the ring. Five Pulling signs sit about three quarters of the way out from the center, at the west-southwest, west-northwest, north, northeast and south. All are inverted, with the stem toward the center and the arrowhead pointing outward toward the ring. The northern one is drawn a little rough. At the east-southeast, in the same ring of positions, sits an unfamiliar glyph: a narrow right-angled triangle with a small circle at one corner, its point toward the center. No element sigil is present. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the Refuse sign at the center serves as the core. Refuse is directional and collects unwanted material such as waste toward where it points. Upright, it points north. Pulling draws things toward the seal when its arrow points inward, so these outward-pointing Pulling signs reverse that and push material away from the seal. They are spread evenly around the ring, so the push favors no single side. Pushing debris outward and collecting it northward work together rather than against each other. The east-southeast glyph matches no known sign. It is closest to Convergence, a triangle with one point facing inward, so this reading is a guess. As Convergence, it would focus the magic and pack loose particles tightly together, compacting the refuse it moves. Only three kinds of modifier are present, so the seal is not overloaded. The seal will not activate while the ring is open. Once it is closed, the slightly rough ring would make the effect weaker and shorter-lived, and the rough northern Pulling sign gives a slightly softer push on that side.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it pushes loose waste and debris away from the seal on every side and sweeps it toward the north, compacting it into a tighter clump as it goes. The push is modest, slightly weaker to the north, and fades sooner than it would from a cleaner seal.

name: s42_00099.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background with two concentric rings, both closed. The outer ring is slightly uneven in shape, and the inner ring sits just inside it. A wind sigil sits at the center and is moderately large relative to the inner ring. Its spiral and flanking dashes are drawn a little roughly. A small Repetition sign, a circle with a central dot crossed by a diagonal stroke, sits at the west-northwest about two thirds of the way to the ring. Three small Mimicry signs sit at the west-southwest, east-northeast and south-southeast, each rotated differently: the west-southwest one is tilted, the east-northeast one is roughly upside down, and the south-southeast one stands upright. The signs cluster more on the western and southern side, leaving the north and east emptier. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves and manipulates air without creating it. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity, and the slightly rough strokes make that force a little less even. Mimicry guides or imitates the movements of a target. With no decorative sigil to supply a shape, the moving air copies the motion of the target itself. The three Mimicry signs strengthen this copying. Repetition continually resets what the spell affects to the state it had when the spell first took hold. Applied to mimicked air movement, it makes the motion snap back to its starting point and replay instead of drifting away. The second ring adds strength to the core spell. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they combine without contradiction. Because most of the signs sit on the western and southern side, the effect is weighted toward the southwest.
effect: Stirs moderate currents of air that copy the movements of a target, then snap back to where they began and replay the same motion over and over. The currents are somewhat uneven in strength and are strongest toward the southwest of the seal.

name: s42_00101.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, made of two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. The inner ring sits about two thirds of the way out, leaving a narrow band between the two rings. A small wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes, sits upright at the center. Three Glaives signs, each a trident-like fork on a long stem, sit inside the inner ring at the north-northwest, east-southeast and southwest, roughly halfway to the inner ring, with their prongs facing the center. Four smaller Glaives signs sit in the outer band at the east-northeast, south, west-northwest and west-southwest, with their prongs facing the outer ring. The signs are spread evenly around the seal. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves and manipulates air, and its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Glaives determine how deeply magic embeds itself into flesh. They are most likely semi-directional, so their orientation does not steer the spell, but inverting one should reverse its effect. The four outer Glaives face outward, the usual way Glaives are drawn, and would drive the air magic deep into the body. The three inner Glaives face inward and read as inverted, which would make the magic sit shallow or draw back out. Normal and inverted Glaives directly contradict each other. The outer four dominate, because they outnumber the inner three and sit in the second ring, which adds strength to a seal. Even so, the opposing signs pull against them, so the result is likely unstable. The signs are spread evenly, so the effect favors no direction.
effect: Presses a modest current of air into a living body. The air sinks into the flesh unevenly: it drives deep, then partly works its way back out, so the depth it reaches keeps wavering and the effect may give out early.

name: s42_00102.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring open with a gap at the upper left between the north and west-northwest signs. The ring is neatly drawn and close to round. Two glyphs sit side by side at the center, both small relative to the ring. On the left is a neatly drawn Link sign, and on the right is a roughly drawn fire sigil. Two Stability and Level Planes signs, each a pair of wavy strokes, sit near the ring at the northeast and southwest. Four Projection signs, flat brackets, sit just inside the ring at the north, east-southeast, south and west-northwest. Each has its bar toward the center and its open side facing outward. Several of the outer signs are drawn somewhat roughly. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and shapes flame and heat. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity, and its rough linework weakens it further and shortens its life. Link shares the center as a second core. It identifies material from the same source and connects it, so flames born from this fire stay tied to one another. The four evenly spaced Projection signs push the effect outward from the seal, and because they are balanced, no direction is favored. The two opposed Stability and Level Planes signs are non-directional. They keep the effect balanced in a level plane, like something floating on water. That is three kinds of modifier working together without contradiction, so the seal is not unstable, but the rough fire core and rough outer signs make it uneven. The seal will not activate until the gap in the ring is closed.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it casts modest flames outward from the seal evenly on every side, holding them level in a flat plane. The flames stay linked to one another and move together. They flicker unevenly and die out sooner than a steady fire would.

name: s42_00104.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background. The ring is open, with a gap at the upper left between the north-northwest and west positions, and it is drawn roughly and noticeably out of round. A fire sigil sits upright at the center, roughly a quarter of the ring's radius across and drawn roughly. Six Convergence triangles sit about two thirds to three quarters of the way out, at the east-northeast, east-southeast, south-southeast, west-southwest, west and north-northwest. The ones at the east-southeast and west have a point facing outward toward the ring, while the other four are turned at assorted angles, so the set does not share one orientation. Two Levitation signs sit at the north and south, both with their arrows pointing outward toward the ring. Every glyph is drawn with rough, uneven lines. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil makes this a fire spell, and its modest size gives a modest intensity. Convergence draws the magic down toward a single point. Its usual orientation has a point facing inward, and a semi-directional sign facing outward reverses its effect. Here the two outward-pointing triangles push against the focusing of the others. The four angled ones outnumber them, so convergence dominates, but this direct opposition means the result is likely unstable. Levitation normally lifts with its arrow facing inward. Both are inverted here, and inverted Levitation has only been seen cancelling normal Levitation, so its effect on its own is unclear. Read as a reversal, which is a guess, it removes lift instead of adding it. The pair sits opposite each other and is balanced, so it sets no sideways direction. The flame stays low at the seal instead of rising. The open ring prevents activation. The rough lines and uneven ring make the effect weak and short-lived, with a risk of fizzling.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it gathers a small, modest flame into a tight point that hugs the seal instead of rising. The flame pulses unevenly between a focused knot and a loose flicker before guttering out quickly, and it may fail to catch at all.

name: s42_00105.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background. The main ring is closed but drawn roughly and noticeably out of round, bulging unevenly at several points. A Columns sign stands upright at the center in place of a sigil, with its crossbar at the bottom and its stem pointing north. It is drawn roughly and is moderate in size relative to the ring. Four Orb signs, each a small circle crossed by a diagonal line, sit near the ring at the north-northwest, east-northeast, east-southeast and south-southeast. The east-northeast Orb is drawn heavier than the others and overlaps the edge of a small sub-seal. At the west point near the ring sits a faint, roughly drawn glyph shaped like a Gathering sign with a small circle on its stem, lying sideways with its point toward the center. Inside the main ring at the east-northeast is a small, neatly drawn sub-seal with its ring closed and a wind sigil at its center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The main seal has no element sigil. The Columns sign takes the center and sets the core behavior: the magic manifests in a column and is driven upward. The neat wind sub-seal supplies the element, so the spell moves air. Its small size gives that air only modest force. The four non-directional Orb signs define a spherical space above the seal where the controlled material collects, filling it from the bottom up. The west glyph matches no known sign exactly. It is closest to Gathering, so reading it as Gathering is a guess. Read that way, it actively draws material in from the surroundings, which here means pulling air into the orb. Because it points toward the center from the west, that draw comes chiefly from the west side. The modifiers support one another, gathering material, holding it in a sphere and lifting it, so the seal is not contradictory. However, the rough linework and the out-of-round ring make the effect weak and short-lived, and the ring's poor roundness means the spell may flicker out almost at once or fail to activate.
effect: Draws in air, mostly from the west, and gathers it into a faint spherical pocket that rises a short way above the seal on a weak upward current. The pocket forms unevenly, wavers, and collapses after only a moment, and the spell may sputter without forming at all.

name: s42_00106.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed but a little rough and slightly out of round. A small water sigil sits upright at the center, about a quarter of the ring's radius. Seven Launch signs surround it. Five point inward with their tips toward the center: one each at the southwest, northwest and southeast near the ring, and two at the northeast, one near the ring and one closer in. Two point outward with their tips toward the ring, one at the west and one at the south. A Diamond sign sits at the east, about two thirds of the way out. Most signs are drawn roughly, and the southern Launch is the neatest. The signs are spread evenly around the ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell, and its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Launch generates the spell's material in the direction it points as a powerful but short-lived burst. Five Launch signs point inward and two point outward, so their directions directly contradict each other. The inward group outnumbers the outward pair and dominates, which drives most of the water toward the center while weaker bursts escape west and south. Because the signs oppose each other, the result is likely unstable. Diamond is read as limiting the spell to whatever is held inside the container it is drawn on, leaving the container itself unaffected. The rough linework and slightly uneven ring make the effect weaker and shorter-lived.
effect: Produces brief, sputtering bursts of water inside the container it is drawn on, without affecting the container itself. Most of the bursts rush inward and collide at the middle, while a few weaker spurts break off toward the west and south. The jets are modest and uneven and die out quickly, sometimes fizzling before they fully form.

name: s42_00108.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background. The ring is neatly drawn but open, with a gap at the upper left between the west and north-northwest. A wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes, sits upright at the center and is moderate in size relative to the ring. Four Detection signs, each three parallel strokes of increasing length, surround it. One sits just west of north about halfway to the ring, one at the north-northeast close to the ring, one at the east-southeast drawn with heavier strokes, and one at the southwest. Two Pointing signs sit right against the ring, one at the west just below the gap and one at the east. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves and steers existing air rather than creating it. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Detection is tied to sensing presence and helps a spell react to what is around it, so the four Detection signs make the moving air respond to presences near the seal. Pointing is non-directional and gives the controlled material a conical shape that would normally be aimed by signs such as Columns. No Columns or other directional sign is present, and the signs are balanced around the ring, so the cones are not driven in any set direction. Only two kinds of modifier appear, and they do not conflict. The seal will not activate until the gap in the ring is closed.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it gathers the surrounding air into tapered, cone-shaped currents of moderate strength that stir in response to people or creatures sensed nearby. The currents form around the seal without being sent in any particular direction.

name: s42_00110.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is neatly drawn but open, with a gap at the lower left between the west-southwest and south points. A large Dispersion sign, about half the ring's radius, sits upright at the center in place of a sigil, its stem pointing up and its curve facing down. Six Pointing signs sit just inside the ring at roughly even intervals: north, east-northeast, east-southeast, south, west-southwest and west-northwest, each with its top toward the ring. A seventh Pointing sign sits closer in at the southeast, slightly rotated. There is no element sigil, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the spell is not tied to fire, water, earth or wind, so Dispersion at the center sets its core behavior. Dispersion makes the seal's magic pour outward rather than beam in one direction, and its large size gives that outflow considerable strength. Pointing is non-directional and makes the target manifest in a conical shape, so the outpouring takes a tapering, cone-like form. Because Pointing is non-directional and the signs are balanced around the ring, their placement steers nothing, and the extra inner sign at the southeast only adds weight to the tapering rather than a direction. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they agree. The ring is open, so the seal will not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it pours whatever material is directed into it strongly outward from the seal in all directions, drawn out into tapering, cone-shaped spurts rather than a loose spill.

name: s42_00111.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background. The ring is open, with a gap at the upper right between the north-northeast and the east, and it is drawn a little roughly and somewhat out of round. Two water sigils sit side by side at the center, each moderate in size relative to the ring. The left one is drawn thin and neat, and the right one is heavier and slightly rougher. An Expansion sign of nested corner brackets sits at the north-northwest, with its corners pointing outward, drawn a little roughly. A Stillness sign sits at the north-northeast, turned on its side. A Link sign sits at the east-southeast, also turned sideways. A Sights Set sign sits at the south, with its diamond end toward the ring and its arrow pointing north toward the center. A Coil sign lies almost horizontally at the southwest. The signs are spread evenly around the ring, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The two water sigils set the element, so the spell manipulates water, and having two of them at moderate size gives a fair overall intensity. Expansion is semi-directional, and with its corners pointing outward it makes the target grow. Stillness holds a magical effect static in one location. Link identifies portions that came from the same source and ties them together. Sights Set lets the caster aim the spell at a chosen point. Coil softens solid matter but cannot act on liquids, so with water as the only element it adds nothing. Sights Set and Stillness pull against each other, since one directs the effect and the other pins it in place. The seal also stacks more than three unrelated kinds of modifier: growth, holding in place, linking, aiming and softening. The water sigils dominate, with Expansion and Stillness the strongest modifiers, and Link is secondary. The aiming effect fights the holding effect, so the result is likely unstable. The seal does not activate while the ring is open, and the rough, out-of-round ring would make the effect weaker and short-lived once it is closed.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it swells a mass of water and tries to hold it in one spot, keeping water drawn from the same source bound together. Any attempt to aim it tugs against that hold, so the swollen water lurches and wobbles unevenly instead of staying put or moving cleanly. It soon breaks apart well before a steady spell would.

name: s42_00112.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background. The ring is open, with a gap on the west side, and is drawn somewhat out of round, bulging into an egg shape. A light sigil, a diamond set inside a square with four short spokes, sits upright at the center at moderate size relative to the ring and is neatly drawn. Seven Sights Set signs, each a shaft with an arrowhead at one end and a small diamond at the other, are spread around it at roughly two thirds to four fifths of the way to the ring. The ones at the north-northeast, east, west (just below the gap) and south-southwest point their arrows outward toward the ring. The ones at the north-northwest and south-southeast point their arrows inward toward the center. The one at the west-northwest is drawn heavier than the rest and stands nearly upright, its arrow pointing north. The western and south-southwestern signs are a little rough. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil makes this a light spell, and its moderate size relative to the ring gives a moderate intensity. Sights Set lets the caster aim a spell at a chosen point or target. With most of the signs pointing outward, the light is aimed away from the seal at targets around it. The signs are balanced around the ring, so no single direction is favored and the caster can aim in any direction around the seal. The two inward-pointing signs aim back at the seal itself and contradict the outward majority. The outward signs dominate, but this conflict makes the aim likely unstable, tugging back toward the seal. Only one kind of modifier is present, so the instability comes from this opposing orientation, not from stacking. The seal will not activate while the ring is open. The rough, out-of-round ring and slightly rough signs would make the effect weak and short-lived once it is closed.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it casts a moderate light that the caster can aim at a chosen target in any direction around the seal. The aim wavers and keeps slipping back toward the seal, and the light flickers briefly and fades quickly.

name: s42_00113.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A Levitation sign sits upright at the center inside the inner ring, its arrow pointing north, drawn at a little over a third of the outer ring's radius. Four small zigzag glyphs sit in the band between the two rings. Three are Crushing signs: one at the northwest and one at the southeast are inverted, and one at the west-southwest faces normally. The southeast sign is drawn a little more roughly than the rest. The fourth glyph, at the east-northeast, is a short broken zigzag that looks like a Crushing sign with its lower part missing. No element sigil is present. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, Levitation takes the center and sets the core behavior: the seal floats its target into the air. As a directional sign pointing north, it sends that lift toward the north side of the seal. Its moderate size gives a moderate strength. The second ring adds strength and further effect to the core spell. Crushing is semi-directional, so it steers nothing, but inversion reverses it. The normal Crushing at the west-southwest breaks matter into ever smaller pieces, while the two inverted Crushing signs pull crushed matter back into its original shape. These directly contradict each other. The east-northeast glyph matches no known sign; reading it as a partial normal Crushing is a guess, which would add a weak crushing pull. The crushing and reforming sides are close to even, since the slightly rough southeast sign weakens the reforming pair and the partial glyph only faintly helps the crushing side, so neither clearly wins. Levitation dominates as the steady core, and the Crushing signs fight over the target's form. The result is likely unstable.
effect: Lifts the target object at moderate strength and floats it toward the north, while the object keeps cracking into fragments and pulling back together, flickering between broken and whole without ever settling. Pieces may shed loose or drop out of the lift unevenly as it travels.

name: s42_00114.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is open, with a gap at the lower right between the east and south signs, and it is drawn roughly and noticeably out of round, with flattened, lumpy sides. A fire sigil sits upright at the center, drawn in bold strokes and large relative to the ring, reaching about half of its radius. Four Reflection signs, each an hourglass of two triangles meeting at a point, sit about three quarters of the way out at the north, east, south and west points, each with its top toward the center. The north and east signs are neat, the south sign is slightly rough, and the west sign is drawn roughly. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil makes this a fire spell that creates and manipulates flame and heat. Its large size relative to the ring gives a fairly strong intensity. Reflection directs the spell to act on a reflected image on the object the seal is drawn on. With four of them evenly spaced, no direction is favored and the effect spreads evenly around the seal. Only one kind of modifier is present and it does not contradict the sigil, so the seal is not unstable. The seal will not activate while the ring is open. Once it is closed, the rough, out-of-round ring and the uneven linework of the south and west signs make the effect weaker and fleeting, and the spell may fail to activate at all.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it kindles fairly strong flames within the reflected image on the surface the seal is drawn on, so fire appears to burn evenly across the reflection on all sides. The flames flicker unsteadily, burn weaker on the south and west sides, and die out quickly, and the spell may sputter and fail to catch at all.

name: s42_00116.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background with the main ring closed and neatly drawn. A light sigil sits upright at the center, about half the ring's radius. Four Stability and Level Planes signs, drawn as stacked wavy lines, sit near the ring at the north, east, south and west points, each turned so its top faces the ring. They are evenly spaced. Three smaller closed rings sit outside the main ring, each joined to it by a short line. The one at the north-northeast holds a small water sigil drawn roughly and somewhat blotchy. The one at the west holds a small, roughly drawn wind sigil, and its ring is uneven and slightly out of round. The one at the south-southeast holds a neatly drawn Stillness sign. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil sets the element, so the spell creates light. Its fairly large size relative to the ring gives a fairly strong intensity. Stability and Level Planes is non-directional and makes the target balance on a level plane in the air. Four balanced signs keep that plane steady with no lean to any side. The Stillness sub-seal holds the magical effect static in a single location, so the floating light stays put. The water sub-seal adds water. Its rough sigil makes that contribution weak and short-lived. The wind sub-seal adds air movement, but its rough sigil and uneven ring make that part weak and fleeting. The wind part may also fail to activate. The core of light, level balance and stillness is well drawn and consistent, so the main effect holds steady. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and no signs contradict each other.
effect: Creates a fairly bright sheet of light that floats level in the air above the seal and stays fixed in one place, slowly dimming over time. A faint trace of water collects with it and soon fades. A weak draft of air stirs around it unevenly, sputters and dies out early or does not rise at all.

name: s42_00118.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, main ring closed and neatly drawn. A light sigil, a diamond inside a square with four short spokes, sits upright at the center at a moderate size relative to the ring. Six Columns signs sit just inside the ring. Three face the usual way, crossbar toward the ring and stem toward the center, at the north-northwest, east and south-southwest. Three are inverted, stem toward the ring and crossbar toward the center, at the northeast, south-southeast and west-northwest. Normal and inverted signs alternate around the ring and are evenly balanced. Three small closed sub-seals sit inside the main ring. The one at the north-northwest is neatly drawn and holds a fire sigil that fills about half its ring. The one at the east holds a small light sigil, and its ring and sigil are drawn somewhat roughly. The one at the southwest holds a boldly but roughly drawn Pointing sign inside a slightly rough ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil makes this a light spell, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Normal Columns signs make the magic manifest as an upright column. Inverted Columns signs make it manifest horizontally, leaking outward much like Dispersion. The two sets are evenly balanced, so no side is favored. They do not cancel each other. Instead the spell rises as a column while also spreading sideways. The neat fire sub-seal adds heat, and light falls within the fire domain, so the two blend cleanly into warm light. The east light sub-seal adds more light, but its rough drawing makes that contribution weak and short-lived. The Pointing sub-seal gives the manifested light a conical shape, which the Columns signs then direct upward. Its rough linework makes the taper uneven. The spell has only one kind of main modifier plus three compatible sub-seals, so it is not unstable.
effect: Raises a warm, moderately bright column of light that tapers toward a point as it climbs, while a softer glow spills outward across the area around the seal. The taper is uneven and a faint extra brightness flickers and fades early. The light gradually dims over time.

name: s42_00121.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn neatly in black on a white background. The ring is open, with a clear gap at the north. There is no element sigil. A Convergence sign, a downward-pointing triangle about a third of the ring's radius, sits at the center with one point facing south. Six Glaives signs, each a three-pronged fork on a straight stem, are spread evenly about two thirds of the way out from the center. They sit at the north-northeast, east-northeast, southeast, south-southwest, west-southwest and northwest, each with its prongs toward the ring and its stem toward the center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, Convergence takes the central place and sets the core behavior. It focuses the spell's magic down to a single point and makes it manifest from that point, packing it tightly. Glaives set how deeply magic embeds itself into flesh. Six of them, all facing outward in their usual orientation, give the magic deep penetration. Because they are evenly spaced and Glaives are not directional, no side is favored, and the depth applies equally all around. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they do not conflict. The neat drawing gives a steady, full-strength effect. The spell will not activate while the ring is open.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it gathers its magic into one tightly focused point and drives it deep into the flesh of a living target, embedding it firmly rather than letting it rest on the surface. Because the seal carries no element, it acts as pure concentrated magic rather than fire, water, earth or wind.

name: s42_00123.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed. The ring is hand-drawn and slightly lopsided, a little flattened on the right, but still close to round. A light sigil, a diamond inside a square with four short spokes, sits at the center at a moderate size relative to the ring. Nine Gathering signs surround it in two loose rings. An inner set of five sits about halfway out, at the west, north-northeast, southeast, northwest and southwest. An outer set of four sits near the ring at the north, east, south and west. Eight of them have their arrowheads pointing in toward the center. The southwest inner sign is turned sideways, pointing roughly east instead of at the center. The northwest and southeast inner signs and the north outer sign are drawn a little rougher and heavier than the rest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil makes this a light spell, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Gathering lets a spell actively draw material in from its surroundings to build its effect. Here that material is light. Eight of the nine Gathering signs point inward, their usual orientation, and they are spread evenly in two rings around the sigil. Because of that balance, the light is drawn in from all sides toward the center rather than pushed in one direction, and repeating the sign this many times strengthens and widens the pull. The sideways southwest sign pulls along the ring instead of inward, so light from that side drifts eastward before reaching the center. The handful of rough signs and the slightly uneven ring make the draw a little less steady but do not stop the spell. Only one kind of modifier is present, so the seal is not unstable.
effect: Draws ambient light in from all around the seal and concentrates it into a moderate glow at its center, leaving the surroundings dimmer. Light from the southwest side swirls slightly eastward before it is pulled in, and the pull flickers a little rather than holding perfectly even. The gathered glow gradually fades over time.

name: s42_00124.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. There is no element sigil. A Convergence sign, a downward-pointing triangle, sits upright at the center and is moderate in size relative to the ring. Six Sights Set signs surround it. Two sit in the band between the rings, at the northeast and southwest, with their diamond ends inward and their arrows pointing outward toward the ring. Four sit inside the inner ring, at the north-northwest, northeast, southeast and southwest, each with its diamond end toward the ring and its arrow pointing in toward the center. The northeast and southwest inner signs are drawn heavier than the others. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, Convergence at the center is the core of the seal. It draws the spell's magic down to a single point and can pack loose material tightly, so the spell is not tied to one element and works on whatever is brought into it. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Sights Set lets the caster aim the effect at a chosen point or target. The four inner signs all aim inward and agree with the convergence. The two outer signs aim outward along the same northeast-southwest line as two of the inward ones, which directly opposes them. Because the second ring adds its effect on top of the core, this outward aim cannot simply be ignored. The inward-aiming signs dominate: there are four of them, two are drawn heavier, and the central Convergence reinforces them. The outward pair still pulls against them, so the result is likely unstable along that axis.
effect: Gathers whatever material or magic is brought into it and packs it toward a single focal point that the caster can aim. The aim keeps being tugged outward toward the northeast and southwest. The focal point therefore wavers back and forth along that line and sometimes slips loose before it settles.

name: s42_00125.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background. The main ring is closed but drawn roughly and noticeably out of round, bulging toward a squarish shape. A neatly drawn wind sigil sits at the center, small relative to the ring. Four signs sit near the ring. A small Repetition sign is at the north, an inverted Expansion sign with its nested corner brackets pointing inward is at the west-northwest, a Detection sign of three slanted strokes is at the east-northeast, and a tilted Convergence triangle is at the east-southeast. More of the signs crowd the upper and right side than the lower left. Two small sub-seals sit inside the main ring. The one at the southwest is closed and holds a Dispersion sign at its center. The one at the northeast is open, with a gap on its right side, and holds an earth sigil. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves existing air rather than creating it. Its small size gives it a modest intensity. Convergence draws the magic toward a single point and makes loose matter pack tightly. Inverted Expansion shrinks its target. Repetition keeps resetting what it affects to its starting state. Detection's role is unclear beyond lending a sensing quality. The closed Dispersion sub-seal makes the magic pour outward, which directly contradicts Convergence. The open earth sub-seal does nothing until it is closed. The seal stacks more than three unrelated kinds of modifier: focusing, shrinking, time-resetting, sensing and dispersing. The wind sigil, Convergence and Repetition dominate, with the shrinking effect secondary and Dispersion pulling against them, so the result is likely unstable. The uneven spread of signs biases the effect toward the north-northeast. The rough, out-of-round ring further weakens the spell and shortens its life, and could make it fleeting.
effect: Gathers a weak current of air that tightens and draws inward toward a point at the north-northeast, then keeps snapping back to its starting state, while puffs of air leak out and undo the gathering. The pull flickers and acts unevenly, and it collapses after only a brief moment.

name: s42_00129.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A water sigil sits upright at the center, moderate in size relative to the ring. Two Dispersion signs sit on the east side, one at the east and one at the east-northeast, each with its stem toward the ring and its curve facing the center. A Rain sign sits at the north-northeast, upright and not turned inside out. A small Windows sign sits just inside the ring at the north. A small Mimicry sign sits at the north-northwest, its top toward the ring. A large, boldly drawn Strengthening sign sits at the west-northwest, rotated well off upright. A Cooling sign sits at the southwest, slightly rotated. A small Repetition sign sits at the south-southeast with its top toward the center. The signs crowd the upper right, and the west and south are sparse. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Rain summons the water as falling rain. The two Dispersion signs make it pour or leak outward instead of forming a beam. Because the signs cluster on the north and east, that outflow leans toward the north-northeast. Cooling chills the water. Strengthening makes the material harder and more durable. Repetition keeps resetting affected material to its earlier state, which pulls against both the chilling and the hardening. A single small Windows sign cannot line the ring, so it adds at most a weak link to another space. With no decorative sigil present, Mimicry has nothing to copy and contributes little. The seal stacks well over three unrelated kinds of modifier: dispersal, cooling, strengthening, resetting, linking and mimicry. The water sigil, Rain and the paired Dispersion signs dominate. Cooling and Strengthening are secondary, and Repetition works against them, so the result is likely unstable.
effect: Summons a moderate, chilly rain that spills outward mostly toward the north-northeast, falling unevenly in gusts rather than as a steady shower. Some drops briefly stiffen into hard beads and then snap back to plain water. The rainfall sputters and breaks off early instead of settling into a lasting downpour.

name: s42_00130.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A light sigil, a diamond set inside a square with four short spokes, sits at the center at moderate size relative to the ring. A Pulling sign sits at the north-northwest with its arrowhead toward the ring and its shaft toward the center, so it is inverted. Two Glaives signs appear. One at the east has its prongs toward the ring and its stem toward the center. A smaller one at the southeast has its prongs toward the center. A Windows sign, a small hatched ring, sits at the south. A four-lobed Billow sign sits near the ring at the south-southwest. A Binding sign, two nested arcs, sits at the west-southwest, rotated so its arcs open toward the center. Most signs cluster on the southern half, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil makes this a light spell, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Pulling is directional, and with its arrow pointing outward it is inverted, so it pushes away from the seal toward the north-northwest instead of pulling in. Glaives set how deeply magic embeds itself into flesh, so the two Glaives drive the light into living bodies. Windows connects two spaces that are not physically joined. Billow turns material into a fluffy cloud. Binding halts movement and binds material into a single unit, which directly contradicts the outward push of the inverted Pulling. The seal stacks five unrelated kinds of modifier: pushing, embedding, linking spaces, cloud-forming and binding. The light sigil dominates as the core. The southern cluster of Windows, Billow and Binding outweighs the lone Pulling because the signs lean south, and the two Glaives add a strong embedding pull. With this many conflicting parts, the result is likely unstable.
effect: Produces a moderately bright light that shoves outward toward the north-northwest while much of it bunches into a hazy, cloud-like glow toward the south. The glow flickers in and out as if slipping somewhere else and tries to sink into flesh and hold its target still. Because these pulls work against each other, the light wavers, acts unevenly and collapses well before any steady effect forms.

name: s42_00131.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain white background, with the main ring closed and neatly drawn. A fire sigil sits upright at the center and is fairly large relative to the ring. Eight Projection signs, each a flat bracket with its open side facing the center, surround it in two loose bands. Four sit about two thirds of the way out, at the west-northwest, northeast, east-southeast and south-southwest. Four more sit close to the ring, at the east-northeast, southeast, south and west-southwest. More of them crowd the southern and eastern side, so the arrangement leans toward the south-southeast. A smaller sub-seal sits outside the main ring at the north-northwest and is joined to it by a short line. Its ring is closed but drawn a little roughly, and it holds a neatly drawn light sigil at its center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil makes this a fire spell. It is fairly large relative to the ring, so the flame or heat is fairly strong. Projection pushes a given effect outward from the seal, so the fire is cast away from it rather than held at its surface. Having eight Projection signs strengthens that outward push. Because the signs are unevenly placed and cluster toward the south-southeast, the projection is biased in that direction rather than spreading equally. The attached sub-seal carries a light sigil, which falls within the fire domain, so it adds a glow to the projected fire. Its slightly rough ring makes that glow a little weaker and shorter-lived than the main effect. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing in the seal works against itself.
effect: Casts a fairly strong flame and heat outward from the seal, mostly toward the south-southeast, with less reaching the other sides. The fire carries a glow that is slightly dimmer and fades sooner than the flame itself.

name: s42_00132.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background, ring closed and drawn slightly rough. There is no element sigil. A Dancing Puppets sign sits at the center, an inner ring with four small circles and crossing strokes. It is small relative to the ring and a little rough. Four Envelopment signs, each a slanted stroke with short hooks at both ends, sit near the ring at the northwest, northeast, southeast and southwest. The northwest one is neat and the others are slightly rough. Three Reflection signs, each an hourglass of two triangles meeting at a point, are also present. One sits at the north and one at the south, both about halfway out from the center and standing upright. The third sits at the west, close to the ring, turned on its side and drawn heavier than the rest. There is no matching sign at the east. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no sigil, Dancing Puppets takes the center and sets the core behavior: control over a target's movement. Without a wind sigil, it does not make the target fly. Reflection draws on a reflected image found on the object the seal is drawn on, so the moving target is that reflection rather than the object itself. The four Envelopment signs make the effect surround whatever they target, so the animated reflection wraps around the object instead of staying at one point. The Envelopment signs and the north and south Reflections are evenly placed. The lone west Reflection sits farther out and is drawn heavier, which may weight the effect slightly toward the west side, though how this sign behaves when turned or moved is unknown. The seal uses only three kinds of modifier, and they work together without contradiction. The small central sign and the slightly rough linework give a modest effect that holds less steadily and lasts less long than a clean seal would.
effect: Takes the reflection on the object's surface and wraps it around the object as a moving image that can be made to shift and dance. The animated reflection is faint and wavers a little, leans slightly to the west, and fades sooner than expected.

name: s42_00133.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A large Gathering sign, an upright double chevron on a short stem, sits at the center in place of a sigil, reaching nearly half the ring's radius. Six Collection signs surround it, spaced fairly evenly. Four of them, at the east, south-southeast, south-southwest and north-northwest, have their barred end toward the center and their open side facing the ring. The other two, at the north and west, sit closer to the ring and face the other way, with the barred end toward the ring and the open side facing inward. There is no element sigil, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the Gathering sign at the center acts as the core and draws material in from the seal's surroundings. Its large size relative to the ring makes that draw strong. Collection normally faces inward and collects material above and around the seal for the spell to use. The north and west signs follow that usual orientation and feed material inward. The other four face outward, which reverses that orientation. As a guess, they would release or push gathered material back out instead of holding it. Inward-facing and outward-facing Collection signs directly contradict each other. The strong central Gathering and the four outward Collection signs dominate the two inward ones, so the result is likely unstable. Because the signs are spread evenly, the spell favors no direction, and it works on whatever loose material is nearby rather than on a single element.
effect: Forcefully draws loose material such as dust, sand or debris from all around toward the seal, but most of it is thrown back out almost as soon as it arrives. The material churns in an uneven, swirling heap around the seal that never settles or builds into a lasting pile.

name: s42_00135.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed and neatly drawn, though slightly uneven in its roundness. A Stability and Level Planes sign, three wavy vertical strokes, sits upright at the center in place of a sigil and is small relative to the ring. There is no element sigil. Six signs surround it. A Diamond sign sits at the northeast, a little over halfway to the ring. A Stillness sign sits near the ring at the southwest, with its top toward the center. A Link sign sits at the south-southeast, rotated and drawn a little roughly. A Coil sign sits at the south-southwest, upright toward the center and a little rough. A Solidification sign, two small circles joined by a line, sits close to the ring at the west-northwest, with its top toward the ring. A small Piercing sign sits near the ring at the north-northwest, angled and a little rough. The signs are spread evenly around the ring, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, Stability and Level Planes takes the center and sets the core behavior: the target balances on a level plane in the air. The spell is not tied to one element and acts on whatever material is present. Its small size gives a modest intensity. Diamond limits the effect to the objects held within the container the seal is drawn on, not the container itself. Stillness holds the effect static in one place. Solidification makes the affected material more solid. Link ties together pieces that come from the same source. Coil softens physical matter, which directly contradicts Solidification. Piercing makes the target manifest as a projectile, which works against Stillness. The seal stacks six unrelated kinds of modifier and contains two direct contradictions. The neatly drawn central sign, Diamond, Stillness and Solidification dominate. The rougher Coil, Link and Piercing signs are weaker and act only intermittently. Because the signs are evenly spaced, no direction is favored. The result is likely unstable.
effect: Lifts the contents of the object it is drawn on into a modest, level floating layer and holds them in place, firming them up, while leaving the object itself unaffected. The hold wavers. The floating material alternately stiffens and goes soft, and pieces from the same source drift toward one another. Now and then a fragment jerks loose and shoots off as a small projectile, and the layer collapses sooner than a stable seal would.

name: s42_00136.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background. The main ring is closed but drawn roughly and noticeably out of round, with a lumpy, uneven outline. A large Pointing sign sits upright at the center in place of a sigil and is a little rough. Six smaller Pointing signs are spaced evenly about two thirds of the way to the ring, at the north, northeast, east-southeast, south, west-southwest and west-northwest. Each has its top turned toward the center, and most are drawn roughly; the west-southwest one is heavier and blotchier than the rest. Three smaller sub-seals sit outside the main ring, each joined to it by a short line. The north sub-seal has an open ring with a neat Coil sign at its center. The east-southeast sub-seal has a closed ring holding a slightly rough water sigil. The west-southwest sub-seal has a closed ring holding a neat, upright Levitation sign. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The main ring holds no element sigil, so the attached water sub-seal supplies the material and the spell acts on water; that sigil is about half its small ring, giving moderate strength within a modest sub-seal. Pointing is non-directional and makes the target manifest in a conical shape that other signs can then direct. With seven Pointing signs, including the large central one, the water is formed into several tapered cones, and because they are evenly spaced no side is favored. The closed Levitation sub-seal floats the target into the air. Drawn upright, it lifts the cones upward. The Coil sub-seal would soften solid matter, but its ring is open, so it adds nothing, and Coil does not act on liquids in any case. Only shaping and levitation are active, and they do not conflict. The rough linework weakens and shortens the effect. The main ring is not round enough, so the effect is fleeting and may fail to activate.
effect: Draws water into a small cluster of uneven, tapered cones that float upward above the seal, wobbling and losing shape as they rise and falling apart after only a moment, if they form at all. The softening part adds nothing while it is left unfinished.

name: s42_00137.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black line on a white background. It has two concentric rings, both closed and drawn somewhat out of round, with an empty band between them. A fire sigil sits upright at the center, drawn roughly and small to moderate relative to the ring. Six Dancing Puppets signs surround it, each a small ring with four loops and crossing strokes. They sit at the north, east, southeast, south-southwest, west-southwest and northwest, at varying distances from the center. Their sizes and line weights vary: the north and west-southwest signs are larger and heavier, the east sign is cleaner, and most are drawn roughly. No other signs are present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and manipulates flame and heat. Its modest size relative to the ring gives a moderate intensity at most. Dancing Puppets lets the movement of the spell's target be manipulated, so flames set loose in the air dart around. Paired with fire, this should make the flames move freely. The six signs are spread evenly around the center, and no directional sign sets a course. The motion therefore favors no side and stays erratic. The second ring carries no signs of its own and adds no separate effect. All the modifiers are of one kind and do not conflict, so the seal is not unstable. The rough linework on the sigil and most signs, along with the slightly out-of-round rings, weakens the spell and shortens its life.
effect: Produces modest flames that dart and flit erratically through the air with no set direction. The flames flicker unevenly as they move and burn out fairly quickly.

name: s42_00142.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes, sits upright at the center and is moderate in size, a little over a third of the ring's radius. Four bracket-shaped signs sit just inside the ring, each with its bar toward the ring and its open side facing the center. Three are Projection signs, at the west-northwest, north and east-southeast; the east-southeast one is slightly rough. The fourth, at the south-southwest, is a Projection-like bracket with an extra dot on its inner side. About two thirds of the way out, three more Projection signs at the west-southwest, north and east-northeast face the opposite way, with their bars toward the center and open sides facing the ring; the north one is slightly rough. Two Entwining signs sit at the same middle distance, at the northwest and southeast, each with its top toward the center. The signs are balanced around the ring, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil makes this a spell that moves and manipulates air, and its moderate size gives moderate strength. Projection pushes an effect outward from the seal, so the outer ring of Projection signs casts the moving air away from it. The dotted bracket matches no known sign exactly. Its closest match is Projection, so reading it that way is a guess, and the dot adds nothing known. On that reading there are four outward-casting signs near the ring. The three inner Projection signs are flipped relative to the outer ones. Read as reversed Projection, they draw the air back toward the seal, which directly contradicts the outer set. The outer four outnumber them and sit nearer the ring, so the outward push dominates, but the opposing pull makes the result likely unstable. Entwining makes an effect wrap around other objects, so the projected currents coil around whatever they meet. The balanced layout favors no direction. The two slightly rough signs weaken the push a little on the east-southeast and north sides.
effect: Sends moderate gusts of wind outward from the seal in all directions, curling around and winding about any objects they meet. Part of the air keeps being drawn back toward the seal, so the gusts pulse and waver instead of blowing steadily. They come through slightly weaker toward the east-southeast and north.

name: s42_00143.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with the ring closed and neatly drawn. A fire sigil sits upright at the center. It is large, reaching about half the ring's radius, and its lines are slightly rough. Four Levitation signs sit about two thirds of the way out, at the north-northeast, east, south-southwest and west. Each has its arrowhead toward the ring and its barred end toward the center. The west one is drawn roughly and the others slightly roughly. Two Convergence triangles sit at the west-northwest and the southeast, each with one point toward the ring rather than toward the center. The west-northwest one is neat and the southeast one is drawn heavily and roughly. The signs are spread evenly around the ring, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and shapes flame or heat. Its large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect. Levitation floats the magic into the air, and when the signs are balanced it tends to shape the result into a sphere. Here four are spread evenly with their arrows outward, so no direction wins and the fire is lifted and rounded above the seal rather than sent anywhere. Convergence normally has a point facing inward and pulls the magic together to a single point, packing it tight. Both of these face outward instead. Reading that as an inversion is a guess. Read that way, they loosen the flame instead of focusing it, so the ball is diffuse rather than dense. This loosening does not oppose the lifting, and only two kinds of modifier are present, so the seal is not unstable. The rough sigil and the rough Levitation and Convergence signs make the effect weaker and shorter-lived than the sigil's size alone suggests.
effect: Raises a large, strong ball of fire that floats above the seal, its flames loose and spread out rather than tightly packed. The sphere wavers and flickers unevenly at its edges and burns out sooner than its size would suggest.

name: s42_00144.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. At the center is an earth sigil of moderate size relative to the ring, with a small Rain sign attached to its left side. Two Columns signs sit in the lower half, one at the south-southeast and one at the south-southwest. Each has its stem toward the center and its crossbar toward the ring. A Gathering sign sits at the north-northwest, about halfway out, pointing outward toward the ring. Just beyond it, near the ring, is a small, slightly rough Billow sign. A larger, slightly rough Billow sign sits near the ring at the west. A roughly drawn Pulling sign sits near the ring at the east, its arrowhead pointing inward toward the center. A Collection sign sits at the north-northeast with its open side facing the center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell works on solid matter such as soil, sand and stone. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. The attached Rain sign summons that material, bringing it down from above in a rain-like fall. Collection, Gathering and the inward-pointing Pulling sign all draw material toward the seal. Collection takes in what lies above and around it, Gathering actively draws it in, and Pulling drags it in from the east. The two Billow signs turn that gathered material into fluffy clouds, as in a sand-to-cloud seal. Both Columns signs sit on the south side, so the column of magic is pushed toward the south instead of rising straight up. The seal stacks four unrelated kinds of modifier: drawing material in, billowing, a southward column, and rain-like summoning. The inward pull also works against the outward push of the Columns. The earth sigil, the material-gathering signs and Billow dominate. The column and the rain-like fall are secondary, so the result is likely unstable. The rough Pulling sign and the slightly rough Billow signs further weaken their parts of the effect.
effect: Draws loose soil and sand in from around the seal, most strongly from the east, and puffs it into soft, billowing clouds of earth. The clouds are pushed off toward the south in a leaning column and shed grains back down like a light rain. Because the inward pull fights the southward push, the clouds form unevenly, waver, and thin out sooner than they should.

name: s42_00146.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background, ring closed and neatly drawn. Two sigils sit side by side at the center, both small relative to the ring: a water sigil on the left and a fire sigil on the right, both upright. A small Concealment sign, an eight-armed star with eye marks on its arms, sits at the south-southwest about two thirds of the way from the center to the ring. Five Aeriforms Defined signs, each three short strokes with the longest in the middle, sit just inside the ring at the north-northeast, east, southeast, west-southwest and northwest, each with its top toward the ring. The ones at the north-northeast, west-southwest and northwest are drawn a little more roughly and heavily than the others. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water and fire sigils share the center as a double core, so the spell works on water and heat together, which turns the water warm and into vapor. Both sigils are small relative to the ring, so the intensity is modest. Aeriforms Defined is tied to gases and shares its design with the wind sigil's modifiers, so the five of them push the heated water into a gaseous form around the seal. They are evenly spaced, so the vapor spreads out on all sides with no favored direction. The Concealment sign hides a target, so the vapor serves to hide what lies within it. Only two kinds of modifier are present and they work together, so the seal is not unstable. The three rougher Aeriforms Defined signs at the north-northeast, west-southwest and northwest make the effect weaker and shorter lived on those sides.
effect: Produces a modest cloud of warm steam that spreads evenly outward from the seal and hides whatever lies inside it. The mist is thinner toward the north-northeast, west-southwest and northwest, where it clears sooner and leaves gaps in the cover.

name: s42_00147.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed. The whole seal is drawn roughly, and the ring is lumpy and noticeably out of round. At the center sits a wind-family sigil variant: an S-curve inside a small circle, ringed by eight evenly spaced dots. It is large, reaching nearly half the ring's radius. Four signs sit about two thirds of the way out, one each at the north, east, south and west. The east and south signs are Collection signs. The north sign looks like Collection with an extra dot on one side, and the west sign looks like Collection with an extra stroke from its left edge. All four are rotated at different angles instead of having their open sides squarely toward the center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The S-curve sigil is a variant in the wind family, so the spell works on air. Its large size relative to the ring points to a fairly strong intensity. Collection lets a spell gather material above and around the seal for its use. The two unmarked Collection signs read directly. Reading the dotted and stroked variants as Collection is a guess, and on that reading they add the same gathering effect. The four signs are spread evenly around the ring, so no direction is favored and air is drawn in from all sides. Their uneven angles keep that pull from lining up cleanly. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing works against the sigil. The rough linework weakens and shortens the effect. Because the ring is not round enough, the effect is fleeting and may not activate at all.
effect: Draws the surrounding air in toward the seal from all sides in strong but uneven gusts that sputter and die out after a moment. It may fail to take hold at all.

name: s42_00148.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. Two concentric rings, both closed and slightly rough, with a wide empty band between them. A wind sigil sits upright at the center: an S-shaped spiral with short dashes on each side, moderate in size relative to the inner ring and drawn a little roughly. Seven Piercing signs sit about two thirds of the way from the center to the inner ring, at the north-northwest, northeast, east-northeast, east-southeast, south-southeast, southwest and west-northwest. Each is a short line through a small diamond and points roughly along the radius. Some have their tops toward the ring and others toward the center. The northeast sign is drawn heavier and less evenly than the rest, and the southwest one is slightly smaller. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves and manipulates existing air. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Piercing makes the target material manifest as projectiles or offensive attacks, and the number of Piercing signs sets how many projectiles form, so seven signs give seven. Piercing is non-directional, so the mix of signs facing the ring and signs facing the center changes nothing. There are no directional signs, and the seven signs are spread evenly around the ring, so no single direction is favored and the projectiles go out from the seal on all sides. The empty second ring adds strength to the core spell. The slightly rough rings and sigil make the effect somewhat weaker and shorter lived than a clean drawing would. The roughly drawn northeast sign makes the projectile on that side the least stable. Only one kind of modifier is present, so the seal is not unstable.
effect: Gathers the surrounding air into seven bolts that shoot outward from the seal in all directions with moderate force, then fade somewhat sooner than they should. The bolt on the northeast side forms raggedly and hits more weakly and unevenly than the other six.

name: s42_00150.png
