description: A fully visible seal on a plain background. The ring is closed but drawn roughly and noticeably out of round, with flattened sides and bulging corners like a lumpy rounded square. A fire sigil sits upright at the center, drawn in heavy strokes and large relative to the ring, reaching about half of its radius. Five Stretch signs surround it, each a horseshoe arc with short flicks at its ends. The curved top of each faces the center and the open side faces the ring. Three sit about midway out, at the east-southeast, southwest and north-northwest. Two sit farther out near the ring, at the west-northwest and north-northeast. Their line weights vary from thin to bold. A small Billow sign, a four-lobed clover, sits near the ring at the south. The signs are spread evenly around the seal. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and shapes flame and heat. Its large size relative to the ring would normally give a strong effect. Stretch draws what the spell acts on into long, flexible ribbons. With five of them around a fire sigil, the flame is pulled out into streamers instead of burning as a compact blaze. The single small Billow sign near the ring turns material into a soft, fluffy cloud, so part of the flame puffs into a loose billow. Five Stretch signs against one small Billow means the ribbon shaping dominates. Only two kinds of modifier are present, so the seal is not unstable. No directional sign is present and the signs are balanced, so the effect spreads evenly around the seal instead of leaning one way. The rough linework weakens the spell and shortens its life. Because the ring is not round enough, the effect is fleeting, and the seal may fail to activate at all.
effect: Throws out long, flexible ribbons of flame that unfurl evenly around the seal, with a few soft puffs of billowing fire near the edge. Despite their initial strength, the ribbons flicker and sputter unevenly and die out after a moment, if they catch at all.

name: s42_00151.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The main ring is closed but drawn a little roughly and slightly out of round. An earth sigil sits at the center, roughly drawn and moderate in size relative to the ring. Seven signs sit around it, mostly near the ring. A Stillness sign is at the north-northeast, facing outward. A Solidification sign, two small circles joined by a line, is at the east-northeast. An inverted Crushing sign, a zigzag, is at the east-southeast. A Collection sign is at the south-southeast. A second Stillness sign is at the west-southwest, facing inward. A small Billow sign is at the northwest, and a larger Billow sign sits closer to the center at the south-southwest. All signs are roughly drawn and spread evenly around the ring. Two smaller closed rings, both neatly drawn, sit outside the main ring and are joined to it by short lines. The one at the west-northwest holds a large wind sigil, and the one at the east-southeast holds a large earth sigil. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on solid matter such as soil, sand and stone. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity, and the rough drawing weakens it further. Collection draws in material from above and around the seal. The two Billow signs, one drawn large, turn that material into a soft cloud. Against this, Solidification makes the material more solid, and inverted Crushing pulls crushed material back toward its original form. Both push toward rigid, packed matter and directly contradict Billow's fluffiness. The two Stillness signs hold the effect static in one place. The signs are balanced, so no direction is favored. The neat wind sub-seal adds moving air that stirs the mass, and the neat earth sub-seal reinforces the earth magic. Billow and Collection dominate, with Solidification and inverted Crushing fighting them and Stillness pinning the result in place. Because these parts contradict each other and the main seal is roughly drawn, the result is likely unstable and short-lived.
effect: Gathers loose soil and sand around the seal into a cloud-like mass held in place above it, stirred by moving air. The mass keeps lurching between fluffy and hard-packed, clumping in patches and puffing apart in others. It soon collapses back into loose grit.

name: s42_00152.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but drawn a little rough and slightly out of round. A Dancing Puppets sign sits upright at the center, neatly drawn and moderate in size, reaching a bit under half of the ring's radius. It is an inner ring with four small circles at the north, east, south and west, crossed by short curved strokes. Its own center is empty, with no sigil inside it. Six Solidification signs, each two small circles joined by a short line, sit near the ring. They are at the north-northwest, east-northeast, east-southeast, south-southeast, west-southwest and west-northwest positions. Four are drawn with one end toward the center, and the ones at the east-southeast and west-northwest are turned the other way. The east-southeast sign is drawn with a heavier line than the others. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: No element sigil is present, and none sits inside the center of Dancing Puppets. Dancing Puppets therefore serves as the core and sets the behavior: it lets the target object's movement be consciously manipulated. Without a wind sigil it has no element to carry the object through the air, so it moves the object directly. The six Solidification signs make the magic connected to the seal more solid. The target becomes firm and rigid instead of loose or limp. Solidification is symmetric end to end, so the two signs turned the other way do not change its effect. The six signs are spread evenly around the ring, so no direction is favored and the motion has no set heading. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they support each other, so the seal is not unstable. The slightly rough, out-of-round ring makes the effect somewhat weaker and shorter lived.
effect: Stiffens the object the seal is drawn on into a firm, rigid form that can be moved and steered like a puppet. The motion is not lifted through the air and follows no set direction. The stiffening and control are somewhat weak, slip at moments, and wear off sooner than usual.

name: s42_00153.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background, ring closed but drawn roughly and noticeably out of round, closer to a rounded square than a circle. A fire sigil sits upright at the center, about a third of the ring's radius in size, with rough linework. Near the ring are four signs, all drawn roughly. Two are Coil signs: one at the west, lying sideways with its top toward the ring, and a smaller, fainter one at the south-southwest, also with its top toward the ring. A Binding sign, two nested arcs, sits at the west-northwest with its top toward the center. At the southeast is a small, faint glyph resembling a Gathering sign with a small circle on its stem, rotated to lie almost sideways. Most of the signs crowd the western and southwestern side, and the north and east are empty. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell works through heat and flame. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Coil softens physical matter and cannot affect liquids or gases, so with fire it acts as heat that softens solid material rather than burning it. Two Coil signs strengthen that softening. Binding halts the movement of the target material and makes it act as a single unit, so the softened matter is held together as one mass. The southeast glyph matches no known sign. Its closest match is Gathering, so reading it that way is a guess. As Gathering, it draws material in from the surroundings for the spell to use, and the small circle on its stem may tighten that pull. These three kinds of modifier, softening, binding and gathering, complement each other and do not contradict. Most signs sit on the west and southwest, so the effect is weighted toward that side. The rough linework weakens the spell and shortens its life. Because the ring is not round enough, the effect is fleeting and may fail to activate at all.
effect: Gives off a modest, uneven heat that softens nearby solid material, draws it in, and works it into a single pliable mass, acting most strongly toward the southwest. The warmth sputters and the material only partly fuses before the spell gives out after a few moments, and it may fail to start at all.

name: s42_00155.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background, ring closed and drawn a little roughly. A fire sigil sits upright at the center and is fairly large, reaching a little under half the ring's radius. A Rain sign sits at the north, a little over halfway to the ring, drawn in its normal orientation: a square with concave sides and short rays on each side. A Launch sign sits at the east, about two thirds of the way out, its apex pointing east toward the ring. A smaller Rain sign sits at the west-southwest. It is drawn roughly and turned inside out, with its points facing outward, so it reads as inverted. The signs are unbalanced and lean toward the north. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and shapes flame and heat. Its fairly large size relative to the ring gives a strong intensity. Rain summons the spell's material, and when it surrounds or accompanies a sigil it brings that material down like rainfall, so the normal Rain at the north calls down fire. Rain is semi-directional, and turned inside out it reverses its effect. The inverted Rain at the west-southwest creates an area where the material cannot exist or is pushed away. These two directly contradict each other. The normal Rain is larger, cleaner and sits on the heavier northern side, so it dominates, while the small, rough inverted Rain carves a weaker repelling patch on its side. Launch is directional and sends the material out in a powerful but brief burst toward where it points, which here is east. With two Rain signs working against each other, the result is likely unstable. The slightly rough ring and signs further weaken it and shorten its life.
effect: Throws a strong but brief burst of flame eastward, then lets it fall back as an uneven shower of fire that is heaviest toward the north. The fire sputters and is pushed out of a patch to the west-southwest, so the rain of flame flickers and gaps unpredictably and dies out sooner than it otherwise would.

name: s42_00158.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed and neatly drawn. There is no element sigil. A large Regions sign, a thick upright chevron about half the ring's radius, sits at the center pointing north, with slightly rough linework. A heavily drawn Strengthening sign sits near the ring at the north-northeast. Two Convergence triangles are present. One sits near the ring at the west-southwest with a point facing in toward the center. The other sits about halfway out at the east-northeast, rotated so its point faces roughly east, away from the center. A small, neatly drawn Dispersion sign sits near the ring at the south-southeast, tilted, with its stem angled in toward the center and its curve facing outward. Most of the signs crowd the eastern half of the seal. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the spell is not tied to fire, water, earth or wind and works on whatever material reaches it. The Regions sign takes the center and, being directional and large, dominates the seal: it sends the magic out toward the north, where it points. Strengthening makes the result harder and more durable. The inward-facing Convergence focuses the magic down to a single point and packs loose particles tightly. The outward-facing Convergence and the Dispersion sign work against it, since Dispersion makes magic pour outward instead of focusing. Focusing and pouring out contradict each other directly, and the seal stacks four kinds of modifier: direction, strengthening, convergence and dispersion. The central Regions sets the direction. The two Convergence signs outweigh the single Dispersion, so focusing wins overall, but the result is likely unstable. Because the signs lean east, the effect drifts east of north.
effect: Draws whatever material reaches the seal into a hardened, tightly packed point and drives it north, drifting toward the northeast. The point keeps loosening and leaking outward in uneven spurts, wavering as it goes, and it breaks apart before it fully hardens.

name: s42_00159.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in thin black line on a white background. The ring is neatly drawn but open, with a wide gap at the upper right between roughly the north-northeast and east-northeast. No element sigil is present. The center holds a single wide arc, open side facing north like a shallow bowl, spanning about half the ring's radius. Four signs sit roughly two thirds of the way out, spaced evenly. At the north-northeast is a small stick-like glyph resembling a Gathering sign with a small circle on its stem. At the east-southeast is a slim triangle tapering to a point toward the center, with a small circle crossed by a line at its outer end; it matches no known sign. At the south-southwest and west-northwest are two Sights Set signs, each with its diamond end toward the ring and its arrow pointing in toward the center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the central arc acts as the core. It matches no known sign exactly. Its closest match is Binding drawn with a single curve, so reading it as Binding is a guess. Binding halts the movement of target material and holds it together so it acts and moves as one unit. Its large size relative to the ring gives the binding moderate strength. The north-northeast glyph is read as Gathering, also a guess, so the spell actively draws material in from its surroundings. The east-southeast triangle points inward and is closest to Convergence, another guess. That reading packs the gathered material tightly toward a single point and makes loose particles somewhat rigid. The two Sights Set signs let the caster aim the effect, and both arrows point inward toward the center. Gathering, converging and aiming are compatible kinds of modifier, and the signs are evenly spaced, so the seal acts steadily once active. Without a sigil, the spell is not tied to any element and works on whatever loose material lies around it. The open ring keeps the seal from activating.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it draws loose material from around the seal inward toward its center and packs it into a firm, single mass that holds together and moves as one piece. The caster can aim where that mass gathers, and the binding holds with moderate strength.

name: s42_00162.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background. The main ring is closed and drawn a little roughly. A small Coil sign, two thin arcs crossing at top and bottom, sits upright at the center, about a quarter of the ring radius, with no element sigil beside it. Five Repetition signs, each a small circle with an inner curl and dot crossed by a diagonal stroke, sit near the ring at the north-northeast, northwest, west-southwest, south-southwest and southeast, each with its top toward the center. The south-southwest one is drawn heavier than the others. One Entwining sign sits near the ring at the east-northeast, roughly drawn and turned almost upside down so that it lies on its side. Two small closed sub-seals sit inside the main ring. The one at the north-northwest holds a Collection sign and the one at the south-southeast holds a wind sigil. Both glyphs are large relative to their own rings. The signs are spread evenly around the ring, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil in the main ring, Coil at the center sets the core behavior. It softens solid matter but cannot act on liquids or gases. Its small size keeps that softening mild. Repetition keeps resetting what the spell affects to its original state, like a spring, so softened material snaps back into shape instead of staying deformed. These two together make a soft object elastic. Five Repetition signs spaced evenly around the ring make this reset strong and give it no direction. Entwining makes the affected object wrap itself around other objects. There is only one, it is rough and turned on its side, and it is not a directional sign, so the wrapping is weak and has no set direction. The Collection sub-seal draws in material from above and around the seal for the spell to use. The wind sub-seal adds moving air, which carries the softened material toward what it wraps. Softening, elastic reset, wrapping and gathering all serve one purpose and do not contradict each other, so the seal is not unstable. The slightly rough ring and signs make it somewhat weaker and shorter-lived.
effect: Draws loose solid material from around the seal and softens it into a springy, elastic mass that keeps snapping back to its original shape. A light draft of air carries the mass so that it loosely wraps around nearby objects. The wrapping is weak and uneven, and the whole effect fades somewhat sooner than it would from a cleanly drawn seal.

name: s42_00164.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn neatly in black on a white background. The ring is open, with a gap at the east-southeast, and the center is empty with no element sigil. A Launch sign sits at the northwest, about three quarters of the way out, opening toward the ring. At the west, about halfway out, is a bracket shape like a Projection sign with its lower portion missing; its crossbar faces the center. An inverted Crushing zigzag sits near the ring at the east, its points facing the center. At the southeast is a ring-shaped glyph lined with diagonal hatch marks, like a Windows sign, with an extra dot on its edge, rotated about 202 degrees. Near the ring at the southwest is a circle crossed by a diagonal line, like an Orb sign, with an extra stroke running past its lower edge. The signs are unevenly spaced and weighted toward the southwest. Nothing is hidden or cut off.
justification: With no sigil, the seal is tied to no element and works only on material brought to it. Launch sends generated material out in a powerful but short-lived burst toward where it points, here outward to the northwest. Inverted Crushing pulls crushed material back into its original shape. The bracket is closest to Projection, a guess given its missing part, and would push the effect outward from the seal. The hatched ring is closest to Windows, also a guess, and would link this space to another location. The crossed circle is closest to Orb, another guess, and would gather material in a sphere above the seal. That is five unrelated kinds of modifier, and Orb's holding works against the outward push of Launch and Projection. Launch and inverted Crushing are the clearest glyphs and dominate, with Orb's pull adding to the southwest weighting, so the result is likely unstable.
effect: Once the ring is closed, material fed into the seal is briefly drawn back toward its original form and flung out in a sharp burst to the northwest. The reformed matter sags and partly pools toward the southwest instead of travelling cleanly, and the spell sputters with flickering, half-formed side effects before collapsing early.

name: s42_00167.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background. The ring is open, with a wide gap at the upper right between the north and east points. A water sigil sits upright at the center and is moderate in size relative to the ring. A large Strengthening sign sits near the ring at the east point. Three Refuse signs sit at the north, west and south points with their diamond ends toward the center and crossed legs toward the ring. The north one is drawn a little less tidily than the others. Two smaller Refuse signs sit closer to the ring at the southeast and northwest, facing the other way with their diamond ends toward the ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Refuse is directional and collects unwanted material toward where it points. The three larger inward-facing Refuse signs draw waste toward the center of the seal. The two smaller outward-facing ones push waste out toward the southeast and northwest edges. These opposing Refuse signs contradict each other. The three larger inward signs dominate the two smaller outward ones, so the result is likely unstable, with some waste slipping outward instead of collecting. The slightly rough north sign pulls a little more weakly than the west and south ones. Strengthening makes the water firmer and more durable, so it holds together while the waste is sorted. The ring is open, so the seal will not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it gathers water and draws the waste in it toward the center, with a weaker pull from the north than from the west and south. Some of that waste drifts unevenly out toward the southeast and northwest edges instead, so the separation wavers and stays incomplete. The water holds together firmly and does not scatter while this happens.

name: s42_00168.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn neatly in black on a white background. The ring is open, with a wide gap at the bottom. There is no element sigil. A large, boldly drawn Entwining sign sits upright at the center, about half the ring's radius in size. Five Cooling signs, each a short slanted stroke between two pairs of dots, surround it. Three sit about halfway to the ring, at the west-northwest, southwest and northeast. Two sit close to the ring, at the northwest and southeast. More signs cluster on the western side than the eastern side. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, Entwining takes the center as the core of the spell. It makes the object the seal is drawn on wrap or twine itself around other objects, and its large size makes that grip strong. Cooling cools things down. It is not directional, so the uneven placement does not steer the spell, but the heavier cluster on the west-northwest side concentrates the chill there. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they complement each other, so the seal is not unstable. The neat linework supports a steady effect, but the seal will not activate until the ring is closed.
effect: Once the ring is closed, the object it is drawn on wraps itself firmly around nearby objects and chills whatever it holds. The cold is unevenly spread, strongest on its west-northwest side and milder toward the east.

name: s42_00171.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background. The ring is closed but drawn roughly and noticeably out of round, with a lumpy, almost polygonal outline. A light sigil sits at the center, drawn a little roughly and small relative to the ring, reaching about a quarter of the way to it. Five Launch signs, each a caret shape, sit about halfway to the ring. Those at the north-northwest, east-southeast and southwest have their peaks pointing in toward the center. The one at the northeast is rotated to point roughly west, across the ring. The one at the southeast is rotated to point back and sideways. The northeast and southeast Launch signs are drawn with heavy, uneven strokes, and only the north-northwest one is neat. A small four-lobed Billow sign sits near the ring at the northwest. A Binding sign, two stacked arcs bulging outward, sits near the ring at the south. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil makes this a light spell. Its small size gives modest intensity, and light from this sigil diminishes over time. Launch generates the effect in the direction it points, as a powerful but short-lived burst. Three Launch signs point inward and the signs are balanced overall, so their bursts meet over the center and rise as one upward surge rather than favoring a side. The two rotated Launch signs point across the ring instead of at the center, which pushes the burst off-line and gives it a sideways wobble. Billow turns material into a fluffy cloud, so the light takes a soft, puffy form instead of a beam. Binding makes the effect act and move as a single unit, so the puff holds together as one clump. Launch dominates by number, with Billow shaping and Binding holding the result. These three kinds of modifier work together. The rough linework and uneven ring make the whole effect weaker and more fleeting.
effect: Throws a single soft, puffy clump of light upward from the seal in a quick burst. It wobbles off-line as it rises and gives off only a modest glow. It dims and breaks off early, after a brief flare.

name: s42_00173.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background, drawn neatly with two concentric closed rings. An Entwining sign sits upright at the center, fairly large relative to the inner ring. Four Strengthening signs, each a triangle crossed by a bar, are spaced evenly about halfway to the ring at the north-northeast, east-southeast, south-southwest and west-northwest. Each is rotated to a different angle as it follows the circle. A short line runs from the top of the outer ring to a small sub-seal at the north. Its ring is closed but drawn roughly and somewhat out of round, close to a rounded hexagon. An earth sigil sits at its center, drawn a little roughly and large relative to that small ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The main seal has no element sigil, so the Entwining sign at the center acts as its core. Entwining makes the object the seal is drawn on wrap itself around other objects. Strengthening makes objects stronger, harder and more durable. The four Strengthening signs are evenly balanced, so they reinforce the wrapping on all sides without pushing it in any direction. The second ring adds strength to the core spell. The joined sub-seal brings in an earth sigil, which works on solid matter such as stone, wood, sand and soil. That sigil is large for its ring, but the sub-seal itself is small, rough and not round enough, so its contribution is weak and fleeting and may fail to activate. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they support each other without contradiction.
effect: Makes the object it is drawn on wind tightly around nearby objects, and hardens that grip so it holds firm and resists tearing. It also tries to draw stone, soil or other solid matter into the wrap, but that earthen part is weak, flickers and may give out early, while the hardened wrapping itself stays steady.

name: s42_00174.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed and neatly drawn. There is no element sigil. An upright Envelopment sign, a slanted stroke with short hooks at both ends, sits at the center at moderate size relative to the ring. Six Concealment signs, each an eight-armed star with small eye marks on four of its arms, surround it. One sits at the north about halfway out and one at the south about halfway out. One sits at the west-northwest and one at the east-southeast, a little farther out. Two more sit close to the ring at the north-northwest and south-south-east. These two outer signs are drawn larger and heavier than the rest, and several of the signs are slightly rough. The signs are spread evenly around the ring, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the central Envelopment sign serves as the core of the seal. It makes the spell's effect envelop and surround whatever it targets. The six Concealment signs supply that effect, which is hiding the target. Their even spread around the ring favors no side, so the concealment wraps the target uniformly rather than covering one part. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they reinforce each other without contradiction. The moderate size of the central sign gives a moderate strength. The slight roughness of several Concealment signs makes the effect a little weaker and shorter lived, though the neat, closed ring lets the seal activate reliably.
effect: Wraps the object it is drawn on, and anything that object covers, in an even shroud of concealment that hides it from view on all sides. The cover is moderately strong but thins slightly in places and fades somewhat sooner than a cleanly drawn version would.

name: s42_00175.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but noticeably uneven and out of round. A wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes, sits upright at the center and is moderate in size relative to the ring. Three Link signs sit near the ring at the east, south-southeast and north-northwest, each turned so its top faces the center. The east Link is drawn roughly, and the other two are slightly rough. At the west, near the ring, sits a small, lightly drawn octagon with an X inside that matches no known sign exactly. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves and manipulates existing air rather than creating it. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. The three Link signs identify things that broke off from, or were made from, the same source and link them, and they all face inward in the same way. The octagon with an X is closest to Selection, a cross drawn through an enclosing shape, so this reading is a guess. Read as Selection, it confines the spell's effect to the object the seal is drawn on. The signs are spread evenly around the ring, so no direction is favored. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they do not contradict each other. The ring is not very round and the Link signs are roughly drawn, so the effect is weak and fleeting and may fail to activate.
effect: Stirs a faltering current of air around the object the seal is drawn on that nudges it toward pieces broken from the same source, pulling them back together without favoring any direction. The current gusts unevenly, may fail to start at all, and dies away after a few moments.

name: s42_00177.png
description: A fully visible seal on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. Two sigils share the center, each about a quarter of the ring radius: a water sigil just left of center and a light sigil just right of it. Seven signs surround them. At the north, close to the ring, is a Refuse sign with its diamond toward the center. At the north-northwest is a circle holding an S-curve, ringed by small dots, which resembles a wind sigil variant. A Billow sign sits at the west-northwest. A Partition sign sits near the ring at the northeast, facing outward. A rotated Pointing sign, drawn heavier than the rest, sits at the east. An inverted Rain sign, a four-pointed star with its strokes turned outward, sits near the ring at the southeast. An Aeriforms Defined sign, three slanted strokes, sits at the southwest. More signs crowd the north and northeast than the south. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell. The light sigil falls within the fire domain and adds a glow that diminishes over time. Both sigils are small relative to the ring, so the intensity is modest. The dotted, circled S matches no listed sign. Its closest match is the Whorling Wind sigil, so reading it as a whorl is a guess; on that reading it sets the air turning. Aeriforms Defined ties the spell to gases. Billow turns material into a fluffy cloud, so together these push the water toward a swirling, vaporous cloud. Pointing forces a conical shape, which works against Billow's soft cloud. Inverted Rain creates an area where the target cannot exist or is pushed away. Refuse, pointing toward the center, draws unwanted material inward, which works against Rain's push. Partition, facing outward, outlines the borders of the area of effect. The seal stacks well over three unrelated kinds of modifier, and two pairs directly contradict each other, so the result is likely unstable. The two sigils and the northern cluster of Refuse, the whorl glyph and Partition dominate, which pulls the effect toward the north-northeast.
effect: Forms a faintly glowing, swirling cloud of water mist that bulges unevenly toward the north-northeast, partly billowing soft and partly tapering into a lopsided cone. Water is shoved out of its southeast side while stray grit and debris are tugged toward its middle. The cloud wavers, its glow dims, and it collapses well before it settles into a steady shape.

name: s42_00178.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and drawn a little roughly. A water sigil sits upright at the center, small relative to the ring at about a quarter of its radius. Six zigzag Crushing signs are spread around the inside of the ring at the north-northwest, northeast, east, south-southeast, south-southwest and west-northwest. They are drawn at different rotations, and the one at the west-northwest is inverted. At the west-southwest sits a small, thinly drawn glyph shaped like a Gathering sign lying on its side, with a small circle on its stem. The signs are spread evenly around the ring, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell, and its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Crushing is semi-directional, so its rotation does not steer the spell, but inversion reverses it. The five normal Crushing signs break their target into smaller and smaller pieces, which for water means splitting it into fine droplets. The single inverted Crushing sign does the opposite and pulls broken material back together, so it directly contradicts the others. The five normal signs dominate, and the result is likely unstable. The glyph at the west-southwest matches no known sign exactly. It is closest to Gathering, so reading it that way is a guess. Read as Gathering, it actively draws water in from the surroundings to feed the spell. Because the signs are balanced around the ring, the effect has no favored direction. The slightly rough ring makes the spell somewhat weaker and shorter lived.
effect: Draws in nearby water and shatters it into a fine spray of droplets around the seal, but parts of the spray keep clumping back into larger drops, so the mist sputters and forms unevenly. The effect is modest in strength and fades somewhat sooner than a cleanly drawn seal would.

name: s42_00179.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background with two rings, one just inside the other. The outer ring is open, with a clear gap at the upper left, and both rings are drawn somewhat roughly and slightly out of round. A neatly drawn light sigil, a diamond inside a square with four short spokes, sits upright at the center and is moderate in size relative to the ring. Six Binding signs, each made of two nested arcs, are spaced evenly around the inside of the inner ring at about two thirds of the way out. They sit at the north-northeast, east-southeast, south-southeast, southwest, west and north-northwest. Each has its larger arc toward the center and its smaller arc toward the ring. The south-southeast sign is drawn a little more roughly than the rest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil makes this a light spell, and its moderate size relative to the ring gives a moderate intensity. Binding halts the movement of the target material and binds it together so it acts and moves as a single unit. With six Binding signs spread evenly and all facing the same way, no side is favored. The light is held still and gathered into one cohesive body instead of radiating freely or travelling in any direction. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing contradicts. The second ring adds strength to the core spell. The seal does not activate while the outer ring is open. Once it is closed, the rough, slightly out-of-round linework would weaken the spell and shorten its life, and light from this sigil naturally diminishes over time.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it gathers a moderate amount of light into a single still mass held fixed in place. The light holds together as one unit rather than spreading as a glow. It flickers a little and dims steadily, fading sooner than a cleanly drawn seal would.

name: s42_00182.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn neatly in black on a white background. The ring is open, with a gap at the lower right between the east-southeast and south points. A small upright fire sigil sits at the center, about a quarter of the ring's radius in size. Five Diamond signs surround it. Three sit close to the ring, at the north, east-southeast and west-southwest. Two sit closer to the center, at the northeast and south-southeast. Each diamond is tilted to point along a line out from the center. The signs are spread evenly around the seal, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil makes this a fire spell that creates and controls heat or flame. Its modest size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Diamond is the only modifier present. It most likely limits a spell to the contents of the container it is drawn on, leaving the container itself unaffected. Diamond is symmetric, so whether its top faces the ring or the center makes no clear difference. The five signs are evenly balanced, so no direction is favored. The signs at different distances spread the effect through the whole space inside the ring rather than focusing it at one depth. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing conflicts, and the neat drawing keeps the effect steady. The seal will not activate until the gap in the ring is closed.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it gives off a modest, steady heat that warms only the contents of the container it is drawn on, spread evenly throughout. The container itself stays cool.

name: s42_00183.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background with two concentric rings. The outer ring is open, with a gap running from the north to the east-northeast. The inner ring sits just inside it and also appears open, with a gap at the east. A water sigil sits upright at the center, about a third of the ring radius in size and drawn a little roughly. Three Refuse signs are present. One sits inside the inner ring at the northwest, about two thirds of the way out, drawn heavier than the others, with its diamond end toward the ring. A second sits on the outer ring at the west-southwest with its diamond end toward the center. A third sits at the east-northeast near the end of the outer ring's gap, also with its diamond end toward the center. The signs are unevenly spread and cluster toward the northwest side. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell. Its moderate size relative to the ring gives a moderate intensity, and its slightly rough drawing makes it somewhat weaker and shorter lived than a clean sigil. The second ring adds strength to the core spell. Refuse is a directional sign that collects unwanted material toward where it points. The two Refuse signs at the west-southwest and east-northeast point inward, so they draw waste from those sides toward the center. The northwest Refuse sign points outward, so it sends the collected waste out toward the northwest. Only one kind of modifier is used, and its orientations form a single path from the two sides, through the center, and out to the northwest, so the seal is not contradictory. The signs lean northwest, which biases the flow that way. Both rings are open, so nothing activates until they are closed.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it takes hold of water and pulls dirt and other waste out of it from the east-northeast and west-southwest toward the center. It then expels that waste toward the northwest, leaving the water cleaner. The cleansing is moderate in strength, runs a little unevenly, and fades somewhat sooner than a cleanly drawn seal would.

name: s42_00184.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background, ring closed. The ring is lumpy and noticeably out of round, closer to a rounded pentagon than a circle. A light sigil, a diamond inside a square with four short spokes, sits upright at the center and reaches about halfway to the ring. Three Cooling signs, each a short vertical stroke flanked by pairs of dots, sit at the north near the ring, at the south, and at the southwest. The southwest one is larger and tilted so its top faces the ring. Two Orb signs, each a circle crossed by a line, sit at the west and east. The western one is upright, and the eastern one has its line turned diagonally. Most strokes are slightly rough. The signs are weighted toward the southwest, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and shapes light. At about half the ring's radius it gives a moderately strong effect. Orb is non-directional and defines a spherical space above the seal where the spell's material collects, filling from the bottom. Two Orb signs give the light a rounded, contained form. Cooling cools things down, so the light comes out cool rather than warm, which fits light's place within the fire domain. Cooling and Orb are only two kinds of modifier and do not contradict each other. Neither sign is directional, so the southwest lean steers nothing, but the larger, heavier Cooling sign there makes that side the coldest. The out-of-round ring and rough linework weaken the seal and make its effect fleeting.
effect: Forms a sphere of moderately bright, cool light above the seal, pooled toward its lower half and coldest on its southwest side. The glow flickers unevenly, dims quickly, and gutters out much sooner than a steady lamp would.

name: s42_00186.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background. The ring is open, with a gap at the lower right between the south and east-southeast, and it is drawn a little roughly and slightly out of round. A small, neatly drawn fire sigil sits upright at the center. A neat Rain sign sits near the ring at the north-northeast. A large, heavy Regions chevron sits at the east-northeast with its point toward the ring. A roughly drawn Binding sign, two nested arcs turned on their side, sits at the east-southeast, closer to the center than the other signs. An Envelopment sign, a slanted stroke hooked at both ends, sits at the south-southeast just beside the ring gap. A small Pointing sign sits near the ring at the southwest. The signs cluster on the eastern side, leaving the west and northwest empty. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, and its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Rain summons the spell's material falling from above, so the fire comes down as a shower. The single Regions sign points outward at the east-northeast, so the magic manifests outside the ring and is sent that way. Binding would hold the material together as one unit, Envelopment would make it surround its target, and Pointing would shape it into a cone. Binding and Pointing pull against the scattered fall of Rain. The seal stacks five unrelated kinds of modifier: summoning, direction, binding, enveloping and shaping. The neat fire sigil, the neat Rain sign and the heavy Regions sign dominate. The roughly drawn Binding is the weakest part, and Envelopment and Pointing only partly take hold, so the result is likely unstable. The seal does not activate while the ring is open, and the rough, out-of-round ring would make the effect weaker and shorter lived once closed.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it calls down a modest shower of fire beyond the seal toward the east-northeast. The falling flames clump unevenly into loose, cone-like clots that partly wrap around whatever lies there. The shower wavers and gutters out early.

name: s42_00187.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background, with the main ring closed and neatly drawn. An earth sigil sits just left of center at moderate size relative to the ring. A Selection sign, a square crossed by a plus, sits just right of center beside it. Four Purification signs, small hooked curls, sit near the ring at the north, northeast, southeast and southwest. At the west-northwest, near the ring, is a glyph of six crossing spokes that matches no known sign exactly. Three smaller sub-seals sit inside the main ring. The one at the northwest is open, with a gap on its lower left, and holds a small light sigil. The one at the east is closed and holds a single upward-pointing Regions sign, drawn a little roughly; its edge touches the Selection sign. The one at the south-southwest is closed and holds a wind sigil. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil makes this an earth spell acting on solid matter, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Selection shares the center and confines the effect to the object the seal is drawn on. The four Purification signs separate waste from what they act on. They are the most numerous modifier, but their effect normally applies to water, which fits loosely with earth. The six-spoked glyph is closest to Concealment without its eye marks, so reading it as Concealment is a guess. Read that way, it would partly hide the affected matter. The closed wind sub-seal adds a movement of air. The closed Regions sub-seal points north, so it sends the magic in that direction. The open light sub-seal contributes nothing until it is closed. Taken together, the seal stacks more than three unrelated kinds of modifier: confinement, purification, concealment and direction. The earth sigil, Selection and the four Purification signs dominate, and the wind and Regions sub-seals steer the loosened material. The concealment reading is the weakest part, so the result is likely unstable.
effect: Works unevenly on the stone, sand or soil of the object it is drawn on, sifting grit and impurities out of it in fits while a gust of air pushes the loosened debris northward. The affected matter flickers partly out of sight at moments, and no light is added because that part is left unfinished. The effect wavers throughout and gives out early.

name: s42_00190.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A fire sigil sits upright at the center, moderate in size relative to the ring and slightly rough. Six Dispersion signs surround it. Four sit near the ring at the northeast, southeast, southwest and northwest, each with its stem pointing toward the center and its curve facing outward. The northeast and southwest signs sit closer to the ring than the southeast and northwest ones. Two more Dispersion signs, drawn larger and heavier, sit about two thirds of the way out at the north-northeast and south-southwest. They are turned sideways, roughly across the radius rather than along it, and face roughly opposite ways. Some signs are slightly rough, but all are readable and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and works heat and flame. Its moderate size relative to the ring gives a moderate intensity. Dispersion makes a seal's magic pour or leak outward instead of beaming it in one direction. The four intercardinal signs are in their usual orientation and evenly spaced, so the fire spills out evenly on all sides. Whether Dispersion responds to angling is not known. If it does, the two sideways signs would bend part of that outflow along the ring. Because they sit roughly opposite each other and face opposite ways, they would add a gentle turning motion without favoring one side. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing conflicts. The slight roughness of the sigil and some signs makes the output a little less steady than a fully clean drawing.
effect: Pours moderate flame and heat outward from the seal evenly on every side, with a faint swirling drift as it spreads. The outflow flickers slightly and rises and falls a little unevenly as it burns.

name: s42_00191.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed and neatly drawn. An earth sigil sits upright at the center and is small relative to the ring. Six signs shaped like a diamond on top of crossed legs surround it, matching the Refuse sign. Two sit about two thirds of the way out, at the northeast and southwest, with their diamond ends toward the center. Four more sit close to the ring at the north, east-southeast, south and west-northwest, with their diamond ends toward the ring. The east-southeast one is drawn smaller than the others and has a tiny light sigil attached to its inner end. The signs are spread evenly around the seal, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil makes this an earth spell acting on solid matter such as soil, sand, grit and stone, and its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Refuse is directional and collects unwanted material toward where it points. The four outer Refuse signs point toward the ring and drive debris outward to the edge. The two inner ones point toward the center and draw debris inward. These directly contradict each other. The outer four outnumber the inner two and dominate, so the net movement is outward, but the result is likely unstable. The glyph at the east-southeast is read as Refuse with a light sigil fused to it, which is a guess. Light falls within the fire domain, so that spot would also give off a faint glow where debris is pushed. Because the signs are evenly spaced, no single compass direction is favored beyond inward versus outward.
effect: Sweeps loose dirt, grit and other solid debris outward from the center toward the rim of the seal, but a weaker inward pull keeps dragging some of it back, so the debris shuttles unevenly, gathers in patchy heaps and the sweeping wavers before giving out early. A faint glow marks the debris gathering at the east-southeast edge.

name: s42_00192.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A small fire sigil sits upright at the center, about a quarter of the inner radius. Eight Launch signs surround it. Four sit in the band between the two rings. Those at the north, northeast and south have their apex pointing inward toward the center, and the one at the west has its apex pointing outward toward the ring. The other four sit inside the inner ring and are drawn with heavier strokes. Those at the northeast and southwest have their apex pointing toward the center, and those at the west-northwest and east-southeast have their apex pointing outward. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, and its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Launch sends magic in the direction it points as a powerful but short-lived burst. The second ring adds strength to the core spell. Five Launch signs point inward. Their bursts converge on the center and, with nowhere to spread inside the ring, drive the flame upward from the seal. Three point outward and throw bursts away from the seal toward the west, west-northwest and east-southeast. The inward and outward signs directly oppose one another. The inward majority dominates, so the main burst rises from the center while the outward signs pull part of the fire sideways. Because the signs work against each other, the result is likely unstable. The spread of signs keeps the effect from favoring one side, but the outward jets make it uneven.
effect: Erupts in a sudden, forceful but modest jet of flame that shoots straight up from the center of the seal. Smaller tongues of fire spit outward to the west, west-northwest and east-southeast and tug against the main jet, so the eruption lurches unevenly and burns out after a brief moment.

name: s42_00194.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, with the ring closed and neatly drawn. A small fire sigil sits upright at the center. Four Pulling signs sit well out toward the ring, at the north-northwest, northeast, south-southeast and south-southwest. Each has its tail toward the center and its arrowhead pointing outward toward the ring, so all four are inverted. The south-southwest one is smaller and set closer in than the others. Four Aeriforms Defined signs, each a cluster of three short strokes, sit about halfway out at the north-northwest, northeast, east and west-southwest. Three have their tops toward the center. The one at the west-southwest is turned the other way, with its top toward the ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil makes this a fire spell, and its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Pulling is directional: pointing inward, it draws the target toward the seal. Here all four signs point outward, so they reverse that pull into a push away from the seal. Because they are spread around the ring, the push goes outward on every side rather than favoring one direction. Aeriforms Defined shares its design with the strokes of the wind sigil and its name with the sigil for creating air, so it brings air into the spell as a medium. Paired with fire, that means heated air. Three of these signs share one orientation and set the main behavior. The single reversed one at the west-southwest has no established inverted effect, so it is treated as a minor variation rather than a true contradiction. With only two kinds of modifier, working together, and a neat, closed ring, the spell activates and holds steady.
effect: Produces a modest amount of heat and drives it outward with the surrounding air, sending warm air pushing away from the seal in every direction. It acts like a steady warm gust radiating out from the seal's surface rather than an open flame.

name: s42_00196.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with neat linework. The main body has two concentric rings. The outer ring is open, with a gap at the west. The inner ring also shows a break at the south-southwest. Two sigils sit side by side at the center, each about a quarter of the ring radius: a wind sigil on the left and a water sigil on the right. In the band between the rings sit four signs. A Gathering sign at the north-northeast points inward. A Convergence triangle at the east has its flat side toward the center and its point toward the ring. A small Glaives sign is at the east-southeast, facing inward. A Repetition sign is at the northwest. Inside the inner ring, about halfway out, sit three more signs. A Crosshair sits at the southeast. A Sights Set at the west-southwest has its arrow pointing outward toward the ring. A Mimicry sign sits at the south, its top toward the center. The signs are spread evenly around the seal. Three smaller closed rings are joined to the outer ring by short lines. The one at the northwest is drawn roughly and holds a somewhat rough earth sigil. The one at the east holds a large light sigil in a slightly rough ring. The one at the south-southwest is neat and holds a Repetition sign at its center.
justification: The wind and water sigils set two elements, moving air and water together, and their modest size gives a moderate intensity. Gathering, pointing inward, draws material in from the surroundings. Convergence normally focuses magic to a point with a tip facing inward; here its point faces outward, so that focusing is loosened. Sights Set, pointing toward the west-southwest, aims the spell, and Crosshair reinforces targeting at a specific point. Glaives set how deeply the magic embeds itself in flesh. Repetition keeps resetting the affected matter to its first state. Mimicry, with no decorative sigil to copy, would make the effect imitate the target's movements. Several of these modifiers are unrelated: gathering and focusing, aiming, embedding, time reset and mimicry. That is more than three kinds, so the spell is likely unstable. The two sigils with Gathering and the aiming signs dominate. Repetition, Mimicry and Glaives act only partially. The attached sub-seals are closed and add their own effects. The light sub-seal adds a glow. The neat Repetition sub-seal strengthens the resetting. The roughly drawn earth sub-seal contributes only a weak, short-lived pull on solid matter. Neither main ring is closed, so nothing activates until both gaps are closed.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it draws in surrounding air and moisture into a glowing, loosely bound mass of swirling water and wind. It hurls that mass toward a target to the west-southwest, where it presses in and tries to shadow the target's movements. The mass keeps snapping back to its original form and drags a faint, fading pull of grit. It wavers, misfires and acts unevenly, often breaking apart before it fully takes hold.

name: s42_00197.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background, ring closed. The ring is drawn a little rough and is noticeably out of round, bulging into a lumpy, almost squarish outline. A water sigil sits at the center, upright, roughly drawn, and fairly large relative to the ring. Five Dispersion signs surround it at the north-northwest, east-northeast, south-southeast, south-southwest and west-southwest. Each has its stem toward the ring and its curve facing the center, the reverse of the usual orientation. The south-southwest sign is drawn much larger than the others. An octagon crossed by an X sits neatly drawn near the ring at the north-northeast. An Entwining sign sits at the west, and at the east is a Columns-like sign with a small circle at the foot of its stem. Apart from the octagon, the signs are drawn roughly. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil sets the element. Its fairly large size gives a strong intensity, but the rough drawing weakens it. Five Dispersion signs dominate, making the water pour outward rather than beam in one direction. They are drawn in the reversed orientation, and how that changes Dispersion is unclear, so they are read as still pouring outward. The oversized south-southwest sign makes the flow heaviest on that side. The crossed octagon is closest to Selection, which is a guess. As Selection, it would confine the effect to the object the seal is drawn on, which works against outward dispersion. Entwining makes the effect wrap around objects. The circled Columns sign reads, also as a guess, as a blend of Columns and Solidification, adding a short push and a firming of the water. Together that is four unrelated kinds of modifier: dispersing, confining, wrapping and solidifying. Dispersion and the water sigil dominate, while the confining sign pulls against them, so the result is likely unstable. The rough signs and the out-of-round ring make the effect weak and fleeting, and the seal may fail to activate.
effect: Spills a fairly heavy flow of water outward from the seal in sputtering, uneven bursts, running heaviest toward the south-southwest. Part of the water tries to cling and wrap around the object the seal is drawn on, briefly thickening into stiff strands before slipping loose. The whole effect wavers and gives out after a short time, and it may fail to start at all.

name: s42_00198.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, neatly drawn. The ring is open, with a gap at the upper right between the north and northeast signs. A small light sigil, a diamond set inside a square with four short spokes, sits upright at the center, about a quarter of the ring's radius in size. Six Concealment signs, each an eight-armed star with small eye marks on its arms, are spaced evenly around the seal near the ring. They sit at the north, northeast, east-southeast, south, southwest and west-northwest, each with its top toward the ring. The west-northwest sign is drawn a little more roughly than the others. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and manipulates light. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity, and light made this way diminishes over time. Concealment hides a target. Paired with light, it turns the light toward hiding, masking the object rather than lighting it up. The six Concealment signs are evenly spaced and balanced, so the effect favors no direction and covers all sides equally. The one slightly rough sign weakens its part of the seal a little but does not unbalance the spell. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing conflicts. The ring is open, so the seal will not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it manipulates light around the object the seal is drawn on, hiding it from sight evenly from every side. The concealment is modest in strength, with a faint thin patch on one side, and it gradually fades as the light diminishes.

name: s42_00200.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with two concentric rings, both closed. The outer ring is drawn somewhat roughly and noticeably out of round, and the inner ring sits close inside it with a slightly uneven curve. The band between the two rings is empty. There is no element sigil. At the center sits an Expansion sign made of nested corner brackets with its corners pointing outward. It is drawn a little roughly and spans roughly a quarter of the ring's radius. Four more Expansion signs sit about halfway to two thirds of the way out from the center, at the northwest, north-northeast, east-southeast and south-southwest. Each is rotated differently, but all keep their corners pointing outward, so none is inverted. The north-northeast sign is drawn heavy and bold. The northwest sign is smaller and fainter, and the east-southeast and south-southwest signs are thin and slightly sketchy. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the central Expansion sign takes the core position and sets the spell's purpose, which is changing a target's size. Expansion is semi-directional with radial symmetry. Rotating it changes nothing, and only flipping it inside out inverts it. Every Expansion here has its corners pointing outward, so all five call for growth, and their combined count strengthens the effect. The four outer signs are spread evenly around the seal, so the growth favors no direction. No Selection or Diamond sign is present to limit the effect to the object the seal is drawn on or to nearby objects. Without a sigil, the effect is not tied to any element. The second ring normally adds strength to a seal, but its band holds no signs, so it contributes nothing beyond that. All the signs share a single purpose and do not contradict each other. However, the out-of-round outer ring and the rough central sign weaken the spell and shorten its effect.
effect: Makes the object it acts on swell considerably in size, evenly on all sides. The growth surges and wavers rather than holding steady, and it slips back after only a short time.

name: s42_00201.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but drawn roughly and noticeably out of round, with a lumpy outline. A fire sigil sits upright at the center, large relative to the ring and a little rough. Seven Pulling signs surround it. Four sit near the ring at the north, east, south-southwest and west. Two sit closer in, at the north-northwest and southwest. All six of these are inverted, with their arrowheads pointing outward toward the ring. A seventh Pulling sign near the ring at the southwest is drawn heavier than the rest and points inward, its arrowhead toward the center. A small Piercing sign, a short stroke with a diamond at its middle, sits at the south-southeast, turned almost horizontal. Several of the signs are roughly drawn, and more of them cluster on the southwest side than anywhere else. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, and its large size relative to the ring gives a fairly strong intensity. Piercing makes the magic manifest as projectiles, and one Piercing sign gives a single projectile. Pulling is directional. Pointed inward it draws things toward the seal, and inverted it pushes them away. The six outward-facing Pulling signs therefore drive the fire away from the seal. They are bunched toward the southwest, so the push favors that direction. The heavy inward-facing Pulling sign at the southwest directly contradicts them, pulling back on the same side the push favors. The six outward signs outnumber it and dominate, but the clash makes the result likely unstable. The rough linework weakens the spell and shortens how long it lasts. Because the closed ring is not round enough, the effect is fleeting and the seal may fail to activate.
effect: Forms a fairly strong bolt of fire and hurls it outward from the seal, mostly toward the southwest. A counter-pull on that side drags against it, so the bolt wobbles and sputters in flight and burns out quickly. The seal may fizzle without firing at all.

name: s42_00204.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but rough and lumpy, noticeably out of round. A Concealment sign fills the center: an eight-spoked star with an eye mark at the north, east, south and west ends, drawn neatly and fairly large, about two fifths of the ring's radius. No element sigil is present. Four Pulling signs sit about halfway to the ring at the north, east, south and west, each with its arrowhead pointing inward toward the center. The north and east ones are drawn a little rougher, and the north one is heavier. Two more Pulling signs sit farther out, near the ring at the northwest and southeast. Both are inverted, with their arrowheads pointing outward toward the ring. The northwest one is drawn heavier than the rest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the central Concealment sign is the core of the seal, so the spell hides its target and is not tied to any element. Pulling with its arrow pointing inward draws the target toward the seal. The four inward Pulling signs are evenly spaced and straight, so they pull from all sides with no twist. Inverted Pulling likely pushes things away instead, so the two outward signs push along the northwest-southeast axis. That directly contradicts the inward pull on that line. The four inward signs outnumber the two inverted ones, so the inward pull dominates, but the opposed pair makes the result likely unstable. The rough, out-of-round ring weakens the spell and shortens its life, and it may make the effect fleeting or prevent activation altogether.
effect: Draws nearby objects in from all sides toward the seal and wraps them in concealing shadow, while things along the northwest-southeast line are shoved back outward. The tug-of-war on that diagonal makes the concealment flicker and the pull jerk unevenly, and the whole effect is weak and fades quickly, if it activates at all.

name: s42_00205.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, neatly drawn, with two concentric rings, both closed. All glyphs sit inside the inner ring, and the band between the rings is empty. No element sigil is present. A small Stretch sign sits upright at the center: an arch open at the bottom with short outward-turned feet. There are three Sights Set signs. The ones at the north-northwest and south-southeast have their diamond ends near the ring and their arrows pointing in toward the center. The one at the east-northeast is reversed, with its diamond toward the center and its arrow pointing out toward the ring. Two Regions signs, drawn as heavy chevrons, sit at the north-northeast and the west, each with its point facing outward toward the ring. The signs are unevenly spread and weighted toward the north-northeast. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the Stretch sign takes the center and sets the spell's core behavior: turning solid matter it touches into long, flexible ribbons. Without an element, it works on any solid material. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. The second ring adds strength and steadiness to the core spell. Regions sets where magic manifests relative to the seal. With both pointing outward, the effect appears outside the ring and not within it, and the unbalanced layout biases it toward the north-northeast. Sights Set lets the caster aim the spell at a chosen target. The two inward-facing Sights Set signs agree and set that aim. The single outward-facing one has an unknown inverted effect. As a guess, it slightly loosens the aim rather than overriding it. Only two kinds of modifier accompany the core, and they do not directly contradict each other, so the seal holds together.
effect: Turns solid objects just beyond the seal's edge into long, flexible ribbons, reaching outward mainly toward the north-northeast. The caster can aim it at a chosen target, though the aim holds a little loosely. The reshaping is modest in strength but steady.

name: s42_00206.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background with two rings, both closed. The outer ring is roughly drawn and noticeably out of round, and a second ring sits just inside it, leaving an empty band between them. A Detection sign of three vertical strokes rising in height sits upright at the center in place of a sigil, at about a quarter of the ring's radius and a little rough. There is no element sigil. Six different signs are spread fairly evenly around it, each with its top toward the center unless noted. A Pointing sign sits at the north-northwest and a Purification curl at the north-northeast, both drawn roughly. A Stability and Level Planes sign of wavy strokes sits at the east-northeast, also rough. A Solidification sign of two small circles joined by a line sits at the southeast, with its outer circle touching the inner ring. A Reflection hourglass sits at the southwest. A Projection bracket sits at the west-northwest, rotated so its open side faces roughly upward, with its outer stroke crossing the inner ring into the band.
justification: With no element sigil, the central Detection sign is the core, so the spell senses something nearby rather than working on fire, water, earth or wind. Reflection targets a reflected image, and Projection casts an effect outward from the seal. Together with Detection, these three dominate and form a clear chain: sense, take an image, cast it out. Pointing shapes the cast effect into a cone, and Solidification makes it firmer, so the image is pushed out as a defined, pointed form. Stability and Level Planes keeps the effect level as it hangs in the air. Purification normally separates waste from water and fits poorly here. Read as a guess, it would only strip some clutter from the image. Stacking six unrelated kinds of modifier around one core makes the result likely unstable, with Purification the least predictable part. The rough linework and the out-of-round ring make the effect weaker and fleeting.
effect: Senses something near the seal and casts a faint reflected image of it outward as a pointed, cone-shaped projection that tries to hang level in the air. The image flickers, firms up only in patches, and comes out unevenly cleaned of detail. It wavers and collapses after a few moments.

name: s42_00207.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, with the ring closed and neatly drawn. An upright earth sigil sits at the center, moderate in size relative to the ring. A Stretch sign sits near the ring at the south, with its arch bulging toward the ring and its open side facing the center. A Gathering sign sits at the east-northeast with its arrowed top toward the ring. A Launch sign sits at the west-southwest, turned nearly upside down so its apex points in toward the center. A Cooling sign sits close to the ring at the north. A Regions sign sits at the northwest with its point aimed inward toward the center. The five signs are spread fairly evenly around the ring, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on solid matter such as soil, sand and stone. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Stretch turns solid matter it touches into long, flexible ribbons. Gathering draws material in from the surroundings for the spell to use. The inward-pointing Regions sign confines the magic to the inside of the ring. Launch normally fires its effect in a powerful but short burst in the direction it points. Here it points toward the center, so the burst is driven inward rather than out. Cooling chills the material. These signs do not directly contradict each other, and the inward Launch agrees with the inward Regions. However, the seal stacks five unrelated kinds of modifier: stretching, gathering, bursting, cooling and confinement. The earth sigil, Stretch and Gathering dominate and set the core behavior. Regions and Launch shape where it happens, and Cooling is a secondary layer. With this many unrelated modifiers, the result is likely unstable.
effect: Draws in nearby soil and stone and stretches it into long, cold, flexible ribbons of earth that form only inside the seal's bounds, snapping inward toward the center in a sharp, brief burst. The ribbons form in uneven fits, some only half-stretched and some crumbling back into rubble, and the chill spreads patchily before the spell gives out early.

name: s42_00209.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background. The ring is open, with a wide gap across the bottom between the south-southwest and the southeast. A light sigil, a diamond set inside a square with four short spokes, sits upright at the center. It is large, about half the ring's radius, and its lines are slightly uneven. Six Gathering signs form three pairs set roughly a third of the way around the ring from each other: one pair at the east and east-northeast, one at the northwest, and one at the south-southwest. In each pair, one sign sits about halfway to the ring and the other sits near the ring. All but one have their arrowheads pointing toward the center. The outer northwest Gathering sign is drawn heavier and rougher and is turned sideways, so it points along the ring rather than inward. Three small Mimicry signs sit near the ring at the north, west-southwest and southeast, each oriented outward or sideways. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil makes this a light spell, and its large size relative to the ring gives a fairly strong effect. Its slightly rough lines make the light a little uneven. Gathering lets a spell actively draw material in from its surroundings. Here that material is ambient light, pulled from three evenly spaced directions so no side dominates. The sideways outer Gathering at the northwest draws less cleanly than the rest, adding a slight unevenness on that side. Mimicry imitates the movements of a target. No decorative sigil names what to imitate, so the gathered light copies the motion of whatever target the spell is directed at rather than taking a creature's form. The seal uses only two kinds of modifier and they do not conflict, so it is not unstable. It cannot activate until the ring is closed.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it draws in surrounding light from all sides and gathers it into a fairly bright glow that copies the movements of its target, following it as it moves. The glow flickers slightly and pulls a little unevenly from the northwest, and it gradually dims over time.

name: s42_00210.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background, ring closed but badly out of round, bulging into a lumpy, rounded-diamond shape. A fire sigil sits at the center, upright and large, reaching nearly half the ring's radius. A small, tilted Mimicry sign sits at the northwest. A Regions sign sits near the ring at the south with its point facing inward toward the center. An Immobility sign at the east-southeast is rotated so its top faces the ring. Two Stretch signs sit in the upper right. The one at the northeast is large, with its arch toward the ring and its open side toward the center. The one at the north is smaller and inverted, with its curve toward the center and its open side toward the ring. The signs cluster toward the north and northeast. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, and its large size relative to the ring gives a strong intensity. Stretch draws matter out into long, flexible ribbons. Two of them make it the dominant modifier, so the flame is pulled into ribbons. Stretch has no known inverted behaviour, so the inverted northern sign most likely reinforces the drawing-out effect rather than reversing it. The lone Regions sign at the south points inward, so it sends the magic northward across the seal. The clustering of signs toward the northeast bends that flow toward the northeast. Immobility holds a target fixed in relation to the seal. Mimicry makes a target imitate movements. These two directly contradict each other. Together with Stretch and Regions, the seal stacks four unrelated kinds of modifier, so the result is likely unstable. The fire sigil and the two Stretch signs dominate, Regions sets the heading, and the fixing and mimicking pull against each other. The uneven ring is not round enough, so any effect would be fleeting and the seal may fail to activate. The rough linework further weakens it and shortens its life.
effect: Throws out strong but fleeting ribbons of flame that stream northward from the seal and veer toward the northeast. The ribbons jerk unevenly between freezing in place and copying nearby motion. They gutter out almost as soon as they form, and the spell may fail to ignite at all.

name: s42_00212.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background. The ring is open, with a wide gap at the upper left, and the ring and glyphs are otherwise drawn neatly. Two glyphs share the center, each small relative to the ring: an earth sigil on the left and a Reflection sign, an hourglass of two triangles meeting at a point, on the right. Nine Dispersion signs surround them. Six sit about halfway out at the south-southeast, southwest, west-northwest, north-northwest, northeast and east-southeast, each with its stem toward the center and its curve facing the ring. Three more sit farther out near the ring at the north-northwest, east-southeast and southwest. The north-northwest and east-southeast ones match the inner signs' orientation. The southwest one is inverted, with its stem toward the ring and its curve facing inward, and it is drawn with noticeably heavier strokes than the rest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on solid matter such as stone, sand and soil. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Reflection shares the center as a second core and targets a reflected image found on the object the seal is drawn on, so the earth magic works from that image. Dispersion makes a seal's magic pour outward rather than beam in one direction. With eight of them in the same orientation spread around the ring, the outflow is balanced on all sides, and the extra outer signs widen its reach. The single inverted Dispersion at the southwest is heavier but alone.
