The difference between normal and inverted Dispersion is unclear, so it is outweighed by the eight normal signs and adds at most a slight local change on that side, not a contradiction. Only one kind of modifier is present, so the seal is not unstable. The open ring keeps it from activating until the gap is closed.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it takes the image reflected in the surface it is drawn on and lets earth magic pour outward evenly on all sides. Nearby stone, sand and soil shift into a modest, loose likeness of that reflection spreading out around the seal.

name: s42_00213.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background, drawn roughly. There are two rings, one just inside the other. The outer ring is open, with a wide gap at the upper left. The inner ring also appears to break on the upper right, between the northeast and east-southeast signs. A small water sigil sits at the center, upright and roughly drawn, at about a quarter of the ring's radius. Three Stretch signs sit about two thirds of the way out, at the north, northeast and south. Each is an arch with small feet, its rounded top toward the ring and its opening facing the center. A single Columns sign sits at the east-southeast, with its crossbar toward the ring and its stem toward the center. The signs cluster on the eastern side, and the west half of the seal is empty. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Stretch normally turns matter touched by the spell into long, flexible ribbons and is meant to surround the central sigil. Its normal action is on solid matter, so applying it to water is a guess: here it would draw the water out into ribbon-like streamers. The lone Columns sign gives the effect a column shape and drives it in one direction. Because it is unbalanced and sits alone at the east-southeast, with the other signs also leaning east, the column is pushed toward that side instead of rising straight up. Only two kinds of modifier are present and they do not contradict each other. The rough linework and the imperfect rings weaken the spell and shorten its life. The seal will not activate until the rings are closed.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it draws a modest amount of water into long, flexible ribbons that stream out in a column leaning toward the east-southeast. The ribbons waver and thin unevenly, then break apart and spill soon after forming.

name: s42_00215.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn neatly in black on a white background. The ring is open, with a gap at the top just east of north. At the center is a small sigil, drawn as an S-curve inside a circle and ringed by eight dots. It is a variant of the wind sigil family and does not match the standard wind sigil. Two Entwining signs sit near the ring. One is at the north-northeast with its top toward the center, and the other is at the west-southwest with its top toward the ring. Two Convergence triangles sit close to the ring at the east and south, each with a point facing inward. Three Purification signs sit partway out: one at the north-northwest, one at the southeast and one at the west-southwest, the last slightly closer to the center. The signs are spread evenly around the seal. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The central glyph is a wind-family variant, so the spell works on air. Its exact variant does not match a named sigil. Reading it as a wind sigil that encloses its air is a guess, and under that reading the spell holds air rather than only moving it. The sigil is small relative to the ring, which gives a modest intensity. The two Convergence signs point inward in their usual orientation. They focus the magic toward a single point and pack loose matter tightly. The two Entwining signs make the effect wrap itself around other objects. They face opposite ways, but their inverted behavior is unknown, so they are read as working together. Purification normally separates waste from water. Applied to air, it would strip impurities out of the gathered air. It is asymmetric, so its exact behavior is less predictable than the rest. There are only three kinds of modifier, they do not contradict each other, and they are evenly placed, so the effect has no set direction. The spell will not activate while the ring is open.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it draws the surrounding air together into a modest, tightly packed current and wraps it around nearby objects. It strips dust and impurities from that air as it coils, leaving each object enveloped in a thin layer of cleaned air.

name: s42_00216.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a plain background. Two rings, both closed: a thick outer ring that is noticeably out of round and slightly rough, and a second ring just inside it. The band between them is empty. A wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes, sits upright at the center at a moderately large size relative to the ring, drawn a little roughly. Six Dispersion-type signs sit about halfway to two thirds of the way out, spread evenly around the center. Four are plain Dispersion signs: at the north-northwest and south-southeast with the stem toward the ring and the curve toward the center, and at the west-southwest and east-southeast with the stem toward the center and the curve toward the ring. The sign at the east-northeast is a Dispersion with an extra stroke from its bottom edge, stem toward the center. The sign at the west-northwest is a Dispersion with a small Binding-like arc attached at its bottom, stem toward the ring. All signs are a little rough, and the north-northwest and south-southeast ones are drawn roughly. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves and manipulates existing air. Its fairly large size relative to the ring gives a moderately strong effect. Dispersion makes magic pour or leak outward rather than beam in one direction. Three signs face one way and three the other, so normal and inverted Dispersion are mixed. The difference between the two orientations is unclear, so they do not contradict each other. The east-northeast glyph is read as Dispersion with a stray stroke, which is a guess, so it adds the same outward spill. The west-northwest glyph is read as Dispersion fused with Binding, also a guess. Binding holds material together as a single unit, so the air released on that side would stay denser and more cohesive. The signs are balanced around the ring, so no direction is favored overall. The second ring frames the seal but carries no extra signs. The rough strokes weaken the spell and shorten its life, and the out-of-round outer ring makes the effect fleeting.
effect: Sends air spilling outward from the seal in every direction as a moderately strong, spreading draft rather than a focused blast. The flow pulses unevenly and dies away quickly, with the air on the west-northwest side pushing out as a slightly denser, more cohesive puff.

name: s42_00217.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A small fire sigil, about a quarter of the ring radius, sits upright at the center. Inside the inner ring are four signs about halfway out: Purification signs at the northwest and southeast, and Pointing signs at the east-northeast and south-southwest, each with its top toward the center. The band between the two rings holds four more Purification signs at the north-northwest, east-southeast, south-southeast and southwest. Two of these are rotated differently from the rest. The signs cluster more heavily on the southern and eastern side, so the layout leans toward the south-southeast. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and works with flame or heat. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Purification is asymmetric and separates waste from water. With six of them across both rings, it is the dominant modifier and turns the heat toward cleansing, driving impurities out of water rather than simply burning. Pointing is non-directional and makes the effect manifest in a conical shape. There are no Columns or other directional signs to aim that cone, so the uneven placement of signs biases it toward the south-southeast. The second ring carries more Purification signs and strengthens that part of the spell. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they do not contradict each other. Because Purification is asymmetric, its varied rotations make its exact behavior hard to predict.
effect: Produces a modest cone of heat that leans toward the south-southeast and separates waste and impurities from the water it touches, leaving cleaner water behind. The cleansing is strong for the spell's size, while the heat itself stays mild.

name: s42_00218.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background, with the ring closed and drawn a little roughly. Two small sigils sit side by side at the center, both upright and roughly drawn: a light sigil on the left and a water sigil on the right. Each is about a quarter of the ring's radius. Nine Detection signs, each three parallel strokes of increasing length, surround them. Six sit toward the outer part of the seal, at the south-southwest, south-southeast, west, northwest, north-northeast and east, with their tops turned toward the ring. Three more sit closer to the center, at the northeast, southeast and northwest, each rotated to a different angle. Most of the signs are drawn roughly. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil makes the spell create light, which falls within the fire domain, and the water sigil adds the creation and manipulation of water. Both sigils are small relative to the ring, so the intensity is low. Detection senses presence and makes the spell respond to it. Nine of them spread evenly around the ring give that sensing a range on every side, with no direction favored, and their varied angles add no steering. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing contradicts and the seal is not unstable. The rough linework on the sigils, the signs and the ring makes the effect weaker and shorter-lived.
effect: Gives off a faint glow and a thin trickle or mist of water that stir in response to presences sensed on any side of the seal. The light and water flicker unevenly and fade soon after they appear.

name: s42_00219.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background. The ring is neatly drawn but open, with a gap at the bottom just right of south. A Refuse sign sits upright at the center, with its diamond at the top and crossed legs below. It is fairly large relative to the ring. Eight Gathering signs surround it, each with its arrowhead pointing toward the center. Five sit in an outer circle near the ring, at the north, northeast, southeast, southwest and northwest. Three sit a little closer in, at the east, south-southeast and west-southwest. The signs are spread evenly around the seal. Several are slightly rough, and the southwest one is the roughest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: There is no element sigil, so Refuse at the center sets the core behavior. Refuse is a directional sign that collects unwanted material, such as waste, toward where it points. Drawn upright, it points north. Its fairly large size gives the collecting effect solid strength. Gathering lets a spell actively draw material in from its surroundings. With all eight pointing inward and balanced around the ring, material is pulled evenly from every side toward the center, where Refuse sorts it and moves it northward. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they reinforce each other, so the seal is not unstable. The slight roughness of several Gathering signs, especially the southwest one, makes the pull from those sides a little weaker and shorter-lived. The ring is open, so nothing activates until it is closed.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it pulls loose waste and debris in from all around the seal and heaps it toward the north side of the center. The pull from the southwest side is slightly weaker and fades sooner than the rest.

name: s42_00220.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn, with a wide band between them. There is no element sigil. A Rain sign, a square with concave sides and short strokes on each side, sits upright at the center at a moderate size. Four smaller Rain signs sit in the band between the rings at the north, east, south-southeast and west-northwest. The northern one looks slightly rougher than the others, and none is flipped inside-out. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the central Rain sign takes the place of a sigil and sets the core behavior, which is summoning material so it falls the way rain does. Rain is semi-directional and radially symmetric, so rotating it changes nothing. It only reverses its effect when flipped inside-out, and none of these signs is, so all five work normally. The four band signs repeat and reinforce the same effect, and the second ring adds strength to the core spell. Because the signs are roughly balanced around the seal, the effect is not pushed in one direction. The slightly rough northern sign weakens that side a little. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing conflicts.
effect: Calls down a strong, even, rain-like shower from above over the seal and the area around it. With no element to set its substance, it brings down whatever loose material is available overhead. The shower falls slightly thinner on the north side.

name: s42_00221.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but drawn a little roughly and somewhat out of round, with lumpy, uneven curves. A water sigil sits at the center, upright and of moderate size relative to the ring, its strokes slightly rough. Six Regions signs, each a simple chevron, sit near the ring at the north, east, east-southeast, south-southeast, west-southwest and west-northwest. Every chevron has its point toward the ring, so all six point outward. They are spread fairly evenly around the seal. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell, and its moderate size relative to the ring gives a moderate intensity. Regions sets where magic manifests relative to the seal. When all Regions signs point outward, the magic appears outside the ring and does not take effect within its bounds. The six signs are balanced around the ring, so no side is favored and the water appears evenly on all sides. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing contradicts. The ring is closed, so the spell activates, but its uneven shape and the rough sigil make the effect weaker and fleeting.
effect: Brings up a moderate amount of water in a band all around the outside of the seal while the area within it stays dry. The water forms weakly and unevenly, wavering in places, and disperses after only a short time.

name: s42_00223.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but drawn a little roughly and noticeably out of round, with flattened and bulging stretches. There is no element sigil. A Launch sign sits upright at the center, opening downward with its peak toward the north, and is small relative to the ring. Six signs are spread near the ring, all drawn roughly. A Coil sign sits at the northeast, a Pointing sign at the east and a Piercing sign at the southeast, all with their tops toward the ring. An Orb sign sits at the south, also top toward the ring. A Concealment sign sits at the southwest and an Entwining sign at the west-northwest, both with their tops turned toward the center. The north and northwest stretch of the ring is empty, so the signs cluster on the east and south sides. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, Launch takes the center as the core of the spell. It sends material out in its pointing direction, northward and up from the seal, in a powerful but short-lived burst. Its small size gives modest strength. Because the signs crowd the east and south, the burst is pulled toward the southeast. Pointing shapes the material into cones and Piercing turns it into projectiles. These two agree and, sitting on the heavier southeast side, dominate the modifiers. Coil softens solid matter, which directly undercuts the sharp projectiles. Orb holds material in a sphere above the seal, which works against Launch throwing it outward. Concealment hides the result, and Entwining makes it wrap around what it meets. The seal stacks well over three unrelated kinds of modifier, including softening, containment, hiding and wrapping, and two of them contradict the dominant parts, so the result is likely unstable. The rough linework and the out-of-round ring make it weak and fleeting, and it may fail to activate at all.
effect: Spits out a brief, sputtering burst of material fed into the seal, thrown northward and upward but skewed toward the southeast as a few cone-shaped projectiles. Their tips go soft and they half-vanish from sight in flickers. They try to wrap around whatever they strike, but part of the material sags back toward the seal, and the whole burst wavers and collapses almost at once, if it activates at all.

name: s42_00225.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with two concentric rings, both closed. Both are drawn roughly and noticeably out of round, with flattened, angular sides that give them an uneven, almost hexagonal outline. The inner ring sits just inside the outer one, and nothing is drawn in the band between them. A large earth sigil sits upright at the center, reaching about half the radius of the inner ring, and its strokes are somewhat uneven. Six Crushing signs, drawn as small zigzags, are spaced evenly around it about halfway to the ring, at the southwest, west-northwest, north-northwest, northeast, east-southeast and south-southeast. All six are inverted, with the top of each zigzag turned toward the center. Several are drawn shakily. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil makes this an earth spell acting on solid matter such as stone, sand and soil. Its large size relative to the ring gives the spell high intensity. Crushing is semi-directional, so its angle does not steer the spell, but inverting it reverses its effect. Normal Crushing breaks solids into ever smaller pieces, while inverted Crushing pulls crushed material back into its original shape. All six signs are inverted and evenly spaced, so the seal is built purely to reform matter and favors no direction. The added inner ring strengthens the core spell. However, both rings are rough and not round enough, and the sigil and several signs are shakily drawn. That makes the effect fleeting and unreliable and may keep the seal from activating at all, so the strength of the large sigil is largely wasted.
effect: Forcefully draws powdered or smashed earth and stone back toward the shape of the object it came from, but the pieces knit together unevenly and hold that shape only for a moment before crumbling back into fragments. At times the spell sputters and fails to take hold at all.

name: s42_00226.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background, ring closed and neatly drawn. An earth sigil sits upright at the center, moderate in size relative to the ring. An inverted Expansion sign, its nested corner brackets pointing inward, sits at the west-northwest about halfway to the ring. A four-lobed Billow sign sits at the east-northeast at a similar distance. At the east-southeast is a circle crossed by a single diagonal stroke drawn symmetrically from top to bottom; it closely resembles an Orb sign but does not match it exactly. A Coil sign sits near the ring at the northwest. An Aeriforms Defined sign, three splayed strokes, sits against the ring at the west-southwest with its top toward the center. An Envelopment sign sits near the ring at the south. The signs are spread evenly around the seal, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell works on solid matter such as soil, sand and stone. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Billow turns available material into a fluffy cloud, and Coil softens physical matter. Both act on solids, so together with the earth sigil they form the dominant core: loosening earth into a soft, cloud-like mass. Envelopment makes the effect surround its target. The inverted Expansion sign shrinks its target. The circled glyph is read as Orb, which is a guess. Under that reading it would gather the material into a spherical space above the seal. Aeriforms Defined is tied to air, which here would thin and lighten the mass. These are six unrelated kinds of modifier, well past three. Shrinking also works against Billow's puffing, so the earth sigil, Billow and Coil dominate, with Envelopment next. The shrinking, sphere and air effects pull unevenly, so the result is likely unstable. The balanced placement means no direction is favored.
effect: Loosens nearby soil and sand into a soft, fluffy cloud of earth that wraps around its target and tries to draw itself into a small sphere. The cloud swells and shrinks unevenly, wavering between loose fluff and a compact ball. It collapses back into ordinary soil sooner than expected.

name: s42_00229.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background with two closed rings, one just inside the other. Both are drawn as rounded pentagons rather than circles. An upright Entwining sign sits at the center, drawn boldly at about 40% of the ring radius. There is no element sigil. Six Stretch signs surround it at the north, northeast, east-southeast, south, southwest and west-northwest. The northeast and south signs are much larger than the rest and overlap the inner ring line, with their tops facing the center. The other four are small and face outward. Most of the linework is slightly rough, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, Entwining takes the center and sets the core behavior: the object the seal is drawn on wraps itself around other objects. Stretch turns solid objects touched by the spell into long, flexible ribbons and is meant to surround the central glyph, as it does here. Stretch is most likely non-directional, so the inward and outward orientations do not change its effect. The two larger Stretch signs give a stronger stretching pull on the northeast and south sides, while the six signs together stay roughly balanced. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they support each other: material is drawn out into ribbons and then wound around a target. The second ring strengthens the spell. However, both rings are pentagonal rather than round, so the effect is fleeting and may fail to activate. The slightly rough strokes weaken it further.
effect: Draws the object it is drawn on, and solid matter it touches, out into long flexible ribbons that try to wind around nearby objects. The ribbons stretch unevenly, longer and thicker toward the northeast and south. They coil loosely, catch only briefly before slipping free, and on some attempts never form at all.

name: s42_00230.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A light sigil, a diamond set inside a square with four spokes, sits upright at the center and is fairly large relative to the ring. Four small Sights Set signs sit in the band between the two rings, at the north-northwest, northeast, southeast and southwest positions. Each has its diamond end toward the outer ring and its arrow pointing in toward the center. The northeast sign is drawn slightly less cleanly than the others. They are spaced evenly around the seal, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil makes this a light spell, and its fairly large size relative to the ring gives a strong intensity. The second ring adds strength to the core spell. Sights Set lets the caster aim a spell at a chosen point or target. All four signs point inward and are balanced around the ring, so none of them pushes the spell in a fixed direction. The aim is set by the caster rather than by the layout. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing conflicts. The neat drawing and closed rings mean the spell activates and holds steady, and the slight roughness of one sign does not meaningfully weaken it.
effect: Produces a strong, bright light that the caster can aim at any chosen point or target, directing its glow wherever they focus. The light holds steady while in use but gradually dims over time.

name: s42_00231.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background, ring open with a gap at the top between the north and northwest. A water sigil sits upright at the center and is fairly large, about half the ring's radius. Six Stillness signs are spaced evenly around it at the north-northeast, east-northeast, south-southeast, south-southwest, west and northwest. Each is rotated so its top faces the ring. Most sit a little over halfway to the ring, and those at the northwest, east-northeast and south-southwest sit somewhat farther out. The signs at the east-northeast, south-southeast and south-southwest are drawn a little more roughly than the rest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell, and its large size relative to the ring gives a fairly strong effect. Stillness holds magic in place and keeps the effect static in one location. It is the only modifier present, so nothing conflicts with it. The six signs are balanced around the ring and none is directional, so the effect has no preferred direction and stays centered on the seal. The three slightly rough signs hold a little less firmly on their sides, giving a mild unevenness without undermining the spell. The seal will not activate while the ring is open.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it holds a sizable body of water motionless in place over the seal, keeping it from flowing or spilling away. The hold is firm overall but slightly looser along its southern and eastern edges, where the water may ripple faintly.

name: s42_00233.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background, ring closed but drawn somewhat roughly and noticeably out of round, with a lumpy outline. An upright earth sigil sits at the center, fairly large at roughly two fifths of the ring's radius. Five Dispersion signs sit around it about two thirds to three quarters of the way to the ring. Those at the north, east, south and west have their stems toward the ring and their curves toward the center. The one at the southwest is inverted, with its curve toward the ring. Two Refuse signs sit near the ring at the southeast and north-northwest, each with its diamond end pointing in toward the center. Several of the signs are drawn a little roughly. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil makes this an earth spell acting on solid matter such as soil, sand and stone. Its fairly large size relative to the ring gives a fairly strong effect. Dispersion makes the magic pour outward rather than beam in one direction, and with the signs spread evenly around the ring, the earth magic leaks out on all sides. The southwest Dispersion is inverted. How inverted Dispersion differs is unclear, so that side may behave slightly differently from the rest. Refuse is directional and collects unwanted material toward where it points. Both point inward, so waste is drawn toward the center of the seal. Spreading earth outward while drawing waste inward act on different material, so the two do not contradict each other. The rough linework and the out-of-round ring weaken the spell and shorten its duration.
effect: Loosens soil and sand and pushes it outward from the seal on all sides, while drawing waste and debris inward to its center, sifting refuse out of the surrounding ground. The outward flow is fairly strong but uneven and sputters on the southwest side, and the whole effect fades quickly.

name: s42_00234.png
description: A fully visible seal on a white background, with the main ring closed and neatly drawn. A Stillness sign sits upright at the center in place of a sigil, moderate in size relative to the ring. Five Link signs surround it. Four sit near the ring at the northeast, east-southeast, southwest and northwest, each with its top facing the ring. A fifth sits about halfway out at the south-southwest with its top facing the center, the reverse of the others. Two small sub-seals are joined to the main ring by short lines, both with closed rings. The one at the southwest holds an upright Launch sign, its point facing north. The one at the northeast holds a light sigil that fills about half of its small ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: There is no element sigil in the main ring, so Stillness forms the core. It holds a magical effect static in a single location. The attached light sub-seal supplies the element, so the effect is light, and its large size within the small ring gives a fair brightness. The four outward-facing Link signs identify and connect pieces that came from the same source, so the held light stays tied together as one connected effect. These signs are spread evenly, so no direction is favored. Link is likely semi-directional, so the single inward-facing Link at the south-southwest would reverse its linking on that side. This is a guess, and it would loosen the connection there. The Launch sub-seal points north and adds a strong but short-lived upward burst. That directly opposes Stillness, which keeps the effect in place. Stillness dominates, because it is central and larger, while Launch only acts briefly, so the result is likely unstable.
effect: Produces a connected glow of light that hangs fixed in one spot above the seal and slowly dims over time. When it activates, the light jolts upward in a short burst and sputters before settling back into place. Its south-southwest side holds together more loosely than the rest.

name: s42_00235.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is open, with a gap at the upper left between the west and north points, and is otherwise neatly drawn. At the center sits a glyph like a light sigil, a diamond set inside a square with four short spokes, plus an extra filled dot just off its lower left side. It is moderately sized relative to the ring. Four Purification signs, small curls, sit near the ring at the north, east, south and west points, each with its top toward the ring. The western one is drawn slightly heavier and rougher than the others. No other signs are present.
justification: The central glyph matches no known sigil exactly. Its closest match is the light sigil, with the extra dot read as a minor variant mark, so treating it as light is a guess. Read that way, the spell creates light at moderate intensity, and that light diminishes over time. Purification is asymmetric and separates waste and impurities from water. Four of them are spaced evenly around the ring, so no direction is favored and the cleansing quality applies evenly across the light. Only the center and one kind of modifier are present, and they do not conflict. The slightly rough western sign may make the effect a little weaker on that side. The ring is open, so the seal will not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it gives off a moderate, even glow around the seal that cleanses water within its light, drawing dirt and impurities out of it. The cleansing may be slightly weaker toward the west, and the light gradually dims over time.

name: s42_00236.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background. The ring is closed but drawn a little roughly and slightly out of round. A large light sigil, a diamond set inside a square with four spokes, sits upright at the center and reaches about half the ring's radius. Eight different signs surround it. A Cooling sign sits at the north. A small Glaives sign sits at the north-northeast near the ring, not touching it. A Coil sign sits at the east-northeast. A small Expansion sign sits near the ring at the east-southeast, its corners pointing outward. A Collection sign sits at the southeast with its barred end toward the ring and its open side facing the center. A Dispersion sign sits at the south, inverted, with its stem toward the ring and its curve facing the center. A Reflection sign sits at the southwest, and a Purification spiral sits at the west. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil sets the element. Its large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect. Expansion with its corners outward makes the effect grow. Collection, open side inward, draws in surrounding material for the spell to use. Inverted Dispersion still lets the magic leak outward, likely as a low spread across the seal rather than a beam. Reflection points the spell at a reflected image, so the light works off reflections. Coil softens physical matter and Glaives set how deep magic embeds in flesh, but light is not solid matter, so neither has much to act on. Cooling works against light, which belongs to the fire domain, and Purification normally separates waste from water, which does not fit a light spell. The seal stacks eight unrelated kinds of modifier, and several contradict the sigil. The large light sigil dominates, with Expansion and Dispersion shaping its spread, so the result is likely unstable. The rough ring further shortens and weakens it.
effect: Produces a bright but cold light that swells outward and spills unevenly across nearby reflective surfaces, flickering and dimming in patches. It wavers between flaring and fading and collapses well before a steady light would.

name: s42_00237.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background, ring closed, drawn a little roughly and slightly out of round. Two glyphs sit near the center, both small relative to the ring. On the left is a neatly drawn Dancing Puppets sign, a small ring with four loops and crossing curved strokes. On the right is a slightly rough light sigil, a diamond inside a square with four short spokes. Six Collection signs sit evenly spaced just inside the ring, at the north-northeast, east, southeast, south-southwest, west and northwest. Five have their barred top toward the ring and their open side facing the center. The one at the north-northeast is reversed, with its barred top toward the center and its open side facing outward. It and the southeast sign are drawn heavier than the rest. A small closed sub-seal sits inside the main ring at the southeast, just inward of the southeast Collection sign. Its ring is drawn roughly and holds a single upright Stretch sign, an arch open at the bottom. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil makes this a light spell. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity, and light made this way diminishes over time. Dancing Puppets lets the movement of the spell's target be consciously manipulated, so the light can be steered and made to move through the air. Collection gathers material above and around the seal for the spell to use. Five face inward in their usual orientation and are evenly spaced, so the spell draws in surrounding light from all sides. The reversed sign at the north-northeast has never been seen inverted, so reading it as the opposite of gathering is a guess. Read that way, it lets some of the gathered light leak outward on that side instead of being drawn in, which leaves a slight weak point there but does not dominate the other five. The closed sub-seal adds Stretch, which draws what it affects into long, flexible ribbons, so the gathered light takes a ribbon-like form. This is three kinds of modifier: movement, gathering and shaping. They work together rather than against each other, so the seal is not unstable. The slightly rough ring and rough sigil make the effect somewhat weaker and shorter lived, and the roughly drawn sub-seal makes the ribbon shaping less even.
effect: Draws in surrounding light and spins it into soft, ribbon-like streamers that can be steered and sent darting through the air. The ribbons are modest in brightness and uneven in width, thinning and leaking a little toward the north-northeast. They dim and fade sooner than a cleanly drawn version would.

name: s42_00238.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. The inner ring sits a short way inside the outer one, forming a band between them. At the center is a small fire sigil, about a quarter of the ring radius, with a small diamond shape like the head of a Refuse sign attached to its top point. Every other sign sits in or near the outer band. A Refuse sign lies at the west, its diamond end toward the center and its crossed end toward the ring. A glyph like a Regions sign with an extra dot on one side sits at the east-southeast, its point toward the ring. A Crushing sign sits at the south-southwest with its peaks pointing toward the center. A Detection sign of three parallel strokes sits at the southwest and straddles the inner ring. The signs crowd the lower left, so the layout leans toward the south-southwest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, and its small size gives a modest intensity. The attached diamond matches no known sigil variant. Reading it as a fused Refuse mark is a guess, and on that reading it ties the fire to unwanted material, so it burns waste rather than anything at hand. The Refuse sign at the west points inward, so waste is collected toward the center. Crushing faces inward in its normal orientation, so it breaks material into smaller pieces rather than reforming it. The dotted chevron is closest to Regions, which is also a guess. A lone Regions sign pointing outward sends the magic out of the ring toward the east-southeast. The extra dot has no known meaning. Detection is a sensing sign whose exact role is unclear. The second ring adds strength and further effect to the core. This stacks four unrelated kinds of modifier: collection, crushing, direction and detection. In addition, the inward pull of Refuse works against the outward push of the Regions sign. The fire core, Refuse and Crushing dominate. The direction toward the east-southeast is secondary, and Detection is the weakest and least predictable part. The unbalanced layout favors the south-southwest. The result is likely unstable.
effect: Draws nearby waste inward, grinds it into fragments and burns it with a modest flame, venting heat and ash toward the east-southeast. The burning favors the south-southwest side, so material there is consumed first and more completely. The process stutters, pulling in and spitting out debris unevenly instead of running steadily.

name: s42_00244.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background, ring closed but drawn roughly and noticeably out of round, with flattened, lumpy sides. A small earth sigil sits upright at the center, about a quarter of the ring's radius and a little rough. Four Windows signs, each a small ring lined with hatched markings, are scattered around it. Two sit close to the ring at the east-southeast and west-northwest, and two sit nearer the center at the northeast and southwest. A single Diamond sign sits near the ring at the north. All the signs are drawn roughly, and with the Diamond at the north the layout leans toward that side. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell moves existing solid matter such as soil, sand and stone rather than creating it. Its small size gives only modest intensity. Windows connects two spaces that are not physically joined, making a portal-like link. Here it appears as four separate small rings rather than its usual band lining the seal, so the link is fragmented and weaker. Diamond limits the spell to what lies inside a container the seal is drawn on, leaving the container itself untouched. There are only two kinds of modifier, and they work together without contradiction. Neither sign is directional, so the northward lean sets no direction. The rough linework weakens the spell and shortens its life. The ring's poor roundness makes the effect fleeting and puts activation at risk.
effect: Faintly and intermittently passes soil, sand or stone held inside the container the seal is drawn on through to another place, leaving the container itself untouched. The connection flickers open only briefly, carries little material each time, and may sputter out before activating at all.

name: s42_00246.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed and neatly drawn. The center is empty, with no sigil or central sign. Seven Stillness signs are arranged in two loose circles, all with their tops toward the ring. Four sit near the ring at the north, east, south and west points. The north one is drawn bold and clean, while the others are slightly rough. Three more sit about halfway out, just inside the outer signs at the north, east and south. The east one is drawn roughly and the other two are a little rough. There is no inner sign at the west. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: There is no element sigil and no sign standing in for one, so the seal has no core and generates nothing of its own. Every sign is Stillness, which holds magic in place so an effect stays static in one location. Seven copies of the same modifier reinforce one another without contradiction, so the seal is not unstable. The signs are spread around all four sides, so no direction is favored. The missing inner west sign leaves that side with only one Stillness against two elsewhere, a slight weak point. The closed ring lets the seal activate. The roughness of most signs makes the hold somewhat weaker and shorter-lived than a cleanly drawn version.
effect: Holds whatever magic or material already lies within the seal's area fixed in place, keeping it static without adding any effect of its own. The hold is moderate and fades sooner than it otherwise would, slackening slightly toward the west before it gives out.

name: s42_00247.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, neatly drawn. The ring is open, with a wide gap at the lower left between the west and south-southwest points. Two small sigils sit side by side at the center: a light sigil on the left and a wind sigil on the right, each small relative to the ring. Seven Reflection signs, each an hourglass of two triangles meeting at a point, surround them. Four sit close to the ring, at the north-northwest, east-northeast, west-southwest and south-southeast. Three sit about halfway out and are drawn a little heavier, at the northwest, east (just beside the wind sigil) and south-southwest. Each sign is angled roughly along a line toward the center. The signs are spread evenly around the seal, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil creates and shapes light, and the wind sigil moves air. Their small size relative to the ring gives both a modest intensity. Reflection targets the reflected image found on the object the seal is drawn on, so the spell works with that reflection rather than producing light from nothing. Seven Reflection signs strengthen that focus. Because they are spread evenly and no directional sign is present, the effect is pushed in no particular direction. The seal combines two elements with only one kind of modifier, and nothing contradicts, so it should hold steady once active. The open ring means the seal does not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it takes the reflection on the surface the seal is drawn on and casts it as a soft, modest light. A gentle stir of air carries the glow evenly around the seal. The light gradually dims over time.

name: s42_00248.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, neatly drawn, with the main ring open at a gap on the east-northeast side. An earth sigil sits at the center, upright and about a quarter of the ring's radius. Four signs sit near the ring. An Entwining sign is at the north-northwest, a Link sign at the west turned to lie along the curve of the ring, a small Repetition sign at the south-southwest, and a Regions sign at the south-southeast with its point facing the center. Three small closed sub-seals sit inside the main ring. The one at the north holds a large upright Refuse sign. The one at the southeast holds an earth sigil, drawn a little rough. The one at the west-southwest holds a water sigil. The signs are unevenly placed and cluster toward the west-southwest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on solid matter such as stone and soil. Its size relative to the ring gives modest intensity. The earth sub-seal reinforces that element, though its slightly rough drawing makes its added strength weaker. Link identifies and joins pieces that came from the same source. Entwining makes the affected matter wrap around other objects. Repetition keeps resetting what it affects to its original state, so the matter keeps springing back. The single Regions sign points inward, which keeps the magic inside the ring, and because it is alone on one side it skews the effect. The Refuse sub-seal is directional and upright, so it collects unwanted material toward the north. The water sub-seal adds water to the spell. The seal stacks more than three unrelated kinds of modifier: linking, entwining, time reset and waste collection. The earth core and earth sub-seal dominate, with Link and Entwining shaping the matter, while Repetition and Refuse are secondary. The result is likely unstable. Because the signs lean west-southwest, the effect is pulled that way. The spell will not activate until the main ring is closed.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it draws together fragments of stone and soil that came from the same source and winds them, damp with a little water, around nearby objects, while repeatedly snapping them back toward their original state. Loose debris is swept toward the north of the seal. The modest effect stays within the seal but lurches unevenly toward the west-southwest, flickering between binding and resetting before collapsing early.

name: s42_00249.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background. The ring is closed but drawn unevenly and noticeably out of round, with flattened and bulging stretches. A modest-sized earth sigil sits upright at the center. Four Entwining signs surround it. Two sit on the inner circle at the north and south with their tops toward the center. Two sit near the ring at the east-northeast and west-southwest with their tops toward the ring; the east-northeast one is drawn heavily and roughly. Two Coil signs sit near the ring at the northwest and south-southeast. At the east, on the inner circle, is a small unnamed glyph: an S inside a circle, ringed by dots. The linework is a little rough throughout. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on solid matter such as stone, soil and wood. Its size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Coil softens physical matter, so the earth it works on becomes pliable. Entwining makes material wrap itself around other objects, so the softened earth winds around whatever is near. The east glyph matches no known sign. It is closest to the Whorling Wind sigil, a wind-family variant, so reading it as a second sigil is a guess. Read that way, it adds a small rotating draft that gives the wrapping a twisting motion. Entwining has never been seen inverted. The outer pair faces the opposite way to the inner pair, so the outer pair may partly loosen the grip, which would make it uneven. The signs are balanced around the ring, so no direction is favored. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they reinforce each other. However, the rough strokes and poorly rounded ring weaken the spell, shorten how long it lasts, and risk a fleeting effect.
effect: Softens nearby stone and soil into pliable, rope-like strands that twist around objects close to the seal, carried by a faint swirling draft. The grip is weak and uneven, slackening in places, and the strands may sputter or slump back after only a brief hold.

name: s42_00250.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A Rain sign sits upright at the center in place of a sigil: a small square with inward-curving sides and short paired strokes at its edges. It is small relative to the ring, about a quarter of the radius, and its lines are slightly rough. Its central space is empty. Six four-lobed Billow signs sit just inside the ring at the north-northwest, northeast, east-southeast, south-southeast, southwest and west-northwest. They are spaced roughly evenly, each turned with its top toward the center. The Billow signs at the north-northwest and west-northwest are drawn a little rougher than the others. No element sigil or other sign is present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: No fire, water, earth, wind or light sigil is present, so the spell is not tied to one element. Rain takes the central position as the core. It is drawn upright rather than inverted, so it keeps its normal effect: summoning material so that it comes down from above like rainfall. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity, and its slightly rough lines weaken it a little more. Billow turns available material into a soft, fluffy cloud. Six evenly spaced Billow signs spread that conversion around the whole seal without favoring any direction. There are no Collection signs, so the spell has no means of drawing in extra material and works only with what Rain brings down. The two kinds of modifier work together without contradiction. The slightly rough signs at the north-northwest and west-northwest may leave that side a little thinner than the rest.
effect: Brings down a light, gentle fall of soft, fluffy cloud puffs over the area above the seal, like a slow drizzle of cushions. The fall is modest and slightly patchy, a little sparser toward the northwest, and tapers off sooner than a strongly drawn seal would.

name: s42_00251.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in thin black line on a white background. The ring is closed but drawn roughly, bulging into a lopsided, rounded-square shape rather than a true circle. A small Coil sign, two crossing curved strokes forming a narrow vertical lens, sits upright at the center. There is no element sigil. Five Dispersion signs are spread around the seal about two thirds of the way to the ring. Those at the northwest, northeast, southeast and southwest have their stems toward the ring and their curves toward the center. The one at the south is flipped, with its stem toward the center and its curve toward the ring. The northwest and south signs are drawn thinner and shakier than the others. At the north-northwest sits a neatly drawn glyph turned on its side, a central stroke with mirrored branching marks on both halves. It matches no known sign exactly. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, Coil at the center acts as the core. It softens physical matter and has no effect on liquids or gases. The five Dispersion signs make the magic pour outward from the seal rather than staying on one spot. They are balanced around the ring, so no direction is favored. The flipped southern Dispersion has no clearly known difference in effect, so it reads as part of the same outward spread. The sideways glyph at the north-northwest most closely resembles Stillness with its halves mirrored. This reading is a guess. As Stillness, it would hold part of the effect static in one place, pulling slightly against the outward spread. Because it is a single sign against five Dispersion signs, the spreading dominates. The ring is far from round and the drawing is rough, so the spell is weak and short-lived and may fail to activate.
effect: Softens solid matter around the seal in a faint, uneven wave that seeps outward on all sides, with a small patch toward the north-northwest lingering a moment longer than the rest. Liquids and gases are unaffected. The softening is fleeting and often sputters out almost at once, and the spell may fail to take hold at all.

name: s42_00252.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed and neatly drawn, though its outline is slightly uneven rather than perfectly round. Two glyphs sit side by side at the center, both small relative to the ring. On the left is a water sigil. On the right is a glyph like an earth sigil without its top crossbar: two inward brackets meeting in a V, with a dot on each side. Six signs are spaced evenly about two thirds of the way out from the center, at the west-northwest, north, northeast, east-southeast, south-southeast and southwest. Each is three short strokes with the middle one longest and its top toward the ring. Five match Aeriforms Defined. The one at the west-northwest is a mirrored variant. The ones at the northeast, southwest and west-northwest are drawn a little more roughly than the rest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell. The glyph beside it matches no sigil exactly. Its closest match is the earth sigil missing its crossbar, so reading it as earth is a guess. Read that way, the seal works on water and solid matter such as soil or sand together. Both sigils are small relative to the ring, so the intensity is modest. Aeriforms Defined shares its design with the wind sigil's modifiers and its name with the sigil that creates air. Here it gives the spell's material a gaseous, airy quality. The mirrored west-northwest glyph is closest to Aeriforms Defined, also a guess, and is read as adding the same effect. The six signs are evenly spaced and non-directional in placement, so no side is favored and the effect stays centered on the seal. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing contradicts. The rougher strokes on three of the signs make the effect slightly thinner on those sides.
effect: Works water through nearby soil and fills the mixture with air, producing a modest, light, frothy mud that swells up evenly around the seal. The froth is slightly thinner and settles a little sooner toward the northeast, southwest and west-northwest.

name: s42_00253.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A small water sigil, slightly rough, sits upright at the center. Eight Columns signs are spread around the seal. Five sit in the band between the two rings, at the north-northeast, east, south, west-southwest and northwest. The ones at the east and north-northeast are inverted, with their crossbars toward the center. The other three have their crossbars toward the ring. Three more Columns signs sit inside the inner ring at the north-northeast, southeast and west-southwest, all with their crossbars toward the ring. A smaller closed sub-seal attaches by a short line at the east-northeast, outside the main ring. It holds a fire sigil that fills about half of its ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil sets the element. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest base intensity, and its slightly rough drawing makes the flow a little uneven. The second ring adds strength to the core spell. The eight Columns signs are balanced around the seal, so the water rises as a column straight up rather than leaning to one side. Their number increases the amount of water produced. The two inverted Columns signs manifest horizontally, like Dispersion, so part of the water spreads outward at the base instead of rising. The attached fire sub-seal is closed and has a large sigil relative to its own ring, so it adds strong heat to the water. Only one kind of modifier is present, and the fire supplements the water rather than contradicting a sign, so the seal is not unstable.
effect: Raises a sizable column of hot, steaming water straight up from the seal, while some of the water spills outward across the ground around its base. The flow surges slightly unevenly.

name: s42_00254.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, neatly drawn, with the ring open by a gap on the right side between east and southeast. A large Immobility sign sits upright at the center, filling a good part of the inner space. There is no element sigil. Nine Mimicry signs surround it, each with its top toward the ring. Three larger ones sit near the ring at the west, north-northeast and south-southeast. Six smaller ones form an inner circle about halfway out, at the north, northwest, east-northeast, southeast, south and west-southwest. The east-northeast one is drawn a little heavier and rougher than the rest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the central Immobility sign is the core of the seal. It makes the target immovable relative to the seal, so it holds its shape as if frozen while still being carried along when the seal moves. Its large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect. Mimicry makes a target follow or imitate movements. Paired with Immobility, the target copies the motion of the seal instead of moving on its own. The two signs reinforce each other rather than conflicting. The nine Mimicry signs are spread evenly in two circles, so no direction is favored and the following is equal on all sides. The single slightly rough Mimicry sign adds a small unevenness on that side. The seal does not activate while the ring is open.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it locks the target firmly in shape and position relative to the seal and makes it follow every movement of the seal, as if rigidly fixed to it. The hold is strong and even, with only a slight lag in how closely the target follows on the east-northeast side.

name: s42_00256.png
description: A fully visible seal on a white background. The ring is closed but drawn a little roughly and slightly out of round. A large Stillness sign sits upright at the center in place of a sigil, and there is no element sigil. A Coil sign sits at the north. A Collection sign sits near the ring at the east-northeast, with its closed end toward the center and its open side facing the ring. A Binding sign sits at the southwest, its arcs curving toward the ring. A small Mimicry sign lies at the west-northwest with its top toward the center. A small Windows sign, a hatched little ring, sits near the ring at the west. An Aeriforms Defined sign sits at the south. The Collection and Aeriforms Defined signs are drawn a little roughly, and more signs cluster on the western side than the eastern. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, Stillness takes the center and sets the core behavior: holding magic and material static in one place. Its large size makes that hold the strongest part of the seal. Binding supports it by halting movement and making the held material act as one unit, so the two together dominate. Collection draws in nearby material, but here its open side faces outward instead of in its usual inward orientation. That inversion is untested, so it is read as a weaker, scattered gathering from beyond the ring. Aeriforms Defined ties the spell to air. Coil softens physical matter but cannot act on gases, so it clashes with the air focus. Mimicry makes the target imitate movement, which directly contradicts Stillness and Binding. A single small Windows sign, rather than a full lining ring, gives only a faint link to another space. The seal stacks well over three unrelated kinds of modifier and includes direct contradictions, so the result is likely unstable. None of the signs is directional, but the western cluster weights the effect toward the west. The rough, slightly uneven ring further weakens and shortens it.
effect: Draws in nearby air and loose material and tries to hold it still as a single bound mass, but the hold wavers. The mass softens, twitches as if copying movement around it, flickers as though briefly opening onto somewhere else, and sags toward the west. It collapses after a short time.

name: s42_00257.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but noticeably out of round, with flattened, bulging sides. A water sigil sits upright at the center, moderate in size relative to the ring. Four Stability and Level Planes signs sit at the northeast, east-southeast, west-southwest and west-northwest, each with its top toward the center; the east-southeast one is slightly rough. At the south is a Stability and Level Planes sign with a small light sigil fused to its top. At the north is a thin, single wide arc that matches no known sign exactly. The signs are evenly spaced, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Stability and Level Planes is non-directional and keeps its target balanced on a level plane, floating while staying level. Five of them, counting the fused one, are spread evenly, so the effect favors no direction and holds the water flat and steady. The light fused to the south sign has no exact match. As a guess, it combines leveling with light and adds a soft glow to the leveled water. The north arc most closely resembles Binding drawn with one line, also a guess. It would bind the water together so it moves as a single unit. That makes three kinds of modifier, which work together without contradiction. The out-of-round ring weakens the seal, so the effect is fleeting and may barely take hold.
effect: Draws water into a single bound sheet that floats level above the seal with a faint glow, but the sheet wobbles and flickers and breaks apart soon after it forms.

name: s42_00259.png
description: A fully visible seal on a white background, made of two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. There is no element sigil. A Selection sign, a square divided into four cells with its cross arms extending beyond the edges, sits upright at the center. It is moderately sized relative to the ring and drawn with heavy, slightly rough strokes. Three small Diamond signs sit in the band between the two rings, near the outer ring. One is at the north, slightly east of true north, one at the southeast, and one at the west-southwest. Each has its top toward the ring, and all three are drawn neatly. They are spaced evenly around the seal. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: No fire, water, earth, wind or light sigil is present, so Selection takes the center in place of a sigil. It sets the core of the spell, but it supplies no element or action. Selection is non-directional and confines a spell's effect to the object the seal is drawn on. The three Diamond signs sit in the outer band, where a second ring adds further effects. Diamond does the opposite of Selection: it limits the effect to objects held inside a container and leaves the container itself untouched. The two signs therefore directly contradict each other about what is targeted. The large central Selection dominates. The three small Diamonds pull the focus partly toward the object's contents, so the result is likely unstable. The Diamonds are evenly spaced, so they add no direction. The slightly rough center makes the seal a little weaker and shorter-lived. With no element and no acting sign, the seal only defines a target and produces no force of its own.
effect: Marks the object it is drawn on as the target of magic but produces no visible force or element of its own. Its focus wavers unevenly between the object itself and whatever is held inside it, and the marking fades somewhat sooner than a cleanly drawn seal's would.

name: s42_00263.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background. The ring is neatly drawn and open, with a gap at the upper right between the north-northeast and east-northeast signs. There is no element sigil. The center holds a fairly large glyph of three vertical strokes: a tall middle stroke flanked by two shorter, heavier bars of equal height. It is upright and a little rough. It resembles Detection but is symmetric rather than stepped. Five star-shaped signs sit near the ring. Four are Concealment signs: eight-armed stars with eye marks on some arm ends. They sit at the north-northeast, west-southwest, east-northeast and south-southeast. The north-northeast and west-southwest signs have their tops toward the center. The east-northeast and south-southeast signs have their tops toward the ring. The north-northeast sign is drawn roughly and the west-southwest one a little roughly. The fifth sign, at the southeast, is a bolder star with eye marks on only its lower arms and no upper part. Its top faces the center. More of the signs crowd the east and southeast side than the west. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the central glyph serves as the core of the spell. It matches no known sign exactly. Its closest match is Detection, drawn mirrored so both sides match, and reading it that way is a guess. Read as Detection, the core senses the presence of things around the seal rather than acting on an element, and its fairly large size gives that sensing a solid reach. The four Concealment signs hide a target. The southeast star lacks its top part, so its closest match is a partial Concealment, also a guess, and it would add a weaker share of the same hiding effect. Concealment is not known to change with orientation, so the mixed facing of the stars does not reverse anything. The signs are unbalanced and crowd the east-southeast, so the hiding is heavier on that side. Only one kind of modifier is stacked on the core, so the seal is coherent. The slightly rough center and the roughly drawn north-northeast sign make the effect a little uneven. The open ring means nothing activates until it is closed.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it senses presences around the seal and shrouds them from sight. The concealment is thickest toward the east-southeast and thins out on the opposite side, where it flickers slightly and lets glimpses show through.

name: s42_00264.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A fire sigil sits upright at the center and is fairly large, about a third of the ring's radius. Five Regions signs, each a chevron with its point facing the center, sit around the seal. Four sit close to the ring at the north-northeast, east-southeast, south-southwest and west-northwest. The fifth sits partway in at the east-southeast, just inside the outer one there. Three small Windows signs, each a ring of short hatch marks around an empty center, sit at the north near the ring, at the west about halfway out, and at the south-southeast. The south-southeast Windows sign is drawn a little roughly. The signs are spread evenly around the seal, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil makes this a fire spell, and its fairly large size relative to the ring gives a solid, fairly strong intensity. All five Regions signs point inward. When every Regions sign points inward, the magic manifests only within the ring of the seal and not outside it. Windows connects two spaces that are not physically joined, like a portal. Three of them spread around the seal open the space inside the ring onto another location. Windows is radially symmetric, so its rotation does not change its effect. The slight roughness of one Windows sign weakens that part of the connection a little, but it does not break it. Only two kinds of modifier are present, confinement and connection. They work together without contradiction, and the balanced layout pushes the effect in no direction.
effect: Produces a fairly strong fire held strictly within the bounds of the seal, with its flames and heat carried through to a separate linked location, as if they were burning on the other side of a window. The passage holds steady overall but flickers slightly along one edge.

name: s42_00266.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background. The main ring is neatly drawn but open, with a gap at the north-northwest. There is no element sigil. An upright Columns sign sits at the center, about a third of the ring's radius in size. Six signs sit near the ring: an inverted Rain sign at the north-northwest beside the gap, a slightly rough Pointing sign at the north-northeast, a Stillness sign at the east-northeast, an Envelopment sign at the south-southeast, a slightly rough Levitation sign at the south-southwest with its arrow pointing toward the center, and an Aeriforms Defined sign at the west. A small sub-seal sits inside the main ring at the north-northeast. Its ring is roughly drawn and open at the lower left, and it holds a Reflection sign at its center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the central Columns sign is the core of the spell. It gives the magic a column-shaped area of effect and drives it upward. Aeriforms Defined is the only element-related mark, so reading the material as air or gas is a guess. Pointing shapes the column into a cone, and Columns directs it. The single Levitation sign points inward from the south-southwest, so it lifts the effect and pushes it toward the north-northeast. Its rough drawing weakens this push. Several signs contradict each other. Stillness tries to hold the effect in one place against the movement from Columns and Levitation. Inverted Rain pushes things out of its area, while Envelopment tries to wrap around a target. The seal also stacks far more than three unrelated kinds of modifier. Columns, Pointing and Levitation dominate, so the result is likely unstable. The sub-seal's own ring is open, so its Reflection sign contributes nothing. The main ring must be closed before anything activates.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it raises a narrow, cone-tipped column of air that leans toward the north-northeast, stalling and lurching as it moves. It fitfully tries to wrap around a target and shoves nearby things away in uneven bursts, then collapses early. The small inner seal adds nothing while its own ring remains open.

name: s42_00267.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed but drawn roughly and noticeably out of round, bulging at the lower left and flattened at the upper right. A neatly drawn water sigil sits at the center, moderate in size relative to the ring. A large, heavily drawn Strengthening sign sits at the northeast, partway to the ring, with its apex toward the ring. A small Gathering sign sits near the ring at the northwest, its forked arrow pointing toward the center. A Collection sign sits near the ring at the west-southwest, its closed end facing the center. A small Diamond sign sits at the southeast, about halfway out and tilted. A small Selection sign, a cross through a square, sits near the ring at the south. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Gathering and Collection both draw material in from around the seal, so together they pull nearby water into the spell, and being on opposite sides of the west they add no strong direction. Strengthening, drawn large and heavy, makes the result firmer and more durable and is the strongest modifier present. Diamond and Selection directly contradict each other. Diamond limits the effect to the contents of a container while sparing the container, but Selection confines it to the very object the seal is drawn on. Diamond sits closer to the center and is drawn slightly larger, so it leans dominant, but the conflict means the result is likely unstable. The gathering and strengthening parts dominate overall. The rough, uneven ring weakens the spell and shortens its life, and its poor roundness makes the effect fleeting.
effect: Draws nearby water into the vessel the seal is drawn on and firms it into a denser, reinforced mass, but the hold flickers between the water inside and the vessel itself, stiffening each unevenly. The gathered water stays firm only briefly before the spell collapses and it slackens back to ordinary water.

name: s42_00268.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background, drawn neatly, with two concentric rings. Both are open. The outer ring has a gap at the lower left, between the west-southwest and the south-southwest. The inner ring has a gap at the lower right, between the east and the south. A light sigil, a diamond set inside a square with four short spokes, sits upright at the center. It is moderately large relative to the ring, a little over a third of the radius. Four Repetition signs sit inside the inner ring, a little over halfway out from the center, at the north, east, south-southwest and west. Each is drawn with its top toward the center. Three Selection signs, each a small crossed square drawn at a different rotation, sit in the band near the outer ring at the north, west-southwest and south. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil makes this a light spell. Its moderately large size relative to the ring gives a fairly bright effect. Light from this sigil normally diminishes over time. Repetition continuously resets what it affects to the state it had when the spell first took hold. Four Repetition signs are spaced around the sigil, so the light keeps returning to its initial brightness instead of dimming. Selection is non-directional and confines a spell's effect to the object the seal is drawn on. The three Selection signs keep the light on that object rather than letting it spread or project outward. The signs are balanced around the ring, so no direction is favored. The two kinds of modifier support each other without conflict. A seal activates only when its ring is closed, so neither ring works while both have gaps.
effect: Once both rings are closed, the object it is drawn on gives off a fairly bright, steady glow that stays on the object and does not spread. Instead of slowly dimming, the light keeps renewing itself to its original brightness, so it lasts far longer than an ordinary light.

name: s42_00269.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background, its main ring closed and neatly drawn. A light sigil, a diamond set inside a square with four short spokes, sits upright at the center and is fairly large, reaching about half the ring's radius. Five Reflection signs, each an hourglass of two triangles meeting at a point, sit at the northeast, south-southeast, south-southwest, west and northwest. The northeast one sits closest to the ring, the others about two thirds of the way out, and each is turned at a different angle. The northwest Reflection is drawn a little roughly. Three smaller sub-seals sit outside the main ring, each joined to it by a short line. The one at the north-northeast has its ring closed and holds an earth sigil. The one at the south-southeast has its ring closed and holds a Partition sign. The one at the west holds a small light sigil, but its ring is open, with a gap at the upper left. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil sets the element, so the seal creates and shapes light. Its large size relative to the ring gives a strong intensity. Reflection draws on a reflected image found on the object the seal is drawn on. Five of them spread evenly around the sigil favor no direction, so the light works with that reflected image across the whole seal. Their varied rotations do not change this, since Reflection has no known directional behavior. The single rough Reflection slightly weakens that part of the effect but does not unbalance it. The closed earth sub-seal adds manipulation of solid matter such as stone or wood, so the effect also acts on the solid surface the seal is drawn on. The closed Partition sub-seal outlines the borders of the area of effect, so the light and reflection are held within a defined boundary. The western light sub-seal has its ring open and adds nothing. Only Reflection and Partition act as modifiers, alongside a second element, and none of them contradict each other.
effect: Draws a strong light out of the reflected image held in the solid surface the seal is drawn on and casts that image brightly within a clearly bordered area. The light is slightly uneven on one side and gradually dims over time, and the unfinished western light attachment adds no extra brightness.

name: s42_00271.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but a little rough and slightly out of round. A water sigil sits upright at the center, also a little rough, and is moderate in size relative to the ring. Four Aeriforms Defined signs, each three short strokes fanning outward, sit at the northwest, northeast, southeast and southwest, about three quarters of the way to the ring, with their tops toward the ring. The northeast one is a little rougher than the others. A single Regions sign sits near the ring at the east point, its apex pointing inward toward the center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Aeriforms Defined shares its design with the wind sigil's modifiers and its name with the Aeriforms sigil, which creates air. Its exact function is uncertain, so reading it as giving the water a gaseous, airy form is a guess. With four evenly spaced and none inverted, that quality spreads evenly with no pull in any direction. Regions sets where magic manifests relative to the seal. Pointing inward, it keeps the effect inside the ring instead of letting it spread beyond the seal. These are only two kinds of modifier and they do not conflict. The rough ring and sigil make the effect somewhat weaker and shorter-lived.
effect: Produces a moderate cloud of fine water vapor that hangs within the bounds of the seal and does not drift past its edge. The mist forms slightly thin and uneven and thins out sooner than a cleanly drawn version would.

name: s42_00272.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. Two sigils sit side by side at the center, each about a quarter of the ring's radius: a water sigil on the left and a wind sigil on the right, both upright and neat. A Rain sign, a little rough, sits at the northwest about halfway to the ring and is drawn in its normal orientation, not inside-out. A large Regions sign sits near the ring at the east, its point aimed inward toward the center. A Reflection sign, an hourglass shape, sits at the northeast. A Pointing sign sits near the ring at the west-northwest. A Partition sign sits near the ring at the west-southwest, rotated at an angle. A roughly drawn Purification sign lies on its side at the south. The signs are spread evenly around the ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water and wind sigils set two elements: water and moving air. Their small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity.
