Rain in its normal orientation summons the water as falling rain, and the wind sigil drives that rain. Regions is directional. With a single sign at the east pointing inward, all Regions signs point to the same side, so the magic is pushed westward across the seal. Pointing gives the material a conical shape. Partition outlines the borders of the area of effect. Purification separates waste from water, but its rough drawing weakens that part. Reflection targets a reflected image, which has little relation to the rest of the seal. The seal stacks six unrelated kinds of modifier: rainfall, direction, cone shaping, boundary, cleansing and reflection. That is well beyond three, so the result is likely unstable. The paired sigils, Rain and Regions dominate. Partition and Pointing shape the result only loosely. The rough Purification and the unrelated Reflection add little beyond flicker and unevenness.
effect: Summons a light, wind-driven shower that sweeps westward across a bounded patch. The water gathers fitfully into narrow, cone-shaped gusts. Only patches of the water come out cleansed, and the shower sputters and breaks apart early instead of settling into steady rain.

name: s42_00273.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A fire sigil, upright, sits at the center at a moderate size relative to the ring. Four Binding signs, each a larger arc over a smaller arc, sit about halfway between the center and the ring at the northwest, northeast, southeast and southwest points. Each has its curved top facing outward toward the ring. No other signs are present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil makes this a fire spell. Its moderate size relative to the ring gives a moderate intensity. Binding halts the movement of the target material and binds it together so it acts and moves as a single unit. Applied to fire, it keeps the flames from scattering or spreading and holds them as one cohesive body. The four Binding signs are evenly spaced at the intercardinal points and carry no direction, so the effect is balanced on all sides and stays centered on the seal. Only one kind of modifier is present, and the neat drawing and closed ring let the spell activate and hold steady.
effect: Produces a moderate fire that holds together as a single, compact body of flame and stays still over the seal instead of spreading or flickering outward. The bound flame can be moved as one unit without breaking apart.

name: s42_00274.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short strokes, sits upright at the center. It is fairly large, a little under half the ring's radius, and slightly rough. Five signs sit near the ring. Two plain Rain signs are at the north-northwest, drawn roughly, and the west-southwest, a little rough. At the south-southeast is a slightly rough Rain sign with a small Collection sign attached to its lower side. At the east-southeast is a neatly drawn Rain sign with an extra dot, turned so the dotted side faces the center. At the east-northeast is a single wide arc, like a Binding sign with only one curve, faintly drawn and slightly rough. The signs are spread evenly around the ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil makes this a spell that moves and manipulates air without creating it. Its fairly large size gives a fairly strong intensity. Rain summons its material so that it comes down from above over the seal's area. With wind, it brings air down rather than producing new air. Rain is radially symmetric, so turning a sign does not invert it. Only flipping it inside out would, and none of these signs is flipped, so all of them act in the normal sense. The dotted Rain matches no known sign exactly. Reading it as a Rain variant is a guess, and it adds to the same downward summoning. The Collection attached to one Rain sign gathers material from above and around the seal, so nearby air is drawn in to feed the fall. The single arc is closest to Binding, also a guess. Binding makes moving material act as a single unit, so the descending air holds together. That is three compatible kinds of modifier with no contradiction. Even spacing means no direction is favored. The rough Rain signs weaken the fall and make it uneven, while the neatly drawn ring lets the spell activate and hold.
effect: Draws in surrounding air and sends it pouring down from above over the area around the seal in fairly strong, rain-like gusts that hold together as a single cohesive downdraft. The downpour is patchy, coming down harder on some sides than others, and it slackens sooner than a cleanly drawn seal would.

name: s42_00275.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed. The ring is drawn roughly, with flattened sides that make it look somewhat hexagonal rather than round. The center is empty, with no sigil or sign. Four small Sights Set signs sit about three quarters of the way out from the center, one each at the north, east, south and west points. Each has its diamond end toward the ring and its arrowhead pointing inward toward the center. The signs are slightly rough, and the east one is drawn heavier and more roughly than the others. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil and no sign in the center, the seal has no element and no core effect, so the four Sights Set signs are the whole spell. Sights Set aims a spell at a point or target chosen by the caster. All four arrows point inward and are evenly balanced, so the aim converges on the center of the seal rather than favoring any side. Only one kind of modifier is present and nothing contradicts it, so the seal is not unstable. It is still weak: the signs are small and rough, which makes the effect faint and short-lived. The ring is not round enough, so any effect is fleeting and the spell may fail to activate at all.
effect: Creates a faint aiming focus directed inward onto the center of the seal, but it carries no element and does nothing on its own. The focus flickers, holds only briefly, and may fail to take hold at all.

name: s42_00276.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A fire sigil sits upright at the center and is fairly large relative to the ring, reaching a little under half the radius. Five single signs are scattered around it, mostly on the left side. A Stretch sign sits at the west, about two thirds of the way to the ring, with its arc toward the center and its opening toward the ring. A small Expansion sign sits at the west-northwest near the ring, its nested corner brackets pointing outward. A Projection sign sits at the south, with its flat bar toward the ring and its open side facing the center. An Envelopment sign sits near the ring at the north-northeast. A small Repetition sign sits close to the ring at the southwest. The signs are unbalanced and cluster toward the west-southwest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil makes this a fire spell. Its fairly large size relative to the ring gives a strong intensity. Projection pushes the effect outward from the seal. The signs lean toward the west-southwest, so the output is biased that way. Stretch draws affected matter into long, flexible ribbons. It normally works on solids, so its hold on flame is weak. Expansion, with its corners outward, makes the effect grow. Envelopment makes the effect wrap around whatever it reaches. Repetition keeps resetting its target to its starting state, which works directly against the growth from Expansion. The seal stacks five unrelated kinds of modifier, and two of them contradict each other. The large fire sigil and Projection dominate, with the westward lean setting the direction. Stretch and Envelopment shape the flame only loosely, and the clash between Expansion and Repetition makes the size swing back and forth. The result is likely unstable.
effect: Throws strong fire outward from the seal toward the west-southwest as loose, ribbon-like streams of flame. The streams swell, then snap back to their starting size, and try to coil around whatever they reach, but they wrap only in patches. The flames waver and sputter between bursts and break apart well before a steady effect can form.

name: s42_00277.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. Two glyphs share the center: an earth sigil just left of center and a Link sign just right of it, both modest in size relative to the ring. Five Columns signs sit around them, each with its crossbar toward the ring and its stem pointing toward the center: one at the northwest, one at the northeast, one at the west, one at the southwest and one at the southeast. The west and northeast Columns are drawn larger and heavier. The southeast Columns is smaller and more roughly drawn than the rest. There is no sign at the east, so the arrangement leans toward the west-northwest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on solid matter such as stone, sand and soil. Its modest size relative to the ring gives a moderate intensity. Link shares the center as a second core. It identifies pieces that broke off from, or were made from, the same source and creates a link between them. Columns gives the magic a column-shaped area of effect and drives it with force, and five of them raise the range and quantity of material moved. Because the signs are unbalanced, with none at the east and the weight on the western side, the column is pushed toward the west-northwest instead of rising straight up. The roughly drawn southeast Columns contributes less, which makes that side slightly weaker. Only two kinds of modifier are present, linking and column force, and they do not contradict each other.
effect: Draws together fragments of stone or soil that came from the same source and drives them as a moderately strong column slanting toward the west-northwest. The push is a little weaker and less even on its southeastern side.

name: s42_00278.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A fire sigil sits upright at the center and is fairly large, about half the ring's radius. Seven Levitation signs surround it. Four sit near the ring at the northeast, southeast, southwest and northwest, each with its arrowhead pointing in toward the center. Two smaller Levitation signs sit closer to the sigil at the north and south, also pointing inward. The seventh, at the west near the ring, is inverted, with its arrowhead pointing outward toward the ring. The southeast sign is drawn with a heavier stroke than the others. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, and its large size relative to the ring gives a strong flame. Levitation floats its target into the air, and inward-pointing signs arranged evenly around a seal tend to shape the floating material into a sphere. Shorter signs carry the effect a shorter distance, so the small north and south signs add less lift than the four outer ones. Inverted Levitation counteracts regular Levitation, so the outward-pointing west sign directly contradicts the inward signs. The six inward signs dominate, so the fire still rises as a sphere. The lone inverted sign weakens the lift and adds an outward push toward the west, so the result is likely mildly unstable. The heavier southeast stroke adds a little extra lift on that side, which reinforces the lean away from the southeast toward the west.
effect: Lifts a strong, roughly spherical ball of fire into the air above the seal, where it hovers lower than its size would suggest and keeps leaning and drifting toward the west. The flame bobs and wobbles as it floats instead of holding a steady position.

name: s42_00280.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed and drawn slightly rough. A neatly drawn wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short rays, sits upright at the center and is fairly large, reaching a little under half the ring's radius. Six different signs are spaced around it near the ring. At the north-northwest is a Holding sign, a pair of facing curves with dots, turned nearly upside down. At the north-northeast is a Dispersion sign, with its stem pointing toward the center and its curve toward the ring. At the east-northeast is a Reflection sign, an hourglass shape lying on its side. At the southeast is a Detection sign, three parallel strokes of increasing length. At the south is a Stretch sign, its arch opening toward the ring. At the west-southwest is a stretched zigzag Crushing sign with its peaks toward the center, which is inverted. The signs are evenly balanced around the ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves and manipulates existing air, and its fairly large size gives a fairly strong effect. Dispersion makes the magic pour outward instead of beaming it in one direction. Holding works against this by keeping the target in a shape defined by the seal, so these two parts pull in opposite directions. Stretch turns solid matter into long, flexible ribbons. The inverted Crushing sign pulls crushed material back toward its original form. Both act only on solids, which wind magic does not create, so they can only work on dust or debris the air sweeps up. Reflection would turn the effect toward reflected images. Detection assists a sensing function whose exact role is unclear. The seal stacks six unrelated kinds of modifier, and two of them directly contradict each other. The large wind sigil and the outward pour of Dispersion dominate, Holding acts as a partial brake, and the other four contribute only faint, erratic touches. The result is likely unstable, and the slightly rough ring shortens and weakens it further.
effect: Releases a fairly strong rush of air that pours outward from the seal, surging and stalling unevenly as it keeps half-snapping back toward a fixed shape. Any dust or grit it catches is briefly drawn into stringy ribbons or clumped back together before scattering. The airflow sputters and collapses after a short time.

name: s42_00281.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background with two concentric rings, both closed and drawn slightly roughly. A Convergence sign, a downward-pointing triangle, sits upright at the center in place of a sigil and is fairly large relative to the ring. No element sigil is present. Six bracket-shaped signs sit about two thirds of the way out from the center. Five are Projection signs, at the north-northwest, northeast, east-northeast, east-southeast and south-southeast. Four of them have their tops toward the ring. The one at the east-southeast is inverted, with its top toward the center. The sixth sign, at the west-southwest, is a Projection-like bracket with an extra short stroke rising from its right edge. The northeast, east-northeast and west-southwest signs are drawn a little roughly. Most signs cluster on the eastern side, leaving the west nearly empty.
justification: With no element sigil, Convergence at the center serves as the core. It focuses the spell's magic to a single point and packs loose particles tightly together. Because no element is set, the spell works on whatever material is brought to it. Projection casts an effect outward from the seal, so the four upright Projection signs push that focused mass away from the center. The west-southwest glyph matches no known sign exactly. Its closest match is Projection, so reading it that way is a guess, and under that reading it adds a weaker outward push to the west. The inverted Projection at the east-southeast would turn its push inward on that side. It is a single sign against five outward ones, so it only dampens the push there and does not destabilize the seal. Most signs sit on the eastern side, so the outward push leans east and northeast rather than spreading evenly. The slightly rough rings and the few roughly drawn signs make the spell somewhat weaker and shorter-lived.
effect: Gathers material directed into the seal into a tight, compact point and casts it outward, mostly toward the east and northeast. Only a faint push goes west, and the push to the east-southeast is held back. The effect is somewhat weak and fades sooner than a cleanly drawn seal would.

name: s42_00283.png
description:
A fully visible seal on a clean background. The ring is closed and neatly drawn. A water sigil sits at the center, upright and small relative to the ring. Five signs are spread unevenly around it, about three quarters of the way out:
- An inverted Crushing sign sits at the north-northwest, drawn as a heavier zigzag with its top toward the center.
- A small Piercing sign sits at the northeast, tilted, with its top toward the center.
- A Refuse sign sits at the east-northeast, rotated so its diamond head points inward and slightly north, with its crossed legs toward the ring.
- A Mimicry sign sits at the west, lying sideways with its top toward the ring. It is drawn roughly and is cramped and shaky.
- A Selection sign sits at the southwest near the ring, drawn as a tilted grid of crossing lines.
The southern and southeastern parts of the seal are empty, so the signs cluster toward the north-northwest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification:
The water sigil makes this a water spell, and its small size gives it a low intensity. Each sign adds its own effect:
- Piercing makes the water manifest as projectiles.
- Refuse is directional and drags unwanted material toward where it points, which here is inward toward the seal.
- Inverted Crushing reforms crushed material into its original shape. Water is not a crushed solid, so it only acts on debris the seal draws in.
- Selection confines the spell's effect to the object the seal is drawn on.
- Mimicry imitates movement but has no decorative sigil to copy. Its rough drawing makes it weak, so it adds only jittery motion.
The seal stacks five unrelated kinds of modifier: projectiles, waste collection, reforming, confinement and imitation. Selection also directly contradicts Piercing, since projectiles must leave a surface that Selection holds them to. The water sigil and Piercing dominate, with Refuse second. The uneven spread biases the effect toward the north-northwest. The result is likely unstable.
effect: Forms a little water into short, sharp darts that sputter weakly off the marked object, mostly toward the north-northwest. Most of the darts break apart or cling to the surface instead of flying free. At the same time, grit and debris creep inward toward the seal and briefly clump back together, with jerky, erratic motion, before the whole effect collapses early.

name: s42_00285.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but drawn roughly and noticeably out of round, with flattened, lumpy sides. A wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes, sits upright at the center and is modest in size relative to the ring. Six Piercing signs, each a short stroke through a small diamond, surround it with the top of each glyph toward the center. Four sit near the ring at the north-northeast, east-southeast, south-southwest and west-northwest. Two more sit closer in, at the east-northeast and north-northwest. The north-northeast and north-northwest signs are drawn heavier and rougher than the others. More signs crowd the upper half, so the arrangement leans toward the north-northeast. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves air rather than creating it. Its modest size gives a modest intensity. Piercing is non-directional and makes the spell's material manifest as projectiles, with the number of signs setting how many. Six signs give about six bolts. With no directional sign, the bolts follow no set direction. Because the Piercing signs cluster on the northern side, more of the bolts should form on that side, giving an uneven spread rather than a deliberate aim. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing conflicts. However, the rough linework and the poorly rounded ring make the spell weak and fleeting, and it may sputter or fail to hold.
effect: Whips the surrounding air into about six small, thin darts of wind that shoot out from the seal in loose, scattered directions, with more of them flying off toward the north than the south. The darts are weak and uneven, flicker as they form, and break apart into harmless gusts after a moment. Some may fail to form at all.

name: s42_00286.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background. The ring is closed and mostly round, with a slightly uneven outline. There is no element sigil. A large Glaives sign stands upright at the center, about half the ring's radius in size, drawn in heavy, rough strokes. Seven signs surround it. A Projection bracket sits at the north, its open side facing the center. An Aeriforms Defined sign of three short strokes sits near the ring at the north-northeast, rotated at a slant. A small Envelopment sign sits near the ring at the east-northeast. A roughly drawn Dispersion sign sits at the southeast with its top toward the ring. A Reflection hourglass sits at the south-southeast. A Sights Set sign sits at the southwest, its arrow pointing out toward the ring and its diamond toward the center. A smaller Glaives sign sits near the ring at the west-northwest, its prongs pointing toward the center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the large central Glaives sign forms the core of the seal. Glaives set how deeply magic embeds itself into flesh, and their large size relative to the ring points to deep embedding. The second Glaives sign at the west-northwest reinforces this. Sights Set lets the caster aim the effect at a chosen target. Envelopment makes the effect surround that target. Projection casts the effect outward from the seal, and Dispersion makes it pour outward rather than hold to a beam. Reflection targets a reflected image. Aeriforms Defined ties the effect to gases. Together these stack well over three unrelated kinds of modifier, and Envelopment's wrapping pulls against the outward pour of Projection and Dispersion. The central Glaives dominate, with Sights Set aiming the effect and Envelopment and Projection delivering it. Reflection and Aeriforms Defined are the weakest links. The result is likely unstable. The signs are balanced around the ring, so no direction is favored beyond the caster's aim. The rough linework on the central Glaives and several signs further weakens the spell and shortens its duration.
effect: Casts a wavering surge of magic outward at a target chosen by the caster, sinking deep into its flesh and partly wrapping around it. The surge leaks away unevenly in thin, misty wisps and flickers across reflected images instead of holding to its target. It collapses well before taking full hold.

name: s42_00287.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A large fire sigil sits upright at the center, about half the ring's radius in size. Six signs surround it at uneven spacing. A Diamond sign sits near the ring at the southeast. A single Columns sign, drawn a little roughly, sits at the south with its stem toward the center and its crossbar toward the ring. An Expansion sign of nested corner brackets sits at the west-northwest with its corners pointing outward. A Pulling sign sits near the ring at the northeast with its arrowhead pointing outward toward the ring, so it is inverted. A Pointing sign, drawn rotated with its curled ends, sits at the west-southwest. A Sights Set sign sits at the east with its diamond end toward the center and its arrow pointing east toward the ring. The signs are unbalanced and weighted toward the south-southeast. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, and its large size relative to the ring gives a strong, intense flame. Pointing shapes the fire into a cone that Columns can direct. The lone, unbalanced Columns sign at the south drives the column toward the south instead of straight up, and its slight roughness weakens that push a little. Expansion with its corners outward makes the effect grow. The inverted Pulling sign, arrow outward, pushes away instead of pulling, sending force toward the northeast. Sights Set lets the caster aim the effect, pointed east. Diamond limits the spell to objects inside a container the seal is drawn on, leaving the container itself unaffected. These signs stack more than three unrelated kinds of modifier: shape, growth, direction, pushing, aiming and containment. Their directions also contradict each other, with the column pulling south, the push going northeast and the aim pointing east. The large fire sigil, the cone shape and the southward column dominate, and the aim and push fight against them, so the result is likely unstable.
effect: Produces a strong, swelling cone of flame that acts only on the contents of the container the seal is drawn on, sparing the container itself. The flame lurches between the south, east and northeast as it tries to follow the caster's aim, sputtering unevenly and collapsing well before its full strength is reached.

name: s42_00289.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background. A double ring, an outer ring with a second ring just inside it, both closed and neatly drawn. A small Crosshair sign sits upright at the center, its four short arms aimed north, east, south and west. Three Refuse signs sit about two thirds of the way to the inner ring, at the northeast, southeast and southwest, each rotated so its top faces the center. At the northwest, in the matching position, is a small triangular glyph drawn in heavy, dark, scribbled ink. Its strokes are hard to separate, but it reads as a triangle with a small loop at one corner and matches no known sign. Two smaller closed sub-seals sit outside the main ring, each joined to it by a short line. The one at the north-northeast holds a fire sigil of moderate size. The one at the south-southwest holds a large earth sigil that fills most of its ring. The main ring holds no element sigil.
justification: With no sigil in the main ring, the Crosshair at the center is the core. It is directional and aims the seal's effect at whatever its short ends point at. Upright, it points the effect along the north, south, east and west axes around the seal. Refuse is directional and collects unwanted material toward where it points. All three point inward, so waste is drawn into the middle of the seal. The northwest glyph is closest to Convergence, a triangle, though its loop also recalls the fire sigil. Reading it as Convergence is a guess. Read that way, it packs the gathered material tightly toward a single point. The attached fire sub-seal adds heat to the effect. The large earth sigil in the other sub-seal gives strong control over solid matter such as grit, soil and stone, so solid refuse can be handled as well as loose dirt. The signs are evenly spaced, so no side is favored. The modifiers are targeting, refuse collection and the guessed convergence, which work together without contradiction. The slight roughness of the Crosshair and the northwest glyph makes the aim and compaction a little less precise.
effect: Draws waste, dirt and debris inward from the four directions around the seal and presses it into a compact mass at the center, where steady heat scorches it and strong earth magic binds the solid grit and soil together. The aim wavers slightly, so some scattered refuse is missed or gathered unevenly.

name: s42_00292.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A small water sigil, an S-curve between two teardrops, sits upright at the center. Five Launch signs, each a peaked caret shape, sit around it. Three point inward toward the center: at the southwest, the east-southeast, and the north-northeast, the last one sitting closer to the center and drawn a little rough. Two point outward toward the ring, at the north-northwest and the south-southeast, roughly opposite each other. Two Detection signs, each three parallel strokes of different lengths, sit at the west-northwest and east-northeast, angled toward the center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell, and its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Launch sends the spell's material out as a powerful but short-lived burst in the direction it points. The three inward Launch signs are spread roughly evenly around the seal, so their bursts drive water toward the center and meet there. The two outward Launch signs sit on one axis and fire in opposite directions, toward the north-northwest and the south-southeast. Inward and outward Launch signs directly contradict each other. The inward trio outnumbers the outward pair and dominates, so the result is likely unstable. The rough north-northeast sign is slightly weaker than the others, which makes the inward push lopsided. Detection's function is not fully known; its name and its use in path-lighting magic suggest it senses a nearby presence. Reading it that way is an inference, and it would make the bursts respond to something approaching from the upper sides. Only two kinds of modifier are present, so the instability comes from the opposed Launch signs alone.
effect: Fires short, modest bursts of water that rush in toward the center of the seal and collide there unevenly, while weaker spurts break away toward the north-northwest and south-southeast. The bursts likely trigger when something is sensed nearby. They sputter, splash erratically, and die out quickly instead of forming a steady jet.

name: s42_00296.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, with the main ring closed and neatly drawn. A fire sigil sits upright at the center, moderate in size relative to the ring. Three Link signs sit close to the ring at the north-northeast, east-northeast and south-southwest, each with its top toward the center. Five Concealment signs, eight-armed stars with eye marks, also sit close to the ring at the north-northwest, west-northwest, west-southwest, south-southeast and east-southeast, each with its top toward the ring. The north-northwest one is drawn a little roughly. All eight signs are spread evenly around the ring. Two closed sub-seals sit inside the main ring. The western one is round and neat, with a small wind sigil at its center. The eastern one is drawn roughly and is noticeably out of round, with a small light sigil at its center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil makes this a fire spell, and its moderate size gives the flames and heat a moderate intensity. Link identifies objects that broke off from, or were made from, the same source and joins them, so the fire's effect carries across all such pieces. The five Concealment signs hide what the spell acts on, so the flame and the linked pieces stay out of sight. The signs are evenly balanced and none is directional, so the effect has no set direction. The western wind sub-seal moves air around the effect, giving it a steady draft. The eastern light sub-seal adds light, which belongs to the fire domain. Its ring is rough and out of round, so its contribution is weak and fleeting. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they do not contradict each other, so the main seal holds steady.
effect: Kindles a hidden flame of moderate strength that spreads its heat to every fragment from the same source, warming all of them at once while the fire itself stays unseen. A gentle draft circulates the warmth around the linked pieces. A faint glow flickers briefly at the edge and fades almost at once.

name: s42_00297.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed and neatly drawn. Two sigils share the center: an earth sigil on the left, moderate in size relative to the ring, and a smaller light sigil on the right, drawn a little roughly. Two Cooling signs, each a vertical stroke between pairs of dots, sit near the ring at the north-northeast and south-southwest. Two Dispersion signs sit near the ring at the northwest and east-northeast, each with its stem toward the center and its curve facing outward. Three of the four signs cluster on the upper side, so the layout leans toward the north-northeast. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the main element, so the spell acts on solid matter such as stone and soil. It is the larger of the two sigils and gives a moderate intensity. The light sigil, which falls within the fire domain, adds light. It is smaller and slightly rough, so its contribution is modest and less steady. Cooling lowers the temperature of what the spell acts on. Dispersion lets the magic pour outward rather than holding it in a fixed beam, and both Dispersion signs are in their normal orientation. The signs are unevenly placed, with most on the north-northeast side, so the outflow is weighted toward that direction. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they do not contradict each other.
effect: Chills nearby stone and soil, spreading the cold outward from the seal, with most of it flowing toward the north-northeast. A faint, slightly flickering glow seeps out along with the cold and gradually fades over time.

name: s42_00298.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed. The ring is drawn roughly and is noticeably out of round, bulging wider than it is tall with uneven, lumpy curves. An earth sigil sits upright at the center, large relative to the ring at roughly half its radius. Four Expansion signs, each made of nested corner brackets forming a square, sit near the ring at the north-northeast, east-southeast, south-southwest and west-northwest positions. Their corners point outward, the normal orientation, and some of the brackets are drawn a little less evenly than others. The four signs are spaced roughly a quarter turn apart, so the layout is balanced. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on existing solid matter such as stone, soil, sand and wood rather than creating any. Its large size relative to the ring gives a strong intensity. Expansion is semi-directional. With its corners pointing outward it makes its target grow, and its placement does not steer the effect. The four signs are evenly balanced, so the growth favors no direction. No Selection or Diamond sign is present to limit the spell to the object the seal is drawn on or to the things near it, so it acts on the earthen material within its reach. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing contradicts. The ring is closed, so the spell activates. However, its rough, poorly rounded shape and the roughly drawn sigil make the effect fleeting and uneven.
effect: Makes nearby stone, soil or wood swell to a larger size in a strong but lopsided surge that pulses unevenly. The enlarged material soon shrinks back as the spell gives out after only a brief moment.

name: s42_00299.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A small earth sigil sits upright at the center, about a fifth of the ring's radius. A Projection sign, a flat bracket with its open side facing the center, sits at the northeast about two thirds of the way to the ring. A Partition sign, layered arcs under a small peaked triangle, sits at the west at a similar distance. It is tilted slightly and drawn a little roughly. A Coil sign, two crossing curved strokes, sits at the north-northwest a little closer to the center and is also slightly rough. A Diamond sign, a small upright rhombus, sits near the ring at the south-southeast. The signs are spread evenly around the ring, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on solid matter such as stone, wood and soil. Its small size gives a modest intensity. Coil softens physical matter, and paired with earth it makes the spell's core action softening solid material. Projection sends an effect outward from the seal, and its placement pushes the effect toward the northeast. Partition outlines the borders of an area of effect reaching outward and upward, here on the west side. Diamond confines a spell to the contents of the container it is drawn on without affecting the container itself, which directly contradicts Projection's outward push. That makes four unrelated kinds of modifier. The earth sigil and Coil dominate, so softening is the main outcome. Projection and Diamond pull against each other, Partition only loosely bounds the result, and the rougher Coil and Partition signs weaken it further, so the result is likely unstable.
effect: Softens stone and soil weakly and unevenly. The softening wavers between staying on the material held within the marked object and spilling outward toward the northeast, with a loose boundary forming on the west side. It fades or collapses well before the matter is fully softened.

name: s42_00301.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background. The outer ring is closed and neatly drawn, with a second closed ring just inside it, leaving a narrow band between them. An Envelopment sign, a slanted stroke with short hooks at both ends, sits upright at the center of the inner ring. It is moderate in size, and there is no element sigil at the center. Five signs sit in the band between the rings. At the north-northwest is a Levitation sign with its arrow pointing outward toward the ring. At the northeast is a small unfamiliar glyph: a right-angled triangle with a small circle at its lower-left corner. Three Expansion signs, each made of nested corner brackets, sit at the west, east and south-southeast. The west one is drawn heavily and roughly. The south-southeast one is neat and faces the same way as the west one. The east one is slightly rough and turned the other way, with its top toward the center. Two small closed sub-seals sit inside the inner ring. The one at the west-northwest holds a small fire sigil. The one at the east-southeast holds an earth sigil that fills more of its small ring. The signs are spread unevenly, with more weight toward the north-northeast. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil at the center, Envelopment serves as the core, so the spell's effect wraps around and surrounds its target. The two attached sub-seals supply the elements. The earth sub-seal, with its relatively large sigil, brings in solid matter such as soil and stone. The smaller fire sub-seal adds heat. Both sub-seals are small relative to the main seal, so their contributions are modest. Expansion is semi-directional, so its orientation decides whether it grows or shrinks the target. The west and south-southeast signs face the normal way and enlarge it. The east sign is inverted and shrinks it, which directly contradicts the other two. Growth dominates because two signs favor it, but the rough west sign weakens that side and the inverted east sign pulls back against it. Levitation is directional, and pointing outward at the north-northwest it lifts and carries the effect that way. The northeast glyph matches no known sign; its closest match is Convergence, a triangle. Reading it as Convergence is a guess. Read that way, it focuses and packs the material toward a single point, which partly works against the swelling. The seal stacks growth-versus-shrinking, lifting and focusing on top of the enveloping core, and the Expansion signs contradict each other. Envelopment and the earth sub-seal dominate, Levitation sets the direction, and the size modifiers are the least reliable part, so the result is likely unstable.
effect: Wraps the target in a shell of warm packed earth that swells and contracts in uneven pulses, bulging on some sides while pulling tight on the eastern side. The shell lifts and drifts toward the north-northwest while it shifts, often cracking or losing its shape and collapsing before it fully settles.

name: s42_00302.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. The inner ring sits about three quarters of the way out, leaving a wide band between the rings. A Selection sign, a square cross-hatched into four cells with a long cross through it, sits at the center in place of a sigil and is fairly large relative to the ring. Just inside the inner ring at the south is a Sights Set sign with its diamond toward the center and its arrow pointing south toward the ring. An Immobility sign sits inside the inner ring at the northeast, rotated so its base bar faces the center. In the outer band, a small Rain sign sits at the north and a very small Piercing sign lies across the band at the east, close to the outer ring. There is no element sigil, and more signs sit toward the east-northeast than elsewhere. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, Selection takes the center and sets the core: the effect is confined to the object the seal is drawn on, and the spell is not tied to fire, water, earth or wind. Its large size gives the core a fairly strong presence, and the second ring adds strength and further effects. Immobility makes the target immovable relative to the seal so it holds its shape. Rain summons material from above, Piercing turns it into projectiles, and Sights Set, arrow pointing south, aims the effect in that direction. Rain and Piercing are drawn very small, so their part is weak. The seal stacks more than three unrelated kinds of modifier: confinement, fixing in place, summoning, projectiles and aiming. Immobility also works against the outward aimed projectiles, and confinement to the drawn object works against summoning from above. Selection and Immobility dominate, Sights Set sets the direction, and the faint Rain and Piercing contributions are least reliable, so the result is likely unstable. The uneven placement pulls the effect toward the east-northeast.
effect: Locks the object it is drawn on rigidly in place while it spits a thin, sputtering scatter of small projectiles aimed toward the south that drift off toward the east-northeast. The volleys come in uneven bursts and the hold flickers, and the spell collapses well before it settles.

name: s42_00303.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring open with a wide gap at the upper left, between the west-northwest and the north-northwest. A Binding sign, two stacked arcs opening downward, sits upright at the center in place of a sigil. It is large, reaching about half the ring's radius, and its strokes are slightly rough. Six Partition-like signs sit evenly spaced about three quarters of the way to the ring, each with its peaked top pointing toward the center. Five are clean Partition signs, at the north-northeast, east, south-southeast, south-southwest, and west. The sixth, at the northwest, is a Partition sign with an extra short stroke running from its top edge, which matches no known sign. The rest of the seal is neatly drawn, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: There is no element sigil, so Binding takes the central role and sets the spell's core behavior: it halts the movement of target material and binds it together so it acts and moves as a single unit. Its large size relative to the ring gives a fairly strong hold, and its slight roughness makes that hold a little less steady. Partition is directional and outlines the borders of an area of effect, extending outward and upward. With six of them evenly spaced and all facing inward, they enclose a balanced, roughly hexagonal zone around the seal, and the binding acts inside it. The northwest glyph is closest to Partition, so reading it as a Partition variant is a guess. Read that way, it simply continues the boundary on that side, and the arrangement stays balanced. With no element sigil, the spell is not tied to one material and binds whatever lies within the outlined area. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they agree with each other. The ring is open, so the seal will not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it marks out an enclosed zone around the seal, rising upward from it. Any material inside the zone is stopped in place and held together so it moves as one solid unit. The hold is strong but slightly unsteady, with a faint tremor in how firmly the material stays fixed.

name: s42_00304.png
description: A fully visible seal on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A fire sigil sits upright at the center at moderate size relative to the ring. Six Gathering signs sit near the ring at the north-northeast, east-northeast, east-southeast, south-southwest, west-southwest and west-northwest. The east-northeast and west-southwest signs point straight in toward the center, and the other four are tilted at various angles along the ring. The west-southwest sign is drawn heavier and rougher than the rest. At the south-southeast sits an octagon crossed by two lines, which matches no named sign exactly. At the north-northwest sits a small narrow triangle with a circle at one corner, which also matches no named sign. Two small closed sub-seals sit inside the main ring. The one at the lower left holds a fire sigil that fills about half of its ring. The one at the upper right holds a water sigil, and its ring is drawn more roughly. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and works heat and flame at a moderate intensity. Gathering lets a spell draw material from its surroundings to build its effect. Six of them spaced evenly around the ring pull material in from all sides, so the fire is fed inward toward the seal rather than sent in any direction. The tilted signs suggest that some material comes in at a slant, which is a guess, and the roughly drawn west-southwest sign draws a little more weakly on that side. The crossed octagon is closest to Selection, which is a guess. Read that way, it confines the effect to the object the seal is drawn on. The triangle with a circle is loosely fire-like and closest to Strengthening, also a guess, so it would reinforce the flame. The fire sub-seal has a large sigil for its size and adds extra heat. The water sub-seal brings an opposing element. Its small size and rough ring make it weak, so the main fire dominates, but the clash means the result is likely somewhat unstable.
effect: Draws heat and combustible material in from all around and feeds it into a moderate, contained flame on the object the seal is drawn on. The flame burns a little stronger than its size suggests, but it sputters and flickers unevenly, with faint bursts of damp mist that briefly dampen it, and it draws less fuel from the west-southwest side.

name: s42_00306.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background, drawn as two concentric rings. The outer ring is open, with a gap between the northeast and east. The inner ring is also open, with a gap at the south-southeast. A light sigil sits upright at the center, moderate in size relative to the ring: a diamond inside a square with four short spokes. Six Stability and Level Planes signs, each a pair of small wavy lines, sit in the band between the two rings at the northeast, east, south-southeast, south-southwest, west and north-northwest. All six have their tops toward the outer ring. They are spaced evenly, and the south-southwest sign is drawn with a heavier stroke than the others. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil makes this a light spell, and its moderate size relative to the ring gives a moderate intensity. Light made this way diminishes over time. Stability and Level Planes is non-directional and makes its target balance on a plane in the air, free to turn and drift but always staying level, like something floating on water. Six of these signs evenly spaced around the band mean no side is favored, and the heavier south-southwest stroke does not change the sign's direction. No Columns, Levitation or Regions signs push the effect anywhere, so the light simply holds level where it forms. The second ring adds strength to the core spell. Neither ring will let the seal activate while open, so both gaps must be closed.
effect: Once the ring is closed, the seal produces a moderate light that floats in a steady, level plane in the air. It can drift and turn without tipping and slowly dims over time.

name: s42_00307.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn neatly in black on a white background. The ring is open, with a gap at the top spanning roughly north-northwest to north-northeast. A small light sigil, a diamond inside a square with four short spokes, sits upright at the center and is small relative to the ring. Six Strengthening signs, each a triangle crossed by a bar, are spaced evenly about three quarters of the way out from the center. They sit at the south-southeast, southwest, west, north-northwest, northeast and east, each with its apex pointing outward toward the ring. No other signs are present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil makes this a light spell. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Strengthening makes its target stronger, harder and more durable. Applied to light, which normally diminishes over time, it reinforces the glow so it holds steady and lasts longer rather than fading quickly. All six signs are the same kind and evenly balanced, so no side is favored. There are no directional signs, so the light is not cast or aimed anywhere and stays at the seal. Only one kind of modifier is present, and the neat drawing gives a stable result. The seal will not activate until the gap in the ring is closed.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it produces a modest, even glow at the seal. The light is reinforced to stay steady and resist fading, lasting well beyond an ordinary light spell of its size.

name: s42_00309.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, drawn neatly, made of two concentric rings with the inner one just inside the outer, both ring closed. A large crossed octagon, an eight-sided outline with an X inside, sits upright at the center and fills about half the inner radius. Six chevron signs surround it at roughly even spacing, about two thirds of the way out, with their points facing the center. Five are Regions signs, at the northeast, east, south-southeast, south-southwest and west. The sixth, at the north-northwest, is a heavier, wider chevron that reads as a stretched Regions sign. Two small sub-seals sit outside the main ring, each joined to it by a short line and each ring closed. The one at the northwest holds a small, slightly rough earth sigil. The one at the southeast holds a Diamond sign at its center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The crossed octagon matches no known sign exactly; its closest match is Selection, a cross inside an enclosing shape, so reading it as Selection is a guess. Read that way, it confines the spell to the object the seal is drawn on, and its large size gives that confinement a strong hold. All six Regions signs, including the stretched one, point inward. That keeps the magic manifesting only within the ring and not outside it. Because they are balanced, no direction is favored. The main seal has no element sigil, so the attached earth sub-seal supplies the element, and the spell acts on solid matter such as stone, sand and soil. That sigil is small and a little rough, so the earth effect is weak. The Diamond sub-seal makes a spell affect only what lies inside the container it is drawn on, not the container itself. This directly contradicts Selection, which targets the object itself. The large Selection reading in the main seal dominates, and the small Diamond sub-seal pulls against it, so the result is likely unstable.
effect: Weakly shifts and loosens stone, sand or soil, and only within the bounds of the seal. The effect keeps flickering between the object the seal is drawn on and whatever that object holds, acting unevenly on each and never settling on either.

name: s42_00310.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, neatly drawn, with the ring open at the lower right between the south-southeast and east-southeast points. No element sigil is present. Two signs share the center: a Binding sign, two stacked arcs opening downward, just left of center, and a Rain sign, a square with bowed sides and short rays on each side, just right of center. Both are moderate in size relative to the ring. A Cooling sign, a slash flanked by dots, sits near the ring at the north-northwest with its top toward the ring. A second Cooling sign sits at the south with its top toward the center, so it faces the opposite way. A Piercing sign, a diamond on a straight line, lies diagonally at the east-northeast. A Partition sign sits at the west with its peak facing outward toward the ring. A Launch sign at the east-southeast is rotated so its point faces roughly south-southwest, and it is drawn much heavier and thicker than the other signs. Near the ring at the south-southeast is a small, faint glyph lying on its side. It has a Columns-like crossbar and stem with a small circle at the foot of the stem, the circle toward the west and the crossbar toward the east. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, Rain at the center acts as the core and summons material falling from above. The spell is not tied to any one element. Binding beside it halts the material's movement and binds it into a single unit. Cooling chills the effect. The two Cooling signs face opposite ways. Cooling has never been seen reversed, so whether the southern one inverts it is unknown, but if it does, the two would partly cancel. The single Piercing sign turns part of the magic into one projectile. Partition at the west, facing outward, outlines a boundary for the area of effect on that side. Launch produces a powerful but short-lived burst in the direction it points, here south-southwest, and its heavy drawing makes that burst stand out. The faint south-southeast glyph matches no known sign. It most closely resembles Columns fused with Solidification, which is a guess. Read that way, it would push the effect along an east-west line and make it more solid. The seal stacks well over three unrelated kinds of modifier, and Launch's outward burst directly opposes Binding's hold. Rain and Binding at the center dominate, with Launch as the strongest outer force, so the result is likely unstable.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it calls down a chilled, rain-like fall of material inside an area bounded on its western side. The falling material clumps and stiffens into bound masses as it lands, while a single sharp projectile and a brief, forceful burst shoot off toward the south-southwest. The fall comes unevenly, the clumps keep breaking apart as the burst tears at them, and the spell sputters out well before it finishes.

name: s42_00312.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but noticeably out of round, bulging into a lumpy, roughly five-lobed shape. Two small glyphs sit side by side at the center, both small relative to the ring: an upright Regions chevron, pointing north, on the left, and a thin Coil sign on the right. Three four-lobed Billow signs sit about two thirds of the way out from the center, at the north, southeast and west-southwest, each turned at a different angle. All the glyphs are drawn somewhat roughly. There is no element sigil, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the seal is not tied to fire, water, earth or wind. It acts on whatever material is brought to it. Billow turns available material into a soft, fluffy cloud. It is non-directional, so its rotations change nothing, and three evenly spaced Billows spread that effect around the seal. Coil softens physical matter and has no effect on liquids or gases, so it loosens solid material and makes it easier to puff into cloud. Regions is directional and sets where magic manifests relative to the seal. A single upright chevron at the center points north, so the effect is pushed toward that side. These three kinds of modifier work together without contradiction. The small central glyphs and rough linework make the spell weak and short-lived. The ring is not round enough, so any effect is fleeting and the seal may fail to activate.
effect: Softens nearby solid material and briefly puffs it into a thin, lumpy cloud that drifts toward the north side of the seal, sputtering unevenly and dispersing almost as soon as it forms. It acts only on solid matter, not liquids or gases, and may fizzle without producing any cloud at all.

name: s42_00315.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A fire sigil sits upright at the center, small relative to the ring and drawn roughly. Four Collection signs sit about three fifths of the way out from the center, at the north-northeast, east-southeast, southwest and northwest. Each is rotated so its barred end points toward the center and its open side faces the ring. The northeast and east-southeast signs are slightly rough, and the southwest and northwest signs are drawn more roughly, with the southwest one heavily inked. The signs are spaced roughly evenly around the seal. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil makes this a fire spell. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity, and its rough drawing weakens it further. Collection normally gathers material above and around the seal for the spell to use, with its open side facing inward. Here all four open sides face outward, which reverses that usual orientation. Collection has never been seen this way, so this reading is a guess. If the sign behaves like other semi-directional signs, the reversal flips its effect, scattering material away from the seal instead of drawing it in. The four signs are balanced, so the effect favors no direction. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing contradicts. However, the rough strokes on the sigil and two of the signs make the spell weaker and shorter lived.
effect: Kindles a small, flickering flame at the seal that pushes loose material around it outward evenly on all sides instead of feeding on it. Starved of fuel, the flame burns weakly and unevenly, and it dies out sooner than a cleanly drawn fire would.

name: s42_00316.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A large Dancing Puppets sign sits upright at the center in place of a sigil, drawn boldly at about half the ring's radius: a small ring with four loops at north, east, south and west, crossed by curved strokes and short ticks. There is no element sigil. Five single signs sit near the ring. A small Windows sign, a circle lined with radial hatching, is at the northwest. A Piercing sign, a line through a small diamond, is at the northeast, angled with its stem along the line toward the center. A Holding sign, two curved strokes with dots, is at the west-southwest, turned well off upright. A Pulling sign is at the south, its arrowhead pointing inward toward the center. An Immobility sign is at the east, turned so its crossbar faces the ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, Dancing Puppets at the center is the core, so the spell manipulates the movement of objects, and with no element it is not tied to any one material. The inward-pointing Pulling sign at the south draws targets toward the seal. Holding keeps the target in a defined shape while letting it move, and Immobility fixes it in place relative to the seal. That fixing works directly against the free movement Dancing Puppets and Pulling provide. Piercing turns the effect into projectiles, and the single Windows sign would connect the seal to a separate space. This stacks four unrelated kinds of modifier: portal, projectile, pulling, and shape-holding or fixing. Dancing Puppets and Pulling dominate, so the main behavior is movement drawn toward the seal. Immobility and Holding are secondary and fight that movement, while Piercing and Windows act only intermittently. The result is likely unstable. The even spacing means no single side is favored beyond the inward pull.
effect: Drags nearby objects in toward the seal and jerks them about erratically, seizing them rigid for moments before they lurch free again. At times pieces are flung off as sharp projectiles, or flicker briefly as if passing through to somewhere else. The motion never settles into steady control and breaks down well before a stable seal would.

name: s42_00317.png
description: A fully visible seal on a white background, main ring closed and neatly drawn. An earth sigil sits at the center at moderate size, about a third of the ring's radius. Inside the main ring are six signs, crowded toward the south. A Stillness sign sits near the ring at the northwest. A Dispersion sign sits at the northeast, about two-thirds of the way out, pointing outward. An Envelopment sign sits at the southeast, about halfway out. Just beyond it, almost on the ring, is an Immobility sign turned with its top toward the center. A Rain sign sits at the south-southwest, about halfway out. A Pointing sign sits below it near the ring, also turned with its top toward the center. Two smaller sub-seals are joined to the main ring by short lines. The northeast one has its ring closed and holds a wind sigil at its center. The southwest one has an open ring, with a gap at its lower right, and holds a Partition sign at its center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell works on solid matter such as soil, sand and stone, and its moderate size gives moderate intensity. Earth does not create matter, so Rain, which summons its target, here calls existing earth down from above. Envelopment makes the material surround its target, and Pointing gives it a conical shape. Stillness tries to hold the effect in one place. Immobility is drawn turned toward the center, opposite the other signs, and as a semi-directional sign it reads as inverted, so it would loosen the material instead of fixing it. That clashes directly with Stillness. Dispersion pours the magic outward, which also works against Stillness and Envelopment. With the signs bunched to the south, the effect leans that way. The closed wind sub-seal adds moving air. The Partition sub-seal has an open ring, so it adds nothing and no boundary is set. The seal stacks more than three unrelated kinds of modifier and contains direct contradictions. The earth sigil, Rain and Envelopment dominate, while Stillness, the inverted Immobility and Dispersion pull against each other, so the result is likely unstable.
effect: Calls down a moderate shower of loose soil and grit that drifts toward the south and tries to close around its target in a rough cone. Gusts of air push the mass about, and it keeps alternating between briefly locking in place and crumbling outward, so it never sets firmly and collapses early with no clear edge to the area it covers.

name: s42_00319.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background. The ring is closed but drawn roughly and noticeably out of round, with a lumpy outline. Two glyphs share the center: a Selection sign on the left and a slightly larger water sigil on the right, both small relative to the ring and a little rough. A single Columns sign sits near the ring at the southwest, with its stem toward the center and its crossbar toward the ring. Four Billow signs, each a four-lobed clover, sit about three quarters of the way out at the north-northwest, north-northeast, east and south-southwest. The north-northeast and south-southwest ones are drawn heavier and rougher than the rest. Three smaller closed rings sit outside the main ring, each joined to it by a short line. The north sub-seal holds an Expansion sign with its corners pointing outward, the southeast sub-seal holds a Glaives sign, and the west-southwest sub-seal holds an Envelopment sign. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil sets the element, and its small size gives a modest intensity. Selection shares the center and confines the effect to the object the seal is drawn on. The four Billow signs are non-directional and turn the material into a fluffy cloud, so the water becomes a soft mist. Their orientation does not change this, and their even spacing favors no side. The lone Columns sign at the southwest is unbalanced, so it pushes a column-shaped effect toward the southwest. This pulls against Selection, which holds the effect to the object. The attached sub-seals add more effects. Expansion with its corners outward makes the cloud swell, Envelopment makes it wrap around its target, and Glaives sets how deeply the magic embeds into flesh. That stacks more than three unrelated kinds of modifier: cloud forming, direction, growth, envelopment and embedding into flesh. The water sigil and the four Billow signs dominate, so the core result is a water cloud. The southwest push and the confinement to the object contradict each other, so the result is likely unstable. The rough, out-of-round ring and linework make the effect weak and fleeting, and it may barely activate.
effect: Puffs water into a thin, soft cloud that swells in uneven bursts around the object it is drawn on, tugging off toward the southwest before snapping back. Where the cloud touches skin, it seeps in patchily. The cloud flickers between clinging and drifting and breaks apart after only a short time.

name: s42_00320.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background. The ring is open, with a wide gap at the bottom between the south-southwest and south-southeast. A wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes on each side, sits upright at the center and is fairly large relative to the ring. Six Solidification signs, each two small circles joined by a short line, surround it. Five sit near the ring at the north-northeast, east, southeast, west-southwest and northwest, each angled roughly toward the center. The sixth sits closer in, at the south, tilted slightly. The east sign is drawn with a heavier line, and the north-northeast and northwest signs are slightly rough. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves and manipulates existing air rather than creating it. Its fairly large size relative to the ring gives a fairly strong intensity. Solidification makes the magic drawn within or connected to it more solid, so the moved air is firmed into a denser, more solid mass. All six signs are the same kind of modifier and are spread evenly around the ring. That adds no direction, so the firmed air stays gathered around the seal instead of being pushed to one side. The slightly rough signs at the east, north-northeast and northwest make the firming somewhat less even on those sides. The seal will not activate until the gap in the ring is closed.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it draws in the surrounding air and stiffens it into a fairly strong, cushion-like mass of solid air held in place over the seal. The mass is slightly softer and less even toward its north and east sides.

name: s42_00323.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background, ring closed but drawn roughly and noticeably out of round, with a lumpy, uneven outline. An earth sigil sits at the center, roughly a third of the ring's radius, drawn roughly. Six signs sit near the ring, all drawn roughly. A Selection sign is at the north and an Orb sign at the east. An inverted Rain sign is at the southeast, flipped inside out so its sides curve inward. A Stillness sign at the south is rotated almost upside down. An Expansion sign at the west-southwest is drawn heavily, with its nested brackets inked thick and dark. A Pointing sign is at the northwest. A small closed sub-seal sits inside the main ring at the west, neatly drawn, with a small water sigil at its center. The signs are spread evenly around the ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on solid matter such as soil, stone and sand. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. The neat, closed water sub-seal adds a small amount of water, so the matter is dampened. Selection confines the effect to the object the seal is drawn on. Expansion, not inverted, makes the target grow. Stillness holds the effect static in one place. Orb defines a spherical space where material collects, while Pointing forces a conical shape, and these two shapes directly contradict each other. Inverted Rain creates an area that pushes material away, which contradicts Orb's collecting. The seal stacks six unrelated kinds of modifier: confinement, growth, stillness, spherical collection, conical shaping and repulsion. The earth sigil, Selection and Expansion dominate, so the core is growing the matter of the drawn-on object, held in place by Stillness. The clashing shape and repulsion signs make the result likely unstable. The rough linework and out-of-round ring make the effect weaker and fleeting, and it may fail to activate at all.
effect: Briefly swells the soil or stone of the object it is drawn on, dampening it with a little water while the mass stays fixed in place. The swelling lurches unevenly between a rounded lump and a tapered point and sheds loose grit outward. It often sputters out without taking hold, and when it does hold, it collapses after a few moments.

name: s42_00324.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, neatly drawn, with the ring open by a gap at the north-northwest. An upright Crosshair sign sits at the center in place of a sigil, moderately sized relative to the ring. Five Stillness signs sit near the ring at the west-northwest, northeast, east, south-southeast and southwest, each with its top toward the ring. The south-southeast one is a little rougher than the others. A small, thinly drawn glyph sits right at the gap in the ring at the north-northwest. It looks like a Gathering sign with a small circle on its stem and matches no known sign exactly. No element sigil is present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the spell is not tied to fire, water, earth or wind and acts on whatever material it is given. The central Crosshair is directional and makes the seal's effect target whatever its short ends point at. Upright, its ends point north, south, east and west, so the effect is aimed at those four points around the seal. Stillness keeps a magical effect static in a single location, and five of them spread around the ring hold the targeted effect firmly in place. The unnamed glyph is closest to Gathering, so reading it that way is a guess. Gathering draws material in from the surroundings for the spell to use, and the added circle on the stem may tighten that pull. Read together, these signs gather loose material and hold it fixed at the aimed points. The signs complement one another rather than contradicting each other, so the seal is not unstable. The slightly rough Stillness at the south-southeast makes the hold a little weaker on that side. The ring is open, so nothing activates until the gap is closed.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it draws in loose material from around the seal and pins it motionless at points to the north, south, east and west of the seal, where it hangs still in place. The hold is slightly weaker toward the south-southeast, where the material may drift a little.

name: s42_00325.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but noticeably out of round, with a lumpy, uneven outline. Two sigils sit side by side near the center, both small relative to the ring. On the left is a light sigil, a diamond inside a square with four short spokes, drawn roughly. On the right is a water sigil, an S-curve between two teardrops, drawn a little rough. Two Solidification signs, each two small circles joined by a short line, sit about halfway out at the north and south points. Six small Diamond signs sit close to the ring at roughly even intervals: north-northeast, east-northeast, southeast, south-southwest, west-southwest and northwest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell. The light sigil, which falls within the fire domain, adds light that diminishes over time. Their small size relative to the ring gives both a modest intensity. Solidification makes the magic connected to it more solid, so the water firms up instead of staying loose and liquid. The two signs face each other across the center and balance one another. Diamond limits the spell to objects inside a container it is drawn on without affecting the container itself. Six of them spread evenly around the edge apply that limit on all sides. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they agree, so the seal is not unstable. However, the rough sigils make the effect weaker and shorter lived. The ring's poor roundness makes the effect fleeting and puts its activation at risk.
effect: Firms the water held inside the vessel the seal is drawn on into a faintly glowing, jelly-like mass, leaving the vessel itself untouched. The firmness sets unevenly and the glow is weak and patchy. Both fade within moments, and the spell sometimes fails to take hold at all.

name: s42_00326.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with two rings, both closed. The rings are drawn roughly and are noticeably out of round, closer to a rounded hexagon than a circle. The band between them is empty. A large Stability and Level Planes sign, three wavy vertical strokes, sits upright at the center in place of a sigil. It spans about half the ring radius and is slightly rough. Seven signs surround it, all inside the inner ring. A Windows sign, a small circle edged with hatching, sits at the northwest, drawn neatly. A Pointing sign sits at the north, rotated off-axis. A Holding sign, a pair of curved strokes, sits at the northeast, rotated diagonally. A Regions chevron sits at the west with its point aimed inward toward the center. A Stillness sign sits at the southwest with its top toward the center, slightly rough. A Crushing zigzag sits at the south with its peaks toward the ring. An Aeriforms Defined sign, three short strokes, sits at the southeast with its top toward the ring, slightly rough. No element sigil is present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the central Stability and Level Planes sign is the core of the seal. Its large size makes it the strongest part, so whatever the seal affects is held balanced on a level plane. Holding keeps the target in the shape the seal defines. Stillness keeps the effect static in one place. Together with the core, these two dominate and point toward a held, motionless mass. Aeriforms Defined ties the effect to air or gas, so that is the most likely material. Pointing shapes the material into a cone. The inward Regions sign keeps the magic inside the ring. Windows tries to connect the space to another location, which works against Regions confining the effect to the ring. Crushing, with its peaks toward the ring in its normal orientation, breaks matter into pieces. This directly contradicts Holding and Stillness, which keep the shape intact. The seal stacks well over three unrelated kinds of modifier: holding, stillness, gas, cone shaping, confinement, portal and crushing. The holding core dominates, Crushing and Windows fight it, and the result is likely unstable. The rough, out-of-round rings and the slightly rough signs further weaken it and shorten how long it lasts.
effect: Within the bounds of the seal, a small mass of air settles into a level, cone-shaped pocket and is held still. It is repeatedly torn apart and pulled back together in uneven fits, and it flickers as though briefly opening onto somewhere else. The effect wavers throughout and collapses after only a short time.

name: s42_00328.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background, with the main ring closed and neatly drawn. The center of the main ring is empty, with no sigil. Three small Dancing Puppets signs sit about halfway out from the center, at the east-northeast, south and west-northwest. The southern one is drawn heavy and dark, almost blotted. Three Purification signs sit near the ring at the north-northeast, southeast and west, each curling with its top toward the ring. The western one is drawn more roughly than the others. A small closed sub-seal sits outside the main ring at the north, joined to it by a short line. It holds a fire sigil of moderate size relative to its own ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The main ring has no element sigil, so its signs act on whatever the seal works on. The attached fire sub-seal is closed, so it supplies heat to the spell. Its small ring keeps that contribution modest. Dancing Puppets lets a target's movement be manipulated from a distance. It has no wind sigil here to lift objects into the air, so it steers motion rather than causing flight. Its three signs are evenly spaced, so they set no fixed direction. The rough, heavy southern sign makes that control less smooth. Purification separates waste from water. It is asymmetric, so its exact behavior is less predictable, and the roughly drawn western sign weakens it further. The seal combines only two kinds of modifier with one element, and they do not contradict each other.
effect: Gives off a modest heat while letting the warmed material be steered from a distance, sifting waste out of any water it moves. The steering is somewhat jerky and uneven rather than smooth, and the cleansing works patchily, with some impurities left behind.

name: s42_00329.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, made of two neat concentric rings. The outer ring is open, with a wide gap at the west-northwest. The inner ring is also open, with a gap at the northeast. The center is empty, with no sigil. Seven Reflection signs, each an hourglass of two triangles meeting at a point, are spread around the seal. Three sit in the band between the rings or on the outer edge: one at the north and one at the south, both upright with their tops toward the ring, and one at the west-northwest inside the gap of the outer ring, with its top toward the center. Four more sit inside the inner ring about halfway out: one at the south with its top toward the ring, and one each at the north-northwest, west-southwest and east-northeast with their tops toward the center. More signs cluster on the western half, so the layout leans west. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: There is no element sigil, so the spell is not tied to fire, water, earth or wind. With the center empty, the Reflection signs set its whole purpose. Reflection targets a reflected image found on the object the seal is drawn on. The second ring strengthens that core effect. No Projection, Concealment or other sign is present to shape, display or alter the image, so the spell only takes hold of the reflection. The signs face different ways, but Reflection is not known to change with orientation, and only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing in the seal contradicts itself. Because more signs sit on the western side, the effect is weighted toward the west. Both rings are open, so nothing activates until they are closed.
effect: Once the rings are closed, it latches onto the reflected image on the surface the seal is drawn on, gripping most strongly on the western side of that surface. The image is held fast but is not projected or displayed anywhere.
